common_confusions: BC-MIS-10022 (radius and interval reported for one another)
BC-SKL-10060 (writing the general term rather than reading it)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10013 (the endpoints are located relative to the centre)
BC-QA-10014 (the radius is measured from the centre)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response recognises the power series form, names the centre as the number subtracted from x inside the powers, and states the coefficients as a sequence in n separate from the powers; the centre is read from x minus a rather than from a sign convention. BC-ERR-10034 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The form is recognised and the centre is reported with the wrong sign, so x plus three is read as centre three, or the coefficients are described with the power of x minus a still folded into them.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The general term cannot be separated into a coefficient and a power from the sigma, which is BC-PRQ-10008.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-CON-10001 (centre and coefficients of a power series) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10008 (reading the general term) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a series, recognise the power series form and state its centre and its coefficients.
skills.description_plain: Read off the number the powers are taken around.
skills.name: Identify a power series and its centre

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10014 (a ratio limit of one taken as a result)
BC-SKL-10031 (the same ratio for a numerical series)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10013 (the ratio and the limit are the first two of five points)
BC-QA-10014 (the radius rests on this limit)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response forms the ratio of the term with index n plus one to the term with index n for the series in x, cancels the common powers and factorials, and evaluates the limit as an expression in the absolute value of x minus the centre with limit notation present. BC-ERR-10021 and BC-ERR-10017 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The ratio is formed with n plus one substituted in some positions and not others, which is BC-ERR-10021, or the reciprocal ratio is presented and carried through consistently, which is BC-SIG-10003 and blocks only the final interval point, or the limit symbol is dropped, which is BC-ERR-10017.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The factorial ratio does not simplify, which is BC-PRQ-10002, the powers with a common base do not reduce, which is BC-PRQ-10007, or the limit in n cannot be taken, which is BC-PRQ-10004.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-CON-10001 (the ratio test applied in the variable x) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10007 (ratios of powers) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a power series, write the ratio of the term with index n plus one to the term with index n, simplify, and evaluate the limit as an expression in the absolute value of x minus the centre.
skills.description_plain: Form the ratio of consecutive terms of the series in x and take its limit.
skills.name: Apply the ratio test to a power series

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10014 (a ratio limit of one treated as a result)
BC-SKL-10025 (the limit comparison quotient of two different series)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10013 (the ratio is the first of five points and is banked once earned)
BC-QA-10014 (the limit point requires the ratio point first)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response writes the absolute value of a sub n plus one over a sub n with n plus one substituted in every place the index occurs, including inside factorials and exponents such as two n plus three where two n plus one stood, and keeps the absolute value bars. BC-ERR-10021 and BC-ERR-10022 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The substitution is made in some positions and not others, most visibly in an exponent, which is BC-ERR-10021 and keeps the early points while blocking the final interval, or the bars are dropped, which is BC-ERR-10022.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: A ratio of factorials cannot be simplified, which is BC-PRQ-10002, or a quotient of powers with the same base cannot be reduced, which is BC-PRQ-10007.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-CON-10001 (what the ratio test compares) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10002 (factorial ratios) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a series, write the quotient of the term with index n plus one by the term with index n, taking absolute values and substituting n plus one everywhere the index appears.
skills.description_plain: Write the next term over the current term, in absolute value.
skills.name: Set up the ratio of consecutive terms of a series

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10014 (a ratio limit of one taken as a conclusion)
BC-SKL-10011 (the limit of a sub n rather than of the ratio)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10013 (the limit is scored separately from the ratio)
BC-QA-10014 (the radius rests on this limit)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response cancels the factorials and the common powers in the ratio, then evaluates the limit as n increases without bound with the limit symbol present, producing either a number or an expression in the absolute value of x minus the centre. BC-ERR-10017 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The ratio is formed correctly and the limit is evaluated to the wrong value, which is BC-SIG-10002 and banks the ratio point while losing the limit point, or the limit symbol is omitted, which is BC-ERR-10017.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The factorial ratio does not reduce, which is BC-PRQ-10002, or the powers with a common base are mishandled, which is BC-PRQ-10007.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-CON-10001 (the ratio limit as the deciding quantity) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10002 (simplifying factorial ratios) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the ratio of consecutive terms, simplify factorials and powers, and evaluate the limit as n increases without bound with limit notation present.
skills.description_plain: Simplify the quotient and take its limit as the index grows.
skills.name: Evaluate the limit of the ratio of consecutive terms

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10023 (the interior taken as the finished interval of convergence)
BC-SKL-10059 (the final interval with endpoint inclusion)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10013 (the interior is a point of its own and an incorrect interior that earned it still supports the endpoint point)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response sets the ratio limit less than one and solves the absolute value inequality into a compound inequality in x or an open interval, showing both bounds around the centre. BC-ERR-10035 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The inequality is solved as a one sided statement, producing a half interval, which is BC-SIG-10007 and BC-ERR-10035, so the interior point is not earned although the ratio and limit points stand.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The absolute value inequality cannot be split into two inequalities, which is BC-PRQ-10001, or the result cannot be written in interval form, which is BC-PRQ-10006.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-CON-10001 (the interior as the set where the ratio limit is below one) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10001 (solving absolute value inequalities) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a ratio limit set to be less than one, solve the resulting absolute value inequality and present the interior of the interval as a compound inequality or an open interval.
skills.description_plain: Turn the inequality in absolute value into a two sided inequality in x.
skills.name: Solve the ratio inequality for the interior of the interval

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10023 (the ratio test result taken as final)
BC-MIS-10024 (one endpoint's verdict transferred to the other)
BC-SKL-10066 (evaluating a series at a point inside the interval)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10015 (the endpoint series has to be produced before it can be tested)
BC-QA-10013 (considering both endpoints is a scored step)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response substitutes each endpoint value for the variable x in the general term, not for the index, and simplifies each result to a numerical series, keeping the alternating factor that a negative endpoint produces; both endpoint series are written out. BC-ERR-10034 and BC-ERR-10037 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: One endpoint is substituted and the other is left untouched, or the substitution drops the sign factor that a negative endpoint creates, which is BC-ERR-10034, or the open interior is reported with no endpoint work at all, which is BC-SIG-10004 and BC-ERR-10037.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The general term cannot be read from the sigma so the variable cannot be located in it, which is BC-PRQ-10008, or the resulting power cannot be simplified, which is BC-PRQ-06002.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10023 (why the endpoints need separate treatment) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10008 (substituting into the general term) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the interior of the interval, substitute each endpoint value for the variable in the general term and simplify the resulting numerical series, including any alternating factor that appears.
skills.description_plain: Put each endpoint value into the general term and simplify to a series of numbers.
skills.name: Substitute each endpoint to produce the two numerical series

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10024 (one verdict transferred to both ends)
BC-MIS-10007 (a test named without its hypotheses)
BC-SKL-10021 (test selection in general)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10015 (the reason point is lost when the test named does not fit the series)
BC-QA-10013 (the analysis at both endpoints carries the final interval)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response names a test at each endpoint whose conditions that particular series meets, so an alternating endpoint series takes the alternating series test and a positive term endpoint series takes a comparison, a p-series criterion, or the integral test, and it runs the two endpoints independently with a verdict at each. BC-ERR-10015 and BC-ERR-10037 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: One endpoint is tested correctly and its verdict is carried to the other, which is BC-SIG-10005, or a test is named whose conditions the endpoint series does not meet, which is BC-SIG-10006 and BC-ERR-10015.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The endpoint series were never produced, so no test has an object: that is BC-SKL-10057 rather than a test selection gap; reading the signed general term is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10024 (the two endpoint series as separate problems) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-10021 (matching a test to a form) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the two endpoint series, name and apply a suitable convergence test at each endpoint separately, and report convergence or divergence at each.
skills.description_plain: Apply a test that fits each endpoint series, which may differ between the two ends.
skills.name: Test each endpoint series with an appropriate test

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10023 (endpoints never examined and the interval reported open)
BC-MIS-10022 (an interval given where a radius was requested)
BC-SKL-10056 (the radius)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10013 (the final interval point requires the interval to match the endpoint analysis)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response writes the interval with a bracket at each end matching that endpoint's verdict, closed where the endpoint series converges and open where it diverges, and leaves an unbounded end open. BC-ERR-10038 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Both endpoints are tested correctly and the brackets written do not match those findings, which is BC-ERR-10038, or the interior is reported as the interval with both ends open although one endpoint converges.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Interval notation itself is not controlled, so open and closed ends cannot be written, which is BC-PRQ-10006.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10023 (what the endpoint verdicts decide) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10006 (interval notation) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the interior and the endpoint results, present the interval of convergence with brackets or inequality symbols that match the endpoint findings.
skills.description_plain: Report the interval with each end open or closed as its test showed.
skills.name: State the interval of convergence with the correct endpoint inclusion

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10012 (the alternating factor treated as the whole of the test)
BC-SKL-10034 (forming the absolute value series for a different purpose)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10004 (the shape of the series decides which test may be named)
BC-QA-10015 (a negative endpoint produces the alternating factor)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response points to the factor that changes the sign from term to term, a power of negative one or a cosine of n pi, and writes the sequence of absolute values of the terms as a separate object with the sign factor stripped. BC-ERR-10015 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The alternating factor is spotted and the absolute values are never written, so the size conditions have nothing to be checked on, or a series of positive terms is treated as alternating because a negative sign appears in a constant, which is BC-ERR-10015.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The sign factor cannot be read out of the sigma notation, which is BC-PRQ-10008 rather than an alternating series gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10012 (what the alternating factor alone establishes) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10008 (reading an alternating factor) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a series in sigma or expanded form, identify the factor that alternates the sign and write the sequence of absolute values of the terms.
skills.description_plain: Spot the factor that flips the sign from term to term.
skills.name: Recognise a series as alternating

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10012 (the alternating factor taken as the whole test)
BC-MIS-10007 (the test name treated as the argument)
BC-SKL-10058 (the same test applied at an endpoint)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10004 (a conclusion with no supporting condition earns the first point only)
BC-QA-10015 (an alternating endpoint series needs both conditions stated)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response names the alternating series test, states both that the terms alternate in sign with absolute values decreasing and that those absolute values have limit zero, and concludes convergence for the named series. BC-ERR-10020 and BC-ERR-10009 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: One of the two conditions is stated and the other is left out while the verdict is given, which is BC-ERR-10020, or the test is named with no condition attached at all, which is BC-ERR-10009.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The terms cannot be read as a signed sequence in n, which is BC-PRQ-06005, so neither condition can be stated.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10012 (the full hypothesis set of the alternating series test) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-06005 (reading the signed general term) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an alternating series whose terms decrease in absolute value to zero, state both conditions and conclude convergence by the alternating series test.
skills.description_plain: Name the test and state that the terms decrease in magnitude to zero.
skills.name: Conclude convergence by the alternating series test with both conditions stated

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10017 (an error bound treated as a formula with no hypotheses)
BC-SKL-10030 (the same two conditions used for convergence rather than for the bound)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10008 (the justification point requires the conditions and the inequality together)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response states, before any bound is written, that the series alternates in sign and that the absolute values of its terms decrease to zero, and presents those two statements as what licenses the alternating series error bound. BC-ERR-10020 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The correct bounding term is used and the two conditions are never stated, which is BC-SIG-10015 and BC-ERR-10020, so the justification point is lost while the term point stands.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The signed general term cannot be read, so neither condition can be asserted about it, which is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10017 (what licenses the alternating series bound) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-10028 (verifying the decrease) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a request to bound the error of a partial sum, state that the series is alternating with terms decreasing in absolute value to zero, which is the condition that licenses the bound.
skills.description_plain: State that the series alternates and its terms decrease to zero before using the bound.
skills.name: Confirm the alternating series test conditions before bounding the error

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10017 (the bound treated as a formula attached to the partial sum)
BC-SKL-10049 (the next derivative, the analogous step in the Lagrange bound)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10008 (the first point is earned only for the correct omitted term)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response counts the terms already contained in the partial sum and writes the very next term of the series explicitly, in its symbolic form, as the quantity that bounds the error. BC-ERR-10024 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The bounding term is identified one place too far along or is taken from inside the partial sum, which is BC-SIG-10016 and BC-ERR-10024, so the term point is not earned even when the subsequent arithmetic is clean.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The general term cannot be evaluated at the required index, which is BC-PRQ-10008, or the index cannot be shifted to locate the next one, which is BC-PRQ-10003.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-CON-10001 (the omitted tail as what the bound measures) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10003 (index counting) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a partial sum of a stated number of terms, identify the next term of the series as the one that bounds the error and write it explicitly.
skills.description_plain: Find the term just past the last one used.
skills.name: Identify the first omitted term of the partial sum

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10018 (the bounding expression treated as the exact error)
BC-SKL-10040 (identifying the term, the step before the substitution)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10008 (the point attached to using the term correctly turns on the value substituted)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response substitutes the input the prompt names into the first omitted term, evaluates its absolute value, and reports a number; the value substituted is the stated input rather than the centre or the index. BC-ERR-10025 and BC-ERR-10024 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The correct omitted term is identified and the index or the centre is substituted in place of the input, which is BC-ERR-10025, or the power in the term is evaluated with an arithmetic slip while the setup stands.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The power or factorial in the term cannot be evaluated, which is BC-PRQ-06002, or the term cannot be read from the sigma, which is BC-PRQ-10008.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10018 (bound against exact error) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-06002 (evaluating the power) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the first omitted term and a numerical input, substitute and evaluate the absolute value of that term.
skills.description_plain: Substitute the stated value into the first omitted term and compute its size.
skills.name: Evaluate the bounding term at the given input

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10018 (the bound read as the exact error)
BC-SKL-10051 (the same comparison for the Lagrange bound)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10008 (an equality statement does not earn the justification point)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response presents a chain of inequalities, the absolute error is at most the evaluated bounding term and that term is at most the stated tolerance, with inequality symbols rather than an equals sign and with the tolerance named. BC-ERR-10026 and BC-ERR-10027 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The bounding value is correct and the relation is written as an equality, which is BC-SIG-10014 and BC-ERR-10026, or the value is computed and never set against the tolerance the prompt named, which is BC-ERR-10027.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The inequality against the tolerance cannot be resolved once absolute value bars are present, which is BC-PRQ-10001.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10018 (at most against exactly) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10001 (inequalities with absolute value) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an evaluated bounding term and a tolerance, present the inequality stating that the error is at most the bounding term and that the bounding term is at most the tolerance.
skills.description_plain: Write the chain of inequalities that puts the error under the required number.
skills.name: Compare the error bound with a stated tolerance

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10020 (the requested number of terms not treated as binding)
BC-SKL-10069 (term by term integration, the inverse operation)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10018 (the general term of the differentiated series carries its own point)
BC-QA-10016 (the first terms are scored separately)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response differentiates each displayed term with respect to x, differentiates the general term with the index kept as a parameter rather than differentiated, lowers each exponent by one with the coefficient multiplied by the old exponent, and reports the first nonzero terms and the general term of the derivative series. BC-ERR-10039 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The displayed terms are differentiated correctly and the general term is not, often because the index was treated as the variable, which is BC-ERR-10039, so the terms point stands and the general term point is lost.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The exponent arithmetic in the power rule on a general power fails, which is BC-PRQ-06002, or the general term cannot be read from the sigma, which is BC-PRQ-10008.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-CON-10001 (term by term differentiation of a power series) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-06002 (the power rule on a general exponent) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a power series, differentiate each displayed term and the general term with respect to the variable, and present the first several nonzero terms and the general term of the derivative series.
skills.description_plain: Differentiate each term, including the general term.
skills.name: Differentiate a power series term by term

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10020 (the requested object confused with a truncated polynomial)
BC-SKL-10067 (the polynomial as a partial sum)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10016 (the first terms and the general term are two separate points)
BC-QA-10018 (the general term of the differentiated series is scored on its own)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response writes a general term in n that reproduces the displayed terms when the first index values are substituted, with the alternating factor, the factorial or coefficient pattern, and the power of x minus the centre all in agreement, and the starting index stated. BC-ERR-10039 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The first nonzero terms are correct and the proposed general term does not regenerate them, which is BC-SIG-10021 and BC-ERR-10039, usually through an off by one index or a mishandled sign factor; the terms point stands while the general term point is lost.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The index cannot be shifted to align the pattern with the displayed terms, which is BC-PRQ-10003, or the alternating factor cannot be written in sigma form, which is BC-PRQ-10008.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-CON-10001 (a general term as a rule producing every term) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10003 (index alignment) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: isolated by BC-QA-10016
skills.description_formal: Given the first several terms or the derivative pattern of a Taylor series, write a general term in n that reproduces them, including any alternating factor and the correct power of x minus the centre.
skills.description_plain: Give the pattern that produces every term, with the index in it.
skills.name: Write the general term of a Taylor series

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10025 (preservation extended from the radius to the endpoints)
BC-MIS-10022 (radius and interval reported for one another)
BC-SKL-10071 (rechecking the endpoints)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10018 (the radius point rests on the preservation statement)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response states that term by term differentiation or integration leaves the radius unchanged and reports the original radius as the radius of the new series, without a second ratio test and without extending the claim to the endpoints. BC-ERR-10042 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The derived series is correct and its radius is recomputed to a value inconsistent with the original, which is BC-SIG-10022 and BC-ERR-10042, or the preservation is stated and then stretched to cover the interval including its ends.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The radius of the original series was never established, so there is nothing to preserve: that is BC-SKL-10056 rather than a preservation gap; reading the notation is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10025 (what term by term operations preserve) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-10056 (stating the original radius) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the radius of convergence of a power series, state that the series obtained by term-by-term differentiation or integration has the same radius, and report that value.
skills.description_plain: Carry the radius across to the new series without recomputing it.
skills.name: Apply the preserved radius to a differentiated or integrated series

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08009 (an expression treated as complete once the quantity is named)
BC-SKL-08012 (the amount at a time, which adds the initial value to this integral)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08004 (the requested net change must be written before it is evaluated)
BC-QA-08005 (the integrand is a difference of two rates, so its structure is visible in the expression)
adaptive.mastered_if: A single definite integral is produced whose value is the requested net change, carrying the rate as integrand, the two inputs from the context as limits, and the differential in the variable of the rate; the expression stands on its own without a stray equals sign to a number, and neither BC-ERR-08018 nor BC-ERR-08019 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The integrand and the limits are right while the differential is missing, which is BC-ERR-08018; or the expression is complete in form and the limits are taken from inputs other than the ones the context bounds, which is BC-ERR-08019.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The rate in the stem cannot be separated from the amount, so the integrand is the wrong function, which is BC-PRQ-06005 rather than a setup gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08009 (the integral expression as the object being scored) for the conceptual case; BC-ERR-08018 (attaching the differential and the correct limits) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an applied description of a rate, produce a definite integral, with differential and limits, whose value is the requested net change.
skills.description_plain: Turn the sentence into an integral with the right integrand and limits.
skills.name: Write a definite integral expression that answers an applied question

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08003 (a calculator value treated as standing on its own)
BC-MIS-08009 (a result treated as complete once the number is named)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08004 (an applied amount must be both evaluated and reported in context)
adaptive.mastered_if: The integral is evaluated by an antiderivative or with technology and the number is reported in the context with the units of the accumulated quantity, to three places after the decimal point when technology is used; unrounded intermediates feed the final step, so neither BC-ERR-08005 nor BC-ERR-08007 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The evaluation is correct and the number is reported bare, without the units of the accumulated quantity, which is BC-ERR-08007; or an intermediate decimal is truncated before the last computation and the reported value moves in the third place, which is BC-ERR-08005.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The reported value carries the wrong number of decimal places or is rounded against the stated convention, which is BC-PRQ-08006 rather than an evaluation gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08009 (what a reported accumulation must state) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08006 (storing intermediates and reporting to three places) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Evaluate the definite integral, by antidifferentiation or with technology, and report the result as the quantity the context asks for, at the required decimal accuracy.
skills.description_plain: Compute the integral, then answer the question in a sentence with units.
skills.name: Evaluate an applied accumulation integral and report it in context

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06013 (the integral of a rate read as the amount of the quantity)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06005 (net change from a rate with an initial condition supplied at one endpoint)
adaptive.mastered_if: Net change is written as a definite integral of the given rate over the stated interval, with limits in the variable the rate actually uses, so elapsed hours are substituted where the question supplies clock times. The learner separates the rate value at an endpoint from the accumulated amount and says which one the question asked for, and when two rates act on the quantity integrates only the one named. Units accompany the reported amount, and the numerical evaluation is done in radian mode for a trigonometric integrand.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The integral is written correctly and the number is wrong, a calculator workflow failure rather than an accumulation failure, including BC-ERR-06032 (degree mode left on for a trigonometric integrand), which forfeits the value point but not the later ones. Rounding short of the required accuracy sits in the same band. A different intermediate state is BC-ERR-06015 (the initial condition omitted, so the integral of the rate is reported as the quantity at the later input), which is the boundary between this skill and the one that builds on it.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: When the wrong object is integrated, for instance f itself where f prime was the rate, the gap is BC-PRQ-06005 (reading function notation, composition, and evaluation), and the tell is a learner who cannot say which of the supplied symbols is the rate. If the integral is set up right and evaluated wrong by hand, the gap is BC-SKL-06034 (endpoint substitution).
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06013 (accumulated change as distinct from the amount present) for the conceptual failure; procedural failure points instead to BC-SKL-06034 (evaluating the definite integral itself)

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a rate of change function over an interval, compute the net change in the quantity as the definite integral of the rate over that interval.
skills.description_plain: Integrate the rate to get how much the quantity changed.
skills.name: Compute net change in a quantity from its rate over an interval

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08003 (a calculator value treated as standing on its own)
BC-MIS-08009 (a reported result treated as complete once the number is named)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08001 (the integrand has no elementary antiderivative, so the written setup is the only evidence of method)
adaptive.mastered_if: The page carries the integral expression with its limits and its differential, visible evidence of the division by the interval length, and a value reported to three places after the decimal point; stored values rather than truncated decimals feed the final computation, so neither BC-ERR-08004 nor BC-ERR-08005 is present.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A correct decimal appears alone with no integral and no quotient written down, which is BC-ERR-08004; or the setup is complete and an intermediate decimal is truncated to two or three places before the last step, moving the reported value, which is BC-ERR-08005.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The answer is correct but given to one place, or rounded rather than truncated against the convention, which is a reporting gap at BC-PRQ-08006 rather than a failure of the average value setup itself.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08003 (that the written expression, not the calculator display, is the mathematical claim) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08006 (three place reporting and storing unrounded intermediates) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: isolated by BC-QA-08002
skills.description_formal: Show the definite integral together with evidence of division by the length of the interval, then report the value accurate to three places after the decimal point.
skills.description_plain: Write the integral and the division before reporting the decimal the calculator gives.
skills.name: Present the calculator setup for an average value and report it

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08002 (the definite integral itself read as the average)
BC-SKL-08004 (average of the values confused with average rate of change)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08001 (the interval has length other than one, so the division is visible in the answer)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response writes the quotient with the definite integral of f over [a,b] above and b minus a below, evaluates it by antidifferentiation with endpoint substitution, and reports a number carrying the units of f; the limits and the divisor both come from the interval the prompt names, and neither BC-ERR-08001 nor BC-ERR-08002 appears when the function arrives as a model formula and when it arrives as a graph.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The integral of f over the stated interval is correct and its value is handed in as the average with no quotient anywhere, which is BC-ERR-08001 and the observation recorded in BC-SIG-08001; or the averaging structure is right while the limits and the divisor are read off an interval the prompt did not name, which is BC-ERR-08002.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The antiderivative of f is wrong or the endpoint substitution is mishandled before any averaging takes place, which is an evaluation gap at BC-SKL-06034 rather than an average value gap; a model whose function notation is misread, so that f(a) and a itself are interchanged, is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08002 (that the integral accumulates the function and the division converts the accumulation to a mean) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-06034 (evaluating the definite integral itself) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given f by an analytic expression and an interval [a,b], compute the definite integral of f over [a,b] and divide by b minus a.
skills.description_plain: Integrate the function over the interval and divide by the length of the interval.
skills.name: Apply the average value formula to a function given by a formula

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08001 (average value and average rate of change treated as one quantity)
BC-MIS-08002 (the integral itself read as the average)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08001 (asks for the mean of the values)
BC-QA-08002 (asks for an average rate of change and then for the instant matching it, so the two quantities appear in one question)
adaptive.mastered_if: Given a prompt, the response selects the integral quotient when the mean of the function values is wanted and the difference quotient of the endpoint values when the average rate of change is wanted, and the units attached to the answer are the units of f in the first case and units of f per unit of the input in the second; BC-ERR-08006 does not appear in either direction.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: One of the two quantities is built correctly and the other is answered with the first, which is BC-ERR-08006; the specific pattern in BC-SIG-08002 is the change in the function over the change in the input reported under the name average value.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Net change over the interval cannot be formed at all, so neither quotient can be assembled, which is BC-SKL-06036 rather than a discrimination gap; misreading which symbol in the prompt names the function is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08001 (that one averages function values and the other averages a rate) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-06036 (forming net change over an interval) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: isolated by BC-QA-08002
skills.description_formal: Given a prompt, select the integral quotient when the average of the function values is wanted and the difference quotient when the average rate of change is wanted.
skills.description_plain: Decide which of the two averages a question is asking for before computing.
skills.name: Distinguish average value from average rate of change

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08001 (average value and average rate of change treated as one quantity)
BC-SKL-08015 (interpreting an accumulation integral rather than an average)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08001 (requires the average reported in context)
BC-QA-08007 (a displayed integral must be described with quantity, interval, and units)
adaptive.mastered_if: A sentence names the quantity being averaged, the interval over which the average is taken, and units that are the units of the integrand rather than rate units; when the reported figure is an average rate of change the units are per unit of input, and BC-ERR-08007 and BC-ERR-08006 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The value and the quantity are named while the units are left off or assembled from the wrong factors, which is BC-ERR-08007; or the sentence is well formed but describes the other average, which is BC-ERR-08006.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The sentence cannot name what f measures because the function notation in the context has not been decoded, which is BC-PRQ-06005 rather than an interpretation gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08001 (which of the two averages carries rate units) for the conceptual case; BC-ERR-08007 (building units from the factors already in the integrand) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Report an average value as a quantity in the units of the integrand, naming the quantity and the interval over which the average is taken.
skills.description_plain: Say what the average stands for in the situation and attach its units.
skills.name: State the meaning and units of an average value in context

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08007 (two rates acting at once combined by addition)
BC-MIS-08006 (the integral of a rate read as the amount of the quantity)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08005 (a rate in and a rate out act on one stored quantity, so the order of subtraction is visible in the sign)
adaptive.mastered_if: The net rate is written as the inflow rate minus the outflow rate, in that order, the difference enclosed in parentheses when it is placed inside an integral, and the net change over the interval is the definite integral of that difference; neither BC-ERR-08013 nor BC-ERR-08014 appears, and the sign of the result agrees with which rate is larger.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Both rate functions are identified correctly and combined with a plus sign, or subtracted in the reverse order, which is BC-ERR-08013; or the difference is substituted into the integrand without parentheses so that only its first term is integrated or negated, which is BC-ERR-08014.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Which of the two given functions is the inflow cannot be decided from the stem, so the difference is assembled from the wrong pair, which is BC-PRQ-06005 rather than a net rate gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08007 (that the two rates move the stored amount in opposite directions) for the conceptual case; BC-ERR-08014 (parenthesising a substituted difference) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given separate inflow and outflow rate functions, write the net rate as their difference and express the net change over an interval as the definite integral of that difference.
skills.description_plain: Subtract the outflow rate from the inflow rate before integrating.
skills.name: Set up a net rate as rate in minus rate out

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08008 (a local extremum argument taken to settle an absolute extremum)
BC-SKL-05020 (classifying an interior critical point, which is the local question)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08006 (the amount is defined by an integral on a closed interval, so an endpoint can carry the maximum)
adaptive.mastered_if: The net rate is set equal to zero and solved on the interval, the interior candidates are listed together with both endpoints, and the maximum is settled either by a table of the amount at every candidate or by a stated sign change of the net rate from positive to negative with the uniqueness of that change asserted; BC-ERR-08015 and BC-ERR-08016 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The critical time is found correctly and the justification is a first or second derivative test presented as settling an absolute maximum, which is BC-ERR-08015; or a candidates table is built that contains only the interior critical time, which is BC-ERR-08016, the sign chart without endpoint comparison recorded in BC-SIG-08005.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The equation net rate equal to zero is solved incorrectly, so the candidate list is wrong before any justification, which is BC-PRQ-08001; classifying a critical point from a sign change at all is BC-SKL-05020, and writing a justification that covers every candidate is BC-SKL-05028.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08008 (why an interval maximum needs the endpoints) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-05028 (writing the global justification) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: isolated by BC-QA-08006
skills.description_formal: Set the net rate equal to zero, identify the candidate times together with the endpoints, and justify the absolute maximum either by a sign change of the net rate with uniqueness or by evaluating the amount at every candidate.
skills.description_plain: Find where the net rate changes from positive to negative, then compare the candidates.
skills.name: Determine when an accumulated amount is maximal and justify globally

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05018 (a local test treated as settling a global question)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05006 (absolute extremum by the candidates test with a global justification)
adaptive.mastered_if: The derivative argument is stated across the interval rather than at a point. Work shows f prime not positive on one side of the candidate and not negative on the other, over the full stretch to each end of the interval, and the conclusion names the absolute extremum that this sign behaviour forces. The 2025 and 2026 guidelines accept either a sign discussion or a candidates comparison for the justification point, and this route is carried far enough that BC-ERR-05029 and BC-ERR-99004 do not apply.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: BC-SIG-05021 captures the recurring middle state, a correct extremum paired with a first or second derivative test at the candidate. BC-ERR-05029 names that substitution of a local test for a global one, and BC-ERR-99004 widens it to include a sign change cited at a single point. The 2019 Q1 and 2021 Q2 commentaries both record critical inputs located correctly and justified only locally.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: If the sign of f prime is assigned wrongly on a stretch, the break is in BC-SKL-05016, building a sign chart on critical points and domain boundaries, and the tell is a partition whose intervals are right while one carries the wrong sign. A response that never identifies the relevant candidate at all sits in BC-SKL-05024 instead.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05018 (local sign change mistaken for proof over the whole interval) is the conceptual target. When the global intent is present and the sign chart underneath it is faulty, the procedural target is BC-SKL-05016, where the signs of f prime on each interval are established.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Show f' not positive on one side of the candidate and not negative on the other across the whole interval, and conclude the absolute extremum there.
skills.description_plain: Argue globally from the derivative keeping one sign on each side.
skills.name: Justify an absolute extremum from the sign of the derivative across the interval

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06010 (a relative extremum test treated as settling an absolute extremum on a closed interval)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06003 (accumulation function analysed from a graph of the integrand made of segments and circular arcs)
adaptive.mastered_if: Every candidate appears and nothing else does, meaning each input where the plotted f is zero together with both endpoints of the closed interval, each evaluated as a signed area to give a value of g, and the comparison of those values is what settles the absolute extremum. Alternatively the argument runs globally from the sign of f on each side of the interior input, which is the form BC-SKL-05029 supplies. BC-SIG-06024 is the positive marker here, since every part names the feature of the plotted integrand that supports its claim, and neither BC-ERR-06011, a local derivative test standing in for a global argument, nor BC-ERR-06012, an incomplete or padded candidate list, is present.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: BC-SIG-06011 describes a correct input justified by a first or second derivative test at that input alone, which is BC-ERR-06011 and loses the justification point while the value point remains available. BC-SIG-06012 describes a comparison that lists the interior critical inputs and drops one or both endpoints, which is BC-ERR-06012, and BC-FRQ-2025-Q4-D records the mirror image where extra candidates are listed and the exactness rule costs the same point. BC-FRQ-2019-Q3-C also records the location of the maximum reported where the maximum value was asked for, and candidate values computed with a sign error in the areas.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Candidate values that are wrong although the candidate list is right points at BC-SKL-06020 or at BC-PRQ-06007, since the areas of the triangular, rectangular and semicircular pieces are being computed or signed incorrectly rather than the extremum logic failing. BC-FRQ-2013-Q4-B names this directly as an accumulation failure rather than an extremum failure, and the tell is a correct method applied to numbers that do not match the figure.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06010 (why endpoints can beat an interior candidate and how that is ruled out) for the conceptual failure; when the global argument is sound and the arithmetic of the candidate values is not, the target is BC-PRQ-06007 (area formulas for triangles, trapezoids and semicircles read off a figure)

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the graph of f and g(x) = the integral from a to x of f(t) dt on a closed interval, identify the inputs where f is zero and the endpoints, evaluate g at each candidate, and conclude which gives the absolute maximum or minimum, or argue globally from the sign of f on each side.
skills.description_plain: Compare candidate values at the critical points and both endpoints.
skills.name: Determine an absolute extreme value of an accumulation function with a global argument

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05016 (the candidates taken to be the critical points only)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05006 (an absolute extremum found by the candidates test and justified over the whole interval)
adaptive.mastered_if: For f continuous on the closed interval from a to b, the candidate list holds every critical point lying strictly inside, together with a and b, and nothing else. Critical points found outside the interval are named and discarded rather than carried forward, so BC-ERR-05025 is absent, and both ends are evaluated rather than assumed to lose, so BC-ERR-05026 is absent. The equation f prime of x equals zero is written and considered, which BC-QA-05006 pays for separately from merely listing zeros, and the open versus closed distinction is respected in how the interval is written, whether f arrives as a formula under BC-REP-01 or as a table or graph under BC-REP-02.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: All interior critical points are present and one or both endpoints are missing from the comparison, which is BC-SIG-05018 and BC-ERR-05026, and BC-FRQ-2019-Q1-C records endpoints omitted from a candidates table directly. BC-FRQ-2013-Q1-D records a candidates table without the endpoints described as a local argument offered where a global one was demanded, and BC-FRQ-2019-Q3-C records a critical point found with only a local sign change cited. BC-FRQ-2013-Q4-B shows the list assembled correctly with the candidate values computed wrongly from the areas, which is an accumulation failure sitting on top of a sound candidate list, and its rubric makes the justification point unavailable once the answer is wrong.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: An empty or partial list of interior candidates comes from BC-SKL-05010 (critical points where f prime equals zero) or BC-SKL-05011 (critical points where f prime fails to exist), the tell being a list correct on smooth pieces and silent where the derivative is undefined. When the endpoints are known to matter and the interval is written with the wrong kind of endpoint, or an interior point is taken for an end, the gap is BC-PRQ-05004 (interval notation and the open versus closed distinction).
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05016 (the ends of the interval not regarded as competitors) is the conceptual target. A procedural failure, where the endpoints are named as candidates and then never evaluated or an outside critical point is dragged into the comparison, points instead to BC-PRQ-05004 (reading the interval and its ends as written).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given f continuous on [a,b], collect the critical points in (a,b) together with a and b as the complete candidate list for the absolute extrema.
skills.description_plain: Write down every critical point in the interval plus the two endpoints.
skills.name: Assemble the candidate list from critical points and both endpoints

common_confusions: BC-MIS-04003 (units as an ornament)
BC-MIS-04001 (the amount reported where the rate was wanted)
BC-SKL-04004 (estimating the rate from a table rather than differentiating a model)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-04005 (a modelled non motion quantity whose rate is computed and reported with units)
adaptive.mastered_if: The model is differentiated or the derivative supplied in the stem is used, the derivative is evaluated at the requested input, and the value is reported with the units of the quantity over the units of the independent variable and in the vocabulary of the context; BC-ERR-04001 is absent, and a model value is not offered in place of its rate.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The derivative value is correct and no units accompany it, BC-ERR-04001 with signal BC-SIG-04001; or the derivative is correct and the evaluation mishandles an exponent, the arithmetic rather than rule failure the 2013 Q3 part D distinctions isolate.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The quantity and its independent variable were never identified, a gap at BC-SKL-04013; or the units cannot be assembled, a gap at BC-SKL-04001.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-04001 (the derivative of the model, not the model, answers a rate question). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-04001 (attaching the assembled units to the value).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a model of a contextual quantity, compute the derivative at a stated input and report the value with the units of the quantity divided by the units of the independent variable.
skills.description_plain: Differentiate the model, evaluate it, and attach the right units.
skills.name: Compute and report a rate of change with context-appropriate units
skills.notation: rate reported with units

common_confusions: BC-MIS-04002 (the sign of a rate treated as formatting)
BC-MIS-04001 (the rate confused with the quantity)
BC-SKL-04010 (a sign comparison between velocity and acceleration, a different judgement)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-04001 (the direction of change is one of the required elements of the interpretation)
adaptive.mastered_if: A negative rate is stated as the quantity decreasing at that instant and a large magnitude as a rapid change, with the sign converted into direction in words rather than restated as a minus sign; BC-ERR-04005 is absent, and the response can say whether the quantity is larger or smaller a moment later.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The magnitude is reported correctly and the sign is left uninterpreted or is described as an increase, BC-ERR-04005; the 2014 Q1 part B commentary records a response that restated a negative rate as decomposition at a negative rate rather than converting the sign into direction.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The value whose sign is being read belongs to the function rather than to its derivative, a gap at BC-SKL-04003 with signal BC-SIG-04002.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-04002 (the sign is the statement that the quantity is falling). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-04002 (writing the direction into the interpretation sentence).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the sign and magnitude of a derivative in a modelled situation, state whether the quantity is increasing or decreasing at that instant and how rapidly.
skills.description_plain: Read a negative rate as a decrease and a large rate as a fast change.
skills.name: Interpret the sign and size of a derivative in context
skills.notation: sign of a rate in context

common_confusions: BC-MIS-03013 (a higher derivative read as a different kind of object)
BC-MIS-03014 (notation treated as decoration, so the order is not tracked)
BC-SKL-03033 (differentiating a derivative expression that still contains y)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-03008 (the second derivative and its value carry separate points)
adaptive.mastered_if: f prime is differentiated again with the same rules to produce f double prime, treating the first derivative as an ordinary function, and the order reported matches the order requested; BC-ERR-03021 is absent, and the response can say that the operation turning the first derivative into the second is the same differentiation.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The differentiation performed is correct and stops one order short of the order requested, BC-ERR-03021 with signal BC-SIG-03013; or, as the 2015 Q4 part B distinctions record, the second derivative is written but still contains the derivative symbol where a substitution back was required.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The first derivative is itself wrong, so the gap sits in the elementary rules at BC-PRQ-03005 rather than in iterating them.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-03013 (the second derivative is the derivative of the first). Procedural failure: BC-PRQ-03005 (reapplying the same differentiation rules).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given f prime, differentiate it to produce f double prime, provided the derivative of f prime exists.
skills.description_plain: Differentiate what you already differentiated once.
skills.name: Differentiate a first derivative to obtain the second derivative
skills.notation: f double prime of x

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05010 (increase and decrease decided from whether the function values are positive or negative)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05008 (intervals of increase or decrease supported by the sign of the named derivative)
adaptive.mastered_if: Given f or f prime symbolically as in BC-REP-01, the zeros and the undefined points of f prime are found first, then the sign of f prime is settled on each resulting open interval, usually by a test value that gets written down. Intervals and reason are kept separate in the write-up, the reason naming f prime rather than restating the conclusion, and BC-ERR-05014, assigning the wrong sign on one interval of the chart, is absent across factored polynomial, rational and chain rule cases alike.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: All partition points are correct and one interval carries the wrong sign, which is BC-SIG-05011 and BC-ERR-05014 and which costs the reason point along with the intervals. Other intermediate work uses the sign of the quantity itself where the sign of its derivative was wanted, the direction-of-change confusion recorded in the 2019 and 2022 commentary, or omits the chain rule factor when a second derivative is built so the inner variable is never treated as a function of time.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: When the number line is partitioned wrongly because a factored or rational expression was not solved correctly, the failure is BC-PRQ-05001, and when the partition points are right but the sign on a piece cannot be determined the gap is BC-PRQ-05002. A derivative that is wrong before any sign work begins points back to BC-SKL-02027.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05010 (the sign of f prime, not the sign of f, drives increase and decrease) for the conceptual failure. A student who has that straight and still misassigns a sign needs BC-PRQ-05002, the number line sign analysis.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given f or f' symbolically, find the zeros and undefined points of f' and determine the sign of f' on each resulting open interval.
skills.description_plain: Work out the sign of the derivative expression on each interval.
skills.name: Determine where the first derivative is positive or negative from a formula

common_confusions: BC-MIS-09017 (a polar area read as an integral of the curve itself)
BC-MIS-09018 (the area between polar curves built from the difference of the radii)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-09012 (a region swept by one polar curve, so the sector formula is the whole setup)
adaptive.mastered_if: The area bounded by a single polar curve is written as one half the definite integral of the square of r with respect to theta between the bounding angles, both the factor of one half and the squaring present in the expression; the integrand is not r itself, so neither BC-ERR-09035 nor BC-ERR-09036 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The square of r is integrated over the correct angles with the factor of one half missing, which is BC-ERR-09035 and doubles the reported area, the state in BC-SIG-09012; or the factor is present and r is not squared, which is BC-ERR-09036.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The Cartesian idea that a definite integral of a function gives area is applied unchanged to r, which is BC-SKL-06028 misapplied rather than a polar gap; reading r as a function of theta in the stem is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-09017 (the sector area that the one half and the square come from) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-09038 (evaluating the assembled integral) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Write the area of a region bounded by a single polar curve as one half the definite integral of the square of r with respect to theta over the bounding angles.
skills.description_plain: Write one half the integral of r squared with respect to the angle.
skills.name: State the polar area integral for a single curve

common_confusions: BC-MIS-09007 (any interval containing the curve assumed to give its length or area)
BC-MIS-09019 (the limits of a polar area taken as the whole interval of the figure)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-09012 (the region is swept over part of the displayed angle range, so the limits alone change the value)
adaptive.mastered_if: The bounding angles are determined from the stem, the figure, or consecutive zeros of r, and the interval chosen sweeps the region exactly once, with the choice stated rather than taken from the axes of the picture; neither BC-ERR-09016 nor BC-ERR-09037 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The sector integrand is correct and the limits are the angle range in which the figure is drawn rather than the angles bounding the region, which is BC-ERR-09037; or the interval covers part of the region twice, which is BC-ERR-09016.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Which angle interval traces the curve exactly once cannot be decided, which is BC-PRQ-09004 rather than an area gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-09007 (what the limits must do) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-09004 (checking that the interval sweeps the region once) for the procedural case.

common_confusions: BC-MIS-09008 (a calculator result treated as standing without its expression)
BC-MIS-09017 (a polar area read as an integral of the curve itself)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-09012 (a numerical polar area, so the written sector integral is the record of method)
adaptive.mastered_if: The polar area integral is evaluated, numerically with the expression written out or by antidifferentiation, and the value reported to three places after the decimal point when technology is used, with the one half and the squared r visible in the expression that produced it; neither BC-ERR-09011 nor BC-ERR-09006 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A correct decimal area appears with no integral expression on the page, which is BC-ERR-09011; or the setup is written and a stored bounding angle is truncated before the evaluation, moving the third decimal place, which is BC-ERR-09006.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The number is right and reported to the wrong number of places or rounded against the convention, which is BC-PRQ-08006; evaluating a definite integral by antidifferentiation is BC-SKL-06034.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-09008 (the written integral as the scored object) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08006 (three place reporting from stored angles) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Evaluate the polar area integral, numerically or by antidifferentiation, and report the value accurate to three places after the decimal point when technology is used.

common_confusions: BC-MIS-09013 (the polar radius treated as a Cartesian coordinate)
BC-MIS-09015 (the slope of a polar curve taken to be the derivative of r)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-09009 (r and the angle are both in play, so using r directly is visible)
BC-QA-09011 (a Cartesian coordinate along the curve is maximised, so the conversion is the first step)
adaptive.mastered_if: With r given as a function of theta and an angle supplied, the Cartesian coordinates are computed as r times cosine theta and r times sine theta, both products written before any value is reported, with the calculator in radian mode; the value of r is not handed in as a coordinate, so BC-ERR-09027 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The value of r at the angle is computed correctly and is then used as the x coordinate or the y coordinate with no conversion, which is BC-ERR-09027.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Sine and cosine are not read as the coordinates of the point on the unit circle, so the conversion has no basis, which is BC-PRQ-09002.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-09013 (r as a distance from the origin rather than a coordinate) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-09002 (the cosine and sine conversion) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: isolated by BC-QA-09011
skills.description_formal: Given r as a function of theta and an angle, compute the Cartesian coordinates of the corresponding point.
skills.description_plain: Multiply r by cosine and by sine of the angle.
skills.name: Convert a point on a polar curve to Cartesian coordinates

common_confusions: BC-MIS-09018 (the area between polar curves built from the difference of the radii)
BC-MIS-09007 (any interval containing the curve assumed to give its area)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-09013 (the outer curve changes at a crossing, so one integral over the full range misses a piece)
adaptive.mastered_if: A symmetric polar region is handled as twice the integral over half the angle interval, with the doubling written explicitly, or a region whose outer curve changes at a crossing is written as a sum of integrals with the limits meeting at that angle; the compensating factor matches the interval used, and BC-ERR-09041 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The symmetry is spotted and half the region is integrated with no doubling, or the whole region is integrated and the result is doubled as well, which is BC-ERR-09041 in its two recorded forms.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Which angle interval traces the region once cannot be decided, so neither the half interval nor the split point is trustworthy, which is BC-PRQ-09004.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-09007 (what the chosen interval covers and how often) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-09039 (locating the crossing angle where the pieces meet) for the procedural case.

skills.name: Use symmetry or a sum of integrals for a polar region with several pieces

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01014 (end behaviour of a quantity and of its rate taken as interchangeable)
BC-MIS-01013 (infinity substituted as a number)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01010 (a contextual model where the expression and the value carry separate credit and the subject of the limit matters)
adaptive.mastered_if: The limit expression is written with the modelled quantity or its rate placed inside according to what the question asks, with the independent variable increasing without bound under the arrow, and the value is produced by notation rather than by substituting the infinity symbol (BC-ERR-01021 absent); the subject inside the limit matches the requested quantity (BC-ERR-01022 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The end behaviour value is correct but the limit expression the question asks for is never written, which is BC-SIG-01011 and carries its own credit in the 2025 guidelines, or the expression is written and then arithmetic is performed on the infinity symbol.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The amount and its rate cannot be told apart in the given notation, so the wrong function is placed inside the limit, which BC-SIG-01012 ties to the notation gap at BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01014 (checking the units of the quantity inside the limit against the question) for the conceptual failure; BC-MIS-01013 (limit notation in place of arithmetic with the infinity symbol) for the procedural failure

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06013 (supplied integral values recombined using constant multiple, sum, reversal, and adjacent interval properties)
adaptive.mastered_if: Given the integral of f over [a,b] and over [b,c], the learner writes the integral from a to c as the sum of the two supplied values, and when the missing piece is the middle one recovers it by subtracting rather than by re-integrating. The same additivity is used on a graph, where a region is cut at a crossing and the two signed pieces are added, and on a list of supplied numerical values under BC-QA-06013, where reversal of limits is combined with additivity in one rewrite. Regions below the axis enter with a negative sign, and the splitting point is chosen at the crossing rather than at a convenient tick mark.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Additivity is applied correctly on supplied numbers but breaks on a figure, where areas are added without signs so a region below the axis is counted as positive, or the interval is never split at the crossing at all so a single unsigned area is reported. Another intermediate state is the value being correct while the adjacent interval property is never stated in writing, which the 2019 Q3 part A rubric treats as a skipped communication step even though the arithmetic holds. A correct decomposition whose value is then carried wrongly into a later part is an import error, not a failure of additivity.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: No prerequisite skill is listed for this one, so a wrong value here traces back to reading the figure rather than to an earlier skill. The tell is a correct sum structure with wrong individual pieces, such as a quarter circle given the area of a full circle, which shows the geometric area formulas rather than the interval property are the failure.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-QA-06013 (rewriting a requested integral in terms of the supplied ones) for the conceptual failure; when the structure is right and only the signed pieces are wrong, the procedural target is BC-SKL-06070 (reading signed area off the figure)

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the integrals of f over [a,b] and over [b,c], evaluate the integral over [a,c] as their sum, or recover a missing piece by subtraction.
skills.description_plain: Integrals over touching intervals add to the integral over the union.
skills.name: Apply the adjacent interval property of definite integrals

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06011 (area formulas recalled without their fractional factors)
BC-MIS-06012 (the definite integral treated as unsigned area between the graph and the axis)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06004 (definite integral evaluated from a graph of segments and arcs as a sum of signed areas)
adaptive.mastered_if: The region is cut at every point where the graph changes character or crosses the axis, each piece gets the area formula that matches its shape with its fractional factor intact, and pieces below the axis enter the sum with a negative sign. A semicircle of radius r contributes one half pi r squared and a triangle one half base times height, so BC-ERR-06013, the semicircle given the area of a full circle, does not occur. The reported number is a signed value rather than a total area, so BC-ERR-06014 is absent, and when two integrals are requested in one part each value is attached to its own label, which BC-QA-06004 and BC-FRQ-2025-Q4-C both make a scoring condition.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: BC-SIG-06013 records a value equal to the sum of the unsigned areas although part of the region lies below the axis, which is BC-ERR-06014. BC-SIG-06014 records a value that misses the correct one by exactly half a circle, the dropped factor in BC-ERR-06013. A further state computes every piece correctly and leaves the values unlabelled, which BC-FRQ-2025-Q4-C treats as earning neither point, and BC-FRQ-2014-Q3-A records the interval left unsplit at a crossing so two opposite contributions cancel into one wrong number.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: BC-PRQ-06007 is the earlier failure that looks like this one, showing as a correct decomposition and correct signs with an area formula misremembered or a length misread off the figure. The tell is that the signed structure of the answer is right and one geometric piece is numerically wrong.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06012 (the definite integral as signed rather than total area) for the conceptual failure; a geometry failure with the signs correct points instead to BC-PRQ-06007 (area formulas for rectangles, triangles, trapezoids, circles and semicircles)

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the graph of f consisting of line segments and circular arcs, evaluate the definite integral over a stated interval as the sum of the areas of the regions above the x axis minus the areas of the regions below.
skills.description_plain: Break the region into triangles, rectangles, and circular pieces and add with signs.
skills.name: Evaluate a definite integral from a graph using area formulas

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06011 (area formulas recalled without their fractional factors)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06004 (definite integral evaluated from a graph by geometry)
adaptive.mastered_if: Accumulated change over an interval comes out as a sum of signed areas, partitioned where the graph changes character, with one half b h for each triangle, one half times the sum of the parallel sides times the width for each trapezoid, and one half pi r squared for a semicircular piece. Regions below the axis enter negatively. The learner splits the interval at every axis crossing and labels each value with the integral it belongs to, so neither BC-ERR-06013 (a semicircle given the area of a full circle) nor BC-ERR-06014 (regions below the axis added as positive area) occurs.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Decomposition is right and a factor is missing. BC-ERR-06013 appears as pi r squared written for a semicircular or quarter-circular piece, and BC-ERR-06014 as every piece added positively so a signed integral is reported as a plain area. The BC-FRQ-2014-Q3-A commentary separates a failure to split at the crossing from a sign failure, and BC-FRQ-2024-Q4-A notes a positive value reported for an input left of the lower limit, where the reversal of limits was not applied. Values given without labels, as BC-FRQ-2022-Q3-A records, cost communication rather than method.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: If the area of a single triangle or trapezoid read off the figure is wrong before any sign question arises, the break is BC-PRQ-06007 rather than this skill. The tell is that asking for one isolated region's area, with no integral attached, still produces the wrong number.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06011 (the halving factor in the triangle, trapezoid, and semicircle formulas) for the conceptual failure. When the formulas are sound and the signs are not, the target is BC-PRQ-06007 (areas from lengths read off the figure) for the measurement side and the signed-area step of BC-QA-06004 for the sign side.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a rate of change function whose graph consists of line segments, compute the accumulated change over an interval as the sum of the signed areas of the resulting triangles, rectangles, and trapezoids.
skills.description_plain: Add up triangle and rectangle areas under a rate graph to get the total change.
skills.name: Compute accumulated change from a piecewise linear rate graph using geometry

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06008 (antiderivative or definite integral by substitution, with limits either converted or restored)
adaptive.mastered_if: An antiderivative F is produced for a continuous f, the integral from a to b is written as F(b) minus F(a) with that difference shown, and the constant of integration is dropped knowingly because it cancels.
