When the integrand is a composite times a constant multiple of the derivative of its inner expression, as in BC-QA-06008, the learner either back-substitutes before using the original limits or converts the limits to u, and never applies x limits to an expression still written in u. Endpoint values read off a figure are matched to the correct function, and the antiderivative of a derivative is written as the function itself rather than as its square.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The setup is right and the numerical value is wrong because the calculator was left in degree mode for a trigonometric integrand, which is BC-ERR-06032 (degree mode used where radian mode is required) and forfeits only the value point while leaving later points available. Other intermediate states are an indefinite integral left unevaluated so the definite integral requirement is not met, bounds imported from the wrong figure, and logarithm arithmetic failing at the limits while the antidifferentiation itself is correct.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: If the endpoint subtraction is executed correctly on whatever expression was produced but the expression is wrong, the gap is BC-SKL-06040 (antidifferentiating power functions) or BC-PRQ-06002 (exponent rules for negative and fractional exponents), and the tell is a radical or reciprocal that was never rewritten as a power before the reverse power rule was attempted.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-PRQ-06002 (exponent rules underneath any antiderivative of a power) for the conceptual failure; procedural failure points instead to BC-SKL-06040 (producing the antiderivative itself before any endpoint substitution)

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a continuous f on [a,b] and an antiderivative F, evaluate the integral from a to b of f(x) dx as F(b) minus F(a).
skills.description_plain: Find an antiderivative and subtract its value at the lower limit from its value at the upper limit.
skills.name: Evaluate a definite integral by antidifferentiation and endpoint substitution

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06013 (supplied definite integral values combined through constant multiple, sum, reversal and adjacent interval properties)
adaptive.mastered_if: Given values for the integral of f and the integral of g over the same interval, a constant is pulled outside the integral sign and an integral of a sum or difference is split into the two supplied integrals before any number is substituted. The rewriting step is written out, so the requested integral is first matched to the supplied ones in the BC-QA-06013 manner and only then evaluated and simplified. The supplied values are used rather than ignored in favour of symbolic integration of an unspecified function, which BC-FRQ-2023-Q5-A and BC-FRQ-2023-Q5-C both record as a way of discarding the given data. No errors or misconceptions are catalogued for this skill in the record.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Linearity is applied to a sum and the constant multiple is left inside, or the constant is pulled out of a difference and distributed over only the first term. Another state reverses the order of subtraction, which BC-FRQ-2023-Q5-A lists as forcing a positive answer without identifying which function comes first. The BC-QA-06013 scoring behaviour notes that a correct value alone earns the point, so a rewriting that is right in structure and wrong in one substituted value sits in this band.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: No prerequisite skills are recorded for this skill, and the earliest failure visible in the record is at BC-TOP level, showing as an inability to say what a definite integral over a stated interval denotes before any property is applied. The tell is that the properties are recited accurately and cannot be attached to the supplied numbers.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-QA-06013 (matching a requested integral to the supplied ones before substituting) for the conceptual failure; an arithmetic or sign slip after a correct rewriting points instead to BC-SKL-06030 (the reversal of limits property, where the sign is decided)

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given definite integrals of f and of g over the same interval, evaluate the integral of a constant times f or of a sum or difference of f and g using the corresponding properties.
skills.description_plain: Pull constants out front and split an integral of a sum.
skills.name: Apply the constant multiple and sum properties of definite integrals

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06026 (the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus part two treated as needing no hypotheses)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06013 (supplied integral values recombined using constant multiple, sum, reversal, and adjacent interval properties)
adaptive.mastered_if: Both hypotheses are named before the conclusion is used, so the learner says that f is continuous on [a,b] and that F is an antiderivative of f on [a,b], and only then writes the integral from a to b of f(x) dx equal to F(b) minus F(a). Asked whether the theorem applies to an integrand with a jump inside the interval, the answer is no, with the continuity hypothesis given as the reason. In the verbal form of BC-QA-06013 the learner distinguishes the theorem from the properties that merely recombine supplied values.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The conclusion is quoted accurately while the hypotheses are left out, so F(b) minus F(a) is applied to any integrand offered. A related state is naming continuity but not the antiderivative condition, which shows up as the antiderivative of a derivative being written as a square of the function, the theorem being confused with a power rule. Reading the wrong curve off a figure, such as integrating the plotted function where its derivative was the integrand, is a graph-reading failure rather than a failure to hold the statement.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: No earlier skill is listed for stating the theorem. When the statement is right and the use is wrong, the earlier failure is reading the figure, and the tell is endpoint values misread from the graph while the form F(b) minus F(a) is written correctly.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06026 (the hypotheses that license F(b) minus F(a)) for the conceptual failure; when the statement is sound and only its application slips, the target is BC-SKL-06034 (carrying out the endpoint substitution)

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: State that if f is continuous on [a,b] and F is an antiderivative of f on [a,b], then the integral from a to b of f(x) dx equals F(b) minus F(a).
skills.description_plain: Name the continuity and antiderivative conditions before using F(b) minus F(a).
skills.name: State the hypotheses and conclusion of the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus part two

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06023 (the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus part one applied as a fixed template with no chain rule)
BC-MIS-06024 (the variable of integration taken to be the independent variable)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06012 (differentiating an accumulation function with a variable upper limit and evaluating the derivative at a point)
adaptive.mastered_if: With f continuous on an interval containing a, the response states that g prime of x equals f of x and attributes it to the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus part one, then uses that identity rather than restating it, for instance reading increase of g from where f is positive as BC-FRQ-2021-Q4-A asks, or supplying g prime as one factor inside a product rule as BC-FRQ-2021-Q4-B asks. The derivative is expressed in the independent variable, so BC-ERR-06028 (an answer left in terms of the dummy variable) is absent, and the response does not report g prime as g itself. Both a formula for f (BC-REP-01) and a graph of f (BC-REP-02) support the same conclusion.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The theorem is quoted and the theorem point earned while the value is wrong, which is the pattern behind BC-ERR-06027 in its simple form and behind the BC-FRQ-2021-Q4-B distractor where the product rule is correct but the imported accumulation value is not. A second state is BC-ERR-06028, the integrand evaluated at t so the derivative never reaches the independent variable. A third is the BC-FRQ-2021-Q4-A behaviour of correct intervals with no reason attached, or intervals reported for f itself instead of for the accumulation.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: BC-SKL-06017 is the earlier failure wearing this one's clothes, and the tell is that the function being differentiated was never written as an integral from a fixed lower limit to x, so there is nothing for the theorem to act on. BC-PRQ-06013 shows when the dummy variable and the upper limit are not held apart even before differentiation.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-PRQ-06013 (bound variables and the dummy variable convention) for the conceptual failure that leaves the derivative in terms of t; a procedural failure to produce the value after the theorem is stated points instead to BC-SKL-06017 (writing the accumulation as an integral with a variable upper limit).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given g(x) = the integral from a to x of f(t) dt with f continuous on an interval containing a, conclude that g'(x) = f(x) for x in that interval.
skills.description_plain: Apply the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus part one to get g'(x) = f(x).
skills.name: Differentiate an accumulation function with a variable upper limit

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06007 (the plotted curve is taken to be the function under discussion)
BC-MIS-06008 (a zero of the integrand is treated as a general turning feature of the accumulation function, so extrema and inflection points land on the same inputs)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06003 (accumulation function analysed from a graph of the integrand made of segments and circular arcs)
adaptive.mastered_if: Relative maxima of g are placed exactly at the inputs where the plotted f crosses from positive to negative, minima where it crosses from negative to positive, and the direction of the crossing is stated rather than left implied. Endpoints are not offered as relative extrema, and the input list for extrema differs from the input list the same figure would produce for inflection points. What BC-ERR-06008 describes, extrema of g taken from the visible extrema of the curve on the page, does not appear, and the response says which curve it is reading.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: BC-SIG-06008 captures the state where the reported extrema of g sit at the visible peaks and valleys of the plotted integrand, which is the graphical form of BC-ERR-06008. A second state locates the critical input correctly and then reports its location where BC-FRQ-2019-Q3-C asked for the value, or cites only a local sign change where the part wanted more. A third gives the crossing inputs without naming the direction, which leaves maximum and minimum undistinguished.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: When the response cannot identify the intervals where g rises and falls in the first place, the failure is BC-SKL-06022 rather than extremum location, and it shows up as a sign change being sought on a curve whose sign was never read. BC-SKL-05021, concluding neither extremum when the derivative keeps its sign, is missing when a stationary touch of the axis with no sign change is counted as an extremum.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06008 (one rule for zeros of f applied to every feature of g) for the conceptual failure; a procedural failure, where the crossings are found but the direction or the value is mishandled, points instead to BC-SKL-06022 (reading the sign of f on each side of the crossing)

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the graph of f and g(x) = the integral from a to x of f(t) dt, locate the relative maxima and minima of g at the inputs where f changes sign, stating the direction of the sign change.
skills.description_plain: Find where f crosses the axis and say which way it crosses.
skills.name: Locate relative extrema of an accumulation function from sign changes of the integrand

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05017 (the last candidate computed is taken to be the extremum)
BC-MIS-05016 (the candidates are the critical points only, so endpoints never compete)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05006 (absolute extremum by the candidates test with a global justification)
adaptive.mastered_if: Ordering happens explicitly. The tabulated candidate values are compared against one another, the largest is named when a maximum is asked for and the smallest when a minimum is asked for, and the selected candidate is stated with its value rather than left implicit in the last line of arithmetic. BC-ERR-05028, choosing the extremum in the wrong direction, is absent, and the comparison covers every row of the table including both endpoint rows.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A correct candidate table followed by the wrong selection, recorded as BC-SIG-05020, is the intermediate state here. BC-ERR-05028 costs the answer point while leaving the table itself intact. The 2022 Q1 commentary notes a related partial shape, where the value is correct but no candidates are listed, so the justification requirement goes unmet even though the selection was sound.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: If the numbers being ordered are themselves wrong, nothing in the comparison is at fault and the gap belongs to BC-SKL-05025, evaluating the function at every candidate. The tell is a table whose ordering is internally consistent while one entry disagrees with the given rate information or the plotted area.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05017 (the comparison is never carried out and the last line becomes the answer) is the conceptual target. Where the comparison is attempted and the direction is simply inverted, the procedural target is BC-SKL-05025, since the ordering rests on the evaluated values.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Order the computed values and identify which candidate gives the absolute maximum and which the absolute minimum on the interval.
skills.description_plain: Pick the largest or smallest of the candidate values.
skills.name: Compare the candidate values and name the absolute extremum

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01005 (limit theorems applied without their conditions, which matters once quotients and composites appear)
BC-SKL-01020 (the quotient theorem, which carries a denominator condition this one does not)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01003 (supplies two limits and asks for a combination, so the theorem rather than any algebra is at stake)
adaptive.mastered_if: With the limits of f and g at c supplied, the limit of f plus g or f minus g is reported as the corresponding sum or difference of those limits, the two supplied values are recorded before combining, and the order of subtraction matches the order in the expression.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The theorem is applied to the right pair of limits but the subtraction runs the wrong way, so only the sign of the result is wrong, or the supplied limits are combined before being recorded, leaving no work to support the value.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The supplied limits are read against the wrong function or the wrong target input, which is a function notation gap at BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01005 (which theorem carries which condition) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-06005 (matching each supplied limit to its function) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given that the limits of f and g at c exist, evaluate the limit of f plus g or f minus g as the corresponding sum or difference of those limits.
skills.description_plain: Split the limit of a sum into the sum of the limits.
skills.name: Apply the sum and difference limit theorems

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01005 (theorems applied as unconditional formal rules)
BC-SKL-01018 (the sum and difference case)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01003 (a product or constant multiple built from two supplied limits, which isolates this theorem from any rewriting)
adaptive.mastered_if: The limit of a product is reported as the product of the supplied limits and a constant factor is carried outside the limit unchanged, with both supplied values recorded and the constant multiple case handled without re-deriving the product rule for it.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The product of the two limits is formed correctly but a constant multiple is also multiplied into itself or dropped, so the structure of the theorem is right and one factor is mishandled.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The supplied limits are matched to the wrong functions or the wrong target, which is a notation gap at BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01005 (the hypotheses each limit theorem needs) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-06005 (reading the supplied limits) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given that the limits of f and g at c exist, evaluate the limit of a product as the product of the limits and the limit of a constant multiple as the constant times the limit.
skills.description_plain: Take the limit of each factor and multiply, and pull constants out.
skills.name: Apply the product and constant multiple limit theorems

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01005 (limit theorems treated as unconditional)
BC-SKL-01029 (classifying the form under substitution, which is what a zero denominator limit calls for next)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01003 (a quotient built from supplied limits, where the denominator condition is expected in a justified response)
adaptive.mastered_if: Before dividing, the response states that the limit of the denominator is not zero and then reports the quotient of the two limits, and where the denominator limit is zero it states that the theorem does not apply rather than dividing anyway (BC-ERR-01006 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The quotient of the two supplied limits is formed correctly and the denominator condition is never written down, so the value stands but the justification naming the theorem is incomplete.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The supplied limits are attached to the wrong functions, which is a notation gap at BC-PRQ-06005, rather than an omission of the condition.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01005 (why the quotient theorem carries a denominator condition) for the conceptual failure; BC-SKL-01029 (classifying the form when the denominator limit is zero) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Evaluate the limit of a quotient as the quotient of the limits, stating first that the limit of the denominator is not zero, and identify when the theorem does not apply.
skills.description_plain: Divide the limits, after checking that the bottom limit is not zero.
skills.name: Apply the quotient limit theorem and check the denominator condition

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01019 (continuity read off the shape of the formula rather than from its domain)
BC-SKL-01029 (classifying the form, which is what substitution at an excluded input calls for)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01014 (several expressions are presented and the procedure must be selected, so substituting where it does not apply is visible)
adaptive.mastered_if: For a polynomial, rational, power, exponential, logarithmic, or trigonometric expression defined at c, the response substitutes c and reports the resulting number as the limit, and states or implies that substitution is legitimate because the expression is defined and continuous there rather than as a default move.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Substitution is carried out correctly where it is legitimate but is also attempted at an input outside the domain, so the value is produced without the check that licenses it.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The inputs at which a radical, logarithm, or rational expression is undefined cannot be named, which is a domain gap at BC-PRQ-01008 and shows up as substitution at an excluded input.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01019 (continuity as a property on a domain) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-01008 (domains of rational, radical, logarithmic, and trigonometric expressions) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: For a polynomial, rational, power, exponential, logarithmic, or trigonometric expression defined at c, evaluate the limit at c by substituting c.
skills.description_plain: Put the target value into the expression when that is legitimate.
skills.name: Evaluate a limit by direct substitution where the function is continuous

common_confusions: BC-MIS-04010 (the relating equation assembled from the rates alone)
BC-MIS-04011 (an instantaneous measurement treated as a fixed feature)
BC-SKL-04021 (eliminating a variable from the relation once it is written)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-04006 (nothing downstream is reachable without the correct relation)
adaptive.mastered_if: An equation tying the named quantities together is written from the geometry of the configuration, a volume or area formula, the Pythagorean theorem, or the description itself, and it describes the figure as drawn rather than a similar one; BC-ERR-04016 is absent, so a fixed diameter is used where the barrel does not widen.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The rates are recorded correctly and the relating equation is skipped or chosen by resemblance to a familiar formula, BC-ERR-04016 with signal BC-SIG-04012, so the differentiation acts on something that does not describe the configuration.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The geometric formula for the named quantity cannot be produced with no calculus involved, a gap at BC-PRQ-04001 or BC-PRQ-04002.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-04010 (rates alone do not determine a geometric relationship). Procedural failure: BC-PRQ-04002 (the volume, area, or distance formula for the configuration).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the named quantities of a related rates scenario, write an equation relating them, drawn from a volume or area formula, the Pythagorean theorem, or the description itself.
skills.description_plain: Find the geometric or contextual formula that ties the quantities together.
skills.name: Write an equation relating the varying quantities
skills.notation: relating equation

common_confusions: BC-MIS-04008 (differentiating a relation read as differentiating with respect to a length)
BC-MIS-04009 (a short product read as one varying symbol)
BC-SKL-04022 (the same operation on a curve given implicitly)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-04006 (the chain rule to time is the step the Chief Reader reports record as rare)
BC-QA-04007 (both coordinates vary with time in one equation)
adaptive.mastered_if: Both sides of the relating equation are differentiated with respect to time, so each varying quantity contributes its own derivative with respect to time through the chain rule and a term in a spatial variable is never left as a bare derivative with respect to that variable; BC-ERR-04017 is absent, and the chain factor that converts a spatial derivative into a time rate is written.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The relation is differentiated with respect to a length or with respect to x and the work stops there, signal BC-SIG-04013 and BC-ERR-04017, the state the 2024 Chief Reader report describes as needing to continue through the chain rule; or the differentiation is with respect to time and one supplied rate is never substituted.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: There is no relating equation to differentiate, a gap at BC-SKL-04018 rather than in the differentiation.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-04008 (time is the variable of differentiation and the dimensions depend on it). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-04018 (having a correct relation before differentiating).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an equation relating quantities that are functions of time, differentiate both sides with respect to time so that each term in a varying quantity carries the derivative of that quantity with respect to time.
skills.description_plain: Differentiate both sides with respect to t, attaching a rate factor to every varying quantity.
skills.name: Differentiate a relation with respect to time using the chain rule
skills.notation: d/dt applied to both sides

common_confusions: BC-MIS-04011 (a value true at an instant treated as true throughout)
BC-MIS-04008 (the variable of differentiation misidentified)
BC-SKL-04024 (substituting after the differentiation, the step this one protects)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-04006 (a measurement given for one instant sits beside a dimension fixed for all time)
BC-QA-04007 (the coordinates of the point are substituted only after differentiating)
adaptive.mastered_if: Quantities that vary are carried as letters through the differentiation and their instantaneous values are substituted only afterwards, so a dimension measured at the instant still contributes its rate; BC-ERR-04020 is absent, and the response can say which of the stated numbers would still hold one second later.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A varying dimension appears as a number in the equation that is then differentiated, so its rate never appears, BC-ERR-04020 with signal BC-SIG-04014, the failure the 2014 Q4 part D distinctions name as substituting before differentiating.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Constants in time and instantaneous values are not separated in the first place, a gap at BC-SKL-04027; or the differentiation with respect to time is itself absent, BC-SKL-04019.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-04011 (only quantities constant in time may be substituted early). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-04027 (classifying each stated number before writing the equation).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a related rates problem with values that hold only at the instant in question, carry those quantities as variables through the differentiation and replace them by their values afterwards.
skills.description_plain: Keep the varying quantities as variables until the differentiation is finished.
skills.name: Substitute instantaneous values only after differentiating
skills.notation: values substituted after differentiation

common_confusions: BC-MIS-04003 (units added only if time allows)
BC-MIS-04002 (the sign of a rate treated as formatting)
BC-SKL-04002 (the interpretation sentence in a non related rates setting)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-04006 (the units instruction is part of the prompt and is scored)
adaptive.mastered_if: The computed rate is reported with the units of the quantity divided by the units of time and with a statement of whether the quantity is increasing or decreasing at that instant, so the sign is converted into direction and the units follow the quantity in the stem; BC-ERR-04001 and BC-ERR-04005 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The value is correct and is given without units, BC-ERR-04001 with signal BC-SIG-04001, which the 2019 Q4 part A distinctions record as ignoring the units instruction; or the magnitude is reported and the negative sign is left uninterpreted, BC-ERR-04005.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The rate itself was never isolated, a gap at BC-SKL-04024 rather than a reporting gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-04002 (a negative rate states that the quantity is falling). Procedural failure: BC-PRQ-04004 (assembling quantity units over time units).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a computed rate, report it with the units of the quantity divided by the units of time and state whether the quantity is increasing or decreasing at that instant.
skills.description_plain: Say what the number means for the situation and attach the units.
skills.name: Report a related rate with units and interpret its sign
skills.notation: rate with units and direction

common_confusions: BC-MIS-04011 (a value true at an instant read as true throughout)
BC-MIS-04008 (time not recognised as the variable everything depends on)
BC-SKL-04023 (acting on the classification by delaying substitution)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-04006 (the configuration mixes a permanent dimension with a momentary measurement)
adaptive.mastered_if: Each stated number is classified as constant over time or as an instantaneous value, so a fixed diameter is marked as always applying and a measured height as applying only now, and only the constants are substituted before the differentiation; BC-ERR-04020 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The scenario is set up correctly and an instantaneous measurement is treated as a fixed feature of the configuration, BC-ERR-04020 with signal BC-SIG-04014, which the 2019 Q4 part A distinctions record in both directions, treating a fixed radius as varying and a varying one as fixed.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The quantities and their rates were never named, a gap at BC-SKL-04017 and BC-PRQ-04008.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-04011 (asking which numbers still hold one second later). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-04017 (recording each quantity and rate before classifying it).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a related rates scenario, classify each stated quantity as constant over time or as an instantaneous value, since only the constants may be substituted before differentiating.
skills.description_plain: Decide which numbers in the scenario always hold and which hold only at this instant.
skills.name: Distinguish quantities constant in time from quantities varying in time
skills.notation: always true against true at an instant

common_confusions: BC-MIS-07010 (the direction of an approximation taken from increase or decrease)
BC-MIS-07009 (an equilibrium level treated as crossable)
BC-SKL-07023 (using this sign to fix the direction of an Euler error)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-07005 (the second derivative in terms of the dependent variable carries its own point)
BC-QA-07010 (rise and fall are described without solving)
adaptive.mastered_if: Increase and decrease are read from the sign of the right side and concavity from the sign of the differentiated right side, with the differential equation substituted back so the second derivative is expressed in the dependent variable rather than in the first derivative; BC-ERR-07018 and BC-ERR-99020 are absent, and the sign is argued across the interval rather than at one input.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The right side is differentiated correctly and the result still contains the derivative symbol, signal BC-SIG-07017, which the 2023 Q3 part C scoring records as not earning the first point although the part stays live; or monotonicity is offered where concavity was required, BC-ERR-07018.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The slope the equation assigns at a point cannot be computed, a gap at BC-SKL-07010; or the chain rule factor is dropped when the right side is differentiated, the failure the 2019 Q4 part B distinctions record.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-07010 (concavity comes from the second derivative, not from direction). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-07010 (substituting the equation back to remove the first derivative).

skills.assessability_basis: isolated by BC-QA-07005, BC-QA-07010
skills.description_formal: Determine where a solution increases or decreases from the sign of the right side, and its concavity from the sign of the differentiated right side, without solving.
skills.description_plain: Use the sign of the derivative and its rate of change to describe the curve.
skills.name: Read monotonicity and concavity of a solution from the equation or the field

common_confusions: BC-MIS-03006 (dy/dx expected to be a number independent of y)
BC-SKL-03011 (the first derivative value alone)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-03008 (the value of the second derivative at a point is its own scoring point)
adaptive.mastered_if: The value of dy/dx at the stated point is computed first from both coordinates, then the coordinates and that slope are substituted into the second derivative expression to give one number; BC-ERR-03011 and BC-ERR-03023 are both absent, so no dy/dx symbol survives into the reported value.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The second derivative expression is fully correct and is evaluated without first computing dy/dx at the point, BC-ERR-03023 with signal BC-SIG-03015, a state in which the product rule and chain rule points remain available while the value point is lost; or only the x coordinate is substituted into dy/dx, BC-ERR-03011.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The slope at the point cannot be produced on its own, a gap at BC-SKL-03011; or the second derivative expression is not obtained, a gap at BC-SKL-03033.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-03006 (the second derivative at a point depends on the slope there). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-03011 (evaluating dy/dx at both coordinates first).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an expression for the second derivative containing x, y, and dy/dx, compute dy/dx at the stated point and substitute all three values to produce the numerical second derivative.
skills.description_plain: Work out dy/dx at the point first, then substitute both coordinates and that slope.
skills.name: Evaluate a second derivative at a point using dy/dx there
skills.notation: second derivative evaluated at a point

common_confusions: BC-MIS-07014 (any equation assumed separable)
BC-MIS-07015 (one side antidifferentiated as though the rearrangement were the method)
BC-SKL-06047 (substitution in an antiderivative, which the separated side often needs)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-07003 (separation is the gateway point, and its absence forfeits the part)
adaptive.mastered_if: The equation is rewritten with the dependent variable and its differential on one side and the independent variable and its differential on the other, with constant factors placed on the side they belong to and a differential present on each side; BC-ERR-07024, BC-ERR-99014, and BC-ERR-99006 are absent, and without this step the 2023 shape awards none of the four points.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The equation is antidifferentiated as written with both variables on the same side, BC-ERR-07024 with signal BC-SIG-07023; or the separation is attempted and a constant factor is left with the wrong differential, or the shifted quantity is placed on the wrong side, the failures BC-ERR-99014 and the 2026 Q3 part D distinctions record.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The right side does not factor into a function of each variable, so separation is not available, a gap at BC-SKL-07028; or the algebraic rearrangement itself fails, BC-PRQ-07002.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-07014 (separation requires the right side to factor). Procedural failure: BC-ERR-99006 (keeping a differential on each side of the separated equation).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Rewrite the differential equation so that one side contains only the dependent variable together with its differential and the other only the independent variable with its differential.
skills.description_plain: Move all the terms in one variable to one side with its differential.
skills.name: Separate the variables onto opposite sides of the equation

common_confusions: BC-MIS-07015 (antidifferentiating one side treated as sufficient)
BC-MIS-07014 (separation applied where it does not hold)
BC-SKL-06047 (the substitution the independent side often requires)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-07003 (the antiderivative points are scored separately from the separation)
adaptive.mastered_if: Both sides of the separated equation are antidifferentiated with respect to their own variables, producing a logarithm from a reciprocal side and a power from a power side, with any inner constant handled by substitution; BC-ERR-07025 and BC-ERR-99014 are absent, and a product on the independent side is recognised as needing parts rather than factor by factor treatment.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The separated form is right and only one side is antidifferentiated, BC-ERR-07025 with signal BC-SIG-07024; or both sides are antidifferentiated and one antiderivative is wrong, such as a logarithm used for a reciprocal square, the misfire the 2013 Q5 part C distinctions separate from a separation failure.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The variables were never separated, a gap at BC-SKL-07024; or the antiderivative of the shape involved is unavailable, BC-PRQ-06003 and BC-SKL-06034.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-07015 (both differentials must be integrated). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-06034 (the antiderivative of the reciprocal and power shapes that arise).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Antidifferentiate the two sides of the separated equation, producing a logarithm where the dependent side is a reciprocal and a power where it is a power.
skills.description_plain: Integrate each side with respect to its own variable.
skills.name: Antidifferentiate both sides of the separated equation

common_confusions: BC-MIS-07016 (the constant of integration treated as optional)
BC-MIS-07005 (one solution expected, so no constant is needed)
BC-SKL-07029 (using the constant once it is in place)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-07003 (the constant carries a point and gates the two that follow)
adaptive.mastered_if: One constant of integration is written on a single side of the antiderivative equation, at the antidifferentiation stage rather than after any exponentiation, so the family it indexes is intact when the initial condition arrives; BC-ERR-07026 is absent, and without the constant the 2023 shape caps the part at two points.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Both antiderivatives are correct and no constant appears anywhere, BC-ERR-07026 with signal BC-SIG-07025, so a general solution is produced where a particular one was asked for; or the constant is attached after exponentiating, the stage error the 2023 Q3 part D and 2024 Q3 part C distinctions record.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Only one side was antidifferentiated, a gap at BC-SKL-07025, so there is no equation for a constant to sit in.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-07016 (the constant is what the initial condition acts on). Procedural failure: BC-ERR-07029 (placing the constant before any exponentiation).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Collect the two constants of antidifferentiation into one constant placed on a single side of the resulting equation.
skills.description_plain: Add one constant, on one side only.
skills.name: Include a single constant of integration

common_confusions: BC-MIS-07016 (the constant treated as optional)
BC-MIS-07003 (the initial condition treated as part of the equation)
BC-SKL-07030 (using the same point to settle a sign rather than the constant)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-07003 (the constant point is earned for including it and substituting the initial values into that equation)
adaptive.mastered_if: The stated input and output are substituted into the antiderivative equation that still contains the constant, before any exponentiation, and the constant is solved for there; BC-ERR-07029 and BC-ERR-99014 are absent, so the constant is not evaluated in an expression where it has already changed form.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The general solution is correct and the response exponentiates first and then substitutes, so the constant is fixed in its transformed form, BC-ERR-07029 with signal BC-SIG-07028; the 2019 Q4 part C distinctions call this an order of operations failure inside the method.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: No constant was written at the antidifferentiation stage, a gap at BC-SKL-07026; or the initial condition was folded into the equation, BC-SKL-07004.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-07016 (the initial condition selects one member by fixing the constant). Procedural failure: BC-ERR-07029 (substituting before the equation is transformed).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Substitute the stated input and output into the antiderivative equation that contains the constant, and solve for the constant.
skills.description_plain: Put the given point in and solve for the constant.
skills.name: Substitute the initial condition to evaluate the constant of integration

common_confusions: BC-MIS-07017 (an implicit relation treated as a finished solution)
BC-MIS-07016 (the constant omitted, so the inversion has no parameter)
BC-SKL-07030 (resolving the absolute value that the inversion exposes)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-07003 (solving for the dependent variable is the last of the four points)
adaptive.mastered_if: The antiderivative equation is inverted, by exponentiating or otherwise, to give the dependent variable explicitly in terms of the independent variable and the constant, so a value can be read off at any stated input; BC-ERR-07027 is absent and the answer is not left as an implicit relation when an expression was requested.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The constant is found and the dependent variable is never isolated, BC-ERR-07027 with signal BC-SIG-07026, which the 2013 Q5 part C and 2021 Q5 part C distinctions record as the final solving point lost with the rest of the part correct.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The constant is absent or misplaced so there is nothing coherent to invert, a gap at BC-SKL-07026; or the logarithm and exponential inversion itself fails, BC-PRQ-07001.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-07017 (an explicit expression is what the question asks for). Procedural failure: BC-PRQ-07001 (exponentiating to undo a logarithm).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Exponentiate or otherwise invert the antiderivative equation to write the dependent variable explicitly in terms of the independent variable and the constant.
skills.description_plain: Rearrange to get the dependent variable by itself.
skills.name: Solve the resulting equation for the dependent variable

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06016 (selecting an antidifferentiation technique from the structure of the integrand)
adaptive.mastered_if: Radicals and reciprocals are rewritten as powers first, then the exponent is raised by one and the result divided by that new exponent, with the constant of integration attached whenever the answer is an indefinite integral. The exponent negative one is excluded by name rather than by accident. Term by term antidifferentiation of a polynomial is carried out completely, and under BC-QA-06016 the learner inspects the integrand's structural markers and rules out techniques whose preconditions fail before applying the reverse power rule.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The exponent is raised and the divisor is left off, so the antiderivative of a power is half remembered while the rest of the method is sound. A related state is the general solution being produced where a particular one was asked, the constant omitted after separating variables, as recorded in 2019 Q4 part C. Correct antiderivatives followed by wrong arithmetic at the limits, and copy errors carried in from an earlier part, are evaluation and transcription failures rather than antidifferentiation failures.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: An integrand left in radical or reciprocal form, with the reverse power rule attempted on it directly, points to BC-PRQ-06002 (exponent rules including negative and fractional exponents). If the power rule itself cannot be reconstructed, the earlier skill is BC-SKL-02027 (deriving a power rule case from the limit definition), and the tell is a learner who treats the rule as a remembered string with no source.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-PRQ-06002 (exponent rules that make a radical or reciprocal into a power) for the conceptual failure; procedural failure points instead to BC-SKL-02027 (the power rule case the reverse rule inverts)

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an integrand that is a power of x with any real exponent other than negative one, determine the antiderivative as x to the next power divided by that power, plus a constant.
skills.description_plain: Raise the exponent by one and divide, after rewriting radicals and reciprocals as powers.
skills.name: Antidifferentiate power functions including negative and fractional exponents

common_confusions: BC-MIS-02012 (the quotient rule treated as symmetric)
BC-SKL-02042 (a constant denominator, where the rule is not needed)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-02008 (the rule with both derivatives present and the simplified result are separately scored)
adaptive.mastered_if: The derivative of a quotient is written with the denominator times the derivative of the numerator minus the numerator times the derivative of the denominator, in that order (BC-ERR-02021 absent), over the square of the denominator (BC-ERR-02022 absent), with both derivatives taken.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The structure is right and the subtraction runs the wrong way, which is BC-SIG-02014 and BC-ERR-02021, so the answer differs only in sign, or the denominator is written without its square, which is BC-ERR-02022.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The product rule cannot be stated with both of its terms, which is a gap at BC-SKL-02036 and shows as a quotient rule numerator with one term missing.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-02012 (applying the rule to a reciprocal and comparing with the power rule result) for the conceptual failure; BC-SKL-02036 (the product rule structure underneath) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: For a quotient of differentiable functions, write the derivative with the stated numerator and with the square of the denominator below.
skills.description_plain: Use the denominator times the derivative of the numerator minus the numerator times the derivative of the denominator, all over the denominator squared.
skills.name: Apply the quotient rule to a quotient of two differentiable functions

common_confusions: BC-MIS-03001 (the inside is copied across unchanged)
BC-SKL-03006 (a composite inside a product needs the enclosing rule as well)
BC-MIS-03012 (rule picked from the look of the expression)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-03001 (the chain rule factor is the discriminating element of the scored answer)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response writes f prime of g of x multiplied by g prime of x, with the outer derivative evaluated at the inner expression rather than at x, and the same structure appears whether the composite is given symbolically, in Leibniz form as dy/du times du/dx, or inside an exponential model as in the 2013 Q3 part D derivative; neither BC-ERR-03001 nor BC-ERR-03002 appears, and the inner factor survives even when the inner function is linear.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The outer derivative is correct at the inner expression and the multiplication by g prime of x is missing, which is BC-ERR-03001 and signal BC-SIG-03001; or every factor is present but one is evaluated at the wrong expression or attached to the wrong term, signal BC-SIG-03002. The 2019 Q5 part A distinctions separate a missing inner derivative from a quotient rule that was misremembered.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The outer function is differentiated wrongly on its own, an elementary derivative rule gap at BC-SKL-02027 rather than a chain rule gap; or the composite is never separated into layers, which is BC-SKL-03001.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-03001 (the inner function is an input that varies, so its rate enters the product). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-03001 (naming the layers before differentiating).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given y equal to f of g of x with f and g differentiable, produce f prime of g of x multiplied by g prime of x.
skills.description_plain: Differentiate the outside, keep the inside, then multiply by the derivative of the inside.
skills.name: Differentiate a two layer composite function with the chain rule
skills.notation: dy/dx equals dy/du times du/dx

common_confusions: BC-MIS-02014 (the derivative value and the function value treated as playing the same role)
BC-SKL-02013 (writing the tangent line, which uses this interpretation)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-02011 (the slope from the derivative and the point of tangency are scored separately, which exposes a swap)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response states that f prime of a is the slope of the line tangent to the graph of f at the point with input a, and uses that number as a slope while f(a) is used as a height, so the function value is never placed in the slope position (BC-ERR-02027 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The sentence identifying the derivative with the tangent slope is correct but the two numbers computed at the point are then used interchangeably, so the statement is held and not applied.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: A correct derivative value is produced and the point slope form cannot be written, which is a gap at BC-PRQ-02003 rather than a misunderstanding of what the derivative means.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-02014 (which of the two numbers has the units of a slope) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-02003 (slope and point slope form) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: isolated by BC-QA-02011
skills.description_formal: State that the derivative of a function at a point is the slope of the line tangent to the graph of the function at that point.
skills.description_plain: Say that the derivative value is the steepness of the line touching the curve there.
skills.name: Interpret the derivative at a point as the slope of the tangent line

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05001 (hypotheses treated as decoration, with the conclusion taken to be the whole theorem)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05001 (a differentiable function with selected values supplied, and the response must decide whether some interior input has a named instantaneous rate of change and justify it)
adaptive.mastered_if: Before any conclusion is written, the learner names continuity on the closed interval [a,b] and differentiability on the open interval (a,b) as the two conditions the Mean Value Theorem demands, keeps the closed and open endpoints distinct in the interval notation, and does this whether the function arrives as a formula, a table, or a verbal statement of differentiability. No response shows BC-ERR-05001 (conclusion used with no mention of continuity or differentiability) or BC-ERR-99008 (a theorem applied without its hypotheses established first).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The conditions appear only when asked for, which is what BC-SIG-05001 records, correct arithmetic and a correct conclusion with no sentence establishing continuity or differentiability. Another intermediate state names one condition and drops the other, or names both but attaches them to the wrong interval type, and the 2013 Q3 part B scoring behaviour of hypotheses never stated with the average rate correct shows the same partial hold, an instance of BC-ERR-05001.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Wrong open or closed endpoints in the stated conditions point back at BC-PRQ-05004 (interval notation and the open versus closed distinction), and a learner who cannot say that differentiability at a point gives continuity there has not secured BC-SKL-02019, the tell being a response that lists differentiability twice rather than listing continuity on [a,b] and differentiability on (a,b).
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05001 (an existence theorem is licensed by its conditions, not by its name); a procedural failure in the endpoint notation points instead to BC-PRQ-05004 (open versus closed interval notation)

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Name continuity on the closed interval and differentiability on the open interval as the conditions the Mean Value Theorem requires.
skills.description_plain: Say what must be true of the function before the theorem may be used.
skills.name: State the hypotheses of the Mean Value Theorem for a function and an interval

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06010 (rational integrand whose denominator factors into distinct linear factors, decomposed and antidifferentiated into natural logarithms)
adaptive.mastered_if: Before any decomposition is written, the denominator is factored into distinct nonrepeating linear factors and the degree of the numerator is checked against the degree of the denominator, so an improper integrand is divided first rather than split directly. Factoring a quadratic such as one whose roots differ produces two separate linear factors, each of which will later carry its own unknown constant, and the factored form is written out rather than held in the head. BC-ERR-06026, an improper rational integrand decomposed without a preliminary division, is absent from the work in BC-REP-01 symbolic form.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The denominator factors correctly but the structural check on the degrees never happens, which is BC-ERR-06026, so the decomposition that follows cannot be solved consistently and the antiderivative point is lost. A second intermediate state is visible in BC-FRQ-2015-Q5-D, where the factors are antidifferentiated one by one without any decomposition being written, showing the technique was not selected even though the factoring itself was fine. Partial factoring, one linear factor found and the rest left as a quadratic, is a third state.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: No prerequisite skills are listed for this record, so a failure here is a factoring failure in its own right rather than a masquerade. The sign that the trouble sits below the calculus is a denominator whose roots are found numerically or by graphing rather than by factoring, leaving no linear factors to attach constants to.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-SKL-06062 itself for the conceptual failure, recognising that a rational integrand must be both proper and factored before a decomposition exists; the procedural failure, factoring arithmetic that goes astray, is the same skill exercised on the algebra rather than on the structural check.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a rational integrand, factor the denominator into linear, nonrepeating factors so that a partial fraction decomposition is available.
skills.description_plain: Factor the quadratic or higher denominator before decomposing.
skills.name: Factor a denominator into distinct linear factors

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06010 (rational integrand whose denominator factors into distinct linear factors, decomposed and antidifferentiated into natural logarithms)
adaptive.mastered_if: With the denominator already factored, unknown constant numerators are attached to each distinct linear factor, denominators are cleared to give a polynomial identity, and the constants come out either by substituting the root of each factor in turn or by equating coefficients of like powers. The solved constants are checked back in at least one convenient value, and the written decomposition is the one that BC-FRQ-2019-Q5-B awards its first point for and that BC-FRQ-2015-Q5-D awards two points for. The identity is treated as holding for all x, not only at the substituted values.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The decomposition is set up with the right shape but the constants come out wrong, which BC-FRQ-2015-Q5-D records as coefficients solved incorrectly, algebra rather than technique. A different stopping point appears in BC-FRQ-2019-Q5-B, where the decomposition is correct and complete and then nothing is antidifferentiated, so the technique is known but execution halts. A third state is a response that clears denominators but never forms a solvable system, substituting arbitrary values instead of the roots.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Constants that cannot be solved because the identity was never cleared properly, or because a small linear system is set up and then mishandled, points at BC-PRQ-06011, solving for undetermined coefficients in a rational identity. The tell is algebra that stalls after multiplying through. If instead the decomposition has the wrong number of terms, or a quadratic denominator still sits under one of them, the gap is BC-SKL-06062 and the denominator was never fully factored.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-SKL-06062 (the factored denominator that determines how many constants there are) for the conceptual failure; the procedural failure, clearing and solving the identity, points instead to BC-PRQ-06011 (undetermined coefficients in a rational identity).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a proper rational function with distinct linear factors, write the decomposition with unknown constant numerators, clear denominators, and solve for the constants by substitution or by equating coefficients.
skills.description_plain: Clear denominators and solve for the numerators.
skills.name: Solve for the constants in a linear partial fraction decomposition

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06010 (rational integrand whose denominator factors into distinct linear factors, decomposed and antidifferentiated into natural logarithms)
adaptive.mastered_if: Each term of the decomposition becomes its constant numerator times the natural logarithm of the absolute value of the linear factor, divided by that factor's leading coefficient, so a denominator such as two x minus three carries a one half out front. Absolute value bars appear inside every logarithm and a constant of integration is attached when the integral is indefinite, the two notation losses that BC-FRQ-2015-Q5-D names alongside an otherwise correct decomposition. The result is a sum of logarithm terms rather than a single logarithm, unless the terms are deliberately combined by the quotient rule.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The logarithm shape is right but the leading coefficient of the linear factor is not divided out, so the antiderivative is off by a constant multiple. Or, as BC-FRQ-2015-Q5-D records, the decomposition is right and the logarithms arrive without absolute values or without the constant, an antidifferentiation notation loss rather than a technique loss. A further state is the response in BC-FRQ-2019-Q5-B that attempts a substitution on the whole rational integrand instead, showing the integrand structure was not read as a sum of simple fractions.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Missing absolute value bars, or a logarithm of a product split wrongly, points at BC-PRQ-06003, the logarithm rules and the domain of ln. The tell is ln of a negative quantity written without comment. Constants that were already wrong before antidifferentiation began points at BC-SKL-06063 instead, and an inability to see one over a linear factor as a logarithm at all points at BC-SKL-06052.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-SKL-06052 (substitution on an integrand that antidifferentiates to a logarithm) is the conceptual target, since it supplies the reason the reciprocal of a linear factor becomes a logarithm with a reciprocal leading coefficient; the procedural failure, absolute values and constants, points instead to BC-PRQ-06003 (logarithm rules and the domain of ln).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a decomposition into ratios with linear denominators, antidifferentiate each term as the constant numerator times the natural logarithm of the absolute value of the linear factor divided by its leading coefficient.
skills.description_plain: Each simple fraction becomes a constant times a natural logarithm.
skills.name: Antidifferentiate a linear partial fraction decomposition

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06010 (rational integrand whose denominator factors into distinct linear factors, decomposed and antidifferentiated into natural logarithms)
adaptive.mastered_if: A proper rational integrand with distinct linear factors is decomposed, each term antidifferentiated as a constant times ln of the absolute value of its factor, and the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus applied by substituting the upper limit minus the lower limit. Logarithms are combined by the quotient rule where that simplifies the arithmetic, and the difference of logarithms is evaluated without dropping a sign or a coefficient. The final number is stated exactly, and the substitution of both limits is visible in the work rather than performed silently.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The decomposition and the antiderivative are both correct and then the endpoint arithmetic collapses, which BC-FRQ-2019-Q5-B describes as logarithm arithmetic wrong at the limits, algebra rather than the integration technique failing. A second intermediate state is the general antiderivative produced with no limits substituted at all, leaving the answer as an expression in x. A third is combining ln terms into a single logarithm incorrectly before substituting, so the quotient rule error is carried into the evaluation.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: An antiderivative that is right but never evaluated at the endpoints, or evaluated as lower minus upper, points at BC-SKL-06034, evaluating a definite integral by antidifferentiation and endpoint substitution. The tell is the absence of the bracket evaluation line. If the logarithm terms themselves are misformed before any limit appears, the gap sits at BC-SKL-06064, and if the logarithm algebra at the limits is the problem, BC-PRQ-06003 is the place it originates.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-SKL-06064 (antidifferentiating the decomposition into logarithms) for the conceptual failure; where the decomposition and antiderivative are sound and only the endpoint work fails, the procedural target is BC-SKL-06034 (definite integral by antidifferentiation and endpoint substitution).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a definite integral of a proper rational function with distinct linear factors, decompose, antidifferentiate, and apply the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, combining the logarithms where useful.
skills.description_plain: Decompose, antidifferentiate, then substitute the limits.
skills.name: Evaluate a definite integral of a rational function by partial fractions

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06011 (integral with an infinite limit of integration or an unbounded integrand, rewritten as a limit of definite integrals and evaluated or shown to diverge)
adaptive.mastered_if: Before any antidifferentiation, the integral is inspected at both limits and across the whole interval, and the response says in words which of the two causes applies, a limit of integration that is infinite or an integrand that is unbounded somewhere on the interval, including at an interior point rather than only at an endpoint. BC-FRQ-2019-Q5-C awards its first point for exactly this indication that the integral is improper. BC-ERR-06025, a finite value reported for a divergent integral, does not appear downstream because the impropriety was named before the evaluation began.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The infinite limit case is caught reliably and the unbounded integrand case is not, which BC-FRQ-2019-Q5-C records as the antiderivative evaluated at the endpoints directly with the singularity inside the interval never noticed. Another intermediate state names the integral improper without saying which cause, so the rewrite that follows has nowhere to put the variable. A third state calls a perfectly ordinary definite integral improper because the integrand is complicated rather than unbounded.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: A response that recognises the infinite endpoint but cannot write it as anything other than a number points at BC-SKL-01054, writing an infinite limit using correct notation. The tell is infinity treated as an ordinary symbol in the limits of integration with no limit process available to describe it.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-SKL-06066 itself for the conceptual failure, since the two causes of impropriety are the content of the skill; the procedural failure, writing the infinite endpoint down, points instead to BC-SKL-01054 (infinite limit notation).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a definite integral, determine whether it is improper because one or both limits of integration are infinite or because the integrand is unbounded somewhere on the interval of integration, and name which.
skills.description_plain: Say whether the limit is infinite or the integrand is unbounded.
skills.name: Classify an integral as improper and name the cause

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06020 (infinity is a number that can be substituted)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06011 (integral with an infinite limit of integration or an unbounded integrand, rewritten as a limit of definite integrals and evaluated or shown to diverge)
adaptive.mastered_if: The offending limit is replaced by a variable and the whole expression is written as the limit as that variable approaches infinity, or approaches the point of unboundedness from the correct side, of a definite integral in which the variable is now one endpoint. The limit symbol is carried on every line from the rewrite onward, which is what BC-FRQ-2023-Q5-B requires for its first point and what BC-FRQ-2026-Q5-D banks as P7 once earned. Neither BC-ERR-06024, arithmetic with infinity written in place of a limit, nor BC-ERR-99007 shows up anywhere in the chain.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Limit notation appears only on the final line, which BC-FRQ-2026-Q5-D names as the notation requirement never actually met, or the rewrite is skipped entirely and infinity is substituted into the antiderivative, which is BC-ERR-06024 and matches BC-SIG-06021, where the antiderivative is seen evaluated at infinity with no limit notation anywhere. The distinguishing probe is to ask for the rewrite on its own; a correct rewrite indicates a notation habit rather than a belief about infinity. Limits written correctly but with no conclusion drawn afterwards is the communication gap BC-FRQ-2019-Q5-C records.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: A rewrite that puts the variable at the wrong endpoint, or that never happens because the integral was not seen as improper in the first place, points at BC-SKL-06066 and the tell is that no cause of impropriety was ever named. An interior singularity left unsplit is the same gap showing at a different place.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06020 (infinity as a limiting process rather than an endpoint value) is the conceptual target; where the rewrite is understood and the limit symbol simply is not carried through the work, the procedural target is BC-SKL-06067 itself as a notation habit.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an improper integral, rewrite it using correct limit notation as the limit of a definite integral whose limit of integration is a variable approaching infinity or approaching the point of unboundedness.
skills.description_plain: Replace the offending limit by a variable and take a limit.
skills.name: Rewrite an improper integral as a limit of definite integrals

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06020 (infinity is a number that can be substituted)
BC-MIS-06021 (every improper integral of a decaying integrand converges)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06011 (integral with an infinite limit of integration or an unbounded integrand, rewritten as a limit of definite integrals and evaluated or shown to diverge)
adaptive.mastered_if: When the limit of the definite integral is infinite or fails to exist, the response writes the word diverges, or states that the limit does not exist, as the answer, and offers no numerical value in its place. The limit is shown going to infinity first, so the conclusion rests on the evaluated limit rather than on the shape of the integrand. This is the conclusion step that BC-FRQ-2019-Q5-C withholds a point for when limits are written and no conclusion follows, and BC-ERR-06025, a finite value reported for a divergent integral, does not appear.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The limit is computed correctly and reaches infinity, then a finite number is written anyway on the answer line, which is BC-ERR-06025 and can come from an arithmetic slip inside the limit or from the assumption that every improper integral converges. A second state stops after the limit expression with no verbal conclusion at all, the missing communication step. A third treats divergence and convergence as interchangeable outcomes, reporting a value while also calling the integral divergent.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: A response with nothing to conclude from, because no limit was ever set up, points at BC-SKL-06067 and the tell is an antiderivative evaluated straight at infinity, so the question of whether a limit exists was never posed.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06021 (an integrand approaching zero taken as sufficient for convergence) for the conceptual failure; where the divergence is understood and only the written conclusion is missing, the procedural target is BC-SKL-06069 itself as the statement step.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an improper integral written as a limit, conclude that the integral diverges when the limit is infinite or does not exist, and state that conclusion rather than reporting a numerical value.
skills.description_plain: Say the integral diverges when the limit is infinite or fails to exist.
skills.name: Conclude that an improper integral diverges

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06011 (integral with an infinite limit of integration or an unbounded integrand, rewritten as a limit of definite integrals and evaluated or shown to diverge)
adaptive.mastered_if: An integral improper at both ends, or one whose integrand is unbounded at an interior point, is split at a convenient finite value so that each resulting piece carries exactly one source of impropriety, and the work states that the original converges only if every piece converges. For an interior singularity at c on the interval from a to b, the split is written as the integral from a to c plus the integral from c to b before any limit is taken, using the adjacent interval property. A single divergent piece is enough to end the question, and that is said rather than assumed.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The split happens at the right point but the two pieces are then handled as one limit with a single variable, so only one impropriety is addressed. Or the interior singularity is never found and the antiderivative is evaluated at the outer endpoints directly, which BC-FRQ-2019-Q5-C describes as the singularity inside the interval never being noticed. A third state splits correctly, finds one piece divergent, and still adds the two results together to report a number.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: An interval that is not split at all, or split at a point that leaves an impropriety on both sides, points at BC-SKL-06066 when the cause of impropriety was never named. The tell is the absence of any statement about where the integrand is unbounded. If the split is attempted but the two integrals are not recombined correctly, or the sum property is applied with mismatched endpoints, the gap sits at BC-SKL-06031.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-SKL-06066 (naming every cause of impropriety, interior ones included) for the conceptual failure; the procedural failure, the mechanics of breaking and rejoining the interval, points instead to BC-SKL-06031 (the adjacent interval property of definite integrals).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an integral improper at both ends or at an interior point where the integrand is unbounded, split the interval at a convenient point so that each piece has one improper endpoint, and require every piece to converge.
skills.description_plain: Break the interval so each piece has a single source of impropriety.
skills.name: Split an improper integral that is improper at more than one place

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10019 (factorial denominators absent or misassigned)
BC-MIS-10020 (the requested degree not treated as binding)
BC-SKL-10067 (the polynomial as a partial sum of the series)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10010 (two points sit on the terms of the polynomial and one on stopping at the requested degree)
BC-QA-10011 (the coefficients carry the credit)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response divides each derivative value at a by the matching factorial, attaches the power of x minus a of the same order, and writes the polynomial to the requested degree and no further, with no trailing ellipsis. BC-ERR-10029 and BC-ERR-10030 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The derivative values are correct and are placed straight onto the powers with no factorial denominators, which is BC-SIG-10018 and BC-ERR-10029, or the coefficients are right and the answer runs past the requested degree or ends in an ellipsis, which is BC-ERR-10030.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The factorials in the denominators cannot be evaluated or simplified, which is BC-PRQ-10002, so the coefficients are never formed.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10019 (why each coefficient carries a factorial) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10002 (factorial arithmetic) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: isolated by BC-QA-10011
skills.description_formal: Given values of f and its derivatives at a, write the Taylor polynomial of stated degree with each coefficient equal to the derivative value divided by the corresponding factorial.
skills.description_plain: Divide each derivative value by the matching factorial and attach the power.
skills.name: Build a Taylor polynomial from derivative values at the centre

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10019 (values attached directly to the powers)
BC-SKL-10044 (the same assembly from values obtained by differentiating)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10011 (the table form isolates the pairing of order to power)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response reads from the table the entries for exactly the orders the requested degree needs, pairs each derivative value with the power of the same order, divides by the matching factorial, and presents the polynomial about the point the table is built at. BC-ERR-10031 and BC-ERR-10029 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The values are located in the table and one is paired with the power of a different order, which is BC-ERR-10031, or every value is placed correctly with the factorial denominators missing, which is BC-ERR-10029.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The table rows cannot be read as orders of derivative at a point, which is BC-PRQ-06005, or the factorials cannot be evaluated, which is BC-PRQ-10002.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10019 (coefficient as value over factorial) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-02008 (reading values from a table) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: isolated by BC-QA-10011
skills.description_formal: Given a table listing f and its derivatives at a point, select the entries for the required orders and assemble the Taylor polynomial of the stated degree about that point.
skills.description_plain: Read the derivative values out of the table and place them in the coefficients.
skills.name: Build a Taylor polynomial from a table of derivative values

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10020 (the requested degree not treated as binding)
BC-SKL-10044 (the general centre case, where powers of x minus a appear)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10010 (a nonzero term of the wrong degree or an ellipsis loses the final point)
BC-QA-10012 (the same polynomial reached through a known series)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response builds the polynomial about x equals zero so each term carries a plain power of x, uses the derivative values at zero divided by the matching factorial, names it a Maclaurin polynomial, and stops at the requested degree. BC-ERR-10030 is absent.
