adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The coefficients through the requested degree are correct and an extra term or a trailing ellipsis is appended, which is BC-SIG-10020 and BC-ERR-10030, so the presentation rather than the mathematics is the gap.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The factorial denominators cannot be formed, which is BC-PRQ-10002, so the Maclaurin coefficients are never produced.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10020 (a polynomial of stated degree as a finite object) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10002 (factorial denominators) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a function with derivatives at zero, write its Maclaurin polynomial of stated degree, recognising it as the Taylor polynomial about x equals zero.
skills.description_plain: Use the centre zero so the powers are plain powers of x.
skills.name: Write a Maclaurin polynomial as the Taylor polynomial about zero

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10021 (the representation assumed valid at every input)
BC-SKL-10062 (the sine and cosine series, which do alternate)
BC-SKL-10063 (the geometric series, which has no factorials)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10017 (the recalled series is the base for substitution or multiplication)
BC-QA-10012 (the related polynomial is built on the recalled series)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response writes the Maclaurin series for e to the x as the sum over n of x to the n over n factorial, displays the first terms one, x, x squared over two factorial, x cubed over three factorial, and gives the general term with no alternating factor present. BC-ERR-10040 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The general term is right and the displayed terms carry a sign pattern that belongs to sine or cosine, or the factorial denominators are omitted so the series reduces to a geometric form.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The factorial notation cannot be written or simplified, which is BC-PRQ-10002.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-CON-10001 (the standard Maclaurin series as recalled objects) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10002 (factorial notation) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Reproduce the Maclaurin series for e to the x as the sum of x to the n over n factorial, with its first several terms and its general term.
skills.description_plain: Write the series for e to the x from memory.
skills.name: Recall the Maclaurin series for the exponential function

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10026 (the centre assumed to move under the operation)
BC-SKL-10064 (substitution rather than multiplication)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10017 (the multiplied terms are the scored object)
BC-QA-10012 (a related polynomial is reached this way)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response multiplies every term of the known series, including the general term, by the given constant or power of x, raises the index on each power correctly, and reports the first several terms together with the general term. BC-ERR-10041 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The displayed terms are multiplied through and the general term is left unmultiplied, or a constant factor is applied to the first term only, which is BC-ERR-10041.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The powers of x do not combine correctly when multiplied, which is BC-PRQ-06002.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-CON-10001 (term by term operations on a series) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-06002 (combining powers) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a function that is a constant or a power of x times a known series, multiply term by term and report the first several terms and the general term.
skills.description_plain: Multiply every term of a known series by the given factor.
skills.name: Construct a series by multiplying a known series by an expression

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10020 (the requested degree not binding)
BC-MIS-10021 (the series treated as valid at every input)
BC-SKL-10065 (multiplying a known series by an expression)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10012 (the derivative relation, the first terms, and the complete polynomial are three separate points)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response produces the requested polynomial for the related function either by differentiating the defining relation with every product or chain factor present or by multiplying, differentiating, or antidifferentiating a known Maclaurin series term by term, and presents terms through the requested degree only, with supporting work for each coefficient. BC-ERR-10028 and BC-ERR-10030 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The route through the known series is taken and terms beyond the requested degree or an ellipsis are carried along, which is BC-ERR-10030, or the defining relation is differentiated with a factor dropped, which is BC-ERR-10028, or a coefficient of the right shape appears with no supporting work.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The defining relation cannot be read as connecting the two functions, which is BC-PRQ-06005, or the factorials cannot be handled, which is BC-PRQ-10002.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-CON-10001 (operations that carry one series into another) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-10044 (assembling the polynomial) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a function defined from another by a product, a derivative, or an antiderivative, produce the requested Taylor polynomial by operating on a known series or by differentiating the defining relation.
skills.description_plain: Combine known series by multiplying, differentiating, or antidifferentiating, then keep the needed degrees.
skills.name: Build a Taylor polynomial for a related function from a known series

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10020 (the requested terms not treated as binding)
BC-SKL-10068 (term by term differentiation)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10019 (the antidifferentiated series and the constant from the initial value are the scored work)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response antidifferentiates each displayed term and the general term, raising each exponent by one and dividing by the new exponent, writes a single constant of integration, and determines that constant by substituting the supplied value of the antiderivative at a point. BC-ERR-10039 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The antidifferentiated terms are right and the constant is omitted or left undetermined although a value was supplied, or the general term does not reproduce the displayed antiderivative terms, which is BC-ERR-10039.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The substitution needed inside the integrand is not selected, which is the hard prerequisite BC-SKL-06047, or the exponent arithmetic fails, which is BC-PRQ-06002, or the variable of integration is not kept distinct from the limit, which is BC-PRQ-06013.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-CON-10001 (term by term antidifferentiation with one constant) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-06047 (choosing the substitution) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: isolated by BC-QA-10019
skills.description_formal: Given a power series and a known value of the antiderivative at a point, integrate each term and the general term, then determine the constant of integration from that value.
skills.description_plain: Antidifferentiate each term and fix the constant from a known value.
skills.name: Integrate a power series term by term and determine the constant

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10021 (the representation assumed valid at every input)
BC-SKL-10066 (evaluating the full series at a point)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10012 (the polynomial is the object being evaluated)
BC-QA-10009 (the approximation is what the error bound is written about)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response substitutes the given input into the Taylor polynomial, evaluates each term, reports the sum as an approximation of f at that input, and keeps the object a polynomial of the stated degree rather than a series. BC-ERR-10030 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The substitution is carried out and the result is presented as the exact value of the function, or extra terms past the requested degree are included before evaluating, which is BC-ERR-10030.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The polynomial cannot be evaluated at the input because function notation and substitution are the blocker, which is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10021 (approximation against exact value) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-06005 (evaluating the polynomial) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a Taylor polynomial for f about a and an input near a, evaluate the polynomial at that input and present the result as an approximation of the function value.
skills.description_plain: Substitute the input into the polynomial and report the value.
skills.name: Approximate a function value with a Taylor polynomial

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06024 (the variable of integration taken to be the independent variable)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06012 (differentiating an accumulation function with a variable upper limit and evaluating the derivative at a point)
adaptive.mastered_if: The accumulation is set up as g(x) equal to the integral from a to x of f(t) dt, with the fixed starting input a in the lower limit, the independent variable x alone in the upper limit, and a bound variable of integration whose letter differs from x. Where a context supplies an initial amount, the setup reads as that initial amount plus the integral of the net rate, as the second point of BC-FRQ-2015-Q1-D requires, and the expression is a function of x rather than a number. BC-ERR-06028 (the answer left in terms of the dummy variable) does not appear, and the same setup is produced from a formula, from a graph, and from a verbal context (BC-REP-01, BC-REP-02, BC-REP-05).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The integral is written with the same letter in the upper limit and inside the integrand, the notation error the BC-FRQ-2015-Q1-D commentary records, which is the setup form of BC-ERR-06028. A separate intermediate state drops the initial amount and equates net change with the amount present, or integrates only the inflow when the context gives a net rate, so the structure of the accumulation is incomplete rather than the notation being wrong.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: BC-PRQ-06013 is the earlier failure that looks like a setup failure, and the sign is that the learner sees no difference between the letter inside the integral and the letter in the upper limit. BC-PRQ-06005 is implicated when f(t) and f(x) are not read as the same function evaluated at different inputs, so the learner cannot say what object g is.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-PRQ-06013 (bound variables and the dummy variable convention) for the conceptual failure about which letter lives inside the integral; a procedural failure that omits the initial amount or the net structure points instead to BC-FRQ-2015-Q1-D, whose second point is the equation joining the initial amount to the integral.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a rate or a function f and a starting input a, represent the accumulation as g(x) = the integral from a to x of f(t) dt, using a bound variable of integration distinct from the independent variable.
skills.description_plain: Set up g(x) as the integral from a fixed start to x.
skills.name: Write an accumulation function as a definite integral with a variable upper limit

common_confusions: BC-MIS-02015 (notation read as labels, so the object entered is not the one requested)
BC-SKL-02017 (reading a derivative from a graph, where no technology is involved)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-02013 (the setup naming the quantity and the value to three decimal places are scored separately)
adaptive.mastered_if: The setup names the quantity being computed, such as the derivative of the given function at the stated input, before the calculator value is reported (BC-ERR-02031 absent), and the value is given to three places after the decimal point with no premature rounding (BC-ERR-02032 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A correct numerical derivative is reported with nothing indicating what was computed, which is BC-SIG-02017 and loses the setup point although the value stands.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The derivative cannot be written in a notation that names the function and the input, so the calculator is asked for the wrong object, which is a gap at BC-PRQ-02004.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-02015 (what the derivative symbol names) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-02004 (writing the derivative with its variable and point) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: isolated by BC-QA-02013
skills.description_formal: Use graphing calculator capability to calculate or estimate the value of the derivative of a function at a point, and report the value to the required precision.
skills.description_plain: Use the numerical derivative capability of the calculator at the named input.
skills.name: Estimate a derivative at a point using technology

common_confusions: BC-MIS-04003 (units treated as an ornament added at the end)
BC-MIS-04001 (the quantity and its rate carrying the same units)
BC-SKL-04014 (reporting a computed rate rather than naming the units)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-04001 (units carry their own point whether or not a value is attached)
BC-QA-04002 (a table estimate where units are scored separately from the quotient)
adaptive.mastered_if: The units of the derivative are assembled as the units of the modelled quantity divided by the units of the independent variable, so a quantity in millimetres against a time in days gives millimetres per day, and a rate of a rate carries the independent variable unit twice; the units can be stated from the stem before any computation, and BC-ERR-04001 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The numerical rate is correct and the units are missing from the part entirely, signal BC-SIG-04001 and BC-ERR-04001, which costs a point of its own in the 2024 and 2025 table based questions; or the numerator and denominator units are exchanged.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The unit of the modelled quantity or of the independent variable cannot be read out of the stem, a units and context gap at BC-PRQ-04004 rather than a derivative gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-04003 (the unit is part of what a derivative is). Procedural failure: BC-PRQ-04004 (dividing one named unit by another).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the unit of a modelled quantity and the unit of its independent variable, state the unit of the derivative as the first divided by the second.
skills.description_plain: Give the units of a rate as function units divided by independent variable units.
skills.name: State the units of a derivative in context
skills.notation: units of f per unit of x

common_confusions: BC-MIS-04001 (the derivative and the quantity treated as the same information)
BC-MIS-04003 (units added only if time allows)
BC-SKL-04015 (using the vocabulary of the context rather than of motion)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-04001 (the interpretation and the units are separately scored elements of one sentence)
adaptive.mastered_if: The sentence names the modelled quantity, the instant at which the rate holds, whether the quantity is increasing or decreasing, and the units, so all four elements appear in one statement about the rate rather than about the amount; BC-ERR-04001 and BC-ERR-04002 are absent, and where the value is a rate of a rate the phrasing says so.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The quantity is named and the instant, the direction, or the units is missing, BC-ERR-04002 and BC-ERR-99027; the 2013 Q1 part A distinctions separate a correct value with an interpretation lacking the instant, which is a communication gap, from an interpretation describing the amount, which misreads the order of differentiation.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The value being interpreted is a function value rather than a derivative value, a gap at BC-SKL-04003 and BC-PRQ-04008 rather than a wording gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-04001 (a rate sentence is about how fast, not how much). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-04001 (assembling the units to close the sentence).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a numerical value of a derivative in a modelled situation, write a statement naming the quantity, the instant at which the rate holds, whether the quantity is increasing or decreasing, and the units.
skills.description_plain: Say what the number means, naming the quantity, the instant, the direction, and the units.
skills.name: Write a sentence interpreting a derivative value in context
skills.notation: interpretation with units

common_confusions: BC-MIS-04017 (behaviour claimed from sampled inputs)
BC-MIS-04005 (direction language dropped in favour of speed language)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-04004 (the analysis points attach to the communicated conclusion over the interval, not to the chart)
adaptive.mastered_if: The sign of the velocity is given on each subinterval determined by its zeros, and a sentence says what those signs mean for the direction of motion across the whole interval named in the prompt, so a sign chart is accompanied by its reading; BC-ERR-04011 is absent, and where two particles are compared both analyses are combined into one interval.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A correct sign chart or number line appears with no sentence stating what it shows, BC-ERR-04011 with signal BC-SIG-04008; the 2025 report records that responses in this state did not earn the analysis points even with correct signs.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The zeros that partition the interval were never found, a gap at BC-SKL-04011; or direction is being read from the wrong function, BC-SKL-04009.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-04017 (the conclusion has to hold on every subinterval). Procedural failure: BC-ERR-04011 (writing the sentence that reads the chart).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a velocity function on a stated interval, present the sign of the velocity on each subinterval determined by its zeros, in words or in a chart whose reading is stated, so that the conclusion covers the whole interval.
skills.description_plain: Report the sign on every part of the interval, not just at sampled times.
skills.name: Communicate a sign analysis of velocity across a whole interval
skills.notation: sign chart with a stated conclusion

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05013 (restating the conclusion is treated as a reason)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05008 (intervals of increase or decrease that must be supported by the sign of the named derivative)
adaptive.mastered_if: The written reason names f prime as the object whose sign is being read and names f as the object that rises or falls, so a sentence such as f is increasing on that interval because f prime is positive there stands on its own without the reader having to guess the subject. The naming holds when the derivative is supplied as a plotted graph under BC-REP-04 as well as when it is supplied by formula, and neither BC-ERR-05018 (a reason whose subject is only the function or the graph) nor BC-ERR-99001 (it, the slope or the graph left as an unnamed subject) appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Intervals come out right and the supporting sentence still says the function or the graph rather than f prime, which is BC-SIG-05014 and matches BC-ERR-05018. A second intermediate state shows in the BC-FRQ-2013-Q4-C and BC-FRQ-2014-Q3-B scoring, where intervals earn their point while the reason is phrased about the function rather than the plotted derivative, or about the accumulation function rather than the integrand, so the reason point falls on a referent failure alone. In BC-FRQ-2013-Q1-C the comparison with the processing rate is made and the conclusion sentence is never written, which is the same gap in communication rather than in analysis.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: When the intervals themselves are wrong, the failure sits at BC-SKL-05016 (building a sign chart on critical points and domain boundaries) and not at the wording. The tell is that the sentence names f prime correctly and confidently while the interval endpoints do not match the zeros and undefined points of f prime, so naming is intact and the sign analysis under it is not.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05013 (a second sentence saying the conclusion again is taken for a justification) carries the conceptual failure. A procedural failure, where the student knows a name is required and writes the interval work without ever labelling which curve was plotted, points instead to BC-SKL-05016 (the sign chart, where the names are assigned).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: State that f increases on an interval because f' is positive there, naming f explicitly rather than referring to the function or the graph.
skills.description_plain: Write the reason in words, naming the function whose derivative has that sign.
skills.name: Justify increase or decrease from the sign of the named derivative

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08006 (the integral of a rate read as the amount of the quantity)
BC-SKL-08016 (writing the integral expression alone, without the initial amount)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08004 (a known amount at one time and a modelled rate, so the initial term is the scored difference)
adaptive.mastered_if: The amount at time b is written as the given amount at time a plus the definite integral of the rate from a to b, with the differential and both limits present, and the number reported answers how much is present rather than how much it changed; neither BC-ERR-08011 nor BC-ERR-08012 appears, and the value moves when the initial amount is changed.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The accumulation integral is correct and is reported without the initial amount, which is BC-ERR-08011 and the state in BC-SIG-08004; or the net change is computed and offered as the answer to a question asking what is present at that time, which is BC-ERR-08012.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The initial value plus accumulated change form is not reproduced even for a simple rate, which is BC-SKL-06037; a rate function misread as the amount itself in the stem is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08006 (the integral as change in the quantity) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-06037 (assembling the total from initial value and accumulation) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: isolated by BC-QA-08006
skills.description_formal: Given an initial amount at time a and a rate function, write and evaluate the amount at time b as the initial amount plus the definite integral of the rate from a to b.
skills.description_plain: Write the later amount as the starting amount plus the integral of the rate.
skills.name: Express the amount at a time as an initial amount plus an integral

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05008 (a zero derivative read as the definition of a turning point, so no sign change is checked)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05006 (absolute extremum by the candidates test with a justification covering the whole interval)
BC-QA-05007 (critical point located and classified for a function given through a differential equation or an accumulation function)
adaptive.mastered_if: The equation f prime of x equal to zero appears on the page before any solution is listed, the solutions are screened against the domain of f so that an input where the function itself is undefined is dropped, and the surviving inputs are called critical points. This holds whether f is given by a formula as in BC-REP-01 or through a differential equation or accumulation relation where the derivative must first be written from the given relation, and neither BC-ERR-05009, zeros listed without the derivative condition shown, nor BC-ERR-05010, solutions outside the domain kept, is present.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Correct critical inputs arrive with no equation behind them, which is BC-SIG-05007 exactly and which forfeits the considering the derivative equal to zero point under the candidates test. Other intermediate states keep an input where the derivative expression vanishes but the function is undefined, that being BC-ERR-05010, or find the critical input and then never evaluate the function there, the location-versus-value split recorded in the 2013 and 2021 scoring commentary. A further partial state solves the equation correctly and then asserts an extremum with a purely local sign change, leaving the uniqueness statement out.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: When the derivative is correct but the algebra of setting a factored or rational expression to zero collapses, the failure is BC-PRQ-05001 and not this skill, recognisable by a lost root or a denominator zero mistaken for a solution. When every candidate the algebra produced is kept including one outside the domain, BC-PRQ-05003 is the gap, and where the derivative itself cannot be written from an accumulation relation the shortfall sits in BC-SKL-06021.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05008 (a critical point is a candidate, not a verdict) for the conceptual failure. Where the concept is intact and only the written setup or the domain screen is missing, the target is BC-PRQ-05001 together with BC-PRQ-05003.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Solve f'(x) equal to zero and retain the solutions that lie in the domain of f, presenting the equation rather than only the solutions.
skills.description_plain: Solve the derivative equal to zero and keep the solutions in the domain.
skills.name: Determine critical points where the first derivative equals zero

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05016 (the candidates are the critical points only, so endpoints never compete)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05006 (absolute extremum by the candidates test with a global justification)
adaptive.mastered_if: Every entry of the candidate table carries a computed value of f, whether the value comes from substituting into a formula, reading a given table, or accumulating signed area under a plotted f prime, and the endpoint entries are evaluated with the same care as the interior critical inputs. Values agree with the supplied information, areas under the axis are subtracted rather than added, and BC-ERR-05027, a wrong value at one candidate, does not appear anywhere in the table.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The candidate list is complete and one evaluated entry contradicts the given information, which is BC-SIG-05019. The failure sits in BC-ERR-05027, a single mis-evaluated candidate, and it strips the justification point outright under the 2023 guideline even though the rest of the table stands. The 2013 Q4 commentary describes the same shape, with candidates correctly listed and their values computed wrongly from the plotted areas.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: When the list being evaluated has no endpoint entries in it at all, the break is upstream in BC-SKL-05024, assembling the candidate list from critical points and both endpoints, rather than in the evaluation. A second upstream tell is BC-PRQ-06005, where f(t) and f prime of t are not held apart, so the response evaluates the rate function at the candidate instead of the accumulated amount.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-PRQ-06005 (function notation and evaluation at a stated input) carries the conceptual failure, where a function is not distinguished from its value. Procedural failure, meaning the table is right in form and one number is wrong, points instead to BC-SKL-05024 and to the area bookkeeping behind BC-ERR-05027.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Compute f at each entry of the candidate list, from a formula, from a table, or by accumulating area under a plotted derivative.
skills.description_plain: Work out the function value at each candidate input.
skills.name: Evaluate the function at every candidate

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05018 (a local test treated as settling a global question)
BC-MIS-05017 (the last candidate computed is taken to be the extremum)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05006 (absolute extremum by the candidates test with a global justification)
adaptive.mastered_if: An argument covering the whole interval appears, not a sign change at one input. Evaluations or equivalent reasoning are shown for each candidate, both endpoints are among them, no extra inputs are declared, and a comparison sentence names which candidate beats the rest. The 2023 guideline withholds the justification point from any response that fails to consider both endpoints, and the 2025 exactness rule withholds it for surplus candidates, so BC-ERR-05026 and BC-ERR-99004 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Two intermediate states show up. In BC-SIG-05021 the answer is right and the justification is a first or second derivative test at the candidate, which is BC-ERR-05029 and BC-ERR-99004, a local argument standing in for a global one. In the other, the comparison runs but the ends of the interval are never evaluated, which is BC-ERR-05026. Each leaves the answer point available and removes the justification point.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: A justification that quotes candidate values disagreeing with the given information fails upstream in BC-SKL-05025, evaluating the function at every candidate, and the tell is a well formed comparison built on a bad number. Where the comparison itself picks the wrong direction, the gap is BC-SKL-05026 instead.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05018 (a first or second derivative test believed to prove a claim about the whole interval) is the conceptual target. A response that accepts the global requirement but omits an endpoint row is procedural and points to BC-SKL-05024, assembling the candidate list from critical points and both endpoints.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Present evaluations or reasoning for each candidate, including both endpoints and no additional inputs, and state the comparison that selects the extremum.
skills.description_plain: Show the comparison over all candidates, endpoints included, and nothing else.
skills.name: Write a global justification covering every candidate

common_confusions: BC-MIS-09019 (the limits of a polar area taken as the whole interval of the figure)
BC-MIS-09007 (any interval containing the curve assumed to give its area)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-09013 (the region is bounded by where two curves meet, so the crossing angles are the limits)
adaptive.mastered_if: The two radius functions are set equal, the resulting equation is solved across the stated interval, every solution is accounted for against the figure, and the pair that bounds the region is selected as the limits; neither BC-ERR-09037 nor BC-ERR-09038 appears, and the chosen angles are stored rather than transcribed as short decimals.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The equation is solved and only one of the two intersection angles is found, so one limit is taken from elsewhere, which is BC-ERR-09038; or both are found and the limits used are the ends of the displayed angle range, which is BC-ERR-09037 and the not mastered state in BC-SIG-09013.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The trigonometric equation setting the radii equal is not solved on the interval, which is BC-PRQ-08001; reading sine and cosine values as solutions on a stated interval is BC-PRQ-09002.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-09019 (what determines the limits of a polar area) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08001 (solving the equation of the two radii) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Set the two radius functions equal on the stated interval, solve for every angle at which they agree, and select the pair that bounds the region.
skills.description_plain: Set the two radius expressions equal and solve for the angles.
skills.name: Find the intersection angles of two polar curves

common_confusions: BC-MIS-09018 (the area between polar curves built from the difference of the radii)
BC-MIS-09019 (the limits taken as the whole interval of the figure)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-09013 (inside one curve and outside another, so the roles decide the sign of the result)
adaptive.mastered_if: Both radius functions are evaluated at an angle interior to the interval and the larger value names the outer curve, that assignment then placing the outer radius first in the difference of squares; the integrand is nonnegative on the interval, and BC-ERR-09039 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The comparison at the interior angle is carried out correctly and the integrand still subtracts the square of the outer radius from the square of the inner one, which is BC-ERR-09039 and returns a negative value.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Evaluating each radius function at an angle is itself unreliable because the trigonometric values are misread, which is BC-PRQ-09002.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-09018 (the ring of sectors as a difference of two sector areas) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-09041 (placing the assignment into the integrand) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Evaluate both radius functions at an interior angle of the interval and assign the outer and inner roles accordingly.
skills.description_plain: Test one angle in the interval to see which radius is larger.
skills.name: Determine which polar curve is outer on an angle interval

common_confusions: BC-MIS-09018 (the area between polar curves built from the difference of the radii)
BC-MIS-09017 (a polar area read as an integral of the curve itself)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-09013 (two radii between crossing angles, where the squaring order and the one half are both scored)
adaptive.mastered_if: The area between the curves is written as one half the definite integral of the square of the outer radius minus the square of the inner radius, each radius squared before the subtraction, with the intersection angles as limits; neither BC-ERR-09040 nor BC-ERR-09035 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The limits and the roles are right and the integrand is the square of the difference of the radii, which is BC-ERR-09040; or the difference of squares is correct and the factor of one half is missing, which is BC-ERR-09035 and the doubled value in BC-SIG-09012.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The outer and inner radii were never assigned by comparison at an interior angle, so the order in the integrand is arbitrary, which is BC-SKL-09040; reading which function is which in the stem is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-09018 (the difference of sector areas against a sector of the difference) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-09040 (fixing outer and inner before squaring) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts

skills.description_plain: Write one half the integral of outer squared minus inner squared.

common_confusions: BC-MIS-09008 (a calculator result treated as standing without its expression)
BC-MIS-09019 (the limits taken as the whole interval of the figure)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-09013 (the crossing angles are not exact values, so storing them protects the third decimal place)
adaptive.mastered_if: The area integral between the two curves is evaluated with technology using the stored intersection angles, the expression appears on the page as its own line, and the value is reported to three places after the decimal point; neither BC-ERR-09006 nor BC-ERR-09018 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The integral is correct and the intersection angles are reused as short decimals, so the reported area moves in the third place, which is BC-ERR-09006; or the work runs an expression in the variable into its numerical value in one chain of equalities, which is BC-ERR-09018.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The value is right and reported to the wrong number of places or rounded against the convention, which is BC-PRQ-08006 rather than an evaluation gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-09008 (the written integral as the scored object) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08006 (evaluating from stored angles) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts

common_confusions: BC-MIS-09015 (the slope of a polar curve taken to be the derivative of r)
BC-MIS-09013 (the polar radius treated as a Cartesian coordinate)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-09009 (dr/dtheta is available in the same question, so offering it as the slope is visible)
adaptive.mastered_if: The Cartesian coordinates are written as r times cosine theta and r times sine theta, each differentiated with the product rule so both the derivative of r and the derivative of the trigonometric factor appear, and the slope is the quotient of dy/dtheta by dx/dtheta; neither BC-ERR-09031 nor BC-ERR-09032 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The conversion to Cartesian form is made and the product rule is applied to only one factor, or the two derivatives are multiplied together, which is BC-ERR-09032; or the derivative of r is reported as the slope of the tangent line, which is BC-ERR-09031.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The product rule on a product of two differentiable factors is not available, which is BC-SKL-02036; the cosine and sine conversion itself is BC-PRQ-09002.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-09015 (why the slope requires the Cartesian components) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-02036 (the product rule on each component) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts

common_confusions: BC-MIS-09010 (the integral of a velocity component read as the coordinate)
BC-SKL-09022 (the backwards in time case of the same accumulation)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-09005 (a coordinate at a second time from one known position, so the initial term and the notation are both scored)
adaptive.mastered_if: The coordinate at the requested time is written as the known coordinate at the other time plus the definite integral of the matching velocity component between the two times, with the substitution shown as its own step and the value reported to the stated accuracy; neither BC-ERR-09020 nor BC-ERR-09018 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The accumulation integral is correct and reported as the coordinate with the known value omitted, which is BC-ERR-09020 and the state in BC-SIG-09006; or the answer is complete and written as one equality running from an expression in t to a number, which is BC-ERR-09018.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The one dimensional version, position from an initial position and velocity, is not available, which is BC-SKL-08009; reading which component of the position is known is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-09010 (the integral as change in the coordinate) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-08009 (the same accumulation on a line) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Evaluate a coordinate of the position at a time as the known coordinate at another time plus the definite integral of the corresponding velocity component between the two times.

common_confusions: BC-MIS-09009 (a vector answer treated as a pair of numbers with no structure)
BC-MIS-09001 (the parameter treated as the horizontal coordinate)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-09004 (vector notation is required in the answer)
BC-QA-09005 (the stem gives components separately, so the two notations meet in one question)
adaptive.mastered_if: A parametric description is rewritten as a vector valued function and back again with the horizontal component staying first in both forms, and quantities named in one notation are matched to their counterparts in the other; BC-ERR-09017 is absent across the conversion.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The conversion is carried out and the components are transposed, or the vector form is written with no labels so the order cannot be checked, which is BC-ERR-09017.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The vector and ordered pair notation is not read in the first place, so there is nothing to convert, which is BC-PRQ-09001.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-09009 (what the two notations describe) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-09001 (writing the vector form correctly) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Rewrite a parametric description of a path as a vector-valued function and back, preserving the order of the components.
skills.description_plain: The same motion can be written as a pair of equations or as one vector.
skills.name: Convert between parametric equations and vector-valued notation

common_confusions: BC-MIS-09009 (a vector answer treated as a pair of numbers with no structure)
BC-SKL-09001 (component differentiation in parametric notation, the same operation)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-09004 (a vector must be reported, so labelling and order are part of the answer)
adaptive.mastered_if: Each component of the vector valued function is differentiated with respect to the variable and the result is presented as one vector, with the horizontal component first and the vertical second or both labelled; the pair is not left as two loose numbers, so BC-ERR-09017 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Both component derivatives are computed correctly and presented as two unlabelled numbers with no order made clear, or in the reverse order, which is BC-ERR-09017.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The vector or ordered pair notation in the stem is not read, so which expression is the horizontal component is unknown, which is BC-PRQ-09001.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-09009 (a vector as one object with ordered components) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-09001 (reading and writing the vector notation) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a vector-valued function, compute the derivative of each component with respect to the variable and present the result as a vector.
skills.description_plain: Differentiate each coordinate on its own.

common_confusions: BC-MIS-09009 (a vector answer treated as a pair of numbers with no structure)
BC-SKL-09017 (the acceleration vector, one derivative further)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-09004 (a vector at a stated time, so order and evaluation are both scored)
adaptive.mastered_if: The position vector is differentiated component by component and both derivatives are evaluated at the stated time, the velocity reported as an ordered or labelled pair to the required accuracy; stored values feed the evaluation, so neither BC-ERR-09017 nor BC-ERR-09006 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Both velocity components are correct and appear as two numbers with no labels or in reversed order, which is BC-ERR-09017; or the components are correctly labelled and one is truncated before a later use, which is BC-ERR-09006.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The ordered pair notation for position in the plane is not read, so the components are not separated before differentiating, which is BC-PRQ-09001.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-09009 (the velocity as one vector) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-09001 (the notation the answer is written in) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Evaluate the derivative of the position vector at a time and present both components, labelled or ordered.
skills.description_plain: Report both components of the derivative of position at that time.

common_confusions: BC-MIS-02001 (a difference reported as a rate)
BC-SKL-02015 (the units, which are scored independently of the value)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-02001 (a contextual table where the supporting work must show both a difference and a quotient)
adaptive.mastered_if: The two tabulated inputs the question names, or the pair bracketing the point, are used (BC-ERR-02004 absent), the difference of the function values and the division by the difference of the inputs both appear in the work (BC-ERR-02001 absent), and the quotient is carried through to a number (BC-ERR-02002 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The difference quotient is set up from the right rows and never evaluated, which is BC-SIG-02002 and, in the 2025 and 2026 guidelines, leaves the answer point unearned, or the values are subtracted and not divided, which is BC-SIG-02001.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The rows chosen do not bracket the input or ignore the interval named in the prompt, which is a selection gap at BC-SKL-02016, and inability to form an average rate at all is BC-SKL-01001.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-02001 (why the division is part of the answer) for the conceptual failure; BC-SKL-02016 (choosing the rows the question specifies) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given selected values of a function, approximate the derivative at an input by the average rate of change over an interval from the table that contains or abuts that input, showing the difference and the quotient.
skills.description_plain: Use the two tabulated inputs on either side of the point and divide the change in the values by the change in the inputs.
skills.name: Estimate a derivative at a point from a table using a difference quotient

common_confusions: BC-MIS-02001 (attention on the arithmetic rather than on which values enter it)
BC-SKL-02014 (computing the estimate once the rows are chosen)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-02001 (the supporting work must use the values the question specifies, so a wider interval loses the point)
adaptive.mastered_if: The interval named in the question is used when one is named, and otherwise the pair of tabulated inputs immediately either side of the point of interest, with the chosen rows identified before any arithmetic and wider intervals rejected (BC-ERR-02004 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A bracketing pair is chosen where the question named a different interval, or a pair adjacent on one side only is used, so the rule for selection is partly held.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The rows cannot be sorted relative to the target input, which is a table reading gap at BC-SKL-01016.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-02001 (which pair of values a rate at a point is built from) for the conceptual failure; BC-SKL-01016 (reading rows on each side of a target) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Identify which two tabulated inputs the estimate must use, following the interval named in the question when one is named and otherwise the pair that brackets the point of interest.
skills.description_plain: Choose the tabulated inputs the question names, or the pair that brackets the point.
skills.name: Select the interval of a table that supports the requested estimate

common_confusions: BC-MIS-02008 (units treated as optional decoration)
BC-SKL-02003 (interpreting an average rate, which carries the same compound units)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-02001 (units are scored independently of the numerical estimate, so a correct value with wrong units is visible)
adaptive.mastered_if: The units are given as the units of the modelled quantity divided by the units of the independent variable, in compound form, and they are correct for a rate of a rate where the tabulated quantity is itself a rate; the units are produced whether or not a value accompanies them and are not copied from the table header (BC-ERR-02003 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The numerical estimate is correct but the units given are those of the modelled quantity, which is BC-SIG-02003 and BC-ERR-02003, or one level of the rate is lost so a second derivative carries first derivative units.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The average rate underlying the estimate cannot be formed, so there is no quotient whose denominator can be read for units, which is a gap at BC-SKL-01001.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-02008 (what the denominator of the quotient measures) for the conceptual failure; BC-SKL-01001 (forming the quotient whose units are being named) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Attach to an estimated derivative the units of the modelled quantity divided by the units of the independent variable, whether or not a numerical value accompanies them.
skills.description_plain: Give the units as the units of the quantity per unit of the independent variable.
skills.name: State the units of an estimated derivative in context

common_confusions: BC-MIS-04003 (units as an afterthought)
BC-SKL-04014 (differentiating a model rather than estimating from a table)
BC-MIS-04017 (sampled values taken to settle behaviour across an interval)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-04002 (the answer with supporting difference and quotient and the units are scored as two points)
adaptive.mastered_if: The two tabulated values the named interval determines are selected, a difference of function values over a difference of inputs is written out, the quotient is evaluated, and the units are attached; both the difference and the quotient are visible, which is what the 2025 rubric requires beyond the setup expression, and BC-ERR-04004 and BC-ERR-04001 are absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A single quotient or a bare number appears with no visible subtraction of tabulated values, BC-ERR-04004 with signal BC-SIG-04003; or the quotient is correct and unaccompanied by units, BC-ERR-04001, which the 2013 Q3 part A commentary records as a whole point lost to communication.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Rows outside the named interval are used, so the bracketing requirement is not held, a table reading gap at BC-PRQ-04004; or the units cannot be assembled, a gap at BC-SKL-04001.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-PRQ-04004 (the average rate over an interval approximates the instantaneous rate inside it). Procedural failure: BC-ERR-04004 (writing the difference as well as the quotient).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given tabulated values of a quantity, approximate the derivative at an interior input by the average rate of change over an interval the prompt names, presenting a difference and a quotient and attaching the units.
skills.description_plain: Use the difference quotient over the surrounding interval and report it with units.
skills.name: Approximate a derivative from an average rate of change with units
skills.notation: difference quotient from a table

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05001 (hypotheses treated as decoration, with the conclusion taken to be the whole theorem)
BC-MIS-05002 (writing the name of a theorem taken to complete the argument)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05001 (a differentiable function with selected values supplied, and the response must decide whether some interior input has a named instantaneous rate of change and justify it)
adaptive.mastered_if: Given that f is differentiable on an interval, the written work converts that into continuity explicitly, saying that f is continuous on [a,b] because it is differentiable there, and separately confirms differentiability on (a,b). The same conversion holds from a table, from a graph, and from a verbal hypothesis. BC-ERR-05002 (continuity asserted without being drawn from the given differentiability) is absent, as is BC-ERR-99008 (hypotheses skipped before the conclusion).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A bare sentence that f is continuous, with nothing behind it, is the characteristic middle state and it is exactly BC-ERR-05002, refused by the 2025 guideline. BC-SIG-05001 catches its quieter form, right arithmetic and right answer with no hypothesis sentence at all. The 2018 Q4 part B behaviour of differentiability never converted to continuity marks the same gap, and the 2021 Q4 part D behaviour of a theorem asserted with no hypotheses sits alongside it.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: If the learner cannot list what the Mean Value Theorem requires in the first place, the failure belongs to BC-SKL-05001 rather than to the verification step, and the tell is a response that verifies some property of f that the theorem never asked for.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05002 (a justification has to convince a reader who has never heard of the theorem); a procedural failure, meaning the implication is known but never written down, points instead to BC-SKL-05001 (stating the hypotheses)

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a statement that a function is differentiable, state that it is therefore continuous on the closed interval, and confirm differentiability on the open interval.
skills.description_plain: Check the given information really does supply continuity and differentiability.
skills.name: Verify that the hypotheses hold on the given interval

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05003 (average rate of change read as the average of the endpoint values)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05001 (a differentiable function with selected values supplied, and the response must decide whether some interior input has a named instantaneous rate of change and justify it)
BC-QA-05002 (a function and a closed interval given, with the interior input where the instantaneous rate equals the average rate required)
adaptive.mastered_if: The quotient f(b) minus f(a) over b minus a is formed in that order, with the interval length as the denominator, and the value carries the units of a rate rather than the units of f. The learner produces it from a formula, from a table of values, and from a graph, and accepts the equivalent form of an integral of f prime over the interval divided by the interval length. Neither BC-ERR-05003 (endpoint values averaged, subtraction reversed, or division by the wrong difference) appears in any representation.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The setup is right on a formula but collapses on a table, or the subtraction order flips so the sign of the rate is wrong, both of them forms of BC-ERR-05003. The 2021 Q4 part D behaviour of a difference quotient with the wrong interval length is the arithmetic-setup version, and the 2025 Q1 part B behaviour of the average value of the function substituted for the average rate of change is the other, where the right machinery is aimed at the wrong quantity.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Reporting the mean of the two endpoint outputs, which BC-SIG-05002 flags, is a failure of BC-PRQ-05008 (average rate of change as a difference quotient) and not of this skill, and asking for the units of the computed number separates the two. Misreading f(t) or an evaluation at a stated input instead points at BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05003 (a rate is a change in output divided by a change in input, checkable against the units of f prime); a procedural failure in the subtraction or the denominator points instead to BC-PRQ-05008 (forming the difference quotient)

skills.assessability_basis: isolated by BC-QA-05002
skills.description_formal: Evaluate the quotient of f(b) minus f(a) over b minus a for the stated interval, from a formula, a table, or a graph.
skills.description_plain: Work out the change in output divided by the change in input across the interval.
skills.name: Compute the average rate of change over a closed interval

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05002 (writing the name of a theorem taken to complete the argument)
BC-MIS-05004 (an existence theorem read as naming the input rather than asserting one exists)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05001 (a differentiable function with selected values supplied, and the response must decide whether some interior input has a named instantaneous rate of change and justify it)
adaptive.mastered_if: Three things sit in the same argument. The hypotheses are on the page, the average rate of change is computed, and the response then says yes, there is a c strictly between a and b with f prime of c equal to that rate, naming the Mean Value Theorem. The subject of every sentence is named, so f and f prime are never left to a pronoun. BC-ERR-05004 (arithmetic done but no affirmative answer and no theorem), BC-ERR-05002 (continuity not drawn from differentiability), and BC-ERR-99001 (vague referent such as it or the graph) are all absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Arithmetic and conclusion agree while the theorem named concerns values of the function rather than values of the derivative, which is BC-SIG-05003. Other middle states compute everything and stop short of the word yes or of the theorem's name, the shape of BC-ERR-05004, matching the 2013 Q3 part B behaviour of an average rate correct with the theorem unnamed and the 2018 Q4 part B behaviour of the same gap.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: An unsupported continuity claim under the conclusion is BC-SKL-05002 failing rather than this one, and a wrong value for the average rate, with the existence sentence written correctly around it, belongs to BC-SKL-05003.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05004 (existence is asserted, location is not); a procedural failure, where the affirmative sentence or the theorem name is simply missing from otherwise sound work, points instead to BC-ERR-05004 (writing the answer with its justification)

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: From the verified hypotheses and the computed average rate of change, assert the existence of c strictly between the endpoints with f'(c) equal to that rate, naming the theorem.
skills.description_plain: State that some interior point has instantaneous rate equal to the average rate, and say why.
skills.name: Conclude that a point with the average rate exists on the open interval

common_confusions: BC-MIS-02006 (differentiability and continuity treated as the same property)
BC-MIS-02005 (a hypothesis assumed to be supplied by the setting)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-02004 (continuity must be derived from a stated differentiability inside a larger argument, where a bare continuity claim does not score)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response states that differentiability at a point gives continuity at that point, keeps the implication one directional, and notes that a point outside the domain of f is outside the domain of f prime, so continuity is never asserted without the differentiability reason (BC-ERR-02011 absent) and differentiability is never inferred from continuity (BC-ERR-02012 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The implication is stated in the correct direction but continuity is then used in an argument without the reason attached, so the fact is known and not deployed.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The three conditions of continuity cannot be stated, so there is nothing for the implication to deliver, which is a gap at BC-SKL-01043.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-02006 (a function continuous at a point with no derivative there) for the conceptual failure; BC-SKL-01043 (the conditions of continuity) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: State that if a function is differentiable at a point then it is continuous at that point, and that a point outside the domain of f is outside the domain of f prime.
skills.description_plain: Say that having a derivative at a point forces continuity there.
skills.name: State that differentiability at a point implies continuity at that point

common_confusions: BC-MIS-02005 (the stated context taken to discharge the hypothesis)
BC-MIS-01010 (restating a definition offered as a reason)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-02004 (a stated differentiability must be converted to continuity in writing before a theorem is used)
adaptive.mastered_if: Inside an argument that needs continuity, the response writes that the function is continuous because it is differentiable, drawing the differentiability from the stem, and then uses that continuity as the hypothesis of the theorem or limit step being applied (BC-ERR-02011 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The argument proceeds correctly from continuity but never says that continuity follows from differentiability, which is BC-SIG-02007 and, under the 2025 and 2026 guidelines, loses the point that requires the reason while leaving the following step eligible.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The implication itself is not held, so continuity is asserted or run backwards, which is a BC-SKL-02019 gap, and inability to state a continuity hypothesis before a theorem is BC-SKL-01065.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-02005 (what in the question establishes continuity) for the conceptual failure; BC-SKL-02019 (the implication being invoked) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: In an argument that requires continuity as a hypothesis, derive it from a stated differentiability property and record that reason explicitly.
skills.description_plain: Write that the function is continuous because it is differentiable, as the reason inside a larger argument.
skills.name: Use differentiability to justify continuity in a written argument

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06002 (the endpoint convention treated as cosmetic)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06001 (Riemann sum from a table with over or under estimate reasoning)
adaptive.mastered_if: The sample point is the centre of each subinterval, found as the average of the two partition points, and it is evaluated in f whether f arrives as a formula, as a graph to read, or as a table that already lists midpoint values. Each midpoint value is multiplied by its own subinterval width and the products are added, and the learner treats the midpoint choice as a different sample rule from left or right rather than as a label, so the value differs from the left and right sums on the same partition.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Endpoint sample values are used where midpoints were named, which BC-FRQ-2013-Q3-C and BC-FRQ-2026-Q1-B both record as a misread convention, and in 2026 a completely correct left or right sum still reaches the value point by sg-26:3. A second partial state is the sum computed correctly with the division by the interval length omitted, so an average is reported as a total.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Midpoints taken as the average of the endpoints but widths assumed common across an uneven partition is BC-PRQ-06012, and the tell is a correct midpoint list paired with one repeated width.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06002 (different sample points give different sums) for the conceptual failure. When the midpoint rule is held and the arithmetic of the widths is not, the target is BC-PRQ-06012 (nonuniform subinterval widths).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a function represented graphically, numerically, or analytically and a partition, approximate the integral as the sum over subintervals of f at the midpoint of the subinterval multiplied by its width.
skills.description_plain: Use the value at the centre of each subinterval times its width and add.
skills.name: Compute a midpoint Riemann sum

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06001 (Riemann sum from a table with over or under estimate reasoning)
adaptive.mastered_if: No table is supplied and the learner builds one. The interval length divided by the number of equal subintervals gives the width, the partition points are listed, and the sample values are either evaluated from the formula or read off the graph at those inputs before any product is written. The assembled sum shows one product per subinterval under whichever rule was named, left, right, midpoint, or trapezoidal, and the factor count matches the subinterval count.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The width is found correctly and the sample inputs drift, so values are read at the wrong partition points, or the requested rule is replaced by a familiar one. BC-FRQ-2013-Q3-C records endpoint samples used where midpoints were named, BC-FRQ-2015-Q3-B and BC-FRQ-2022-Q4-C record left endpoints used where the stem named right, and BC-FRQ-2021-Q1-B records the integrand itself misread, with density values summed and the radius factor dropped, which leaves the sum rule intact.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Evaluating f at a stated input, or telling f from f prime and from f of g of x, is BC-PRQ-06005, and the tell is that the partition and the width are correct while the values placed against them are not the function's values at those inputs.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-PRQ-06005 (function notation and evaluation at a stated input) for the conceptual failure, since the sample values must be produced rather than copied. Where the values are right and the assembly is not, the target is BC-QA-06001 (multiply each value by the width of its subinterval, then sum).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a function presented graphically or analytically together with a number of equal subintervals, determine the subinterval width, obtain the required function values, and assemble the Riemann or trapezoidal sum.
skills.description_plain: Read or evaluate the needed function values yourself, then build the sum.
skills.name: Compute a Riemann sum for a function given by a graph or a formula

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06014 (average value and accumulated amount treated as the same quantity)
BC-MIS-06015 (average of a function and average rate of change treated as the same quantity)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06007 (average value of a function over an interval, often with an interpretation in context)
adaptive.mastered_if: One over (b minus a) times the integral from a to b of f(x) dx is written as a single expression, the division by the interval length is visible, and the value follows at the required accuracy. Asked to interpret the result, the learner says average over the interval rather than total accumulated, and gives units of f rather than units of f per unit input. The object being averaged is the function the question named, not its derivative, and a trigonometric integrand is evaluated in radian mode.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The integral is right and the division is missing, which is BC-SIG-06016 with BC-ERR-06016 (the integral reported as the average value with no division by the interval length), confirmed by asking for the units since rate times input units expose the omission. A displayed average value expression described as a total is BC-ERR-06030 (average value expression interpreted as a total), which costs only the interpretation point. Communication failures also sit here, where the correct value appears but the integral is written as equal to the average, earning one of the two points in the 2023 Q1 part C pattern. Answers rounded to the wrong number of places, and values matching degree mode under BC-ERR-06032, are reporting and calculator failures rather than formula failures.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: A difference of function values divided by the interval length, with no integral anywhere, is BC-SIG-06017 with BC-ERR-06017 (average rate of change computed where average value was requested), which is a reading gap ahead of this skill. If the formula is right and the integral itself cannot be evaluated, the gap is BC-SKL-06034 (evaluation by antidifferentiation and endpoint substitution), with the tell of a correct quotient wrapped around a wrong integral.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06014 (separating the integral from the integral divided by the interval length) for the conceptual failure; procedural failure points instead to BC-SKL-06034 (evaluating the integral before the division)

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given f on [a,b], compute the average value of f as one over (b minus a) times the integral from a to b of f(x) dx.
skills.description_plain: Divide the integral by the length of the interval.
skills.name: Compute the average value of a function on an interval

common_confusions: BC-MIS-02010 (the exponent move applied to transcendental functions)
BC-SKL-02025 (the power rule, where the variable is the base)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-02007 (an expression containing the natural exponential, where a lowered exponent is immediately visible)
adaptive.mastered_if: The derivative of the natural exponential is written as the natural exponential itself, with the exponent left intact rather than reduced by one (BC-ERR-02019 absent), and the response identifies that the variable sits in the exponent rather than in the base.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The rule is stated correctly for the bare exponential but a constant multiple of it is differentiated as though the constant also changed, so the transcendental rule is held and the constant multiple step is not.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Negative and fractional exponents are not handled as exponents, so the expression is pattern matched to a power, which is a gap at BC-PRQ-06002.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-02010 (which of base and exponent carries the variable) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-06002 (exponent conventions) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Write the derivative of the natural exponential function as the natural exponential function itself.
skills.description_plain: Recall that the natural exponential is its own derivative.
skills.name: Differentiate the natural exponential function

common_confusions: BC-MIS-02011 (differentiation assumed to distribute across a product, of which a constant factor is the easy case)
BC-SKL-02036 (the product rule, needed once both factors carry the variable)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-02006 (constants must be carried through a term by term differentiation)
adaptive.mastered_if: For a constant times a differentiable function the derivative is written as the constant times the derivative of the function, the constant is carried unchanged rather than differentiated, and negative constants keep their sign through the step.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The constant is pulled out correctly but is also applied a second time, or a negative constant loses its sign, so the structure holds and the coefficient is wrong.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Prime and Leibniz forms are mixed so the expression being differentiated is ambiguous, which is a gap at BC-PRQ-02004.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-02011 (why a constant factor may be pulled out while a variable factor may not) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-02004 (writing the derivative unambiguously) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: For a constant times a differentiable function, write the derivative as the constant times the derivative of the function.
skills.description_plain: Pull the constant out and differentiate what remains.
skills.name: Apply the constant multiple rule

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05011 (questions about the function answered by reading whatever curve is drawn, even when the drawn curve is a derivative or an integrand)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05008 (intervals of increase or decrease supported by the sign of the named derivative)
BC-QA-05009 (relating the graphs of a function and its first two derivatives and identifying which is which)
adaptive.mastered_if: Before anything is reported, the drawn curve in BC-REP-02 is labelled as f prime and f is named as the function under discussion, after which the intervals where the plotted values sit above the axis are reported as intervals on which f increases and those below as intervals on which f decreases. Rising portions of the plotted curve are kept apart from portions above the axis, so BC-ERR-05016, confusing increase of the derivative with positivity of the derivative, does not creep in, and BC-ERR-05015, answering about the drawn curve as though it were f, does not appear even when a compound condition asks about both f and f prime at once.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The intervals handed back are the ones on which the drawn curve rises, which is BC-SIG-05012 and BC-ERR-05015 together and sends every dependent part to the wrong function. Half-answers to a compound condition, such as giving where f increases while leaving out that f prime is decreasing there, and reasons phrased about f where the referent had to be f prime, sit in the same band, as does reading concavity off the sign of the plotted curve.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Trouble extracting zeros, rises and falls from a plotted curve at all is BC-PRQ-05006 rather than a referent problem, and the tell is that the reported intervals do not match the drawing regardless of which function the student thinks it shows.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05011 (naming the plotted object before reading anything off it) for the conceptual failure. When the referent is right and the trouble is above the axis versus rising, the target is BC-SKL-05041 and the separation of positivity from increase.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: From a plotted f', identify the intervals where the plotted values are positive and where they are negative, and report the corresponding behaviour of f.
skills.description_plain: Use where the derivative graph is above or below the axis.
skills.name: Read intervals of increase and decrease from the graph of the derivative

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05008 (every critical point is taken to be an extremum)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05003 (a named input classified as a relative minimum, a relative maximum or neither, with a reason)
adaptive.mastered_if: Every input offered as a possible relative extremum is a critical point, with the equation f prime of x equals zero written out and the inputs where f prime fails to exist carried across as well, and the list is defended by the statement that a relative extremum can occur only at a critical point. Nothing outside that list is tested, so BC-ERR-05020 (inputs that are neither critical points nor endpoints hunted over) does not appear, and the same list is produced whether f is given by formula under BC-REP-01 or read from a table or graph under BC-REP-02.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Correct critical inputs are listed with no equation behind them, which is BC-SIG-05007. BC-FRQ-2021-Q3-B records the same shape, a critical input asserted without the equation that produced it, and the setting of the supplied derivative equal to zero is exactly what the first point pays for. A further intermediate state is the candidate list treated as a finished answer, with each listed input assumed to be an extremum and no sign change checked.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: An incomplete or wrong list traces back to BC-SKL-05010 (critical points where f prime equals zero) when the algebra of the equation is what breaks, or to BC-SKL-05011 (critical points where f prime fails to exist) when only the zeros appear and a corner or a vertical tangent is silently dropped. The tell for the second is a list that is correct on smooth pieces and empty exactly where the derivative is undefined.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05008 (a zero derivative read as the definition of a turning point) is where the conceptual repair sits. When the principle is stated correctly and the list is still short or padded, the procedural target is BC-SKL-05010 together with BC-SKL-05011 (producing the zeros and the undefined points of f prime).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: From the critical points of f, form the list of candidate locations for relative extrema, citing that all relative extrema occur at critical points.
skills.description_plain: List the critical points as the only places a relative extremum can sit.
skills.name: Assemble the candidate relative extrema at the critical points

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05014 (the classification read off the value of the derivative rather than its change)
