diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05003 (a named input classified as a relative minimum, a relative maximum or neither, with a reason)
adaptive.mastered_if: At a critical point c the sign of f prime immediately to the left and immediately to the right is stated, and the classification follows the direction of the change, negative to positive giving a relative minimum and positive to negative giving a relative maximum. The reason cites the change of sign rather than how large f prime is nearby, so BC-ERR-05022 (classification taken from the value of the derivative instead of its change) is absent, and the direction is not inverted, so BC-ERR-05021 is absent. The same reading holds from a formula, from a table and from a plotted derivative, that is BC-REP-01, BC-REP-02 and BC-REP-03 alike.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The sign change is described accurately and the verdict names the opposite extremum, which is BC-SIG-05016 and BC-ERR-05021. BC-FRQ-2013-Q4-A and BC-FRQ-2015-Q5-B both record the sign change read in the wrong direction, and BC-FRQ-2015-Q5-B additionally records the second derivative test attempted and miscomputed where the given information did not support it cheaply, and a verdict written with no reference to the sign of the derivative at all. BC-FRQ-2023-Q4-A records a correct conclusion reached through positive before and after phrasing, which does not state the sign-change criterion.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: If the signs on either side are themselves wrong, the break is at BC-SKL-05016 (the sign chart built on critical points and domain boundaries), and the tell is a correctly stated first derivative test applied to sign information that does not match f prime. If inputs are classified that were never critical points, the break is at BC-SKL-05019 (assembling the candidates at the critical points). Where the function under examination is an accumulation function, the relevant earlier skill is BC-SKL-06023 (locating relative extrema of an accumulation function from sign changes of the integrand), and the tell is sign work done on the accumulation curve rather than on the integrand.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05014 (size or single-sided sign of f prime taken as the classification) is the conceptual target. A procedural failure, where the criterion is stated correctly and the left and right signs are read off the wrong side, points instead to BC-SKL-05016 (the sign chart).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Determine the sign of f' immediately to the left and to the right of a critical point and classify the point as a relative maximum or a relative minimum accordingly.
skills.description_plain: Decide maximum or minimum from how the derivative sign flips there.
skills.name: Classify a critical point from the sign change of the first derivative

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05013 (restating the conclusion is treated as a reason)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05003 (a named input classified as a relative minimum, a relative maximum or neither, with a reason)
adaptive.mastered_if: One sentence carries three named things, f prime as the object changing sign, the direction of that change, and the input where it happens, so a reader meets no pronoun that has to be resolved. Nothing in the sentence is a restatement of the verdict in other symbols, and the naming survives when the derivative arrives only as a plotted curve under BC-REP-04, so neither BC-ERR-05018 (the function or the graph offered as the subject) nor BC-ERR-99001 (it or the slope left unnamed) is present.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The analysis is right and the sentence says the function or the graph rather than f prime, which is BC-SIG-05014 and BC-ERR-05018. The scoring records neighbouring states, BC-FRQ-2013-Q4-A losing the single answer-with-reason point for a correct input with no sign-change reason, BC-FRQ-2015-Q4-C recording a derivative evaluated and the conclusion left unwritten, BC-FRQ-2015-Q5-B recording a verdict with no reference to the sign of the derivative, and BC-FRQ-2023-Q4-A recording a reason given about the function rather than about its derivative.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: When the direction of the sign change written into the sentence is wrong, the writing is not at fault and BC-SKL-05020 (classifying a critical point from the sign change of the first derivative) is. The tell is a fully named, well-formed sentence that asserts a relative maximum for a change from negative to positive.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05013 (a restatement of the claim mistaken for evidence) is the conceptual target. Where the student knows a feature of the given information must be cited and still writes it or the graph out of habit, the procedural target is BC-SKL-05020, whose sign-change statement supplies the names.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Produce a sentence that names f', states the direction of its sign change, and names the input, avoiding an unnamed referent such as it or the graph.
skills.description_plain: Write the reason naming which derivative changes sign and where.
skills.name: Write a first derivative test justification with an explicit referent

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05015 (the location of an extremum and its value treated as the same answer)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05006 (absolute extremum by the candidates test with a global justification)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response answers the question that was posed. A request for the absolute minimum value returns a number produced by f, and a request for where the minimum occurs returns the input, with the two written distinctly rather than folded into one statement. The 2023 guideline awarded the answer point only for the minimum value and not for the input, and a mastered response respects that split, so BC-ERR-05024 does not appear.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Correct location, wrong reported object. BC-SIG-05017 describes work that finds the extremum accurately and then reports the input where the value was wanted, or the value where the input was wanted. BC-ERR-05024 is the named failure, and it costs the answer point on its own, which the 2013 Q4 and 2022 Q3 commentaries both record as a location-versus-value confusion.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: An answer that names the wrong candidate entirely, not merely the wrong object, sits in BC-SKL-05026, comparing the candidate values and naming the absolute extremum. The sign of that earlier gap is a reported input that does not correspond to the extreme row of the candidate table.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05015 (input and extreme value collapsed into one object) is the conceptual target. When both quantities are held apart in the work and the transcription to the final line picks the wrong one, the procedural target is BC-SKL-05026, where the selected candidate and its value are paired.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Distinguish a question asking for the absolute minimum value from one asking for the input at which it occurs, and answer the one posed.
skills.description_plain: Give the value asked for, not just where it happens.
skills.name: Report the extreme value rather than only its location

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06013 (the integral of a rate read as the amount of the quantity)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06005 (net change from a rate with an initial condition supplied at one endpoint)
adaptive.mastered_if: The value at time b is written as the value at time a plus the integral from a to b of the rate, with all three of the integral, the supplied initial value, and the final number present and carried with units, which is the observation recorded in BC-SIG-06023. The same structure survives a change of representation, so a rate given as a table, as a graph, and as a formula all produce the initial value plus accumulated change form. Definite limits appear on the integral rather than an indefinite antiderivative, and when a coordinate is built from a component rate the correct component is integrated.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The reported value equals the integral alone and the supplied initial value appears nowhere, which is BC-SIG-06015 together with BC-ERR-06015 (the initial condition omitted from a net change computation), and the rubric withholds the initial condition point for exactly that response. Asking what the integral alone measures separates a forgotten initial value from a misunderstood one. Another intermediate state is the accumulation written without limits, treated as an antiderivative, so the definite form is not controlled even though the initial value is added.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: If the initial value is added but the accumulated piece is wrong, the gap is BC-SKL-06036 (computing net change from a rate), and the tell is a correct initial value plus an integral whose limits or integrand do not match the interval described. Inability to say which supplied symbol is the value and which is the rate points to BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06013 (why an initial condition is needed at all) for the conceptual failure; procedural failure points instead to BC-SKL-06036 (producing the accumulated change that gets added)

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the value of a quantity at time a and its rate of change on [a,b], compute the value at time b as the initial value plus the integral from a to b of the rate.
skills.description_plain: Add the integral of the rate to the value you were given at the start.
skills.name: Compute a final value from an initial condition and an accumulated change

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05011 (the plotted curve taken to be the function under discussion)
BC-MIS-05020 (concavity and monotonicity treated as the same property)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05004 (intervals of concavity from derivative information with a reason)
BC-QA-05009 (relating the graphs of a function and its first two derivatives)
adaptive.mastered_if: Rising and falling of the plotted f prime drive the answer, not whether that plot sits above or below the axis. Intervals on which the drawn derivative climbs are reported as concave up for the graph of f, the stated reason names the derivative increasing or decreasing rather than the function, the two curves are labelled separately, and the reported intervals stay inside the stated domain. BC-ERR-05031 and BC-ERR-05016, both forms of confusing increase with positivity, do not appear.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: BC-SIG-05023 marks the not-mastered end, where the reported intervals are exactly the stretches on which the plotted derivative lies above the axis, which is BC-ERR-05031 and its wider relative BC-ERR-05016. A milder state appears in the 2014 Q3 and 2013 Q4 commentaries, correct intervals paired with a reason phrased about the accumulation function instead of the plotted derivative, which loses the reason point alone.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: A response that cannot say where the drawn curve rises or falls, independently of any calculus claim, is short on BC-PRQ-05006, reading features of a graph including where it rises, falls, and changes bending. The tell is inconsistent reading of the picture itself, with turning points of the plot placed where the plot crosses the axis.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05020 (rising and bending upward not separated) is the conceptual target, with BC-MIS-05011 alongside it when the drawn curve is answered about directly. Procedural failure, meaning correct intervals with the reason attached to the wrong curve, points to BC-SKL-01059 and the habit of naming the referent before reading a feature off a plot.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: From a plotted f', identify the intervals where the plot is increasing and where it is decreasing, and report the graph of f as concave up or concave down there.
skills.description_plain: Read concavity off the slope behaviour of the derivative graph.
skills.name: Determine concavity from whether the derivative graph rises or falls

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05013 (restating the conclusion counted as a reason)
BC-MIS-05022 (a reason treated as complete once derivative symbols appear)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05005 (points of inflection identified with a reason tied to the given graph)
BC-QA-05004 (intervals of concavity from derivative information with a reason)
adaptive.mastered_if: The reason names the object the question supplied, for instance that the plotted f changes from decreasing to increasing at that input, or that the plotted derivative is positive and decreasing across the interval, instead of asserting a sign change of f double prime. Every subject is named rather than left as it or the graph, so BC-ERR-99001 (vague referent in a justification) is absent, and the phrasing survives both the inflection archetype BC-QA-05005 and the concavity interval archetype BC-QA-05004.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Inputs or intervals are exactly right while the reason cites a sign change of the second derivative, the BC-SIG-05027 observation and BC-ERR-05035, which loses the reason point and leaves the answer point standing. A second state names a subject but the wrong one, such as a reason phrased about the accumulation function when the plotted derivative was given, recorded in BC-FRQ-2014-Q3-B and BC-FRQ-2013-Q4-C as a referent failure, and an unnamed subject falls under BC-ERR-99001.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: When the listed inputs themselves are wrong, the reason wording is not the binding constraint and the gap sits at BC-SKL-05033 (confirming an inflection point by a sign change). The tell is that the correction to the phrasing would still leave the list unearned, and under BC-QA-05004 the reason point is not even available while the intervals are wrong.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05013 (a restated conclusion mistaken for a justification) when the failure is conceptual, and BC-MIS-05022 (symbols standing in for a statement about the given object) when the learner can say what the given plot does but still writes the sentence in derivative notation.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Phrase the reason using the named given function, for example that the plotted f changes from decreasing to increasing, rather than restating the conclusion in second derivative symbols or using an unnamed referent.
skills.description_plain: Write the reason in terms of the object the question actually supplied.
skills.name: Tie a concavity or inflection reason to the representation that was given

common_confusions: BC-MIS-03002 (one input serves both factors)
BC-ERR-03005 (a slope claimed at a corner where the derivative does not exist)
BC-SKL-03019 (reading a graph for an inverse derivative instead)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-03003 (no formula is available, so every factor has to come off the figure)
adaptive.mastered_if: Working from two graphs, the response reads the height of the inner graph at the stated input, reads the slope of the outer graph at that height, reads the slope of the inner graph at the stated input, and multiplies the two slopes; where a graph has a corner the response says the derivative does not exist there rather than reporting a slope, so BC-ERR-03003 and BC-ERR-03005 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The chain rule product is assembled correctly and both slopes are read at the same abscissa, BC-ERR-03003 with signal BC-SIG-03003; or a function value is used where a slope was needed, the distinction the 2013 Q4 part D commentary draws between a correct rule and a misread graph.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Slopes cannot be read off a single graph at all, a graph reading gap at BC-PRQ-03005 and BC-SKL-02021 rather than a composite gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-03002 (the outer slope is read at the inner output). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-02021 (reading a slope from a graph, including where it fails to exist).

skills.assessability_basis: isolated by BC-QA-03003
skills.description_formal: Given graphs of two functions, read the value of the inner function and the slopes of both graphs at the required inputs and assemble the chain rule product.
skills.description_plain: Read the inner output and the two slopes off the graphs, then multiply.
skills.name: Evaluate the derivative of a composite at a point from graphs
skills.notation: slope read from a graph

common_confusions: BC-MIS-03012 (rule chosen by the look of the expression rather than the last operation)
BC-SKL-03028 (ordering three or more rules in one problem)
BC-SKL-03025 (the same nesting with an inverse trigonometric factor)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-03009 (the structure has to be classified before the first derivative line)
BC-QA-03001 (a composite sitting inside a product or quotient)
adaptive.mastered_if: The enclosing product or quotient rule is written first and the composite factor is then differentiated with its inner derivative inside that structure, so a quotient keeps its squared denominator and a product keeps both terms; BC-ERR-03006 and BC-ERR-03002 are absent, matching the 2019 Q5 part A distinction between a denominator that was not squared and an inner derivative that was dropped.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The composite factor is differentiated correctly and the enclosing product or quotient rule never appears, BC-ERR-03006; or every rule appears and the nesting order is wrong so factors attach to the wrong pieces, signal BC-SIG-03002 and BC-SIG-03011.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The product or quotient rule is wrong on an expression with no composite in it, an elementary rule gap at BC-SKL-02036 rather than a nesting gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-03012 (the operation applied last fixes which rule opens the work). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-02036 (the product and quotient rules on their own).

skills.assessability_basis: isolated by BC-QA-03002
skills.description_formal: Given an expression that is a product or a quotient in which at least one factor is a composite, apply the product or quotient rule and the chain rule in the order the structure dictates.
skills.description_plain: Use the outer structure first, then apply the chain rule to whichever factor is itself composite.
skills.name: Combine the chain rule with the product or quotient rule
skills.notation: product rule with a composite factor

common_confusions: BC-MIS-04014 (indeterminate forms treated as numbers)
BC-MIS-04015 (the rule treated as applying to any awkward limit)
BC-SKL-04034 (stating the rule rather than verifying its hypothesis on this limit)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-04009 (the two separate limits carry a point of their own, before the rule is applied)
adaptive.mastered_if: The limit of the numerator and the limit of the denominator are presented as two separate statements, each evaluated by continuity where the function is known to be differentiable, and the form is then named as zero over zero or infinity over infinity in words; the quotient is never written equal to that form, so BC-ERR-04028 and BC-ERR-04029 are absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Both limits are known and the work writes the limit of the quotient explicitly equal to zero over zero, BC-ERR-04028, which the 2023 rubric states does not earn the first point although the rest of the part remains available; or the derivatives are taken with no separate limits shown at all, BC-ERR-04029 with signal BC-SIG-04018.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The limit of the numerator cannot be evaluated because differentiability is not being used to give continuity, a gap at BC-SKL-04038 and BC-PRQ-04008.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-04014 (zero over zero names a form, not a value). Procedural failure: BC-ERR-04028 (writing the two limits on separate lines).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a limit of a quotient, present the limit of the numerator and the limit of the denominator as two separate statements and conclude that the form is zero over zero or infinity over infinity, without writing the quotient equal to that form.
skills.description_plain: Show the limit of the top and the limit of the bottom separately, and say the form is indeterminate.
skills.name: Verify that a limit has an indeterminate form
skills.notation: two separate limits

common_confusions: BC-MIS-04015 (the rule as a general device for stubborn limits)
BC-MIS-04016 (the conclusion read as the derivative of the quotient)
BC-SKL-04033 (verifying the form on a particular limit)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-04009 (the hypothesis step is scored separately from the application)
adaptive.mastered_if: The rule is stated with both hypotheses and its conclusion, that when the limits of numerator and denominator are both zero or both infinite and the derivatives exist, the limit of the quotient equals the limit of the quotient of the derivatives; the response can say that a quotient which is not indeterminate is outside the rule, so BC-ERR-04029 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The conclusion is stated correctly and the hypotheses are omitted or treated as understood, BC-ERR-04029 with signal BC-SIG-04018, which the CED unit overview and the 2023 rubric both tie to the requirement to show that the rule applies.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The limit laws the statement depends on are not held, a gap at BC-SKL-01058 rather than a statement gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-04015 (the rule is conditional on the form). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-04033 (showing the two limits that establish the hypothesis).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: State that when the limits of the numerator and the denominator are both zero or both infinite, and the relevant derivatives exist, the limit of the quotient equals the limit of the quotient of the derivatives.
skills.description_plain: Say when the rule may be used and what it concludes.
skills.name: State L'Hospital's rule with its hypotheses
skills.notation: hypotheses and conclusion of the rule

common_confusions: BC-MIS-04016 (the rule read as differentiating the quotient)
BC-MIS-04015 (no form checked before application)
BC-SKL-03028 (choosing and ordering differentiation rules for each piece)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-04009 (a numerator known only through supplied properties makes the separate derivative visible)
adaptive.mastered_if: The numerator and the denominator are differentiated separately and the new limit is written as the limit of one derivative over the other, with limit notation retained; the quotient rule is not used on the whole expression, so BC-ERR-04030 is absent and at least one correct derivative appears inside a limit as the 2023 rubric requires for the application point.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The two separate limits are correct and one of the two derivatives in the new quotient is wrong, signal BC-SIG-04019, which the 2023 report records as the step at which otherwise correct responses failed; or the derivative of the whole quotient is taken, BC-ERR-04030.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The rule is applied before the indeterminate form is established, a gap at BC-SKL-04033 and BC-SKL-04034 rather than in the differentiation.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-04016 (the conclusion features a ratio of derivatives). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-04034 (the statement that says which derivatives to take).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a limit established to be indeterminate, form the limit of the quotient of the derivative of the numerator and the derivative of the denominator.
skills.description_plain: Differentiate the top and the bottom on their own, not as a quotient.
skills.name: Apply the rule by differentiating numerator and denominator separately
skills.notation: limit of f prime over g prime

common_confusions: BC-MIS-04016 (the derivative of the quotient in place of the quotient of derivatives)
BC-MIS-04014 (an indeterminate form written as a value)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-04009 (the value is the last of the three scored steps and can fail alone)
adaptive.mastered_if: The limit of the quotient of derivatives is evaluated, by substitution where the pieces are continuous or by further analysis where they are not, and the value is reported as the value of the original limit with limit notation carried to the last line; BC-ERR-04031 is absent, so a numerator known only through supplied properties is differentiated using those properties.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The hypothesis and application points are secured and the numerator derivative is mishandled, so the reported value is wrong, BC-ERR-04031 with signal BC-SIG-04019; or the ratio is evaluated with limit notation dropped, the communication failure the 2021 Q4 part C distinctions record.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The quotient of derivatives was never correctly formed, a gap at BC-SKL-04035; or the new form is still indeterminate and is treated as final, a gap at BC-SKL-04037.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-04014 (the value comes from the new limit, not from arithmetic on a form). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-04035 (a correct derivative in each position).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the limit of the quotient of derivatives, evaluate it by substitution or by further analysis and report the value of the original limit.
skills.description_plain: Work out the new limit and report the value.
skills.name: Evaluate the limit that the rule produces
skills.notation: value of the limit

common_confusions: BC-MIS-04015 (no attention to hypotheses before using a rule)
BC-MIS-04014 (a form written where a value belongs)
BC-SKL-04033 (assembling both limits into the indeterminate form statement)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-04009 (the numerator function is given only by properties, so continuity is the only route to its limit)
adaptive.mastered_if: Differentiability at the point is used to conclude continuity there and hence that the limit of the function equals its value, and this is what supplies the numerator limit when the function is known only through given properties; BC-ERR-04028 is absent because the two limits are exhibited rather than the quotient being set equal to a form.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The implication from differentiability to continuity is used silently, so the numerator limit appears with no stated reason; or the numerator limit is taken to be an integrand value rather than the accumulated value, the confusion the 2021 Q4 part C distinctions record.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The relation between differentiability and continuity is not held at all, a gap at BC-PRQ-04008 and the Unit 1 continuity material rather than a limit evaluation gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-04015 (differentiability is a hypothesis that buys continuity). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-04033 (using the value as one of the two separate limits).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given that a function is differentiable at a point, conclude that it is continuous there and that its limit at the point equals its value, in order to establish the limit of a numerator containing that function.
skills.description_plain: A function differentiable at a point is continuous there, so its limit is its value.
skills.name: Use differentiability to evaluate a limit of a given function
skills.notation: differentiable implies continuous

common_confusions: BC-MIS-07011 (the method read as one tangent line over the whole interval)
BC-MIS-07012 (each step restarted from the initial value)
BC-SKL-04029 (a single tangent line approximation, which is the one step case)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-07004 (a named number of equal steps, where one full width step is the visible failure)
adaptive.mastered_if: The step size is computed as the distance from the initial input to the target input divided by the stated number of equal steps, and that size is used for every step rather than the whole interval being traversed at once; BC-ERR-07019 and BC-ERR-99026 are absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The arithmetic is correct for a single step across the entire interval, BC-ERR-07019 with signal BC-SIG-07018, so the number of steps named in the prompt was not acted on; or the size is right and the wrong starting input is used.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The interval endpoints cannot be identified from the prompt, a reading gap at BC-PRQ-07005 rather than an Euler gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-07011 (the derivative is re-evaluated once per step). Procedural failure: BC-PRQ-07005 (dividing the interval length by the step count).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Compute the step size as the difference between the target input and the initial input divided by the stated number of equal steps.
skills.description_plain: Divide the length of the interval by how many steps are asked for.
skills.name: Determine the step size from the interval and the number of steps

common_confusions: BC-MIS-07011 (one evaluation of the derivative for the whole interval)
BC-MIS-07012 (the output not advanced between steps)
BC-SKL-04028 (writing the tangent line rather than stepping along it)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-07004 (the demonstration point turns on the first step being correctly anchored)
adaptive.mastered_if: The right side is evaluated at the given initial point, multiplied by the step size, and added to the initial output, so the first step starts from the stated initial condition with the derivative expression taken from the equation; BC-ERR-07020 and BC-ERR-99026 are absent, which is what the 2025 scoring calls the three conditions of the first step.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The step size is right and the derivative is evaluated somewhere other than the initial condition, such as at the target input, BC-ERR-07020 with signal BC-SIG-07019; later rounding or simplification slips do not affect this point under the 2025 guideline.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The step size is wrong, a gap at BC-SKL-07019; or the right side cannot be evaluated at a point, BC-SKL-07010.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-07011 (the step advances along the tangent at the current point). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-07010 (evaluating the right side at the initial point).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Evaluate the right side at the initial point, multiply by the step size, and add the product to the initial output value.
skills.description_plain: Add the step size times the slope at the starting point.
skills.name: Execute the first Euler step from the initial condition

common_confusions: BC-MIS-07012 (every step restarted from the initial value)
BC-MIS-07011 (the derivative evaluated once)
BC-SKL-07022 (displaying the steps rather than performing them)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-07004 (two steps of equal size, where the running point must be updated)
adaptive.mastered_if: The second step evaluates the right side at the point the first step produced, using both the advanced input and the advanced output, and advances again by the same step size; BC-ERR-07021 and BC-ERR-99026 are absent, so the same derivative value is not reused and no third step is added.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The first step is correct and the second re-evaluates the derivative at the initial point or reuses the initial output, BC-ERR-07021 with signal BC-SIG-07020, which under the 2024 shape costs the demonstration point that requires two correct steps.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The first step is itself misanchored, a gap at BC-SKL-07020; or the step size is wrong, BC-PRQ-07005 and BC-SKL-07019.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-07012 (the output advances with the input). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-07020 (carrying the produced point into the next evaluation).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Evaluate the right side at the point produced by the previous step, not at the initial point, and advance again by the step size.
skills.description_plain: Start the second step from the value the first step produced.
skills.name: Use the previous approximation as the input for the next step

common_confusions: BC-MIS-07013 (the numerical result regarded as the whole response)
BC-MIS-07011 (a single tangent line, so there is nothing to tabulate)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-07004 (the demonstration point and the answer point are separate, so visible steps matter on their own)
adaptive.mastered_if: The input, the running output, and the increment are presented for each step with the columns labelled, so the work stands as a demonstration without relying on the final number; BC-ERR-07022 and BC-ERR-99021 are absent, and the derivative expression entered at each step is visible.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The steps were performed correctly and a single number or an unlabelled table is offered with no visible increments, BC-ERR-07022 with signal BC-SIG-07021; an unlabelled table with a wrong answer earns nothing, as the 2025 Q5 part D distinctions record.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The second step itself restarts from the initial value, a gap at BC-SKL-07021 rather than a presentation gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-07013 (the procedure is the evidence, not the number). Procedural failure: BC-ERR-99021 (labelling the columns and showing each increment).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Present the input, the running output, and the increment for each step, labelling the columns so the work stands without an answer.
skills.description_plain: Show the steps in a table with the columns named.
skills.name: Lay out the computation as a labelled step table

common_confusions: BC-MIS-07019 (a solution formula taken to hold on every input)
BC-MIS-07018 (branch and domain conflated)
BC-SKL-07030 (choosing the branch, which precedes stating the interval)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-07011 (the domain statement is scored as part of the final answer where it is demanded)
adaptive.mastered_if: The largest interval containing the initial input on which the solution expression is defined and continuous is reported, with the input where the expression fails named as the boundary; BC-ERR-07031 is absent, so the formula is not claimed for every input and the reported interval contains the initial point.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: An explicit expression is produced and no domain statement accompanies it although one was demanded, signal BC-SIG-07030; or an interval is reported that excludes the initial input, BC-ERR-07031.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The dependent variable was never isolated, so there is no expression whose domain could be discussed, a gap at BC-SKL-07027; or where the expression fails to be defined cannot be located, BC-PRQ-05003.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-07019 (a particular solution lives on one interval around its initial point). Procedural failure: BC-PRQ-05003 (finding where the expression is undefined).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Report the largest interval containing the initial input on which the solution expression is defined and continuous, and note why the rest is excluded.
skills.description_plain: Say on which interval the particular solution is valid.
skills.name: State the domain restriction the initial condition selects

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10020 (the requested degree not treated as binding)
BC-SKL-10044 (building the polynomial)
BC-SKL-10060 (writing the series general term)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10016 (the first terms and the general term make the partial sum relationship visible)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response states that the Taylor polynomial of degree n is the partial sum of the Taylor series through the degree n term, about the same centre, and keeps the polynomial finite with no ellipsis while describing the series as the full sum. BC-ERR-10030 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The relationship is stated and the polynomial written alongside it carries an ellipsis or terms past the stated degree, which is BC-ERR-10030, so the two objects are not kept apart in the presentation.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Neither object can be written from the given information, which points at BC-SKL-10044 or BC-SKL-10060 rather than at the relationship; reading the notation is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10020 (polynomial as a finite partial sum) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-10044 (writing the polynomial to a stated degree) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: isolated by BC-QA-10016
skills.description_formal: Given a Taylor series and a Taylor polynomial for the same function about the same centre, state that the polynomial is the partial sum of the series through that degree.
skills.description_plain: Say that cutting the series off at a degree gives the polynomial.
skills.name: Identify a Taylor polynomial as a partial sum of the Taylor series

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10019 (derivative values attached to powers with no factorial denominators)
BC-SKL-10044 (assembling the polynomial from the values)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10010 (the form of the rule and the derivative itself are scored separately)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response differentiates the given function or the relation defining its derivative to the required order, displaying the product rule or chain rule form with every factor present, and evaluates each successive derivative at the centre in order, carrying earlier values into the next differentiation. BC-ERR-10028 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The form of the product rule is displayed correctly and the resulting derivative drops a factor, which is BC-SIG-10019 and BC-ERR-10028, so the form point may stand while the derivative point is lost, and the response may carry its own value consistently afterwards.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The relation cannot be read as defining a derivative of a named function, so nothing is differentiated, which is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-CON-10001 (successive derivatives evaluated at the centre) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-10044 (placing the values into coefficients) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a function or a relation defining its derivatives, compute derivatives up to the required order and evaluate each at the centre, carrying product or chain rule steps correctly.
skills.description_plain: Differentiate repeatedly and evaluate each derivative at the centre.
skills.name: Compute successive derivatives of a function at the centre

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10026 (substitution read as moving the centre)
BC-MIS-10021 (the new interval not adjusted with the substitution)
BC-SKL-10065 (multiplication rather than substitution)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10017 (the terms produced by the substitution carry the credit)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response replaces the variable in a standard Maclaurin series by the whole given expression, raises that entire expression to each power with parentheses kept, simplifies the resulting powers, and leaves the centre where it was rather than relocating it. BC-ERR-10041 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The substitution is made and the expression is not raised as a whole, so a constant factor or an exponent is lost, which is BC-ERR-10041, or every term is correct and the series is described as centred at a new point.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The powers of a product or of a negative exponent cannot be simplified, which is BC-PRQ-06002, or the resulting ratio of powers does not reduce, which is BC-PRQ-10007.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10026 (what a substitution changes and what it leaves fixed) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-06002 (raising the whole expression) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a function formed by substituting an expression for x in a known Maclaurin series, carry out the substitution term by term, simplify the powers, and report the resulting series.
skills.description_plain: Replace x in a known series by the expression given and simplify.
skills.name: Construct a Maclaurin series by substitution into a known series

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06001 (a Riemann sum treated as a sum of the listed values)
BC-MIS-06002 (the endpoint convention treated as cosmetic)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06001 (Riemann sum from a table with over or under estimate reasoning)
adaptive.mastered_if: Right endpoints are selected deliberately and each is multiplied by its own subinterval width, so on a monotone table the right sum and the left sum come out as different numbers and the learner says why. Widths are differences of consecutive table inputs, the products are summed, and the count of factors matches the count of subintervals, four products for four subintervals as in BC-FRQ-2021-Q1-B. BC-ERR-06001 (uniform width on a nonuniform partition), BC-ERR-06002 (left endpoints where right were named), and BC-ERR-06003 (values added without widths) do not appear.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: BC-SIG-06003 captures the common intermediate state, a fully correct sum on the wrong convention, which asking for both conventions resolves as a misread rather than a missing distinction. The BC-FRQ-2022-Q4-C commentary separates products shown with a mis-added total from a method failure, and BC-FRQ-2015-Q3-B records a correct sum whose explanation omits units, which costs communication rather than the sum.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Widths assumed equal when the table inputs are not evenly spaced is BC-PRQ-06012, and the tell is that the width list requested on its own is still wrong. Where instead the tabulated function is misread, for example density values summed without the radius factor as BC-FRQ-2021-Q1-B describes, the break is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06002 (whether the left and the right sum on one monotone table must agree) for the conceptual failure. A learner who holds that distinction and still loses factors points instead to BC-PRQ-06012 (each width as a difference of consecutive inputs).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given selected values of f at partition points, approximate the integral of f over the interval as the sum over subintervals of f at the right endpoint multiplied by the width of that subinterval.
skills.description_plain: Use the value at the right end of each subinterval times its width and add.
skills.name: Compute a right Riemann sum from a table of values

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06014 (converting between a limit of Riemann sums in sigma notation and a definite integral)
adaptive.mastered_if: Given f, the endpoints a and b, and n equal pieces, the sigma expression is assembled with delta x written as (b minus a) over n and the sample point written in terms of the index, for instance a plus i times delta x for right endpoints, and the index limits are chosen to match that choice of sample point. The width factor multiplies the function value inside the sigma rather than sitting outside by accident, and the expression reproduces the intended partition when read back term by term.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The width is correct but the sample point expression is not anchored at a, so the sum describes a partition of the wrong interval. Another intermediate state comes from the tabulated analogues in BC-FRQ-2021-Q1-B and BC-FRQ-2022-Q4-C, where the named endpoint rule is not applied or a uniform width is imposed on a nonuniform partition, both of which show the sample point and width choices being made by habit rather than from the stated partition.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: BC-PRQ-06006 is the underlying gap when the sigma expression has no coherent index, limits, and general term, and the tell is that the learner can describe the partition in words or in a picture but cannot place delta x and the sample point into a single indexed term.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-PRQ-06006 (summation notation with an index, limits, and a general term) for the conceptual failure of not seeing the sum as a parametrised list; a procedural failure in forming (b minus a) over n and the sample point points instead to BC-QA-06014, whose first two steps separate the general term into a value and a width.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given f, an interval [a,b], and n equal subintervals, express the corresponding Riemann sum in sigma notation with subinterval width (b minus a) over n and the appropriate sample points.
skills.description_plain: Build the sigma expression from the function, the endpoints, and the number of subintervals.
skills.name: Write a Riemann sum in sigma notation for a given function, interval, and partition

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06003 (Riemann sums treated as exact)
BC-MIS-06005 (approximation direction taken from increase or decrease alone, with concavity never entering)
BC-SKL-06005 (computing a left Riemann sum from a table of values)
BC-SKL-06006 (computing a right Riemann sum from a table of values)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06001 (Riemann sum from a table with over or under estimate reasoning)
adaptive.mastered_if: The direction of the error is tied to a named property of f. For f increasing on the interval of integration, a left sum is called an underestimate and a right sum an overestimate, with the reverse for f decreasing, and the justification sentence states the monotonicity as its reason rather than asserting the direction alone. The learner cites the monotonicity of the function actually being integrated, not of some tabulated factor, and keeps monotonicity separate from concavity when a trapezoidal estimate is also in play, so BC-ERR-06005 (a direction with no supporting behaviour cited) and BC-ERR-06006 (the directions interchanged) do not occur.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: BC-SIG-06006 marks the frequent case, the words underestimate or overestimate present with no reference to increase, decrease, or bending, which is BC-ERR-06005 and loses the justification point even when the direction is right. BC-ERR-06006 shows as a left sum called an overestimate for an increasing rate. The BC-FRQ-2021-Q1-C commentary adds a third state, the monotonicity of the tabulated density cited where the product being integrated was the relevant function.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Comparing an approximation with an exact value and saying which is larger is BC-PRQ-06008, and the tell is that the learner can state whether f rises or falls yet cannot turn that into an inequality between the sum and the integral. If instead the sum itself is built wrongly, the break sits in BC-SKL-06005 or BC-SKL-06006 before any direction question is reachable.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06003 (a Riemann sum as an approximation whose error has a direction) for the conceptual failure, with BC-MIS-06005 as the target once concavity enters. A correct direction stated without its reason points instead to BC-PRQ-06008 (inequality reasoning about approximations).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given that f is increasing or decreasing on the interval of integration, determine and justify whether a left or right Riemann sum is an underestimate or an overestimate of the definite integral.
skills.description_plain: Argue from the function increasing or decreasing which way the estimate is off.
skills.name: Justify whether a Riemann sum under or over estimates using monotonicity

common_confusions: BC-MIS-02011 (differentiation assumed to distribute across a product)
BC-SKL-02038 (expanding first, which avoids the rule for polynomial factors)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-02008 (the rule with both derivatives present and the simplified result carry separate credit)
adaptive.mastered_if: The derivative of a product is written as the first factor times the derivative of the second plus the second times the derivative of the first, with both terms present and both derivatives taken, so the derivatives of the factors are never simply multiplied together (BC-ERR-02020 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The rule is set out with both terms but one factor is left undifferentiated in its term, which the 2025 Q5 guidelines treat as earning the product structure and not the derivative factor, so the structure is held and one derivative is missing.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The polynomial factors themselves cannot be differentiated, which is a gap at BC-SKL-02031 rather than a failure of the product rule.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-02011 (expanding a simple product and comparing with the proposed answer) for the conceptual failure; BC-SKL-02031 (differentiating each factor) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: For a product of differentiable functions, write the derivative as the first factor times the derivative of the second plus the second factor times the derivative of the first.
skills.description_plain: Differentiate one factor at a time and add the two results.
skills.name: Apply the product rule to a product of two differentiable functions

common_confusions: BC-MIS-09011 (speed taken to be one of the two velocity components)
BC-MIS-09005 (a length in the plane taken as the sum of the component contributions)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-09006 (the speed at a time, where an additive answer is directly visible)
adaptive.mastered_if: The speed at a time is written as the square root of the sum of the squares of the two velocity components, each component squared inside parentheses, and evaluated to the required accuracy; the value is nonnegative and larger than either component in absolute value, so neither BC-ERR-09013 nor BC-ERR-09014 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Both components are correct and combined by addition rather than by the Pythagorean relation, which is BC-ERR-09013 and the observation in BC-SIG-09003; or the radical form is right and parentheses are lost inside a squared component, which is BC-ERR-09014.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The magnitude of a two component quantity is not formed by the Pythagorean relation at all, which is BC-PRQ-08007 rather than a speed gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-09011 (speed as the magnitude of the velocity vector) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08007 (writing the magnitude with parentheses intact) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: isolated by BC-QA-09006
skills.description_formal: Given the two velocity components at a time, compute the speed as the square root of the sum of their squares, with the setup shown.
skills.description_plain: Square both components, add, take the square root.

common_confusions: BC-MIS-09009 (a vector answer treated as a pair of numbers with no structure)
BC-SKL-09016 (the velocity vector, one derivative earlier)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-09004 (the acceleration vector with its setup, so presentation and differentiation separate)
adaptive.mastered_if: Each velocity component is differentiated, both derivatives are evaluated at the requested time, and the acceleration vector is presented with the derivative expressions shown alongside the two values; a variable expression is not set equal to its value at one time in a single chain, so neither BC-ERR-09011 nor BC-ERR-09018 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Two correct acceleration components appear with no differentiation and no evaluation shown, which is BC-ERR-09011 and the state in BC-SIG-09005; or the work is complete and written as one equality running from an expression in t to a number, which is BC-ERR-09018.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The vector notation is not parsed, so which component is being differentiated is unclear, which is BC-PRQ-09001.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-09009 (the acceleration as one vector object) for the conceptual case; BC-ERR-09018 (writing the substitution as its own step) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Differentiate each component of the velocity vector and evaluate at the requested time, presenting the acceleration vector with the setup shown.

common_confusions: BC-MIS-09009 (a vector answer treated as a pair of numbers with no structure)
BC-SKL-09017 (computing the acceleration vector, which this presents)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-09004 (the setup is explicitly part of what is scored)
adaptive.mastered_if: The acceleration vector at the requested time is presented together with the differentiation of each velocity component and the substitution of the time, the supporting expressions appearing before the pair of numbers; the chain from expression to value is written in separate steps, so neither BC-ERR-09018 nor BC-ERR-09011 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Two correct components appear with no derivative expressions and no evaluation shown, which is BC-ERR-09011 and the state in BC-SIG-09005; or the derivatives are shown and the expression in t is set equal to its value at one time in a single chain of equalities, which is BC-ERR-09018.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The vector notation is not read, so it is unclear which expression each reported number came from, which is BC-PRQ-09001.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-09009 (the vector and its supporting expressions as one answer) for the conceptual case; BC-ERR-09018 (separating the expression from its value) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts

common_confusions: BC-MIS-09006 (distance in the plane read as the size of the net change in position)
BC-SKL-09020 (displacement, which integrates the components)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-09007 (the path doubles back, so distance and the magnitude of displacement differ)
adaptive.mastered_if: The total distance is written as the definite integral of the speed, the radical of the sum of the squared components, over the time interval, evaluated numerically and reported with units; the components are not integrated before the magnitude is taken, so BC-ERR-09015 is absent, and the speed carried into the integral is the one derived in this part rather than an earlier incorrect one.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The components are integrated first and the magnitude of that vector is reported as the distance travelled, which is BC-ERR-09015 and the state in BC-SIG-09004; or the structure is correct and an incorrect speed declared in an earlier part is carried into the integrand, which is BC-ERR-09024.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The speed itself cannot be formed as a magnitude, so there is no integrand, which is BC-PRQ-08007; the one dimensional total distance integral is BC-SKL-08007.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-09006 (why the magnitude is taken before integrating) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-09023 (forming the speed expression) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: isolated by BC-QA-09007
skills.description_formal: Write and evaluate the definite integral of the speed over the time interval and report the result as the total distance travelled, with units.
skills.description_plain: Integrate the speed expression over the time interval.

common_confusions: BC-MIS-09005 (a length in the plane taken as the sum of the component contributions)
BC-SKL-08056 (the single variable arc length integrand)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-09003 (the integrand is the speed, so an additive integrand is visible in the expression)
adaptive.mastered_if: The length is written as the definite integral of the square root of the sum of the squares of dx/dt and dy/dt over the stated parameter interval, each component squared as a whole inside parentheses and the two squares added under one radical; neither BC-ERR-09013 nor BC-ERR-09014 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Both component rates are correct and they are added rather than combined as a magnitude, which is BC-ERR-09013 and the not mastered observation in BC-SIG-09003; or the radical is right and a squared component loses its parentheses so only part of it is squared, which is BC-ERR-09014.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The magnitude of a two component quantity is not formed by the Pythagorean relation, which is BC-PRQ-08007; the single variable length integral from which this generalises is BC-SKL-08056, and evaluating any definite integral by antidifferentiation is BC-SKL-06034.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-09005 (why the two rates combine by the Pythagorean relation) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08007 (forming the magnitude with parentheses intact) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts

common_confusions: BC-MIS-09006 (distance in the plane read as the size of the net change in position)
BC-SKL-09020 (displacement, the quantity this must be kept apart from)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-09003 (a length along the path)
BC-QA-09007 (total distance from the speed, so the two quantities can be asked side by side)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response states that the integral of the speed over a time interval is the total distance the particle travels along its path, and separates that from the magnitude of the vector of component integrals; the distinction is made for a path that doubles back, and BC-ERR-09015 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The speed integral is recognised as a length and the distance travelled is then computed by integrating the components first and taking a magnitude at the end, which is BC-ERR-09015 and the state in BC-SIG-09004.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The notation for the velocity components and for the position vector is not distinguished in the stem, so the two candidate quantities are not even separated, which is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-09006 (why integrating first and taking a magnitude last measures something else) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-09023 (forming the speed that goes inside the integral) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: isolated by BC-QA-09007
