skills.name: Identify the parametric arc length integral as the distance travelled

common_confusions: BC-MIS-09008 (a calculator result treated as standing without its expression)
BC-MIS-09006 (distance in the plane read as the size of the net change in position)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-09003 (the radical integrand has no elementary antiderivative, so the written expression is the only record of method)
adaptive.mastered_if: The parametric length integral is written on the page with its radical integrand and parameter limits, evaluated numerically, and reported to three places after the decimal point from unrounded stored values; neither BC-ERR-09011 nor BC-ERR-09006 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A correct decimal length appears with no integral expression supporting it, which is BC-ERR-09011; or the integral is shown and a truncated component rate or bound is reused, moving the third decimal place, which is BC-ERR-09006.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The number is right and reported to the wrong number of places or rounded against the convention, which is BC-PRQ-08006; the single variable version of the same numerical step is BC-SKL-08059.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-09008 (the written integral as the scored object) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08006 (three place reporting from stored values) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Evaluate the parametric arc length integral numerically and report the value accurate to three places after the decimal point.
skills.description_plain: Enter the radical integrand and report the decimal.
skills.name: Evaluate a parametric arc length integral with technology

common_confusions: BC-MIS-09010 (the integral of a velocity component read as the coordinate)
BC-SKL-09020 (displacement, which is the integral without the initial value)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-09005 (a known position at one time and a component rate, so the initial term is the scored difference)
adaptive.mastered_if: The requested coordinate is written as the known coordinate at the given time plus the definite integral of the matching velocity component between the two times, the limits running from the time of the known value to the time asked for; the reported coordinate changes when the known position changes, and neither BC-ERR-09020 nor BC-ERR-09021 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The definite integral of the velocity component is evaluated correctly and reported as the coordinate with the known position unused, which is BC-ERR-09020 and the state in BC-SIG-09006; or the initial value is present and the accumulation is added when the known time is the later one, which is BC-ERR-09021.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The pattern initial value plus accumulated change is not assembled even for a scalar rate, which is BC-SKL-06037; misreading which coordinate the given velocity component belongs to is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-09010 (the integral as change in the coordinate) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-06037 (adding the known value to the accumulation) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the position at one time and a velocity component, evaluate the corresponding coordinate at another time as the initial coordinate plus the definite integral of that component.
skills.description_plain: Add the integral of that velocity component to the starting coordinate.
skills.name: Determine a coordinate of position from an initial position and a velocity component

common_confusions: BC-MIS-09009 (a vector answer treated as a pair of numbers with no structure)
BC-SKL-09021 (recovering a coordinate with a definite integral instead)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-09005 (a coordinate is recovered from an initial position, so the per component constant is what the answer rests on)
adaptive.mastered_if: Each component of the vector valued rate is antidifferentiated on its own and each carries its own constant, the result presented as a vector of two expressions; the constants are then fixed separately from the two given initial conditions, and BC-ERR-09019 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Both component antiderivatives are correct and a single constant is attached to the vector as a whole, which is BC-ERR-09019, so only one of the two initial conditions can be satisfied.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The vector notation is not read as two independent component functions, which is BC-PRQ-09001 rather than an antidifferentiation gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-09009 (two components, two constants) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-09001 (writing the vector antiderivative) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a vector-valued rate, produce a vector-valued antiderivative by antidifferentiating each component and carrying a constant in each.
skills.description_plain: Find an antiderivative of each component.
skills.name: Antidifferentiate a vector-valued function component by component

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06017 (a composite integrand is taken to guarantee that substitution applies, without checking that the inner derivative is present)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06008 (a composite times a constant multiple of its inner derivative, taken through u, du, rewriting, antidifferentiating, and back-substitution or converted limits)
BC-QA-06016 (mixed integrands where the structure has to select the technique)
adaptive.mastered_if: u is stated explicitly as the inner expression, and the response can point to a constant multiple of the derivative of that inner expression sitting inside the integrand before committing to the technique. Where the integrand needs rewriting first, a constant is factored out or a fraction split so the du factor is exposed. Neither BC-ERR-06020, substitution attempted when the inner derivative is absent, nor BC-ERR-06019, the constant factor from the differential dropped, appears in the work.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A composite is spotted and substitution is launched on that alone, BC-ERR-06020, so the setup point for the technique is not earned and the line of work leads nowhere. In other attempts the choice of u is right and BC-ERR-06019 follows, the reciprocal constant from du never appearing, which BC-FRQ-2014-Q5-A records as a difference of boundary functions correct with the substitution constant dropped, and BC-FRQ-2024-Q3-C as the inner constant lost from a sine antiderivative.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The inner function and its derivative are present but hidden until the expression is rewritten, and no rewriting is attempted, which is BC-PRQ-06001. A second earlier failure is BC-SKL-03002, where a two layer composite is not differentiated correctly by the chain rule, so the learner cannot say what du should look like in the first place.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06017 (substitution requires the inner derivative, not merely a composite) for the conceptual failure; procedural loss once u is chosen correctly points instead to BC-ERR-06019 (constant factor from the differential dropped).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a composite integrand, choose u equal to the inner expression such that the remaining factor is a constant multiple of du, and state the choice explicitly.
skills.description_plain: Pick u as the inside expression whose derivative is a factor of the integrand.
skills.name: Select a substitution by identifying an inner function whose derivative appears

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06016 (substitution treated as renaming a variable, so differentials and limits carry over unchanged)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06008 (u chosen, du computed and the constant adjusted, the integral rewritten entirely in u, then evaluated)
adaptive.mastered_if: du is written out as g prime of x dx and the balancing constant is computed from it, so the integral that reaches the antidifferentiation step contains no surviving x. The reciprocal constant appears in front of the integral rather than being absorbed silently, and a negative introduced by the differential keeps its sign. Differentiating the finished antiderivative returns the original integrand rather than a multiple of it, so BC-ERR-06019 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: BC-SIG-06019 is the state to watch, the reported antiderivative being a nonzero constant multiple of the correct one, which is BC-ERR-06019 and costs the antiderivative point and the value point with it. BC-FRQ-2021-Q3-A adds the sign of the antiderivative going wrong because the negative from the differential was mishandled, and BC-FRQ-2014-Q5-A the case where the integrand is set up correctly as a difference of curves and only the substitution constant is lost.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The choice of u is itself unsound, so no differential could balance it, and the failure belongs to BC-SKL-06047 rather than here. Separately, BC-PRQ-06001 is the gap when the integrand was never rewritten to expose the derivative factor, leaving a du with nothing in the integrand to cancel against.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06016 (substitution as a change of variable rather than a relabelling) for the conceptual failure; the procedural failure, a constant lost between lines with the method intact, points to BC-ERR-06019 (constant factor from the differential dropped).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a substitution u = g(x), compute du = g'(x) dx and multiply by the constant needed so that the integrand is rewritten entirely in u.
skills.description_plain: Write du = g'(x) dx and balance any constant factor.
skills.name: Convert the differential and adjust the constant when substituting

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06016 (u read as shorthand for the same problem, so limits and differentials carry over unchanged)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06008 (definite integral by substitution, ending in either converted limits or back-substitution before evaluation)
adaptive.mastered_if: For a definite integral taken through u equal to g of x, the lower limit becomes g of a and the upper becomes g of b, both computed and written on the integral sign before any evaluation happens, and no back-substitution is then needed. The learner can say why the limits change, namely that u is a different variable rather than a label, and can produce both converted values on request.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: BC-SIG-06018 is the visible state, the antiderivative written in u with the original x limits attached, which is BC-ERR-06018 and makes the response ineligible for the answer point even when the numerical value comes out correct. BC-FRQ-2021-Q3-A describes the same thing as substitution performed but limits left in the old variable, a bookkeeping failure rather than a failure of the technique. Asking for the two converted limits separates the two cases, since producing them correctly marks an omitted step.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The substitution itself is unbalanced because du was never converted with its constant, so the limits are being changed on an expression that is already wrong. That is BC-SKL-06048, and the tell is correctly computed g of a and g of b sitting on an antiderivative that is a constant multiple of the right one.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06016 (a change of variable changes the interval too) for the conceptual failure; when the reason is stated correctly and the conversion step is simply skipped, the target is BC-ERR-06018 (original limits kept after a substitution).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a definite integral evaluated by substitution u = g(x), replace the lower and upper limits a and b by g(a) and g(b) before evaluating in u.
skills.description_plain: Replace the x limits by the matching u limits.
skills.name: Change the limits of integration when substituting in a definite integral

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08010 (the area between curves read as the integral of one bounding curve)
BC-MIS-08011 (the order of subtraction treated as immaterial)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08008 (the region is bounded above and below by curves rather than by the axis)
adaptive.mastered_if: The area integral is written with integrand the upper function minus the lower function, dx as the differential, and limits that are the x values bounding the region, the difference parenthesised so that the subtraction applies to the whole lower expression; neither BC-ERR-08020 nor BC-ERR-08018 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The limits and the pair of functions are right while the difference is reversed, which is BC-ERR-08020; or the integrand and the limits are complete and no dx is written, which is BC-ERR-08018.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Area read from a graph as a definite integral is not available, so the difference of two curves has nothing to attach to, which is BC-SKL-06028; misreading which expression is f and which is g in the stem is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08010 (that the second boundary is subtracted rather than ignored) for the conceptual case; BC-ERR-08018 (differential and limits on the written expression) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Write a definite integral with integrand the difference of the two functions in the order upper minus lower, with the differential dx and the limits taken from the boundary.
skills.description_plain: Write the integral of the top curve minus the bottom curve, dx.
skills.name: Set up the area integral of upper minus lower with respect to x

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08012 (limits treated as a viewing window rather than the boundary of the region)
BC-SKL-08021 (locating the same crossings with technology)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08008 (the region begins and ends at crossings rather than at stated endpoints)
adaptive.mastered_if: The two expressions are set equal, the equation is solved exactly by factoring, by the quadratic formula, or by an inverse operation, and the solutions that bound the shaded region are selected from the full solution set and used as the limits; extraneous roots outside the region are discarded with the selection stated, and BC-ERR-08019 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The equation is solved correctly and the limits taken are the ends of the displayed domain or the axes of the picture rather than the intersection values, which is BC-ERR-08019 in its limit selection form.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The equation formed by equating the two curves cannot be solved, so no candidate boundary values are produced, which is BC-PRQ-08001 rather than a limit selection gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08012 (what determines where the region begins and ends) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08001 (solving the equation that locates the crossings) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Set the two functions equal, solve exactly for the inputs at which the graphs meet, and select the solutions that bound the region.
skills.description_plain: Solve the two expressions equal to each other by hand.
skills.name: Find intersection points algebraically to set the limits

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05015 (the location of an extremum and its value treated as the same answer)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05003 (a named input classified as a relative minimum, a relative maximum or neither, with a reason)
BC-QA-05006 (an absolute extremum found by the candidates test and justified over the whole interval)
adaptive.mastered_if: The question is read for which of two things it wants, the input c at which the extremum occurs or the extreme value f of c, and the reported answer is that one. Both are available in the work, so when the value is asked for the function is evaluated at c rather than c being handed back, and BC-ERR-05024 (location reported where the value was wanted, or the reverse) does not occur. This holds for a formula under BC-REP-01 and for a justification written in words under BC-REP-04.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The extremum is located correctly and the reported answer is the input where the value was demanded, or the value where the input was demanded, which is BC-SIG-05017 and BC-ERR-05024. BC-FRQ-2021-Q3-B records two related states, a critical input found with the curve never evaluated there so the link from the maximum to the radius is missing, and the derivative value handed in as the radius, which confuses a function value with a derivative value rather than a location with a value.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: If the point was never classified, there is nothing to report either way and the failure belongs to BC-SKL-05020 (classifying a critical point from the sign change of the first derivative). The tell is that the answer is unstable between candidate inputs rather than between an input and its output.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05015 (input and output collapsed into one answer) is the conceptual target. When the distinction is held and the wrong one is still submitted because the question was scanned rather than read, the target is BC-SKL-05020, where the classified point and its value are both on the page.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a classified critical point, report the input where the extremum occurs or the value f(c), according to the wording of the question.
skills.description_plain: Answer with the input or the output, whichever was asked for.
skills.name: Separate the location of a relative extremum from its value

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08020 (a volume of revolution integrating the radius rather than its square)
BC-MIS-08015 (a factor of pi attached to every volume)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08012 (the region touches the axis, so a single radius carries the whole integrand)
adaptive.mastered_if: For a region touching its axis of revolution, the radius of the disc at an input is written as the distance from the curve to that axis, and it is then squared inside the integrand so that pi multiplies the square rather than the function; BC-ERR-08036 is absent, and the radius reduces to the function value only because the axis is the coordinate axis.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The radius is identified correctly as the distance to the axis and the integrand is pi times the function rather than pi times its square, which is BC-ERR-08036.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Distance from a curve to a line is not formed as a subtraction along the axis, so the radius is never a difference, which is BC-PRQ-08004.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08020 (the area of one disc before the integral is written) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08004 (measuring the radius to the axis) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: For a region between a curve and the axis of revolution, write the radius of the disc at an input as the distance from the curve to that axis.
skills.description_plain: The radius is the function value when the axis is the x axis.
skills.name: Identify the radius of a disc as the distance to the axis

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08020 (a volume of revolution integrating the radius rather than its square)
BC-MIS-08015 (a factor of pi attached to every volume)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08012 (revolution about the x axis, where the radius is the function itself)
adaptive.mastered_if: The volume is written as pi times the definite integral with respect to x of the square of the function over the interval the region spans, the constant pi carried through to the reported value; neither BC-ERR-08037 nor BC-ERR-08036 appears, and the squared function is kept as a square rather than distributed.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The integral of the square of the function is correct and the factor pi is dropped from the reported volume, which is BC-ERR-08037 and the state in BC-SIG-08013; or pi is present and the function is not squared, which is BC-ERR-08036.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The radius was never written as the distance from the curve to the axis of revolution, so the wrong quantity is squared, which is BC-PRQ-08004.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08020 (the area of a circular slice) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-08043 (carrying pi through the evaluation) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Write the volume of the solid obtained by revolving the region between a curve and the x axis about the x axis as pi times the definite integral of the square of the function with respect to x.
skills.description_plain: Integrate pi times the square of the function with respect to x.
skills.name: Set up the disc integral about the x axis

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08020 (a volume of revolution integrating the radius rather than its square)
BC-MIS-08003 (a calculator value treated as standing on its own)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08012 (a numerical volume is requested, so the constant factor shows in the reported value)
adaptive.mastered_if: The disc integral is evaluated by antidifferentiating the squared radius or with technology, and the reported volume retains the factor pi, either as an exact multiple of pi or as a decimal that includes it; unrounded intermediates feed the final step, so neither BC-ERR-08037 nor BC-ERR-08005 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The integral of the square of the radius is evaluated correctly and the answer is reported without pi, which is BC-ERR-08037, the integrand without its constant factor being BC-SIG-08013; or pi is retained and a truncated intermediate moves the value, which is BC-ERR-08005.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The antiderivative of the squared radius is wrong because of exponent handling, which is BC-PRQ-06002 rather than a reporting gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08020 (where pi and the square come from) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-06002 (antidifferentiating the squared radius) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Evaluate the disc integral by antidifferentiation or with technology and report the volume, retaining the constant factor of pi.
skills.description_plain: Do the integral and keep pi in the answer.
skills.name: Evaluate a disc volume and report it with the factor of pi

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06016 (several integrands of different structure presented for classification and technique selection)
adaptive.mastered_if: A single fraction with a sum in the numerator is split term by term over its denominator, or a product of polynomials is multiplied out, and every resulting term is written as a power with an explicit exponent, including negative and fractional ones, before any antiderivative is taken. Constants are factored out cleanly, the reverse power rule is applied to each term separately, and a constant of integration accompanies the indefinite result. Radicals and reciprocals appear as powers rather than being carried in their original notation.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The rewrite is performed but one term keeps its original form, so the power rule is applied to some pieces and guessed at for others. A related state splits the numerator correctly and then mishandles a negative or fractional exponent when antidifferentiating. BC-FRQ-2021-Q3-C records a neighbouring pattern where a leading factor is taken as the stated volume, meaning the constant and the target value were confused rather than the method. Under BC-QA-06016, whichever technique ends up applied carries its own scoring behaviour (ced:131).
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Terms that are antidifferentiated without ever being rewritten point to BC-PRQ-06001 (rewriting expressions to expose an inner function and its derivative), and the sign is a learner who accepts a compound integrand as it stands. Exponent arithmetic that fails on radicals or reciprocals belongs to BC-PRQ-06002 (exponent rules including negative and fractional exponents), while a correct rewrite followed by a wrong power antiderivative is BC-SKL-06040 (antidifferentiate power functions including negative and fractional exponents).
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-PRQ-06001 (rewriting to expose a form a basic rule can handle) is the conceptual target when the learner does not see rewriting as part of the method. When the rewrite happens but the exponents misbehave, the procedural target is BC-PRQ-06002 (exponent rules including negative and fractional exponents).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an integrand that is a sum over a single denominator or a product of polynomials, rewrite it as a sum of terms each of which antidifferentiates by a basic rule.
skills.description_plain: Break a single fraction into separate terms or multiply out a product first.
skills.name: Rewrite an integrand by splitting or expanding before antidifferentiating

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06006 (concavity and monotonicity treated as the same property, so the two justifications are exchanged)
BC-MIS-06009 (restating a definition believed to count as a reason)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06003 (accumulation function analysed from a graph of the integrand made of segments and circular arcs)
adaptive.mastered_if: Concave up intervals for g are matched to the intervals where the plotted f is increasing and concave down to where f is decreasing, with the justification naming that rise or fall of f. A decreasing but concave up stretch of f is handled without trouble, so rising is kept apart from being positive. The stated reason ties the claim to the given graph, which is what BC-ERR-06010 lacks, and the object of the claim stays the accumulation function rather than the plotted curve, which is what BC-ERR-06008 loses.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Intervals where the plotted function is positive are reported as the concave up intervals, which BC-FRQ-2021-Q4-A and BC-FRQ-2014-Q3-B both describe as positivity and increase conflated. Correct intervals with no reason at all also sit here, since BC-FRQ-2021-Q4-A awards its single point for intervals together with a reason. A third state supplies the right intervals but phrases the reason about the accumulation function only, the referent failure BC-ERR-06010 describes.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: A missing BC-SKL-06018 leaves the response with no statement that g prime equals f, so the monotonicity of f is never connected to the concavity of g and the analysis is carried out on the visible curve. The tell is that the monotonic stretches of f are identified correctly and the conclusion is labelled with the wrong function.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06006 (separating whether a curve rises from whether it bends upward) for the conceptual failure; a justification that names the right feature but not the given representation points instead to BC-ERR-06010 (anchoring the reason to the plotted graph of f)

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the graph of f and g(x) = the integral from a to x of f(t) dt, determine the intervals on which g is concave up or concave down according to whether f is increasing or decreasing.
skills.description_plain: Say where g bends up or down based on whether f rises or falls.
skills.name: Determine the concavity of an accumulation function from the monotonicity of the integrand

common_confusions: BC-MIS-02011 (supplied values placed in the wrong positions because the rule is remembered as distributing)
BC-SKL-02041 (the quotient rule from supplied values, which has the same substitution risk)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-02009 (four values supplied at one input, where the rule with values in place and the final value are scored separately)
adaptive.mastered_if: The four supplied numbers at the named input are recorded and labelled, the product rule is written with the function names in place, the values are substituted with each derivative value in a derivative position (BC-ERR-02024 absent), and the result is evaluated, with the two terms added rather than the derivatives multiplied (BC-ERR-02020 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The rule is set out with the names in the right positions but one of the four supplied numbers is a function value where a derivative value belongs, which is BC-SIG-02013 and BC-ERR-02024.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The product rule cannot be stated with both terms, which is a gap at BC-SKL-02036 rather than a substitution error.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-02011 (the structure of the rule) for the conceptual failure; BC-SKL-02036 (writing the rule before substituting) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the values of two functions and of their derivatives at an input, evaluate the derivative of their product at that input using the product rule.
skills.description_plain: Substitute the four supplied values into the rule at the named input.
skills.name: Apply the product rule with values supplied by a table or a graph

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06011 (area formulas recalled without their fractional factors)
BC-MIS-06012 (the definite integral treated as unsigned area)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06003 (an accumulation function analysed from a graph of the integrand made of segments and circular arcs)
adaptive.mastered_if: Signed area does the work. From the graph of f the learner splits the region at each crossing of the x axis, computes each piece with the right formula, one half base times height for a triangle and one half pi r squared for a semicircular piece, and subtracts the pieces lying below the axis before reporting g at the requested input, exactly the single value point of BC-FRQ-2014-Q3-A. Neither BC-ERR-06013 (a semicircular piece given pi r squared) nor BC-ERR-06014 (regions below the axis added as positive area) is present, and a negative value for g is accepted without hesitation when the graph calls for it.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The decomposition is correct and the arithmetic is not, in the two documented ways. BC-ERR-06013 gives the semicircle the full circle formula, losing the value point while leaving the method visible. BC-ERR-06014 adds every piece positively, so the reported number is total area rather than a signed integral, and the BC-FRQ-2021-Q4-D commentary notes the same error reaching a later part through an imported endpoint value. A third state omits the split at the crossing entirely, which the BC-FRQ-2014-Q3-A distractors record as a skipped decomposition step.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: BC-SKL-06028 is the earlier skill that fails first, and the tell is that the learner can say g equals a signed area but cannot get a number out of a graph made of segments and arcs for any fixed pair of limits. BC-PRQ-06007 is implicated when lengths are read off the figure correctly but the area formula for a trapezoid or a circular piece cannot be produced.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-SKL-06028 (evaluating a definite integral from a graph using area formulas) for the conceptual failure about signed area; a procedural failure in the formulas themselves, such as a dropped factor of one half, points instead to BC-PRQ-06007 (area formulas for rectangles, triangles, trapezoids, circles, and semicircles).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the graph of f and g(x) = the integral from a to x of f(t) dt, evaluate g at a stated input by computing the signed area of the region between the graph of f and the x axis from a to that input.
skills.description_plain: Find g at a point by measuring signed area from the start value to that point.
skills.name: Evaluate an accumulation function at a specified input from the graph of the integrand

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06019 (antidifferentiation treated as distributing across a product, so each factor is antidifferentiated on its own)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06009 (antiderivative by integration by parts on a product of unlike factors, one of which simplifies on differentiation)
adaptive.mastered_if: All four of u, dv, du, and v are written down before the formula is invoked, and the assignment is defensible, with du simpler than u and v reachable by a basic antiderivative. A linear factor goes to the differentiated side and a trigonometric or exponential factor to the integrated side, matching the model solution in BC-FRQ-2024-Q5-D where the linear expression is differentiated and the cosine integrated with its chain factor carried (sg-24:18). BC-ERR-06022 (factors of a product antidifferentiated separately) is absent, so no answer is formed by multiplying two independent antiderivatives together.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The factors are assigned but exchanged, so the remaining integral grows in degree rather than shrinking, the pattern BC-FRQ-2024-Q5-D and BC-FRQ-2023-Q5-C both record when the choice rule is not applied. A separate state antidifferentiates each factor on its own and multiplies, which is BC-ERR-06022 and earns neither the u and dv point nor the expression point (sg-23:18, sg-24:18). Under BC-QA-06009 the choice may be left implicit and still credited, provided the correct parts expression or a tabular layout makes it visible (sg-23:18).
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: A sound assignment whose v then comes out wrong is a gap in the underlying antiderivative rather than in the choice, pointing to BC-SKL-06040 (antidifferentiate power functions including negative and fractional exponents) for a power factor or BC-SKL-06042 (antidifferentiate basic trigonometric integrands) for a sine or cosine factor. The tell is a learner who explains the choice rule correctly and then cannot produce v.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06019 (the sum rule wrongly extended to products) is the conceptual target, answerable by differentiating the proposed product and comparing it with the integrand. Procedural failure, where parts is correctly selected but v cannot be produced, points instead to BC-SKL-06042 (antidifferentiating basic trigonometric integrands).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a product integrand, select u and dv so that du is simpler than u and v is obtainable by a basic antiderivative, and record both u, dv, du, and v.
skills.description_plain: Assign one factor to differentiate and the other to antidifferentiate.
skills.name: Choose u and dv for an integration by parts

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06019 (antidifferentiation treated as distributing across a product, so each factor is antidifferentiated on its own)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06009 (antiderivative by integration by parts on a product of unlike factors, one of which simplifies on differentiation)
adaptive.mastered_if: Given u, dv, du, and v, the line u times v minus the integral of v du is written with the minus sign intact, and the remaining integral is then carried to a finished antiderivative with a constant of integration where the integral is indefinite. Any chain factor inside v, such as the reciprocal constant from a sine or cosine of a scaled argument, survives into the expression, which BC-FRQ-2024-Q5-D flags as a common loss (sg-24:18). Neither BC-ERR-06022 (factors antidifferentiated separately) nor BC-ERR-06023 (minus sign dropped in the parts expression) appears anywhere in the work.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The expression is assembled as u times v plus the integral of v du, which is BC-ERR-06023, costing the expression point and with it the answer point that depends on it (sg-23:18). Another state reports the product of the two factors' antiderivatives, matching BC-SIG-06020, where asking the student to differentiate the answer and watching them notice the mismatch marks the gap as procedural rather than conceptual. A third writes the parts expression correctly and then abandons the remaining integral or omits the constant of integration, the omission BC-FRQ-2024-Q5-D records as treating an indefinite integral as definite.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: If the formula is applied faithfully but to factors assigned the wrong way round, so the remaining integral is harder than the original, the failure is BC-SKL-06057 (choose u and dv for an integration by parts). The sign is a correctly written u times v minus the integral of v du that nonetheless cannot be finished.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06019 (antidifferentiation wrongly distributed across a product) is the conceptual target when the reported answer is a product of antiderivatives. A dropped minus sign with the structure otherwise intact is procedural and points instead to BC-ERR-06023 (the minus sign in the parts expression).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given u, dv, du, and v, write the integral of u dv as u times v minus the integral of v du, and evaluate the remaining integral.
skills.description_plain: Write uv minus the integral of v du and finish the remaining integral.
skills.name: Apply the integration by parts formula

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10007 (the name of a test treated as the argument)
BC-SKL-10021 (choosing the test without checking that it applies)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10005 (the conditions carry a point of their own and require all three properties)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response names all three hypotheses, that the matching function f is positive, decreasing, and continuous on the interval from the starting index onward, and supports each one, for instance by a sign argument, by the sign of f prime or by the monotone form of the expression, and by the absence of a zero denominator. BC-ERR-10010 and BC-ERR-10009 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Two of the three properties are listed and the third is omitted, which is BC-SIG-10009 and BC-ERR-10010, so the conditions point is not earned although the rest of the integral test work may stand.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The matching function f cannot be written from a sub n, so no property can be argued about it: that is BC-PRQ-06005 rather than an integral test gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10007 (hypotheses as part of the argument) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-06005 (writing f from a sub n) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a series whose terms come from a function f, state that f is positive, decreasing, and continuous on the interval from the starting index onward and support each claim.
skills.description_plain: Check that the matching function is positive, decreasing, and continuous on the interval.
skills.name: State and verify the conditions required by the integral test

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10007 (hypotheses and setup treated as ceremony around a named test)
BC-SKL-06067 (improper integral setup in the integration unit)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10005 (the improper integral is a separate scored step from the conditions and the evaluation)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response writes the integral of f of x with the lower limit equal to the index the series starts at and an upper limit carried as a variable inside limit notation; the integrand matches a sub n with the index replaced by the continuous variable. BC-ERR-10012 and BC-ERR-10011 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The integrand is correct and the lower limit is one when the sigma starts elsewhere, which is BC-ERR-10012, or the integral is opened with the infinity symbol in place of limit notation, which is BC-ERR-10011; a correct subsequent limit keeps the evaluation point in reach.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The switch from the index n to a bound continuous variable is not made, which is BC-PRQ-06013, or f of x cannot be written from a sub n at all, which is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-CON-10001 (the correspondence between the series and the integral) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-06013 (bound variables) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a series of terms f of n, write the corresponding improper integral with the correct lower limit and with limit notation for the upper limit.
skills.description_plain: Write the integral of f from the starting index to infinity as a limit.
skills.name: Set up the improper integral that matches the series

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10007 (test machinery run without its supporting form)
BC-SKL-10015 (the setup step, where the lower limit rather than the notation is the issue)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10005 (the evaluation is scored on the limit notation, not only on the number)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response antidifferentiates the integrand, evaluates between the lower limit and a variable upper bound b, then writes the limit as b increases without bound and reports a finite value or divergence; limit notation is present through the evaluation rather than dropped partway. BC-ERR-10011 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The antiderivative is correct and the infinity symbol is substituted into it, which is BC-ERR-10011 and matches BC-SIG-10010, or limit notation opens the line and is abandoned before the value is produced.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The antiderivative itself is wrong because a negative or fractional exponent is mishandled, which is BC-PRQ-06002, or a logarithm rule is misapplied, which is BC-PRQ-06003.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-CON-10001 (an improper integral as a limit of proper integrals) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-06002 (exponent rules in the antiderivative) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the improper integral that matches a series, antidifferentiate, evaluate between the lower limit and a variable upper bound, and take the limit of that expression, reporting a finite value or divergence.
skills.description_plain: Antidifferentiate, evaluate at the variable bound, and take the limit.
skills.name: Evaluate the improper integral using limit notation

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10008 (the integral test read as an evaluation rather than a comparison)
BC-MIS-10002 (a number reported as the series value)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10005 (the conclusion is the step the conditions and the integral were built for)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response states that the series converges because the matching improper integral converges, or diverges because the integral diverges, names which series the verdict is about, and makes no claim that the integral's value is the sum. BC-ERR-10013 and BC-ERR-10003 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The integral is evaluated to a finite number and that number is reported as the sum of the series, which is BC-ERR-10013, or the verdict is correct and no series is named where several appear in the part, which is BC-ERR-10003.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The correspondence between f of n and a sub n is not held, so the conclusion is drawn about the wrong object, which is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10008 (what the integral test transfers and what it does not) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-06005 (matching f of n to a sub n) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a convergent or divergent improper integral and the verified conditions, conclude that the series converges or diverges by the integral test, naming the series.
skills.description_plain: Report that the series behaves as the integral does, without claiming the two have the same value.
skills.name: Conclude convergence or divergence of the series from the integral

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10011 (the ratio test threshold of one carried into the limit comparison)
BC-SKL-10031 (the ratio of consecutive terms, a different quotient)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10006 (the setup point turns on limit notation and the reciprocal is accepted)
BC-QA-10015 (limit comparison applied at an endpoint)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response forms the quotient of a sub n by b sub n, or its reciprocal, and writes it inside limit notation as n increases without bound, with absolute value bars present when the claim concerns absolute convergence. BC-ERR-10017 and BC-ERR-10018 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The quotient is formed correctly and the limit symbol is omitted, so a value is asserted as the index grows, which is BC-ERR-10017, or the quotient is run on signed terms while absolute convergence is the claim, which is BC-ERR-10018.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The quotient of powers with the same base cannot be simplified, which is BC-PRQ-10007, or the limit of the resulting ratio cannot be evaluated, which is BC-PRQ-10004.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10011 (which quotient the limit comparison takes) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10007 (simplifying ratios of powers) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a series and a chosen comparison series, write the limit as n increases without bound of a sub n divided by b sub n, or its reciprocal, with limit notation present.
skills.description_plain: Write the limit of the quotient of the two general terms.
skills.name: Set up the limit comparison ratio with limit notation

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10011 (one treated as the deciding threshold in a limit comparison)
BC-SKL-10033 (the ratio test conclusion, where one is the threshold)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10006 (the explanation point requires the limit to be positive and the series named)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response evaluates the limit comparison ratio, states in words that it is positive and finite, and transfers the behaviour of b sub n to the series in question, naming that series in the conclusion. BC-ERR-10019 and BC-ERR-10003 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The ratio limit is evaluated correctly and then compared with one as though the ratio test were running, which is BC-SIG-10011 and BC-ERR-10019, or the transfer is made and the series concluded about is left unnamed, which is BC-ERR-10003.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The limit of the quotient cannot be evaluated, which is BC-PRQ-10004, so the criterion never gets a value to judge.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10011 (positive and finite against a comparison with one) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10004 (evaluating the quotient limit) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the value of the limit comparison ratio, state that it is positive and finite, and conclude that the series behaves as the comparison series does, naming the series concluded about.
skills.description_plain: Say that the limit is positive and finite, then transfer the behaviour of the comparison series.
skills.name: Conclude from a positive finite limit in a limit comparison

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10015 (absolute and conditional used as interchangeable labels)
BC-SKL-10027 (recognising the alternating factor, the step before)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10007 (the explanation point requires the absolute value bars to be visible)
BC-QA-10006 (limit comparison is the usual vehicle on the absolute value series)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response writes the series of absolute values of the terms with the sign factor removed, applies a named test to that series, and reports convergence or divergence of the absolute value series as a claim separate from any claim about the signed series; absolute value bars appear in the work. BC-ERR-10018 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A test is run and it is run on the signed terms while the claim made is about absolute convergence, which is BC-ERR-10018, or the absolute value series is written and the verdict never states which of the two series it concerns.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The alternating factor cannot be identified and removed from the general term, which is BC-PRQ-10008.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10015 (two distinct series, two distinct tests) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10008 (stripping the alternating factor) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a series with mixed signs, write the series of absolute values and apply an appropriate test to it, reporting convergence or divergence of that series.
skills.description_plain: Strip the signs and decide whether that series converges.
skills.name: Test the series of absolute values

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10015 (the two labels used interchangeably)
BC-SKL-10036 (the conditional case)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10007 (the classification and its referent are scored together)
BC-QA-10006 (the limit comparison that establishes the absolute value verdict)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response cites convergence of the series of absolute values and concludes that the original series converges absolutely, naming the series the label attaches to when several are in play. BC-ERR-10023 and BC-ERR-10003 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The absolute value series is shown to converge and the label written is conditional, which is BC-ERR-10023, or the label is right and the sentence does not say which series it describes, which is BC-SIG-10012 and BC-ERR-10003.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The absolute value series was never formed, so the label rests on a test of the signed series: that is BC-SKL-10034 rather than a classification gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10015 (what absolute convergence asserts) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-10034 (testing the absolute value series) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given that the series of absolute values converges, state that the original series converges absolutely, naming the series in question.
skills.description_plain: Say the series converges absolutely because the absolute value series converges.
skills.name: Classify a series as absolutely convergent

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10022 (an interval offered as a radius)
BC-SKL-10059 (the interval, which is the other request)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10014 (an interval presented without naming the radius does not earn the third point)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response names the radius as a single value, the distance from the centre to either end of the interior, and writes it as R equals that number rather than presenting an interval and stopping. BC-ERR-10036 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A correct interval is presented where the radius was requested and no value is named, which is BC-SIG-10008 and BC-ERR-10036, so the radius point is not earned although the underlying work is sound.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The solved inequality cannot be converted into a distance from the centre, which is BC-PRQ-10001.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10022 (radius as a distance, interval as a set) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10001 (reading the distance from the inequality) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the solved inequality, report the radius of convergence as the distance from the centre to an endpoint, presented explicitly as a value.
skills.description_plain: Name the radius as a number, not as an interval.
skills.name: State the radius of convergence explicitly

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01017 (an average over an interval read as the rate at a point inside it)
BC-SKL-01003 (instantaneous rate, which requires the limiting step this skill does not take)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01012 (average rates over shrinking intervals, where the quotient must be formed repeatedly and its structure is visible)
adaptive.mastered_if: The quotient of f(b) minus f(a) by b minus a is formed and evaluated for the interval the question names, from a formula and from a table of values, and the reported number carries the units of the quantity divided by the units of the input; the difference is never handed in as the rate (BC-ERR-01029 absent) and the interval endpoints match the rows the question specifies.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The correct pair of values is selected and subtracted but the division by b minus a is missing, which is BC-ERR-01029, or the quotient is set up correctly and the arithmetic in the division is wrong, which the 2014 Q4 commentary records as a computation loss inside a correct setup.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The values placed in the numerator come from the wrong input, or f and f prime are interchanged when reading the table, which is a function notation gap at BC-PRQ-06005 rather than a difficulty with the average rate.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01017 (an average rate describes a whole interval, not one instant) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-06005 (pulling f(b) and f(a) from the correct rows) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given f and an interval from a to b, compute the quotient of f(b) minus f(a) by b minus a.

common_confusions: BC-MIS-02008 (units treated as decoration)
BC-SKL-02015 (units of an estimated derivative, the same compound structure at an instant)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-02001 (the value with supporting work and the units are separately scored on a contextual table)
adaptive.mastered_if: The sentence names the modelled quantity, says that it changed on average at that many units per unit of the independent variable over the stated interval, and attaches the compound units of the quantity divided by the units of the input rather than the units of the quantity alone (BC-ERR-02003 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The value and the interval are reported correctly but the units are copied from the table header, so the compound form is missing, which is BC-ERR-02003 and costs a point that is scored independently of the value.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The average rate itself is wrong or reported as a difference, which is a BC-SKL-01001 gap rather than an interpretation failure.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-02008 (what the denominator of the quotient measures) for the conceptual failure; BC-SKL-01001 (computing the rate being interpreted) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts

common_confusions: BC-MIS-02001 (the difference reported as the rate)
BC-SKL-02001 (the increment form, which uses h)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-02001 (a table where the two inputs are named and the difference and the quotient must both appear)
adaptive.mastered_if: The quotient of f(x) minus f(a) by x minus a is formed for the two named inputs, evaluated to a number when values are supplied, and the numerator and denominator are taken in matching order so the sign of the result is right, with the division present in the work (BC-ERR-02001 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The two function values are subtracted correctly and the denominator is written as x rather than as x minus a, or the difference alone is reported, which is BC-ERR-02001.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The average rate over an interval cannot be computed from a formula or a table at all, which is a gap at BC-SKL-01001 rather than a difficulty with this notation.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-02001 (why the quotient and not the difference answers a rate question) for the conceptual failure; BC-SKL-01001 (forming an average rate over an interval) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08012 (limits treated as a viewing window rather than the boundary of the region)
BC-MIS-08003 (a calculator value treated as standing on its own)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08008 (the crossings are not exact values, so storing them is what protects the third decimal place)
adaptive.mastered_if: The equation of the two curves is solved with technology on the stated domain, the solutions are stored rather than transcribed as short decimals, and the stored values are used as the limits of the area integral; the reported area agrees to three places with a recomputation from the stored limits, and neither BC-ERR-08005 nor BC-ERR-08019 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The crossings are located correctly and then written and reused as two or three place decimals, so the reported area differs in the third decimal place, which is BC-ERR-08005 and exactly the observation in BC-SIG-08008; or the solver is run over a window that returns a crossing outside the region, which is BC-ERR-08019.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The stored value is reported rounded to the wrong number of places or rounded rather than truncated, which is BC-PRQ-08006 rather than a solving gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08012 (which inputs bound the region) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08006 (storing unrounded solutions before reusing them) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts

common_confusions: BC-MIS-04012 (the tangent line treated as the function near the point)
BC-SKL-04029 (evaluating the line rather than writing it)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-04008 (the line is the vehicle for the approximation, so an unchecked line propagates)
adaptive.mastered_if: The tangent line is written in point slope form using the coordinates of the point of tangency and the derivative value there, so the line passes through the point and its slope is the derivative rather than a coordinate; BC-ERR-04023 is absent, and the line is left in point slope form rather than rearranged into an error prone simplified form.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The slope at the point of tangency is right and the line written does not pass through the point, signal BC-SIG-04016 and BC-ERR-04023; the 2025 report records sign and parenthesis errors arising while isolating the dependent variable, which the question did not require.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The slope was never obtained from the supplied derivative, a gap at BC-SKL-04032; or point slope form itself is unavailable, BC-PRQ-04006.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-04012 (the line touches the curve at the point and departs from it elsewhere). Procedural failure: BC-PRQ-04006 (assembling point slope form correctly).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a point on a curve and the value of the derivative there, write the equation of the tangent line in point-slope form.

skills.notation: point-slope form of the tangent line

common_confusions: BC-MIS-04012 (the tangent value read as the function value)
BC-SKL-04030 (judging the direction of the error rather than producing the estimate)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-04008 (a nearby input distinct from the point of tangency is named in the prompt)
adaptive.mastered_if: The tangent line is evaluated at the nearby input, not at the point of tangency, and the result is reported as an approximation of the function value there; BC-ERR-04024 is absent, so the known function value is not returned as the answer, and the anchor of the line is the point whose data the stem supplies.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The line is correct and is evaluated at the point of tangency, BC-ERR-04024; or, as the 2023 Q3 part B distinctions record, the slope and the initial value are exchanged so the approximation is built on the wrong number.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The tangent line itself does not pass through the point, a gap at BC-SKL-04028 with signal BC-SIG-04016.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-04012 (the line approximates the function away from the point). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-04028 (a line anchored at the correct point of tangency).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the tangent line at a point and a nearby input, evaluate the line at that input and report the result as an approximation of the function value there.
skills.description_plain: Put the nearby input into the tangent line equation.
skills.name: Approximate a function value with the tangent line
skills.notation: tangent line value as an approximation

common_confusions: BC-MIS-04012 (the roles of the point and the nearby input blurred)
BC-SKL-03011 (evaluating dy/dx at a point on an implicit curve, the same substitution in Unit 3)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-04008 (the derivative expression is supplied and the point of tangency must be chosen correctly)
adaptive.mastered_if: The coordinates of the point of tangency are substituted into the supplied derivative expression, including both coordinates when the expression comes from an implicitly defined curve, giving the slope at that point and no other; BC-ERR-04027 is absent, so the derivative is not evaluated at the target input.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The supplied derivative is used correctly and evaluated at coordinates other than the point of tangency, BC-ERR-04027, a state in which the approximation point may still follow on the wrong slope; or only one coordinate of an implicit expression is substituted.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Substitution into an expression in two variables fails, an algebra gap at BC-PRQ-04006 rather than a tangency gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-04012 (the slope belongs to the point of tangency). Procedural failure: BC-PRQ-04006 (substituting both coordinates into the expression).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an expression for the derivative, which may involve both coordinates of an implicitly defined curve, substitute the coordinates of the point of tangency to obtain the slope of the tangent line there.
skills.description_plain: Substitute the point into the given derivative to get the slope.
skills.name: Use a supplied derivative expression to obtain the slope at the point of tangency
skills.notation: slope from a supplied derivative

common_confusions: BC-MIS-02014 (height and slope exchanged at the point of tangency)
BC-SKL-02012 (the interpretation, which this skill carries into an equation)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-02011 (the slope, the point, and the equation carry separate credit, so each substitution is visible)
adaptive.mastered_if: The function is differentiated, the derivative is evaluated at the point of tangency to give the slope (BC-ERR-02028 absent), the function is evaluated at the same input to give the height, and the line is written in point slope form through that point with that slope (BC-ERR-02027 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The derivative is evaluated correctly but the line is written through a point other than the point of tangency, which is BC-SIG-02016, or the slope arithmetic is wrong while the line still passes through the given point, which the 2015 commentary records as a separable arithmetic loss.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The point slope form cannot be assembled from a slope and a point, which is a gap at BC-PRQ-02003, and using the height as the slope is a BC-SKL-02012 gap in the interpretation.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-02014 (the two evaluations and their roles) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-02003 (writing the line through a point with a given slope) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: isolated by BC-QA-02011
skills.description_formal: Given a function and a point on its graph, compute the derivative at that input, and write the tangent line in point slope form using that slope and the point of tangency.
skills.description_plain: Use the derivative value as the slope and the point of tangency in the point slope form.
skills.name: Write the equation of the line tangent to a curve at a given point

common_confusions: BC-MIS-09014 (the derivative of r read as the speed along the curve)
BC-MIS-09015 (the slope of a polar curve taken to be the derivative of r)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-09009 (the rate of change of r at a stated angle, so both the differentiation and its display are scored)
adaptive.mastered_if: The polar equation is differentiated with respect to theta, the differentiation appearing as a written expression, and that derivative is then evaluated at the stated angle in radian mode and reported to the required accuracy; neither BC-ERR-09028 nor BC-ERR-09006 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A correct decimal for dr/dtheta appears with nothing on the page showing that r was differentiated, which is BC-ERR-09028 and the observation in BC-SIG-09010; or the derivative is shown and a stored value is truncated before a later step, which is BC-ERR-09006.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The calculator is left in degree measure so the evaluated derivative is wrong although the differentiation is right, which is BC-PRQ-09003.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-09014 (what dr/dtheta measures) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-09003 (radian mode for the evaluation) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Differentiate r as a function of theta, evaluate the derivative at a given angle, and present the differentiation together with the value.
skills.description_plain: Differentiate r with respect to the angle and substitute.
skills.name: Compute dr/dtheta for a polar curve and evaluate it

common_confusions: BC-MIS-03012 (rule selected by visual pattern)
BC-SKL-03028 (ordering several rules once each has been named)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-03009 (rule choice is the scored decision, separate from executing the rule)
adaptive.mastered_if: Given a classified expression the response names the rule that structure requires, choosing among the power, product, quotient, chain, inverse function, and inverse trigonometric rules, and the choice follows the classification rather than the surface pattern, so an exponential term is not given the power rule; BC-ERR-03019 and BC-ERR-99036 are absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The structure is classified correctly and the rule named for it is the neighbouring one, such as the power rule for an exponential term with the exponent decremented, BC-ERR-99036, which then propagates into every later part that uses the derivative.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The classification itself is wrong, a gap at BC-SKL-03026 rather than in the mapping from structure to rule.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-03012 (a rule belongs to a type of function, not to a shape). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-03026 (naming the outermost operation first).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts

skills.description_plain: Match the structure you found to the rule that handles it.
skills.name: Select the differentiation rule that the classification indicates
skills.notation: rule selection

common_confusions: BC-MIS-09014 (the derivative of r read as the speed along the curve)
BC-SKL-09031 (the interpretation of dr/dtheta alone)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-09010 (an angular rate is supplied, so the missing factor changes both the number and the units)
adaptive.mastered_if: The rate at which the distance from the origin changes with time is written as dr/dtheta multiplied by dtheta/dt, both factors present and evaluated at the stated angle, and the reported rate carries units of distance per unit time; BC-ERR-09030 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The derivative dr/dtheta is computed correctly and reported as the time rate, the angular rate never entering the product, which is BC-ERR-09030.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The chain rule combined with a product or quotient is not available, so the composite rate cannot be assembled, which is BC-SKL-03006; reading which given number is dtheta/dt is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-09014 (why the angular rate enters the time derivative) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-03006 (the chain rule product) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: For a particle travelling along a polar curve with a given rate of change of theta with respect to time, compute the rate of change of its distance from the origin as the product of dr/dtheta and dtheta/dt.
skills.description_plain: Multiply dr/dtheta by the rate at which the angle changes.
skills.name: Relate the rate of the distance from the origin in time to dr/dtheta

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06007 (the plotted curve is taken to be the function under discussion, so features of g are read off the integrand)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06003 (accumulation function analysed from a graph of the integrand made of segments and circular arcs)
adaptive.mastered_if: Intervals of increase for g are given as the intervals where the plotted f lies above the axis, and intervals of decrease where f lies below, with the reason phrased about the graph of f rather than about g. The Fundamental Theorem step is visible, so g prime is written equal to f before any sign reading, and the answer is confined to the stated domain. The confusion recorded as BC-ERR-06008, reading features of g straight off the visible features of the plotted curve, is absent, and positivity of f is kept separate from f rising.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Correct intervals arrive with a reason phrased about g itself, which BC-FRQ-2014-Q3-B and BC-FRQ-2018-Q3-C both record as a referent failure that costs the reason point while the answer point stands. Another intermediate state gives only the intervals of increase when both halves were asked for, or extends the intervals past the stated subinterval, which BC-FRQ-2024-Q4-B lists as a domain slip. Partial forms of BC-ERR-06008, where the zeros of g are reported instead of the intervals of increase, show the function and its derivative being exchanged in one part while other parts stay correct.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: BC-SKL-06018 is missing when the response never writes g prime equal to f, so the sign reading is applied to whichever curve is in front of it. The tell-tale sign is that the sign analysis itself is competent while the object it is applied to is wrong.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06007 (separating the plotted integrand from the accumulation function defined by it) for the conceptual failure; when the referent is right and only the written reason is loose, the target is BC-ERR-06008 (tying the stated reason to the given graph of f)

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the graph of f and g(x) = the integral from a to x of f(t) dt, determine the intervals on which g increases or decreases by identifying where f is positive or negative.

common_confusions: BC-MIS-02012 (the two numerator terms treated as interchangeable)
BC-SKL-02039 (the full rule, of which this is the ordering requirement)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-02008 (a quotient whose simplified result reveals a sign reversal directly)
adaptive.mastered_if: The rule is written with the term containing the derivative of the numerator first and the term containing the derivative of the denominator subtracted from it, and a reversed version is identified as producing a derivative of the opposite sign (BC-ERR-02021 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The order is correct in the statement of the rule but reversed when values are substituted, so the sign of the reported derivative is wrong while the structure is intact.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The quotient rule cannot be written at all, which is a gap at BC-SKL-02039 rather than an ordering slip.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-02012 (checking the rule against a reciprocal whose derivative is already known) for the conceptual failure; BC-SKL-02039 (writing the rule) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: State and apply the quotient rule with the term containing the derivative of the numerator first, and identify a sign error produced by reversing the two terms.
skills.description_plain: Put the subtraction the right way round.
