common_confusions: BC-MIS-04004 (the three motion functions stored separately)
BC-SKL-04010 (comparing the signs of velocity and acceleration rather than producing acceleration)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-04003 (acceleration at an instant, from a velocity supplied by formula or by table)
adaptive.mastered_if: The velocity function is differentiated once to give acceleration, and where velocity is supplied by table rather than formula an average rate over the bracketing rows is used instead, with the result evaluated at the stated time; BC-ERR-04006 is absent, so the reported quantity matches the order of differentiation requested.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The differentiation is correct and one order off, so the velocity value is reported where its rate was wanted, the state the 2015 Q3 part C distinctions call a skipped differentiation; or a second differentiation is performed where one was asked for, BC-ERR-04006 with signal BC-SIG-04004.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Velocity itself is not available because the position function was not differentiated, a gap at BC-SKL-04006.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-04004 (acceleration is the derivative of velocity). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-04006 (tracking how many differentiations have been performed).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the velocity of a particle as a function of time, differentiate to produce the acceleration function, and evaluate it at a stated time when asked.
skills.description_plain: Differentiate the velocity function once.
skills.name: Differentiate a velocity function to obtain acceleration
skills.notation: a of t equals the derivative of v of t

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01016 (an existence theorem read as locating or counting solutions)
BC-SKL-05001 (the Mean Value Theorem, the theorem about rates rather than values)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01011 (continuity with its reason, the straddling values, and the conclusion are separately scored)
adaptive.mastered_if: Both hypotheses are stated, that f is continuous on the closed interval from a to b and that the target value d lies between f(a) and f(b), and the theorem is named as the Intermediate Value Theorem rather than as another existence theorem (BC-ERR-01028 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The straddling condition on the target is stated while the continuity hypothesis is omitted, or the conclusion of the theorem is described in place of its hypotheses, so what must hold before use is incomplete.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The closed interval of the hypothesis and the open interval of the conclusion are not distinguished in notation, which is a gap at BC-PRQ-01010.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01016 (what the theorem asserts and what it does not) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-01010 (closed against open interval notation) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: State that the theorem requires f continuous on the closed interval from a to b and a target value d between f(a) and f(b).
skills.description_plain: Name continuity on a closed interval and the target value lying between the endpoint values.
skills.name: State the hypotheses of the Intermediate Value Theorem

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01015 (a hypothesis treated as supplied by the setting of the question)
BC-MIS-01010 (the definition restated in place of a reason)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01011 (a bare statement of continuity does not earn the point, so the reason is the scored behaviour)
adaptive.mastered_if: Continuity on the closed interval is derived from a stated property, most often that the function is differentiable and therefore continuous, and that reason is written in the response, so continuity is never asserted bare (BC-ERR-01025 absent) nor supported by restating the definition of continuity (BC-ERR-01016 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The two attained values that straddle the target are displayed correctly while the continuity statement carries no reason, which is BC-SIG-01013 and, in the 2025 guidelines, loses the continuity point while leaving the conclusion point available.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The function cannot be placed in a family continuous on its domain, or the excluded inputs are not known, which is a domain gap at BC-PRQ-01008, and being unable to state the three conditions at all is a BC-SKL-01043 gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01015 (what in the question establishes continuity) for the conceptual failure; BC-SKL-01043 (the conditions the reason is discharging) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Establish continuity of the function on the closed interval from the stated properties of the function, such as differentiability or membership of a family continuous on its domain, and record the reason in the response.
skills.description_plain: Say why the function is continuous on the interval, with a reason.
skills.name: Verify the continuity hypothesis before applying the theorem

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01016 (the theorem applied without checking where the target lies)
BC-SKL-01065 (the continuity hypothesis, the other condition of the same theorem)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01011 (displaying the two straddling values is a separately scored step in the expected path)
adaptive.mastered_if: The two attained values are displayed and the inequality placing the target strictly between them is written out, drawn from the tabulated or computed values the question supplies, so the straddling is exhibited rather than implied (BC-ERR-01026 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Continuity is established with its reason but the two bracketing values are never displayed, which is BC-SIG-01014, or the values are quoted without the inequality that places the target between them.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Strict and non strict inequalities on an interval are not distinguished, so the target is placed at an endpoint value, which is a gap at BC-PRQ-01010, and being unable to state the hypotheses at all is a BC-SKL-01064 gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01016 (the condition on the target value) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-01010 (writing the strict inequality) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Display the inequality placing the target value strictly between the values of the function at the two endpoints of the interval.
skills.description_plain: Show the wanted output sits between the two endpoint outputs.
skills.name: Verify that the target value lies between the endpoint values

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01016 (an existence theorem read as locating or counting solutions)
BC-SKL-05001 (the Mean Value Theorem, which is about a derivative value)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01011 (the conclusion with the theorem named is scored apart from the hypotheses)
adaptive.mastered_if: The conclusion states that there is at least one input strictly between a and b at which f takes the target value, uses the open interval named in the question, and names the Intermediate Value Theorem correctly, with no claim that the input is unique (BC-ERR-01027 absent) and no other existence theorem named (BC-ERR-01028 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: All hypotheses are verified and the conclusion is stated, but the response claims exactly one input gives the target value, which is BC-SIG-01015 and BC-ERR-01027, so the argument is sound and the claim exceeds it.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The conclusion is stated on the closed interval where the theorem gives an interior point, which is an interval notation gap at BC-PRQ-01010, and a missing continuity reason sits at BC-SKL-01065 rather than in the conclusion.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01016 (existence without uniqueness) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-01010 (stating the conclusion on the open interval) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Conclude that there is at least one number c strictly between a and b with f(c) equal to the target value, and state the conclusion using the interval named in the question.
skills.description_plain: Say that at least one input in the open interval gives the wanted output.
skills.name: State the conclusion of the theorem with the correct interval

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01015 (hypotheses assumed to be supplied by the stem)
BC-MIS-01016 (uniqueness read into the conclusion)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01011 (a function given by a table, where row selection, the continuity reason, and the conclusion are all visible)
adaptive.mastered_if: Two tabulated inputs whose outputs straddle the target are selected, continuity is stated with the reason that the function is differentiable, the straddling inequality is displayed from the table, and the conclusion names the theorem and an input in the open interval between those two rows (BC-ERR-01025 and BC-ERR-01026 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The correct pair of rows is chosen and the inequality shown while continuity is asserted with no basis, which is BC-ERR-01025, or continuity is justified and the bracketing rows are never displayed, which is BC-ERR-01026.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The conclusion cannot be stated on the correct open interval, which is BC-SKL-01067 and BC-PRQ-01010, rather than a failure to read the table.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01015 (deriving continuity from the stated differentiability) for the conceptual failure; BC-SKL-01066 (displaying the straddling values from the table) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given selected values of a function stated to be differentiable or continuous, select two tabulated inputs whose outputs straddle the target value, state continuity with its reason, and conclude existence of an input with that output.
skills.description_plain: Use two table rows that straddle the target value, having first established continuity.
skills.name: Apply the Intermediate Value Theorem to a function given by a table

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06001 (a Riemann sum treated as a sum of the listed values)
BC-MIS-06004 (a trapezoid treated as a rectangle at the average height of the whole interval)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06002 (trapezoidal approximation of an accumulated amount from a table)
adaptive.mastered_if: Every subinterval gets its own trapezoid. The learner averages the two endpoint values of f on that subinterval, multiplies by that subinterval's width, and adds, so a three-term sum shows three products of two factors each with the one half already incorporated, and the result sits between the left and the right sum rather than equalling their plain total. Widths come from differences of consecutive inputs, so BC-ERR-06001 (a single common width) and BC-ERR-06004 (the one half applied to only some terms) are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: BC-SIG-06005 is the clearest intermediate state, a trapezoidal answer equal to the sum of the left and right sums, which asking for a single trapezoid area resolves as a dropped factor rather than a missing formula. BC-ERR-06004 appears as one or two terms halved and one not, which by sg-25:13 can leave the form point standing while the value point goes. BC-FRQ-2025-Q3-C also records the one half applied once to the whole sum, collapsing the per-subinterval structure, and BC-FRQ-2018-Q4-C records a correct sum reported without the division that an average value requires.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Where the area of one trapezoid from its two parallel sides and its width is itself wrong, the break is BC-PRQ-06007 and not the sum rule. Where the trapezoid areas are right and the widths are all the same number on an uneven table, the break is BC-PRQ-06012.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06004 (the single trapezoid on the first subinterval) for the conceptual failure. A dropped or misplaced factor of one half with the structure otherwise intact points instead to BC-ERR-06004 and to BC-PRQ-06007 (the trapezoid area formula).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given selected values of f at partition points, approximate the integral as the sum over subintervals of the average of the two endpoint values of f multiplied by the width of that subinterval.
skills.description_plain: Average the two endpoint values on each subinterval, multiply by the width, and add.
skills.name: Compute a trapezoidal sum from a table of values

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08006 (the integral of a rate read as the amount of the quantity)
BC-SKL-08006 (displacement, which is the integral alone)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08003 (a position value is requested from an initial condition)
BC-QA-08004 (the same structure with a contextual rate rather than a velocity)
adaptive.mastered_if: Position at time b is written as the given position at time a plus the definite integral of velocity from a to b, the initial value appearing as an explicit term in the expression rather than only in words, and the reported coordinate changes when the initial position changes; BC-ERR-08011 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The definite integral of velocity between the two times is evaluated correctly and reported as the position, the known value at the earlier time never entering the expression, which is BC-ERR-08011 and the state observed in BC-SIG-08004.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The pattern initial value plus accumulated change is not available in the simpler unit 6 setting either, which is BC-SKL-06037 rather than a motion gap; reading which symbol carries the initial position is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08006 (that the integral gives change and not the amount) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-06037 (assembling final value from initial value and accumulation) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an initial position at time a and a velocity function, evaluate the position at time b as the initial position plus the definite integral of velocity from a to b.
skills.description_plain: Add the accumulated change to the starting position.
skills.name: Determine a position value from an initial position and velocity

common_confusions: BC-MIS-04008 (differentiation assumed to be with respect to a length)
BC-MIS-04010 (the rates expected to settle the answer without a relation)
BC-SKL-04013 (naming a quantity in a single variable context)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-04006 (several dimensions change at once, so which rate is given and which is wanted must be recorded)
adaptive.mastered_if: Each varying quantity is named as a function of time, the supplied rates are written in derivative notation such as dV/dt, and the requested rate is written in the same notation, so given and wanted are separated on the page before any equation appears; BC-ERR-04015 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The scenario is restated in words with no quantity appearing as a derivative with respect to time, signal BC-SIG-04011; or the rate supplied in the stem is offered as the answer, BC-ERR-04015.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The scenario cannot be read into quantities and rates at all, a contextual translation gap at BC-PRQ-04008 rather than a related rates gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-04008 (every varying quantity is a function of time). Procedural failure: BC-ERR-04015 (writing each supplied rate in derivative notation).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a related rates scenario, name each varying quantity as a function of time, record the rates supplied in derivative notation, and record the rate requested in the same notation.
skills.description_plain: List the changing quantities, the rates you are told, and the rate you are asked for.
skills.name: Identify the variables and which rates are given and wanted
skills.notation: dV/dt given, dr/dt wanted

common_confusions: BC-MIS-04008 (the habit of differentiating with respect to x carried in)
BC-MIS-04009 (a mixed term read as one symbol)
BC-SKL-03009 (implicit differentiation with respect to x rather than t)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-04007 (an eligible attempt and a completely correct differentiation are scored separately)
adaptive.mastered_if: The defining equation of the curve is differentiated with respect to time so that every term in x contributes dx/dt and every term in y contributes dy/dt, with the product rule on any mixed term, giving an equation in both rates; BC-ERR-04017 and BC-ERR-04018 are absent, which is what makes the differentiation completely correct rather than merely eligible.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The curve is differentiated with respect to x instead of time, so dy/dx appears where dy/dt was needed, BC-ERR-04017 with signal BC-SIG-04013; or the differentiation is with respect to time and a mixed term loses one of its two rate factors, BC-ERR-04018.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Differentiating any relation with respect to time is not established, a gap at BC-SKL-04019; or the implicit differentiation of the curve fails independently of time.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-04008 (both coordinates are functions of time along the path). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-04019 (the d/dt sweep across every term).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a curve defined implicitly and a particle moving along it, differentiate the defining equation with respect to time so that every term in x contributes dx/dt and every term in y contributes dy/dt.
skills.description_plain: Treat both coordinates as functions of time and differentiate the curve equation with respect to t.
skills.name: Differentiate an implicitly defined curve with respect to time
skills.notation: dx/dt and dy/dt in the same equation

common_confusions: BC-MIS-04011 (instantaneous values treated as permanent)
BC-SKL-04025 (reporting the rate with units and direction once it is found)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-04006 (the isolated rate is the final scoring point of the part)
BC-QA-04007 (the second coordinate rate is solved for at the stated point)
adaptive.mastered_if: The instantaneous values and the supplied rates are substituted into the differentiated equation and the requested derivative is isolated, so a number rather than an equation is reported; BC-ERR-04021 is absent, and where a chain of two rates is needed the product of the intermediate derivative and the supplied rate is formed as the 2025 Q2 part D scoring describes.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The substitution is complete and the response stops before solving for the requested rate, BC-ERR-04021 with signal BC-SIG-04015, leaving the differentiation points earned and the final point lost; or the supplied rate is reported in place of the answer.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The equation to substitute into is wrong because values were substituted too early, a gap at BC-SKL-04023; or a value needed for the substitution was never recovered, BC-SKL-04026.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-04011 (the substituted numbers describe one instant only). Procedural failure: BC-PRQ-04007 (isolating a single unknown in a linear equation).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the differentiated relating equation with the instantaneous values supplied, substitute and solve for the requested derivative.
skills.description_plain: Put the known numbers in and isolate the rate you were asked for.
skills.name: Solve the differentiated equation for the unknown rate
skills.notation: solving for the requested rate

common_confusions: BC-MIS-04011 (instantaneous values treated as permanent features)
BC-SKL-04021 (eliminating a variable before differentiating rather than recovering its value after)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-04006 (one substitution value is deliberately withheld from the stem)
adaptive.mastered_if: A quantity needed for the substitution but absent from the stem is computed from the relating equation using the values that are supplied, such as recovering a diameter from a height, before the numerical work proceeds; BC-ERR-04022 is absent, so no value is invented and none is silently omitted.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The differentiated equation is correct and the missing quantity is left out of the substitution or replaced by a guessed number, BC-ERR-04022, the failure the 2018 Q4 part D distinctions name as never recovering the diameter from the height.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The relating equation from which the value would come is wrong or absent, a gap at BC-SKL-04018; or the equation cannot be solved for the missing quantity, BC-PRQ-04007.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-04010 (the relating equation also supplies missing values). Procedural failure: BC-PRQ-04007 (solving the relation for the absent quantity).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a related rates problem in which one quantity needed for the substitution is not supplied, compute it from the relating equation using the values that are supplied.
skills.description_plain: When a needed value is not given, get it from the relating equation at that instant.
skills.name: Compute a missing instantaneous value from the relating equation
skills.notation: value recovered from the relating equation

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08011 (the order of subtraction in an area integrand treated as immaterial)
BC-MIS-08010 (the area between curves read as the integral of the bounding curve alone)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08008 (a shaded region between two graphs, where the order decides the sign of the result)
adaptive.mastered_if: One curve is named as the greater on the interval, supported either by evaluating both functions at an interior input and comparing the two values or by reading the figure, and that decision then fixes the order of subtraction in the integrand; BC-ERR-08020 does not follow, and the area reported from the resulting integral is positive.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Both functions are evaluated correctly at the test input and the integrand is still written lower minus upper, so the integral value is negative, which is BC-ERR-08020 and the state observed in BC-SIG-08007.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Substituting the test input into the two expressions is itself done wrongly, so the comparison rests on wrong values, which is BC-PRQ-06005 rather than an ordering gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08011 (why the order of subtraction is part of the claim and not a sign to repair later) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-08019 (writing the integrand once the order is fixed) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given two functions and an interval, determine which function is greater on that interval by evaluating a test input or by reading the given figure.
skills.description_plain: Decide which graph is on top before writing the difference.
skills.name: Identify which curve is upper on an interval

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08011 (the order of subtraction treated as immaterial)
BC-MIS-08010 (the area between curves read as the integral of one bounding curve)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08008 (a numerical area must be produced from the written integral)
adaptive.mastered_if: The area integral is evaluated either by an antiderivative with the limits substituted in the correct variable or with technology, and a nonnegative number is reported as the area; when a substitution is used the limits are converted to the new variable or the antiderivative is returned to the original one, and neither BC-ERR-08021 nor BC-ERR-08022 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The reversed difference is written and then set equal to the positive area, so a correct number sits under an incorrect equality, which is BC-ERR-08021; or an antiderivative found by substitution is evaluated at the original limits, which is BC-ERR-08022; the negative value reported without comment is BC-SIG-08007.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The antiderivative itself is wrong because a fractional or negative exponent is mishandled, which is BC-PRQ-06002; evaluating a definite integral by antidifferentiation and endpoint substitution at all is BC-SKL-06034.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08011 (why a negative value cannot be relabelled as the area) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-06034 (evaluating with correctly converted limits) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Evaluate the area integral by an antiderivative or with technology and report a nonnegative value as the area of the region.
skills.description_plain: Antidifferentiate or use technology, then state the area.
skills.name: Evaluate an area integral and report the area

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08023 (the upper curve assumed to give the outer radius)
BC-MIS-08017 (the difference of squares equated to the square of the difference)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08013 (the region is separated from its axis, so both radii exist and can be exchanged)
adaptive.mastered_if: The two boundary curves are compared by their distance from the axis of revolution on the interval, the farther one is assigned the outer radius and the nearer one the inner radius, and the assignment is supported by a value at an interior input; the resulting integrand is nonnegative, and BC-ERR-08040 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Both radii are written as distances to the axis and the roles are exchanged, so the integral returns a negative number that is reported or silently made positive, which is BC-ERR-08040 and the observation in BC-SIG-08016.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Neither radius is written as a distance to the axis in the first place, which is BC-PRQ-08004 rather than an assignment gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08023 (that distance from the axis, not height in the plane, assigns the roles) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08004 (measuring each radius to the axis) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a region between two curves and an axis of revolution, determine which curve is farther from the axis on the interval and assign the outer and inner radii accordingly.
skills.description_plain: The curve farther from the axis gives the outer radius.
skills.name: Identify the outer and inner radii of a washer

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08017 (the difference of squares equated to the square of the difference)
BC-MIS-08023 (the upper curve assumed to give the outer radius)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08013 (the ring area is the entire content of the integrand, so the two forms are directly comparable)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response states that the ring area is pi times the outer radius squared minus pi times the inner radius squared and uses that form, and it can show with two numerical radii that this differs from pi times the square of their difference by the cross term; BC-ERR-08030 is absent wherever a washer integrand is written.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The washer is described correctly in words as a disc with a hole and the integrand written is still the square of the difference of the radii, which is BC-ERR-08030 and the not mastered observation in BC-SIG-08014.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Expanding the square of a binomial loses the cross term, so the two expressions look identical algebraically, which is BC-PRQ-06002 rather than a washer gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08017 (the ring as the difference of two disc areas) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-06002 (expanding a squared binomial correctly) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: State and use the fact that the ring area is pi times the outer radius squared minus pi times the inner radius squared, which is not pi times the square of the difference of the radii.
skills.description_plain: Square each radius first, then subtract.
skills.name: Subtract the squares of the radii rather than squaring their difference

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08021 (the radius taken as the function value whatever the axis is)
BC-MIS-08023 (the upper curve assumed to give the outer radius)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08013 (two radii and a shifted horizontal axis, so shift and assignment can fail separately)
adaptive.mastered_if: For revolution about y equal to k, the outer radius is written as the distance from the farther curve to the line and the inner radius as the distance from the nearer curve to the line, each as a difference containing k and each nonnegative on the interval; neither BC-ERR-08038 nor BC-ERR-08040 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Both radii are shifted by k and the roles are exchanged, which is BC-ERR-08040 with the negative value recorded in BC-SIG-08016; or the roles are right and the radii are written as bare function values with no k, which is BC-ERR-08038 and BC-SIG-08015.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The distance from a curve to a horizontal line is not formed as a subtraction, which is BC-PRQ-08004 rather than a washer gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08021 (radii as distances to the stated line) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08004 (writing each distance as a difference) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: For revolution about y equal k, write the outer radius as the distance from the farther curve to the line and the inner radius as the distance from the nearer curve to the line.
skills.description_plain: Subtract the line value from each curve before squaring.
skills.name: Write both washer radii as distances from a horizontal line

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08023 (the upper curve assumed to give the outer radius)
BC-MIS-08021 (the radius taken as the function value whatever the axis is)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08013 (the axis lies above the region, so position and distance disagree)
adaptive.mastered_if: The distances from both boundary curves to the axis of revolution are compared on the interval, and the farther curve is named the outer radius even when the axis lies above the region and the upper curve is the nearer one; the comparison is supported at an interior input, and BC-ERR-08040 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Both distances are written correctly and the outer role is given to the upper curve by position in the plane rather than by distance, which is BC-ERR-08040 and produces the negative integrand observed in BC-SIG-08016.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The distance from each curve to the axis is not expressed as a difference, so no comparison is possible, which is BC-PRQ-08004.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08023 (that the axis, not the plane, decides outer and inner) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-08052 (writing both radii as distances before comparing) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Compare the distances from each boundary curve to the axis of revolution on the interval to assign the outer and inner radii, noting that revolving about a line above the region reverses the roles.
skills.description_plain: Check which curve is farther from the line, which can differ from which is higher.
skills.name: Determine which boundary curve is farther from the shifted axis

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08017 (the difference of squares equated to the square of the difference)
BC-MIS-08021 (the radius taken as the function value whatever the axis is)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08013 (a shifted axis with two radii, where the shift and the squaring order are independent)
adaptive.mastered_if: The volume is written as pi times the definite integral of the square of the shifted outer radius minus the square of the shifted inner radius, each radius containing the line of revolution and each squared before the subtraction, over the unshifted interval; neither BC-ERR-08030 nor BC-ERR-08038 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Both radii carry the shift and the integrand is the square of their difference, which is BC-ERR-08030 and BC-SIG-08014; or the difference of squares is correct and the radii are the bare function values, which is BC-ERR-08038 with BC-SIG-08015 as its form.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The distances to the axis are not formed as differences, so both squares are of the wrong quantities, which is BC-PRQ-08004.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08017 (the ring area as a difference of two disc areas) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-08052 (writing both shifted radii) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Write the volume as pi times the definite integral of the square of the shifted outer radius minus the square of the shifted inner radius over the spanning interval.
skills.description_plain: Integrate pi times the difference of the squares of the two shifted radii.
skills.name: Set up the washer integral about a line other than an axis

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08024 (every definite integral read as an area)
BC-SKL-09011 (the parametric length integral, which combines two derivatives)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08014 (the arc length integral must be stated, so the integrand form is the whole answer)
adaptive.mastered_if: The length of the graph of f on [a,b] is stated as the definite integral of the square root of one plus the square of f prime with respect to x, the added one inside the radical and the derivative squared under it, with the limits taken from the interval; BC-ERR-08041 is absent, and the expression is named as a length rather than an area.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: An integral over the correct interval is written with the radical present and the added one missing, or with the derivative under the radical but not squared, which is BC-ERR-08041 in its two recorded forms.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The magnitude of a two component quantity is not formed by the Pythagorean relation, so the radical is not reconstructed, which is BC-PRQ-08007 rather than an arc length gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08024 (what the radical integrand measures) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08007 (the Pythagorean magnitude the integrand comes from) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a differentiable function and an interval, write the definite integral of the square root of one plus the square of the derivative over that interval as the length of the curve.
skills.description_plain: Write the integral of the square root of one plus the derivative squared.
skills.name: State the arc length integral for a function on an interval

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08024 (every definite integral read as an area)
BC-SKL-08056 (stating the general formula rather than instantiating it)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08014 (a specific function on a specific interval, so the substitution and the limits are both visible)
adaptive.mastered_if: The given function is differentiated, the derivative is squared and placed under the radical with the added one, and the limits are the endpoints of the interval described in the stem; the derivative is squared as a whole, and neither BC-ERR-08042 nor BC-ERR-08019 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The derivative is computed correctly and substituted under the radical without being squared, which is BC-ERR-08042; or the integrand is assembled correctly while the limits come from inputs other than the described interval, which is BC-ERR-08019.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The derivative itself is wrong, or the function is not differentiable at a point inside the interval and that is not noticed, which is BC-SKL-02021 and evaluation by antidifferentiation is BC-SKL-06034; misreading the interval from the stem is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08024 (what the assembled integral measures) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-08056 (the integrand the substitution feeds) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Differentiate the given function, substitute the derivative into the arc length integrand, and attach the limits taken from the described interval.
skills.description_plain: Differentiate the given function and place it inside the radical.
skills.name: Set up an arc length integral from a described curve

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10003 (the geometric closed form used whenever terms shrink)
BC-MIS-10004 (the first term assumed to sit at index zero)
BC-SKL-10018 (p-series form mistaken for geometric form)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10003 (the closed form is requested, so a and r have to be named before anything else)
BC-QA-10001 (test selection turns on whether the ratio is constant)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response divides consecutive terms, shows the quotient is the same constant for every index, and reports both the first term as the series is actually written and that common ratio; the ratio equals the quotient of consecutive terms rather than a coefficient or an exponent read off the general term. BC-ERR-10004 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A constant ratio is recognised and the number named as r is the base of the power or the leading coefficient rather than the quotient of consecutive terms, which is BC-ERR-10004, or r is correct and the first term is taken from the index zero position when the sigma starts elsewhere.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Consecutive terms cannot be produced from the sigma at all, which is BC-PRQ-10008, or the quotient is formed and mis-simplified, which is BC-PRQ-10005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10003 (a constant quotient as what makes a series geometric) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10005 (computing a common ratio) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a series in expanded or sigma form, divide consecutive terms, confirm the quotient is constant, and report the first term of the series as written together with the common ratio.
skills.description_plain: Check that consecutive terms share a constant quotient and name a and r.
skills.name: Identify a series as geometric and state its first term and ratio

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10004 (the sum formula read as requiring the index zero term)
BC-MIS-10002 (a partial sum offered as the value)
BC-SKL-10009 (the shifted-index case)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10003 (the closed form is the scored object)
BC-QA-10002 (a value is requested and a partial sum earns nothing)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response forms the quotient of the first term as written over one minus r and reports the value, leaving it unsimplified where the prompt supplies the closed form; the numerator is the term the series actually begins with and the denominator carries one minus the ratio rather than one plus it.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The pair a and r is correct and the sum is built from the index zero term although the sigma begins elsewhere, which is BC-ERR-10006, or the first several terms are added instead of the closed form being applied, which is BC-ERR-10002.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The common ratio cannot be extracted from the terms, which is BC-PRQ-10005; the sum formula is then applied to numbers that were never a and r.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10004 (which term the formula calls a) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10005 (ratio extraction) for the procedural case

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10003 (closed form used with no constant ratio identified)

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10003 (the closed form together with the condition on the ratio is the scored object)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response identifies the constant ratio in x and the first term of the power series as written, presents the closed form as that first term over one minus the ratio, and states the values of x for which the identity holds. BC-ERR-10005 and BC-ERR-10006 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The closed form is written and the set of x where it holds is omitted, which is BC-ERR-10005, or the first term is taken from the index zero position although the sigma begins elsewhere, which is BC-ERR-10006.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The constant ratio cannot be extracted from consecutive terms, which is BC-PRQ-10005, or the resulting condition cannot be solved into an interval in x, which is BC-PRQ-10001.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10003 (what makes a power series geometric) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10005 (extracting the ratio in x) for the procedural case

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06008 (antiderivative or definite integral by substitution, where the integrand is a composite times a constant multiple of the inner derivative)
adaptive.mastered_if: Recognition comes first. The integrand is read as a constant multiple of the derivative of an expression over that same expression, u is set to the denominator, du matches the numerator up to a constant, and the result is written as a constant times the natural logarithm of the absolute value of that expression plus C. The absolute value is present rather than dropped, which is what the logarithmic antiderivative point under BC-FRQ-2023-Q5-A rewards in either accepted form, and a definite version converts its limits rather than carrying x endpoints into u.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The pattern is spotted and u chosen well, but the constant adjustment on du is wrong, so the coefficient in front of the logarithm is off. Another partial state produces the logarithm without the absolute value or without the constant of integration, which BC-FRQ-2015-Q5-D records as an antidifferentiation notation loss after a correct decomposition (samples-15-q5:8). A third shows a reciprocal linear expression antidifferentiated incorrectly once the earlier closed form was right, the pattern BC-FRQ-2014-Q6-C describes when the derivative is found but its antiderivative is not. Under BC-QA-06008 a definite version that applies the original limits to an expression still in u is not eligible for the answer point (sg-23:17, sg-23:16).
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: An antiderivative written as a power of the denominator rather than a logarithm means the inner function was never identified as the object whose derivative sits in the numerator, which is BC-SKL-06047 (select a substitution by identifying an inner function whose derivative appears). Absolute value bars missing, or a logarithm of a product split wrongly across terms, points to BC-PRQ-06003 (logarithm rules and properties of the natural logarithm) rather than to substitution, and a du that never absorbs its constant points to BC-SKL-06048 (convert the differential and adjust the constant when substituting).
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-PRQ-06003 (the natural logarithm, its domain, and the absolute value inside the logarithm of a linear expression) is the conceptual target when the logarithmic form itself is not trusted. Procedural failure, where the form is known but the coefficient or differential is mishandled, points instead to BC-SKL-06048 (converting the differential and adjusting the constant).

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08009 (an interpretation treated as complete once the quantity is named)
BC-MIS-08006 (the integral of a rate read as the amount of the quantity)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08007 (a displayed integral must be described, so quantity, interval, and units are the entire response)
adaptive.mastered_if: The sentence states the quantity that accumulates, the two times or inputs that bound the accumulation, and units that multiply the rate units by the input units; a signed integral is described as the change in the quantity over that span rather than as an amount present, and neither BC-ERR-08007 nor BC-ERR-08017 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The quantity and its units are correct while the interval is left out of the sentence, which is BC-ERR-08017 and the observation in BC-SIG-08006; or the sentence is complete except that units are missing or built only from the rate, which is BC-ERR-08007.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: What the rate function measures in the context cannot be stated at all, which is BC-PRQ-06005 rather than an interpretation gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08009 (that the sentence must fix quantity, interval, and units) for the conceptual case; BC-ERR-08007 (deriving units from the integrand and the differential) for the procedural case.

common_confusions: BC-MIS-09002 (the slope read as the rate of the vertical component)
BC-MIS-09003 (the order of the parametric quotient treated as immaterial)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-09001 (the slope at a stated time, where the inverted quotient gives a different number)
adaptive.mastered_if: The slope is written as dy/dt divided by dx/dt, the quotient appearing on the page as an expression with the vertical rate above the horizontal one, before any value is reported; the two rates are not interchanged and the vertical rate alone is never offered as the slope, so BC-ERR-09002, BC-ERR-09003, and BC-ERR-09004 are all absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Both component derivatives are correct and the quotient is inverted, which is BC-ERR-09002; or dy/dt alone is handed in as the slope, which is BC-ERR-09003; or the correct slope value appears with no quotient written anywhere, which is BC-ERR-09004 and the observation in BC-SIG-09001.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: One of dx/dt or dy/dt is itself wrong, so the quotient cannot be right whatever its order, which is BC-SKL-09001; reading which component the prompt calls x is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-09002 (that a slope compares vertical change to horizontal change) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-09001 (producing both rates before dividing) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts

common_confusions: BC-MIS-09002 (the slope read as the rate of the vertical component)
BC-MIS-09008 (a calculator result treated as standing without its expression)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-09001 (a numerical slope at a stated time, so both the quotient and the reporting are scored)
adaptive.mastered_if: Both component derivatives are evaluated at the given parameter value, the quotient dy/dt over dx/dt is shown with those two numbers in place, and the slope is reported to three places from unrounded stored values; neither BC-ERR-09004 nor BC-ERR-09006 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A correct slope value stands alone with no quotient and no component values shown, which is BC-ERR-09004 and the state in BC-SIG-09001; or the setup is complete and a stored derivative is truncated before the division, moving the reported slope, which is BC-ERR-09006.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The reported number is right but given to the wrong number of decimal places or rounded against the convention, which is BC-PRQ-08006 rather than a parametric gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-09002 (what the quotient of rates means) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08006 (storing the component values before dividing) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts

common_confusions: BC-MIS-09003 (the order of the parametric quotient treated as immaterial)
BC-SKL-09006 (locating vertical tangents, which uses the same condition)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-09001 (dx/dt has a zero on the stated interval, so the condition has something to exclude)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response states that dy/dx as a quotient of parametric derivatives exists only where dx/dt is not zero, and identifies the parameter values on the interval where dx/dt vanishes as points where the slope is undefined or the tangent is vertical; BC-ERR-09005 is absent, and the condition is written rather than implied.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The quotient is formed in the right order and applied at a parameter value where dx/dt is zero without comment, or the condition is omitted where the question asks for it, which is BC-ERR-09005.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The equation dx/dt equal to zero is not solved on the interval, so the excluded parameter values are never located, which is BC-PRQ-08001; misreading which component function is x is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-09003 (which rate sits in the denominator and what its vanishing means) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08001 (solving for the parameter values where dx/dt is zero) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts

skills.name: State the condition that dx/dt is not zero

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06013 (supplied definite integral values combined through constant multiple, sum, reversal and adjacent interval properties)
adaptive.mastered_if: Once the integral of f from a to b is known, the integral from b to a is reported as the negative of that value without recomputing anything, and the negation is attributed to the swapped limits rather than to the sign of f. In the BC-FRQ-2024-Q4-A setting the property is used for an input lying to the left of the fixed lower limit, with the supplied region area giving the magnitude and the reversal giving the sign. Values are labelled with the inputs they belong to, which BC-FRQ-2025-Q4-C requires before either value counts.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A positive value is reported for the input left of the lower limit, which BC-FRQ-2024-Q4-A records as the reversal property simply not applied. A second state applies the reversal and then also negates for a region below the axis that was already accounted for, so two sign decisions collide. BC-FRQ-2022-Q3-A describes the direction of accumulation from the known input reversed, and BC-FRQ-2025-Q4-C describes correct values attached to the wrong labels, both of which leave the property itself intact while the answer fails.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: No prerequisite skills are listed here, and the failure that imitates this one comes from the magnitude rather than the sign, showing as a supplied region area ignored and the region estimated instead, which BC-FRQ-2024-Q4-A names directly. The tell is a correctly negated answer built on a wrong number.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-QA-06013 (the reversal of limits as a statement about orientation of the interval) for the conceptual failure; a sign that is right with a magnitude that is not points instead to BC-SKL-06028 (evaluating the integral from the graph using area formulas)

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the value of the integral of f from a to b, state that the integral of f from b to a equals the negative of that value.
skills.description_plain: Swapping the limits changes the sign of the integral.
skills.name: Apply the reversal of limits property

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05021 (a zero of the second derivative taken to be a point of inflection with no sign change checked)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05005 (points of inflection identified with a reason tied to the given graph)
adaptive.mastered_if: Solving f double prime equal to zero is followed by a domain filter. Inputs where f double prime fails to exist are collected too, anything lying outside the domain of f is discarded, and the surviving list is offered as candidates rather than as a finished set of inflection points, leaving the sign change still to be checked. The 2025 and 2026 guidelines award the answer point only for the exact set, so no surplus input appears and BC-ERR-05032 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: An input where f has no value sits in the declared list, which is BC-SIG-05024 and BC-ERR-05032, and the extra entry costs the answer point on its own. The 2025 Q4 commentary describes a second partial state, two of three required inputs given because a turning point between pieces was missed, and the 2026 Q4 note records the reverse cost, where declaring a point instead of an input value forfeits eligibility for the reason.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Missing or spurious zeros of f double prime come from BC-PRQ-05001, solving equations and inequalities to locate where an expression is zero or undefined, and show up as a candidate list that does not match the second derivative written just above it. When the algebra is right and the undefined inputs are kept anyway, the gap is BC-PRQ-05003, the domain of a function in piecewise, rational, and radical forms.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05021 (candidate condition equated with the conclusion) is the conceptual target. Where the candidate status is understood and an out-of-domain input still survives, the procedural target is BC-PRQ-05003, restricting every conclusion to the set of inputs on which f is defined.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Solve f'' equal to zero and find where f'' fails to exist, retaining only inputs that lie in the domain of f.
skills.description_plain: Find the inputs where the second derivative is zero or does not exist.
skills.name: Locate candidate points of inflection where the second derivative is zero or undefined

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05021 (a zero of the second derivative treated as a point of inflection)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05005 (points of inflection identified with a reason tied to the given graph)
adaptive.mastered_if: A candidate input is only called a point of inflection after the learner writes what the second derivative does on the left and on the right, or equivalently that f prime turns from decreasing to increasing there, and the declared list contains exactly the inputs where that reversal happens. Work on a plotted derivative and work on a formula both produce the same list, and neither BC-ERR-05033 (every zero of the second derivative reported as an inflection point) nor BC-ERR-99023 (inflection points misidentified or justified without the given representation) appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The inputs come out right but the sign change is never written down, which is the BC-SIG-05025 observation of a list that matches the zeros exactly with no sign discussion, so BC-ERR-05033 stands. Another intermediate state is a correct set of inputs carried by a reason phrased purely in second derivative symbols, the split named in the 2025 guidelines where the answer point survives and the reason point does not, close to BC-ERR-99023.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Zeros of the plotted function are offered as the candidates, which is a failure of BC-SKL-05032 (locating candidates where the second derivative is zero or undefined) rather than of the sign check, and the tell is that the reported inputs are extrema or axis crossings of the given curve. A reversed reading of concavity from a rising or falling derivative graph points instead to BC-SKL-05031.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05021 (candidate condition equated with the conclusion) for the conceptual failure. When the concept is held but the two sided check is skipped or botched, the target is BC-SKL-05032 (producing the candidate list correctly before testing it).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Show that f'' takes opposite signs on the two sides of a candidate input, equivalently that f' changes from decreasing to increasing or the reverse, before declaring a point of inflection.
skills.description_plain: Check the bending really changes direction there.
skills.name: Confirm a point of inflection by a sign change of the second derivative

common_confusions: BC-MIS-02011 (the term by term rule extended to products)
BC-SKL-02036 (the product rule, which the term by term habit displaces)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-02006 (an expression of several terms, where a term left undifferentiated or a lost sign shows directly)
adaptive.mastered_if: For a sum or difference of differentiable functions the derivative is written as the sum or difference of the derivatives, every term is differentiated including constants, and the order of subtraction is preserved so signs survive into the result.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Each term is differentiated correctly but a sign is dropped on a subtracted term, so the term by term structure is held and the combination is wrong.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The sum and difference limit theorems underlying the rule are not available, which is a gap at BC-SKL-01018.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-02011 (where term by term differentiation is valid) for the conceptual failure; BC-SKL-01018 (the sum and difference limit theorems) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: For a sum or difference of differentiable functions, write the derivative as the sum or difference of the derivatives.
skills.description_plain: Differentiate term by term.
skills.name: Apply the sum and difference rules

common_confusions: BC-MIS-04009 (a product of two changing quantities read as one object)
BC-MIS-04011 (one factor assumed fixed because its value is given)
BC-SKL-04022 (product terms inside an implicit curve equation)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-04007 (a mixed term where the product rule decides the completely correct differentiation point)
adaptive.mastered_if: A term multiplying two time varying quantities is differentiated with the product rule, so both terms appear and each carries its own derivative with respect to time; BC-ERR-04018 is absent, matching the 2022 Q4 part D requirement of a complete product rule across the two factors with the time derivatives attached.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: One quantity is held constant so only one rate factor appears, BC-ERR-04018; or the product rule is written and the time derivatives are missing from its terms, which the 2022 Q4 part D distinctions identify as the chain rule layer rather than the product structure.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The differentiation is not with respect to time at all, a gap at BC-SKL-04019 with signal BC-SIG-04013.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-04009 (both factors vary, so both contribute rates). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-04019 (attaching a time derivative to each factor).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
