skills.description_plain: A term that multiplies two varying quantities needs the product rule.
skills.name: Apply the product rule inside a related rates differentiation
skills.notation: product rule with respect to t

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06016 (several integrands of different structure are classified and the technique each structure calls for is named or applied)
adaptive.mastered_if: The integrand one over x is antidifferentiated as the natural logarithm of the absolute value of x, e to the x returns itself, and a constant base b to the x carries the reciprocal of ln b as its factor. An inner linear argument brings its own reciprocal constant down, and an improper upper bound is written with limit notation on the integral or on the exponential antiderivative rather than with infinity substituted into the expression, which is one of the three accepted forms in BC-FRQ-2026-Q5-D.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The exponential and reciprocal forms are named correctly but the reciprocal constant from the inner linear argument is dropped, so the antiderivative is a nonzero constant multiple of the correct one, the pattern BC-FRQ-2026-Q5-D records as the chain factor lost. Another intermediate state writes limit notation only on the final line instead of from the step where the improper bound first appears, and a third leaves the integral indefinite where the stem asked for a value.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Logarithm arithmetic collapses at the limits while the antiderivative itself is right, which points at BC-PRQ-06003 rather than this skill. The tell is a correct ln of an absolute value followed by a wrong difference of logarithms, or absolute value dropped from the logarithm of a linear expression.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-PRQ-06003 (logarithm properties and the absolute value inside ln) for the conceptual failure; the procedural failure, where the form is named but the reciprocal constant or the limit notation is lost, stays inside BC-SKL-06041.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an integrand of the form e to the x, a constant base raised to x, or one over x, determine the corresponding antiderivative, using the natural logarithm of the absolute value for the reciprocal form.
skills.description_plain: Recognise the forms whose antiderivatives are exponentials and natural logarithms.
skills.name: Antidifferentiate exponential and reciprocal integrands

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08016 (the cross sectional dimension read as a function value)
BC-SKL-08032 (square sections, where one dimension does determine the area)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08011 (the section is a rectangle whose height is stated separately from its base)
adaptive.mastered_if: The volume is written as the definite integral of the product of the base and the height of the rectangular section, the base being the distance between the boundary curves and the height being the stated multiple or stated function of that distance, so both dimensions appear as factors; BC-ERR-08031 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The base of the rectangle is written correctly as the difference of the curves and the stated height relation is dropped, so the section is treated as a square, which is BC-ERR-08031.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The base itself is taken as a single function value rather than as a distance between two curves, which is BC-PRQ-08004 and shows before the height relation is reached.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08016 (that a rectangle needs two stated dimensions) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-08031 (forming the base as a difference) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Write the volume of a solid whose rectangular cross sections have a stated height relation as the definite integral of the product of the two dimensions over the spanning interval.
skills.description_plain: Multiply the side by the stated second dimension, then integrate.
skills.name: Set up the volume integral for rectangular cross sections

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08017 (the difference of squares equated to the square of the difference)
BC-MIS-08023 (the upper curve assumed to give the outer radius)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08011 (the integrand is a squared difference, so the cross term is the scored detail)
adaptive.mastered_if: The volume integral is evaluated by expanding the squared difference into three terms and antidifferentiating each, or numerically with the unexpanded integrand stored, and the value is reported to the required accuracy; the cross term survives the expansion and no intermediate is truncated, so neither BC-ERR-08030 nor BC-ERR-08005 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The setup is correct and the expansion drops the cross term, squaring each part of the difference separately, which is BC-ERR-08030; or the integration is right and a stored decimal is truncated before the last step, which is BC-ERR-08005.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The antidifferentiation fails on a term with a negative or fractional exponent produced by the expansion, which is BC-PRQ-06002 rather than a volume gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08017 (that squaring does not distribute over subtraction) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-06002 (antidifferentiating the expanded terms) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Evaluate the volume integral by expanding the squared difference and antidifferentiating, or with technology, and report the value.
skills.description_plain: Expand or use technology, then report the volume.
skills.name: Evaluate a cross section volume integral

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06009 (antiderivative by integration by parts on a product of unlike factors, one of which simplifies on differentiation)
adaptive.mastered_if: The boundary term u times v is evaluated at the upper limit and the lower limit and the difference taken, and the definite integral of v du over the same interval is subtracted from it, with the limits attached to both pieces rather than to one. The endpoint evaluation is shown, so the response does not rest on an unsupported value, and the answer is a number rather than an expression still carrying a constant of integration. BC-FRQ-2023-Q5-C notes that the parts expression may earn its points with the choice of u and dv left implicit and with limits present, absent, or partly present in that intermediate work (sg-23:18).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The boundary term is omitted altogether and only the remaining integral is evaluated, which BC-FRQ-2023-Q5-C records as the definite form of the parts expression not being used. Another state carries a constant of integration into a definite evaluation, and a third ignores a supplied integral value and tries to integrate an unspecified function symbolically, which BC-FRQ-2023-Q5-C lists as the given data not being used. Under BC-QA-06009 the three points sit on the choice of u and dv, the u times v minus the integral of v du expression, and the answer.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: If the parts structure itself is wrong before any limits are applied, the failure belongs to BC-SKL-06058 (apply the integration by parts formula). If the structure is right and the endpoint arithmetic fails, with the upper and lower values subtracted in the wrong order or one endpoint never substituted, the gap is BC-SKL-06034 (evaluate a definite integral by antidifferentiation and endpoint substitution).
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-SKL-06058 (the parts expression) is the conceptual target when the boundary term is treated as optional, since the definite form of the formula was never internalised. Procedural failure confined to the endpoints points instead to BC-SKL-06034 (evaluating a definite integral by antidifferentiation and endpoint substitution).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a definite integral requiring parts, evaluate u times v at the upper and lower limits and subtract the definite integral of v du over the same interval.
skills.description_plain: Evaluate the uv boundary term at both limits and subtract the remaining integral.
skills.name: Evaluate a definite integral using integration by parts

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06020 (infinity is a number that can be substituted)
BC-MIS-06021 (every improper integral of a decaying integrand converges)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06011 (integral with an infinite limit of integration or an unbounded integrand, rewritten as a limit of definite integrals and evaluated or shown to diverge)
adaptive.mastered_if: Starting from the integral already written as a limit, an antiderivative of the correct form is found, both the variable endpoint and the fixed endpoint are substituted, and only then is the limit evaluated to a finite number, with the limit symbol retained on every line until the moment it is taken. Where the antiderivative is an exponential or a reciprocal power, its chain factor survives, the constant that BC-FRQ-2026-Q5-D notes gets dropped. The convergence is stated together with its value. BC-ERR-06024 and BC-ERR-06025 are both absent, so infinity is never substituted and no finite number is claimed for a limit that fails to exist.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The antiderivative is correct and the endpoint handling is not, as in BC-FRQ-2022-Q5-C where the antiderivative is evaluated at infinity directly and the loss is in the limit notation rather than the calculus, which is BC-ERR-06024. Or the limit is taken but the antiderivative carries a wrong leading constant because the chain factor was lost, which BC-FRQ-2023-Q5-B and BC-FRQ-2026-Q5-D both record while still allowing the antiderivative shape to be recognised. A third state produces a finite value where the limit is actually infinite, BC-ERR-06025.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Work that has no limit expression to evaluate because the improper integral was never rewritten points at BC-SKL-06067, and the tell is an antiderivative sitting directly against an infinite endpoint. If the limit machinery is fine and the bracket evaluation of the antiderivative at two endpoints is what fails, the gap is BC-SKL-06034 instead.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06021 (convergence inferred from a decaying integrand without examining the limit) is the conceptual target, with the integrals of one over x and one over x squared on the same infinite interval as the discriminating pair; the procedural failure, the antiderivative and its endpoint substitution, points instead to BC-SKL-06034 (antidifferentiation and endpoint substitution).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an improper integral written as a limit, find an antiderivative, evaluate at the variable and fixed limits, and evaluate the resulting limit to obtain the value of the convergent integral.
skills.description_plain: Antidifferentiate, substitute, then take the limit.
skills.name: Evaluate the limit to determine the value of a convergent improper integral

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10013 (the two conditions collapsed into one)
BC-SKL-10029 (the limit condition, the other half of the test)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10004 (the conditions carry the reason point)
BC-QA-10008 (the bound is licensed only once both conditions are stated)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response shows that the absolute values of the terms form a decreasing sequence from the starting index onward, by an explicit inequality between consecutive absolute values or by the sign of the derivative of the matching function, and states the decrease as one of the two alternating series conditions. BC-ERR-10020 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The decrease is asserted from the first few terms with no argument that it continues for every index, or the decrease is shown and the limit condition is never stated, which is BC-ERR-10020 and the collapse described in BC-MIS-10013.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The comparison between consecutive absolute values cannot be resolved because the ratio in n is not handled, which is BC-PRQ-10004.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10013 (the two separate requirements of the alternating series test) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10004 (comparing consecutive terms) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an alternating series, show that the absolute values of the terms form a decreasing sequence from the starting index onward.
skills.description_plain: Check that each term is smaller in size than the one before it.
skills.name: Verify that the terms decrease in absolute value

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10013 (one condition stated for two)
BC-MIS-10005 (a limit of zero read as sufficient for convergence)
BC-SKL-10013 (the inconclusive nth term test case)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10004 (the reason point requires both conditions)
BC-QA-10008 (the error bound rests on the same two conditions)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response evaluates the limit of the absolute values of the terms and states that it is zero, presenting it as the second alternating series condition alongside the decrease rather than as a convergence argument in itself. BC-ERR-10020 and BC-ERR-10008 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The limit of zero is produced and the decrease condition is omitted, which is BC-ERR-10020, or the zero limit alone is offered as the reason the series converges, which is BC-ERR-10008.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The limit of the absolute value expression in n cannot be evaluated, which is BC-PRQ-10004.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10005 (what a zero limit settles on its own) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10004 (limits of the absolute terms) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an alternating series, evaluate the limit of the absolute values of the terms and confirm it is zero.
skills.description_plain: Check that the size of the terms has limit zero.
skills.name: Verify that the terms tend to zero

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10003 (decreasing terms taken as licence for the closed form)
BC-SKL-10019 (the p-series threshold on the exponent applied to a ratio)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10003 (the sum is asked for, so the condition on r is the step that licenses it)
BC-QA-10020 (a geometric ratio argument is an accepted reason for convergence at a stated input)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response states the criterion that a geometric series converges when the absolute value of r is less than one and diverges otherwise, applies it to the r found, and gives the verdict before any sum is written. BC-ERR-10005 is absent, so no finite value is attached to a series with absolute value of r at least one.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The criterion is stated and the absolute value bars are dropped when r is negative, so the comparison is made on the signed ratio, or the closed form is written first and the size of r is checked afterwards, leaving BC-ERR-10005 in reach.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The inequality on the absolute value of r cannot be resolved into a condition on the variable, which is BC-PRQ-10001 rather than a geometric criterion gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10003 (what the size of the ratio controls) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10001 (absolute value inequalities) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a geometric series, state that it converges when the absolute value of the common ratio is less than one and diverges otherwise, and apply that condition to the ratio found.
skills.description_plain: Decide convergence by comparing the size of the ratio with one.
skills.name: Apply the convergence condition for a geometric series

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06006 (rate in minus rate out accumulation, possibly combined with an initial amount)
adaptive.mastered_if: Inflow and outflow are identified by which one raises and which one lowers the quantity, and the net accumulation is written as one definite integral of inflow minus outflow over the shared interval rather than as two separate integrals bolted together afterwards. A constant outflow rate is handled as a constant inside the same integrand instead of being integrated as though it varied. When a variable upper limit is needed, the variable of integration is given a different letter from the limit, the notation point the rubric tracks in 2015 Q1 part D.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Only the inflow is integrated and the outflow never reaches the integrand, so the net rate structure is dropped while the accumulation machinery is otherwise intact. A second state is a correct integral of the difference presented as the amount present, with the initial amount left out, which the same rubric separates from the integral point. Using one letter for both the upper limit and the variable of integration is a notation slip that the rubric penalises even where the structure is right.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: When the difference of rates is formed correctly but the accumulated amount is still wrong, the gap is BC-SKL-06036 (computing net change from a rate over an interval), and the tell is a correct net rate paired with limits that do not match the interval described.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-QA-06006 (net rate as inflow minus outflow inside one integral) for the conceptual failure; procedural failure points instead to BC-SKL-06036 (integrating that net rate over the interval)

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an inflow rate and an outflow rate over the same interval, express the net accumulated amount as the definite integral of the difference of the two rates over that interval.
skills.description_plain: Subtract the outflow rate from the inflow rate inside one integral.
skills.name: Set up a single definite integral for a rate in minus rate out situation

common_confusions: BC-MIS-09006 (distance in the plane read as the size of the net change in position)
BC-SKL-09025 (total distance, which integrates the speed)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-09005 (position is recovered from displacement, so the vector structure is used rather than a length)
adaptive.mastered_if: The displacement over the time interval is written as a vector whose entries are the definite integrals of the two velocity components over that interval, and it is described as the net change in position rather than as a length; the magnitude, if taken, is named the distance between the endpoints, and BC-ERR-09015 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The vector of component integrals is formed correctly and its magnitude is then reported as the total distance travelled, which is BC-ERR-09015 and the observation in BC-SIG-09004.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Net change from a rate over an interval is not available in the single variable setting either, which is BC-SKL-08006; reading which function is the velocity component is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-09006 (net change against path length) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-08006 (the one dimensional displacement integral) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Express the net change in position over a time interval as the vector of definite integrals of the velocity components over that interval.
skills.description_plain: Integrate each velocity component over the interval.
skills.name: Write the displacement as a definite integral of the velocity vector

common_confusions: BC-MIS-09011 (speed taken to be one of the two velocity components)
BC-MIS-09008 (a calculator result treated as standing without its expression)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-09006 (a time is solved for from a speed value, so the written equation is what carries the method)
adaptive.mastered_if: The speed is written as a function of time, set equal to the stated value as an equation on the page, solved numerically over the interval with the calculator in radian mode, and the first such time reported when the question asks for the first; neither BC-ERR-09022 nor BC-ERR-09023 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A correct time appears alone with no speed expression and no equation shown, which is BC-ERR-09022 and the observation in BC-SIG-09008; or the equation is written and solved with trigonometric values taken in degree measure, giving an internally consistent wrong time, which is BC-ERR-09023.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The equation is set up correctly and the numerical solve over the stated interval does not return the solutions, which is BC-PRQ-08001; the radian convention for trigonometric arguments is BC-PRQ-09003.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-09011 (what quantity is being set equal to the given value) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-09003 (radian mode on the solve) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: isolated by BC-QA-09006
skills.description_formal: Write the speed as a function of time, set it equal to the stated value, solve numerically on the interval, and report the first such time when asked.
skills.description_plain: Set the speed expression equal to the number and solve on the interval.
skills.name: Solve for a time at which the speed has a stated value

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08004 (distance travelled and net change in position treated as one quantity)
BC-MIS-08005 (speed treated as another name for velocity)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08003 (both displacement and total distance are asked in the same question, isolating the integrand choice)
adaptive.mastered_if: The integrand is the absolute value of the velocity function, the limits are the time interval stated, and the value returned is nonnegative and named as total distance travelled; the absolute value bars are written in the expression rather than applied to the answer, and neither BC-ERR-08008 nor BC-ERR-08009 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The integral is written over the right interval with velocity itself as the integrand and the result called distance, which is BC-ERR-08008 with BC-SIG-08003 as its observed form; or the word speed is used while the expression keeps the signed velocity, which is BC-ERR-08009.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The absolute value of a sign changing expression cannot be unpacked piecewise, so the integrand is never formed, which is BC-PRQ-08003 rather than a distance gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08005 (speed as the magnitude of velocity) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08003 (absolute value as a piecewise definition inside an integrand) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a velocity function and a time interval, write and evaluate the definite integral of the absolute value of velocity over that interval and report it as total distance travelled.
skills.description_plain: Integrate the absolute value of velocity over the interval.
skills.name: Compute total distance as the definite integral of speed

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08004 (distance travelled and net change in position treated as one quantity)
BC-SKL-08007 (total distance, which needs the absolute value)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08003 (velocity changes sign inside the interval, so displacement and distance separate numerically)
adaptive.mastered_if: Displacement is written as the definite integral of the velocity function itself, with no absolute value, over the time interval the prompt gives, and the reported value keeps its sign so that a negative answer is described as net movement in the negative direction; the integrand is not altered when the velocity changes sign on the interval, and BC-ERR-08008 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The integral of velocity is set up and evaluated correctly and the value is then labelled as the distance travelled, which is BC-ERR-08008 and the observation in BC-SIG-08003; the setup for displacement stands while the naming of the quantity does not.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Net change of a quantity from its rate cannot be assembled at all, so the integral never reaches velocity, which is BC-SKL-06036; failing to read v(t) as the rate that goes inside the integral is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08004 (that the sign of velocity subtracts from displacement and not from distance) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-06036 (net change as the integral of a rate) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a velocity function and a time interval, write and evaluate the definite integral of velocity over that interval and report it as displacement.
skills.description_plain: Integrate velocity over the interval to get the net change in position.
skills.name: Compute displacement as the definite integral of velocity

common_confusions: BC-MIS-02009 (the power rule as a move on the exponent alone)
BC-SKL-02038 (deciding whether to expand a product first, which produces a polynomial to differentiate)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-02006 (a polynomial differentiated by rule, with an evaluation point when a value is demanded)
adaptive.mastered_if: Each term of the polynomial is differentiated by the power rule with its coefficient carried through (BC-ERR-02015 absent), the constant term is sent to zero (BC-ERR-02016 absent), and the terms are recombined with their signs, giving a polynomial of degree one lower than the original.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Most terms are correct while the constant term is copied into the derivative, which is BC-ERR-02016, or one term has its exponent lowered without the coefficient factor, which is BC-ERR-02015.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The power rule itself is not held on a single term, which is a BC-SKL-02025 gap, and dropping a constant factor is BC-SKL-02029 rather than a polynomial specific failure.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-02009 (the coefficient the rule produces) for the conceptual failure; BC-SKL-02025 (the power rule on one term) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Differentiate a polynomial by applying the power rule to each term together with the constant multiple, sum, and difference properties.
skills.description_plain: Combine the power rule with the term by term and constant multiple rules.
skills.name: Differentiate a polynomial function

common_confusions: BC-MIS-02009 (the power rule remembered as a move on the exponent alone)
BC-SKL-02033 (the natural exponential, where the variable is in the exponent and the rule does not apply)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-02006 (a polynomial or power expression differentiated by rule, where BC-SIG-02010 shows as every exponent lowered and no coefficient produced)
adaptive.mastered_if: For x to an integer power r the derivative is written as r times x to the power r minus one, with the factor of the original exponent present on every term (BC-ERR-02015 absent) and negative exponents handled by the same rule.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Every exponent is lowered by one and the multiplication by the original exponent is omitted on one term, which is BC-ERR-02015, so the pattern is partly held.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Negative and fractional exponents are not recognised as exponents at all, which is a gap at BC-PRQ-06002 and shows as terms left untouched rather than as a missing factor.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-02009 (deriving the rule for a squared term from the definition) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-06002 (exponent rules) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: For f(x) equal to x to an integer power r, write the derivative as r times x to the power r minus one.
skills.description_plain: Multiply by the exponent and reduce the exponent by one.

common_confusions: BC-MIS-07006 (segments read as points of a curve rather than directions)
BC-SKL-07020 (the same evaluation used as the first Euler step)
BC-ERR-99035 (solving the equation where it already supplies the slope)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-07002 (slopes at two or three distinguishing points decide the match or the drawing)
adaptive.mastered_if: The coordinates of the named lattice point are substituted into the right side of the differential equation and the resulting number is reported as the slope of the segment there, with the evaluation done at the point asked for rather than a neighbour; BC-ERR-07010 is absent, and the equation is used directly rather than solved first.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The arithmetic is correct for coordinates one grid step away from the one requested, BC-ERR-07010 with signal BC-SIG-07009; or, as the 2023 Q3 part B and 2015 Q4 part C distinctions record, the equation is evaluated at the target input rather than the initial one, or the initial value is used in place of the slope.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The coordinates cannot be read off the printed lattice, a figure reading gap at BC-PRQ-07006; or substitution into an expression in two variables fails, BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-07006 (the right side assigns a direction at each point). Procedural failure: BC-PRQ-07006 (locating the requested lattice point before substituting).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Substitute the coordinates of a lattice point into the right side of the differential equation to obtain the slope of the segment at that point.

common_confusions: BC-MIS-07006 (the field treated as a plot of the solution)
BC-SKL-07014 (drawing a curve rather than the segments)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-07002 (the drawing is accepted when the segments agree with the computed slopes)
adaptive.mastered_if: A short segment of the computed slope is drawn centred at each indicated lattice point, with the relative steepness of the segments consistent from point to point and horizontal ones drawn flat; BC-ERR-07011 is absent, and segments at points sharing one coordinate agree with the computed values rather than with each other by default.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The slopes are computed correctly and every drawn segment carries the same tilt, BC-ERR-07011 with signal BC-SIG-07010; or the signs of the drawn slopes are reversed, the arithmetic failure the 2015 Q4 part A distinctions separate from a point by point evaluation failure.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The slope values themselves are wrong, a gap at BC-SKL-07010; or the lattice cannot be read, BC-PRQ-07006.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-07006 (each segment shows a direction, not a value). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-07010 (computing the slope point by point before drawing).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Draw a short segment of the computed slope centred at each indicated lattice point, keeping the relative steepness of the segments consistent.
skills.description_plain: Sketch short lines of the right steepness at the marked points.
skills.name: Draw the segments of a slope field at given lattice points

common_confusions: BC-MIS-07007 (a horizontal segment read as a maximum of every solution)
BC-MIS-07009 (an equilibrium level treated as crossable)
BC-SKL-07040 (the nonzero zero of a logistic right side as the carrying capacity)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-07002 (the horizontal segments are part of what the drawing is checked against)
BC-QA-07010 (a critical point of a solution is located from the zeros of the right side)
adaptive.mastered_if: The right side is set equal to zero and solved, and the set of points where the segments are horizontal is described, with the constant function at that level recognised as itself a solution rather than as a maximum of every curve; BC-ERR-07012 is absent, so the equilibrium level is available for the sketch and for the critical point work.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The field or the equation is worked through and the right side is never set equal to zero, signal BC-SIG-07011 and BC-ERR-07012; or both factors of a product right side are set to zero where a supplied bound rules one out, the failure the 2024 Q3 part B distinctions record.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The slope at a point cannot be computed from the right side, a gap at BC-SKL-07010 rather than in solving for the zeros.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-07007 (a zero rate marks an equilibrium the constant solution occupies). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-07010 (evaluating the right side, then setting it to zero).

skills.assessability_basis: isolated by BC-QA-07010
skills.description_formal: Solve the right side of the differential equation equal to zero and describe the set of points where the segments are horizontal.
skills.description_plain: Find the points where the equation gives slope zero.
skills.name: Identify where the slope field is horizontal

common_confusions: BC-MIS-03005 (a mixed term read as one symbol)
BC-MIS-03013 (the second derivative treated as a new construction)
BC-SKL-03030 (a second derivative with no implicit variable present)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-03008 (product rule, chain rule, and value are scored as three separate points)
adaptive.mastered_if: The expression for dy/dx in x and y is differentiated again with respect to x, with the product rule on mixed terms and the chain rule on y terms, so dy/dx reappears in the result and can then be replaced by its own expression; BC-ERR-03008 is absent and the two structural elements are separable in the way the 2025 Q5 part A rubric awards the product rule and the chain rule separate points.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The derivative factor is carried and a product term is dropped, or the product structure survives and the derivative factor on the y term is missing, which the 2025 Q5 part A distinctions isolate as a product rule failure and a chain rule failure respectively; or the second derivative is left containing the first derivative symbol with no substitution back, the state the 2015 Q4 part B commentary records.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The mixed term is not treated as a product even in the first differentiation, a gap at BC-SKL-03008; or the algebra of substituting one expression into another fails, BC-PRQ-03002.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-03013 (differentiating dy/dx uses the same rules again, including on y). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-03008 (the product rule on a term holding both variables).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given dy/dx expressed in x and y, differentiate again with respect to x, applying the product rule to mixed terms and the chain rule to y terms so that dy/dx reappears in the result.
skills.description_plain: Differentiate the expression for dy/dx, using the product and chain rules on the y parts.
skills.name: Differentiate a derivative expression that still contains y
skills.notation: second derivative found implicitly

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05019 (rules about the first derivative transferred onto the second without re-deriving them)
BC-MIS-05020 (concavity and monotonicity treated as the same property)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05004 (intervals of concavity from derivative information with a reason)
adaptive.mastered_if: Concavity is reported from f double prime and nothing else. The second derivative is computed, its zeros and undefined inputs partition the domain, the sign of f double prime on each open interval is determined from a test value or a factored form, and concave up is claimed exactly where that sign is positive. In implicit settings the first derivative is substituted back so no derivative symbol survives in f double prime, and BC-ERR-05030, a misread sign on one interval, is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: BC-SIG-05022 gives the shape to watch for, a correct partition with one interval labelled with the wrong concavity, which is BC-ERR-05030. Because the 2023 rubric makes the reason point available only after the interval point is earned, this single sign error removes both. The 2015 Q4 commentary adds a nearby partial state, a sign asserted without naming the variable signs that produce it.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Zeros or undefined inputs of f double prime that are wrong or incomplete place the gap in BC-PRQ-05001, solving equations and inequalities to locate where an expression is zero or undefined. When the partition is right and the sign on each piece is guessed rather than tested, the gap is BC-PRQ-05002, sign analysis of a factored expression across a number line.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05019 (the second derivative assumed to say about f what the first says) is the conceptual target, since it produces intervals of increase in place of intervals of concavity. Procedural failure, where the referent is right and one sign is wrong, points to BC-PRQ-05002.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Compute f'', find its zeros and undefined points, and determine the sign of f'' on each resulting open interval to report concavity.
skills.description_plain: Use where the second derivative is positive or negative.
skills.name: Determine intervals of concavity from the sign of the second derivative

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05008 (every critical point is taken to be an extremum)
BC-MIS-05014 (the classification read off the value of the derivative rather than its change)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05003 (a named input classified as a relative minimum, a relative maximum or neither, with a reason)
adaptive.mastered_if: Where f prime is zero at c and holds one sign on both sides, the verdict is neither, and the sentence says that f prime does not change sign at c, which is the phrasing BC-FRQ-2023-Q4-A treats as sufficient on its own. Saying instead that f prime is positive before and after is not offered as the reason, so BC-ERR-05023 stays away, and no extremum is declared at such a point, so BC-ERR-05013 stays away. Any interval of positivity that is volunteered is correct, endpoints optional, and the conclusion reads the same from a formula under BC-REP-01 as from tabulated or graphical derivative information under BC-REP-02.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A relative maximum or minimum is announced at an input where f prime keeps its sign, which is BC-SIG-05010 and BC-ERR-05013, and BC-FRQ-2023-Q4-A records exactly that as a relative minimum claimed from a zero of the derivative. Closer in is the conclusion of neither reached correctly and supported by positive before and after, which is BC-ERR-05023 and costs the point although the verdict is right. BC-FRQ-2015-Q4-C shows a neighbouring state, the second derivative reached for where the first derivative was not zero, and a derivative evaluated with the conclusion sentence never written.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: A student who cannot produce the signs on each side of c has not secured BC-SKL-05020 (classifying a critical point from the sign change of f prime), and the tell is that the neither case is refused not because the criterion is misunderstood but because no left and right signs were ever obtained.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05008 (f prime equal to zero taken as the definition of a turning point) is the conceptual target. When the verdict of neither is correct and only the wording fails, the target is BC-SKL-05020, where the sign-change criterion is phrased.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: When f' has the same sign on both sides of a critical point, conclude that f has neither a relative maximum nor a relative minimum there.
skills.description_plain: Say neither when the derivative does not flip sign at the point.
skills.name: Conclude neither extremum when the derivative keeps its sign

common_confusions: BC-MIS-07004 (a plausible looking function accepted as a solution)
BC-MIS-07005 (a differential equation read as having one solution)
BC-SKL-07024 (separating and solving where verification was asked for)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-07007 (both the derivative and the substitution must be visible for the demonstration)
adaptive.mastered_if: The candidate is differentiated, then the candidate and its derivative are both substituted into the two sides of the equation and the sides are compared, so the derivative is visible on the page rather than assumed; BC-ERR-07006 is absent, and where the candidate is linear its slope is equated with the right side as the 2015 Q4 part D rubric requires.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The candidate is substituted into both sides and no derivative of it appears, BC-ERR-07006 with signal BC-SIG-07005, so the check never tests the equation; or the substitution is correct and the identity is checked at a single input rather than by matching coefficients.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The candidate cannot be differentiated, an elementary rule gap rather than a verification gap; or what the left side of the equation requires is unclear, BC-PRQ-07002.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-07004 (resemblance is not verification). Procedural failure: BC-PRQ-07002 (substituting a function and its derivative into both sides).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Differentiate the candidate function, substitute the function and its derivative into both sides of the differential equation, and compare the two sides.
skills.description_plain: Take the derivative of the candidate and put both into the equation.
skills.name: Differentiate a proposed solution and substitute it into the equation

common_confusions: BC-MIS-07004 (acceptance or rejection by the look of the function)
BC-SKL-07007 (checking the initial condition rather than the equation)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-07007 (a candidate that fails, where the disagreeing input is the evidence)
adaptive.mastered_if: The candidate is substituted and one specific input is exhibited at which the two sides differ, so the negative verdict rests on a displayed disagreement rather than on an assertion; BC-ERR-07008 is absent, and the comparison uses the derivative of the candidate as well as the candidate.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The verdict that the candidate fails is correct and nothing that fails is shown, BC-ERR-07008 with signal BC-SIG-07007, leaving the conclusion unsupported; or the sides are compared symbolically with no input named.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The substitution itself was never carried out with the derivative, a gap at BC-SKL-07006.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-07004 (a counterexample is what refutes a candidate). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-07006 (substituting both the candidate and its derivative).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Substitute the candidate and exhibit one input at which the two sides of the differential equation differ.
skills.description_plain: Point to the place where the two sides disagree.
skills.name: Show that a proposed function is not a solution

common_confusions: BC-MIS-07002 (a differential equation read as an equation for the quantity)
BC-MIS-07001 (the constant dropped, which also changes what the equation says)
BC-SKL-07033 (the general family against one particular solution)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-07006 (the required answer is an equation in the derivative)
BC-QA-07007 (a candidate function is offered against the equation it must satisfy)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response says whether a written statement constrains the derivative of the quantity or the quantity itself, using what the left side measures as the test, and produces a relation involving the derivative when a differential equation is requested; BC-ERR-07005 is absent, so a formula for the amount is not offered in its place.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The situation is modelled correctly in substance and the answer is an expression for the quantity where a relation on its rate was asked for, BC-ERR-07005 with signal BC-SIG-07004, which leaves no separation step to follow.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The derivative notation in the statement cannot be read as a rate, a notation gap at BC-PRQ-07002.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-07002 (a constraint on the rate is not a formula for the amount). Procedural failure: BC-PRQ-07002 (reading what each side of a written equation measures).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a modelled statement or a written equation, decide whether it constrains the derivative of the quantity or the quantity itself.
skills.description_plain: Tell an equation about the rate apart from an equation about the amount.
skills.name: Distinguish a differential equation from an equation for the quantity

common_confusions: BC-MIS-07005 (one solution expected per equation)
BC-MIS-07016 (the constant treated as optional)
BC-SKL-07007 (checking a candidate against the initial condition)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-07003 (a particular solution is demanded explicitly)
BC-QA-07007 (a candidate is tested against the equation and then the point)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response says which of the two the question asks for, describing the general solution as a family indexed by an undetermined constant and the particular solution as the single member a stated point selects, and the answer given carries a constant only when the general solution was requested; BC-ERR-07033 and BC-ERR-07009 are absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The mathematics is complete and a constant remains where a particular solution was asked for, or the constant is fixed where the general solution was, BC-ERR-07033 with signal BC-SIG-07032, so the answer is of the wrong kind for the question posed.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The constant was never introduced, a gap at BC-SKL-07026 and BC-SKL-07029; or the idea that infinitely many functions satisfy one equation is absent, BC-SKL-07009.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-07005 (the constant is what distinguishes the family from the member). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-07029 (fixing or keeping the constant according to the question).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Explain that the general solution carries an undetermined constant describing infinitely many curves, while a stated point selects exactly one of them.
skills.description_plain: Say which answer carries a constant and which does not.
skills.name: Distinguish the general solution family from the particular solution

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05024 (the two derivative tests treated as interchangeable everywhere)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05013 (second derivative test applied at a critical point)
BC-QA-05007 (critical point located and classified for a function given indirectly)
adaptive.mastered_if: Given a plotted f prime, a formula, or a differential equation, the learner names which derivative the object actually shows and picks the test that information supports, so a graph of the first derivative draws a sign change argument while a differentiable formula or a relation that can be differentiated again admits the second derivative test, and the choice is stated with its reason rather than left implicit. BC-ERR-05040 (a test chosen that the given information cannot support) does not appear.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A second derivative test is started from a graph of the first derivative with nothing said about the slope of that graph, the BC-SIG-05031 observation and BC-ERR-05040, so the argument cannot be finished from what was given. BC-FRQ-2015-Q5-B records the neighbouring state where a second derivative test is attempted and miscomputed when the sign argument was cheaper, and BC-FRQ-2026-Q2-C records a candidates table presented where a derivative test was demanded.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: When neither test can be executed cleanly once chosen, the gap is at BC-SKL-05020 (classifying from the sign change of the first derivative) or BC-SKL-05036 (applying the second derivative test), and the tell is that a defensible choice is followed by a broken execution rather than by an argument the given object cannot carry.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05024 (test picked by habit rather than by what the representation supports) for the conceptual failure, with BC-SKL-05036 as the procedural target when the second derivative test is chosen appropriately and then miscarried.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a function presented as a graph of f', a formula, or a differential equation, select the derivative test that the available information makes usable and say why.
skills.description_plain: Pick the test the given information actually supports.
skills.name: Choose between the first and second derivative tests for a given presentation

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05031 (a relation has critical points only where its derivative is zero)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05012 (critical points and second derivative behaviour of an implicit relation)
adaptive.mastered_if: Horizontal tangents on an implicit relation come from setting the numerator of dy/dx to zero, and the denominator is evaluated at each candidate before it is kept. Discarded candidates are named and the reason is written down, that the denominator vanishes there so no tangent exists, and the surviving solutions are carried into the defining relation. Across the BC-QA-05012 path the derivative is differentiated implicitly rather than as though y were free, and BC-ERR-05057 (points reported where the denominator also vanishes) is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Numerator equals zero is solved correctly and the denominator is never looked at, which is BC-SIG-05046, so points where both parts vanish are listed as horizontal tangents. That is BC-ERR-05057, and the critical point list comes out wrong even though the implicit differentiation earned its point. The BC-FRQ-2015-Q5-C commentary records the neighbouring behaviour where the whole derivative expression was set to zero, denominator included.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: When the candidate equation itself is mis-solved, or the denominator is not recognised as an object that can vanish, the gap is BC-PRQ-05001 (solving equations and inequalities to locate where an expression is zero or undefined), and the sign of it is a factored expression handled correctly in one factor and dropped in another. A failure to combine the candidate with the curve equation points to BC-PRQ-05007 instead, and shaky dy/dx to begin with points to BC-SKL-03014.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05031 (only the numerator is treated as carrying critical point information) for the conceptual failure; procedural failure in solving or in the denominator check points instead to BC-PRQ-05001 (locating where an expression is zero or undefined)

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Set the numerator of dy/dx equal to zero, keep only points where the denominator is nonzero, and solve together with the defining relation.
skills.description_plain: Find the points on the curve with a horizontal tangent.
skills.name: Determine where the derivative of an implicit relation equals zero

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06018 (an antiderivative is treated as a single function, so the arbitrary constant is decoration rather than part of the answer)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06016 (integrands of differing structure, each classified and matched to the technique its markers select)
adaptive.mastered_if: Plus C appears on every indefinite result, and when a value of the antiderivative at a point is supplied it is substituted to solve for that constant, giving a single particular function rather than a family. The constant is attached at the antidifferentiation step, not after a later exponentiation, and the learner can name two functions differing by a constant that share the same derivative.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Antidifferentiation is correct and BC-ERR-06021 appears, the arbitrary constant omitted from an indefinite integral, which BC-FRQ-2024-Q5-D records as an indefinite integral treated as definite. In other work C is written but never solved for although an initial value was given, and in BC-FRQ-2015-Q5-D the decomposition is right while the logarithms arrive without absolute values or constant, a notation loss rather than a technique loss.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The antiderivative the constant would attach to is itself wrong on power functions with negative or fractional exponents, so BC-SKL-06040 is the earlier failure. The tell is a correctly placed plus C sitting on an incorrect power rule result.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06018 (the antiderivative as a family, not one function) for the conceptual failure; the procedural failure, where C is known to belong but is dropped under time pressure, points to BC-ERR-06021 (constant of integration omitted).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an indefinite integral, include an arbitrary constant C in the answer, and when a value of the antiderivative at a point is supplied, solve for the particular value of C.
skills.description_plain: Write plus C, then solve for it when a value of the antiderivative is given.
skills.name: Include the constant of integration and determine it from an initial condition

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06025 (an interpretation counted as complete once the quantity is named)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06015 (interpreting a definite integral in context with units)
adaptive.mastered_if: Units are built as a product. Given a rate in units per unit input, the learner reports the unit of the accumulation as rate units times independent variable units, cancels the per correctly, and states the interval alongside, so gallons per second over seconds is reported as gallons and never as gallons per second. The same product holds whether the rate arrives as a table, as a graph, or as a displayed integral, and BC-ERR-06029 (units of the rate given in place of the accumulated units, or interval omitted) does not appear.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The accumulated quantity is named with the rate's own units still attached, which is BC-ERR-06029, or the units are right and the interval is missing. BC-QA-06015 scoring records exactly this split, and the BC-FRQ-2023-Q1-A and BC-FRQ-2026-Q1-B commentaries separate a correct sum whose interpretation lacks units or interval from an approximation failure, so the arithmetic can be intact while the unit statement is not.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: When f(t) is read as an amount rather than as a rate at time t, the unit product has nothing to multiply, and that is BC-PRQ-06005 rather than a units gap. The tell is an interpretation that names a rate where a count was required, as the BC-FRQ-2026-Q1-B commentary describes.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06025 (what changes in the sentence when the interval changes) for the conceptual failure. A learner who knows the sentence must carry units but mishandles the multiplication of the two units points instead to BC-PRQ-06005 (what f(t) measures per unit input).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the unit of a rate of change function and the unit of its independent variable, state the unit of the area of the region defined by the rate, which is the product of the two units.
skills.description_plain: Give the units of an accumulation as rate units times independent variable units.
skills.name: State the units of an accumulated change

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05002 (writing the name of a theorem taken to complete the argument)
BC-MIS-05005 (one existence theorem used for claims about function values and about derivative values alike)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05001 (a differentiable function with selected values supplied, and the response must decide whether some interior input has a named instantaneous rate of change and justify it)
adaptive.mastered_if: Equal endpoint outputs are presented first, as f(a) equal to f(b) or as a difference of zero, the average rate of change is therefore zero, and the response concludes that some c in (a,b) has f prime of c equal to zero, with the Mean Value Theorem named and continuity drawn from differentiability. The claim is kept about the derivative, so the Intermediate Value Theorem never enters. Neither BC-ERR-05006 (Intermediate Value Theorem cited for a claim about the derivative) nor BC-ERR-05004 (no affirmative answer and no theorem) is present, in the table form or the graph form.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The endpoint equality is computed and the argument then reaches for the wrong existence theorem, BC-SIG-05003, arithmetic sound but the theorem cited concerning values of f. The 2023 Q1 part B behaviours give two more, a yes with no endpoint computation, guessed from the table's shape, and continuity asserted rather than derived, and both leave the second point out of reach because it depends on the first.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: If the endpoint difference itself is mishandled, the break is at BC-SKL-05003, and if the existence sentence is missing its structure rather than its theorem, the break is at BC-SKL-05004, the tell being that the zero average rate is stated correctly and nothing follows from it.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05005 (which theorem speaks about f and which speaks about f prime); a procedural failure, where the right theorem is named but the endpoint equality is never shown, points instead to BC-SKL-05003 (computing the average rate of change)

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Show f(a) equal to f(b), hence an average rate of change of zero, and conclude the existence of an interior c with f'(c) equal to zero.
skills.description_plain: When the two endpoint outputs agree, argue that the derivative must be zero somewhere between them.
skills.name: Justify that a derivative takes a particular value using equal endpoint outputs

common_confusions: BC-MIS-04007 (rate problems read as motion problems)
BC-MIS-04001 (amount and rate language interchanged)
BC-SKL-04002 (the full interpretation sentence, of which vocabulary is one element)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-04005 (a setting other than motion, where borrowed vocabulary is visible)
adaptive.mastered_if: The derivative is described in the language of the situation, as the rate of change of the named temperature, population, or area, while the shared structure with motion is recognised without importing its words; BC-ERR-04013 is absent, so no average value is called an average velocity.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The computation is right and the sentence calls the rate a velocity or the quantity a position, BC-ERR-04013, which the 2025 scoring notes treat as unclear communication scored as scratch work; or the quantity is never named at all, signal BC-SIG-04009.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The quantity and its independent variable have not been identified, a gap at BC-SKL-04013 rather than a vocabulary gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-04007 (the structure transfers and the vocabulary does not). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-04013 (naming the quantity before describing its rate).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a non-motion context, describe the derivative using the language of that context rather than the language of rectilinear motion, while recognising the shared structure.
skills.description_plain: Call it the rate of change of the named quantity, not the velocity.
skills.name: Use context vocabulary rather than motion vocabulary
skills.notation: rate of change of the named quantity

common_confusions: BC-MIS-04005 (speed and velocity used as one word)
BC-SKL-04009 (the sign carries direction, which speed discards)
BC-SKL-04010 (whether speed is increasing, a separate judgement)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-04003 (speed at an instant, where the sign of the velocity is still needed for a later part)
adaptive.mastered_if: The speed is reported as the absolute value of the velocity, so a negative velocity yields a positive speed and the sign is described separately as the direction of travel; in the planar case the speed is the square root of the sum of the squares of the coordinate derivatives rather than their sum, and BC-ERR-04007 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The velocity is correct and is reported as a speed with a minus sign attached, BC-ERR-04007 with signal BC-SIG-04005; or, as the 2024 Q2 part A distinctions record, the components are added instead of combined as a magnitude.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The velocity value itself is wrong, a gap at BC-SKL-04006; or absolute value is not available as an operation, BC-PRQ-04005.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-04005 (speed is a magnitude and velocity carries direction). Procedural failure: BC-PRQ-04005 (taking an absolute value or a magnitude of components).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the velocity of a particle at an instant, report the speed as the absolute value of that velocity.
skills.description_plain: Take the size of the velocity and drop the sign.
skills.name: Compute the speed of a particle from its velocity
skills.notation: speed equals the absolute value of v of t

common_confusions: BC-MIS-07008 (a curve drawn freely through the field)
BC-MIS-07006 (segments read as a plot of the solution)
BC-SKL-07015 (keeping the curve off the equilibrium level)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-07001 (the point is scored against four features of the drawn curve at once)
adaptive.mastered_if: The curve passes through the stated point, is tangent to the nearby segments along its whole length, and extends reasonably close to the left and right edges of the printed rectangle, with no cusp and no second curve drawn; BC-ERR-07014 and BC-ERR-99024 are absent, which is what the single sketch point requires.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The curve starts at the correct point and its slope disagrees with nearby segments, or it stops short of an edge, BC-ERR-07014 with signal BC-SIG-07013; the 2024 Q3 part A distinctions separate a curve through a neighbouring lattice point from one that conflicts with the segments.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The printed point cannot be located in the field, a figure reading gap at BC-PRQ-07006 rather than a sketching gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-07008 (the curve must be tangent to the segment at every point it passes). Procedural failure: BC-ERR-07014 (extending the sketch to both edges of the rectangle).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Draw a curve through the stated point that is tangent to the segments of the field and extends across the given rectangle.
skills.description_plain: Draw a curve from the marked point that follows the segments.
skills.name: Sketch a solution curve through a given point on a slope field

common_confusions: BC-MIS-07009 (a solution taken to be able to cross an equilibrium level)
BC-MIS-07008 (the curve drawn freely)
BC-MIS-07007 (the horizontal level read as a maximum)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-07001 (the curve must lie entirely on one side of the horizontal segments)
adaptive.mastered_if: The level at which the field is horizontal is recognised as a constant solution, and the sketch stays on the side of it where the initial point lies, approaching it without touching or crossing; BC-ERR-07015 and BC-ERR-99024 are absent, and the response can say that the rate is exactly zero at that level.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The sketch follows the segments correctly elsewhere and rises through the row of horizontal segments, BC-ERR-07015 with signal BC-SIG-07014, which the 2023 Q3 part A distinctions attribute to not using the bound on the solution given in the stem.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The equilibrium level was never identified because the right side was not set to zero, a gap at BC-SKL-07012; or the curve does not follow the segments at all, BC-SKL-07014.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-07009 (the constant function at that level is itself a solution). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-07012 (locating the zero slope level before drawing).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Recognise the level at which the field is horizontal as a solution the sketched curve cannot cross, and keep the sketch on the side the initial point lies.
skills.description_plain: Do not let the curve cross the line of horizontal segments.
skills.name: Keep a sketched curve on the correct side of an equilibrium level

common_confusions: BC-MIS-04013 (the error direction taken from increase or decrease)
BC-MIS-04012 (the line treated as the function, so no error arises)
BC-SKL-04031 (supplying the second derivative sign as the written reason)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-04008 (an increasing concave down case separates the two possible reasons)
adaptive.mastered_if: The concavity near the point of tangency is determined and the conclusion follows from it, with concave up giving an underestimate and concave down an overestimate, stated for the function rather than for its derivative; BC-ERR-04025 and BC-ERR-99020 are absent, so the direction of the error is never argued from whether the function is increasing.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The direction of the error is correct and the reason given is that the function is increasing or decreasing, signal BC-SIG-04017 and BC-ERR-04025; or, as the 2026 Q3 part C distinctions record, concavity is attributed to the derivative rather than to the function.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Concavity cannot be read from the sign of the second derivative, a gap at BC-SKL-02013; or no approximation exists to judge, BC-SKL-04029.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-04013 (bending, not direction, places the line above or below the curve). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-02013 (reading concavity from the second derivative).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the concavity of a function near the point of tangency, conclude that the tangent line value underestimates the function value when the graph is concave up there and overestimates it when the graph is concave down.
skills.description_plain: Concave up near the point puts the line below the curve, concave down puts it above.
skills.name: Decide whether a tangent line approximation over or under estimates
skills.notation: under or over estimate from concavity

common_confusions: BC-MIS-04013 (the first derivative sign offered as the reason)
BC-ERR-04026 (concavity claimed with no referent in the given figure or formula)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-04008 (the justification point is separate from the conclusion and requires the sign statement)
adaptive.mastered_if: The sign of the second derivative is stated on an interval containing both the point of tangency and the nearby input, and that sign is tied to the supplied graph, table, or formula and then to the position of the line relative to the curve; BC-ERR-04025 and BC-ERR-04026 are absent, so the reason is neither asserted nor checked at a single time only.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The conclusion is correct and the second derivative sign is asserted without reference to the supplied representation, BC-ERR-04026; or the sign is checked at the initial time alone where the interval was required, the gap the 2023 Q3 part C and 2026 Q3 part C distinctions record.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The relationship between concavity and the position of the tangent line is not held, a gap at BC-SKL-04030 rather than a justification gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-04013 (the second derivative is what licenses the claim). Procedural failure: BC-ERR-04026 (naming where in the given representation the sign is read).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a claim that a tangent line approximation is an under or an over estimate, support it by stating the sign of the second derivative on an interval containing the point of tangency and the nearby input.
skills.description_plain: Name the sign of the second derivative on the interval and connect it to the position of the line.
skills.name: Justify the estimate direction with the sign of the second derivative
skills.notation: second derivative sign as the reason

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05020 (concavity and monotonicity treated as the same property)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05009 (relating the graphs of a function and its first two derivatives, with three objects in play at once)
BC-QA-05004 (intervals of concavity from derivative information, with the reason point available only when the intervals are correct)
adaptive.mastered_if: A claim that f double prime is positive on an interval is turned into concave up for the graph of f and increasing for f prime, and a claim that f double prime is decreasing is kept separate from a claim that it is negative. The statement is made for the whole interval rather than at a single input, and the sign is quoted rather than the direction. BC-ERR-05047, calling the graph concave up where the second derivative is decreasing, does not occur.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A correct reading of f double prime is converted into the opposite concavity claim, which is BC-SIG-05037, and any inflection list built afterwards inherits the error as BC-ERR-05047 notes. The scoring behaviour on BC-FRQ-2023-Q3-C shows a second intermediate state, where the second derivative is left in terms of the first and the substitution back into the differential equation is never carried out, and a third where concavity is argued only at the initial point. BC-FRQ-2026-Q3-C adds the case where concavity is attributed to the derivative rather than the function, and the case where concave up is claimed but an overestimate is asserted, inverting the relationship between bending and tangent line position.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: When nothing can be said about f prime from f double prime without a picture, the gap is BC-SKL-05031, determining concavity from whether the derivative graph rises or falls. If the concavity statement is right and the consequence for a tangent line estimate is inverted, the earlier skill is BC-SKL-04030, deciding whether a tangent line approximation over or under estimates.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05020 (bending and rising treated as one property) for the conceptual failure, while a correct sign statement paired with the wrong estimate direction points to BC-SKL-04030 (whether a tangent line approximation over or under estimates)

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the sign or the monotonicity of f'' on an interval, state the corresponding concavity of the graph of f and the monotonicity of f'.
skills.description_plain: Turn a claim about the second derivative into a claim about bending.
skills.name: Translate a statement about the second derivative into a statement about shape

common_confusions: BC-MIS-07018 (an absolute value dropped without checking)
BC-MIS-07019 (a solution formula assumed valid everywhere)
BC-SKL-07031 (the domain the chosen branch implies)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-07003 (the branch choice is folded into the constant point)
BC-QA-07011 (the branch and the interval are both demanded)
adaptive.mastered_if: The sign of the expression inside the absolute value is settled from the initial value or from a bound stated in the stem, and the absolute value is dropped with the branch that is consistent with the given point; BC-ERR-07030 and BC-ERR-99037 are absent, so the resulting solution does not contradict the initial condition.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The antidifferentiation and the constant are correct and the absolute value is removed by habit with the sign that contradicts the given point, BC-ERR-07030 with signal BC-SIG-07029; the 2023 Q3 part D and 2024 Q3 part C distinctions attribute this to not using the stated bound on the quantity.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The constant was never fixed from the initial condition, a gap at BC-SKL-07029; or the meaning of the absolute value bars is unclear, BC-PRQ-07004.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-07018 (the initial point decides which branch holds). Procedural failure: BC-PRQ-07004 (evaluating the enclosed expression at the initial input).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Determine from the initial value or a stated bound whether the expression inside an absolute value is positive or negative on the interval, and drop the absolute value accordingly.
skills.description_plain: Use the given point to decide which sign applies.
skills.name: Resolve an absolute value or a sign ambiguity from the initial condition

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01013 (infinity treated as an input that can be substituted)
BC-SKL-01055 (one sided infinite limits at a finite input, a different question)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01010 (the limit expression and its value are scored separately, so substituted arithmetic with the infinity symbol is exposed)
adaptive.mastered_if: The degrees of numerator and denominator are compared, or both are divided by the dominant power, and the value is reported as zero, as the ratio of leading coefficients, or as unbounded according to which degree is larger, with the comparison shown and the infinity symbol never substituted into the expression as a number (BC-ERR-01021 absent) and the leading coefficient ratio used only when the degrees match (BC-ERR-01023 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The division by the dominant power is set out correctly but one term is not sent to zero, so the reported value keeps a vanishing term, or the correct verdict is reached with no comparison or division displayed.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The behaviour of a quotient of polynomials for large inputs cannot be described without computing sample values, which is a gap at BC-PRQ-01004 rather than an error in the procedure.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01013 (dividing by the dominant power and asking what each term approaches) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-01004 (degree comparison) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: For a quotient of polynomials, compare the degrees of numerator and denominator, or divide by the highest power of the variable, to evaluate the limit as the variable increases or decreases without bound.
skills.description_plain: Compare the top and bottom degrees to get the end value.
skills.name: Evaluate the limit of a rational function at infinity by comparing degrees

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06009 (integrand is a product of unlike factors, one of which simplifies on differentiation, and parts is applied to an indefinite or definite integral)
adaptive.mastered_if: The integrand x times f prime of x is met by declaring u = x and dv = f prime of x dx, so du = dx and v = f of x, and the work then shows x times f of x evaluated at both limits minus the integral of f of x dx over the same interval, with the supplied values of f and the supplied integral of f substituted into their matching places. The parts expression appears in full before any number is moved, the boundary term keeps its limits, and the final line is expressed entirely in the given data rather than in an invented formula for f. Holds in the BC-QA-06009 archetype whether the data arrive as a table of values (BC-REP-04) or as symbolic statements (BC-REP-01).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Parts is selected and the u times v minus the integral of v du skeleton is written, which is enough for the first two points under BC-FRQ-2023-Q5-C where the choice of u and dv may stay implicit, but one of three things then goes wrong. The factors are exchanged, so f prime becomes u and x becomes dv, and the remaining integral is harder than the original.
