Or the boundary term x times f of x is dropped and only the integral piece survives, meaning the definite form of the parts expression was never used. Or the supplied value of the integral of f is left sitting unused while the response tries to antidifferentiate f itself.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Work that cannot get started because f prime of x is read as a new unrelated function rather than as the derivative of the f whose values were supplied points at BC-PRQ-06005, reading function notation and evaluation. The tell is a response that asks for a formula, or that writes f of x in place of f prime of x when forming v, confusing the function with its value at a point. A separate tell, the u times v minus the integral of v du template itself written wrongly on any integrand at all, points at BC-SKL-06058.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-PRQ-06005 (function notation, so that f prime of x is recognised as the derivative of the tabulated f) covers the conceptual failure, while a failure that is procedural, the parts template itself mishandled, points instead to BC-SKL-06058 (applying the integration by parts formula).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an integrand of the form x times f prime of x with selected values or integrals of f supplied, apply parts with u = x and dv = f prime of x dx to express the result in terms of the supplied values.
skills.description_plain: Use parts when the integrand is x times f'(x) and only values of f are supplied.
skills.name: Apply integration by parts to an integrand containing an unknown function and its derivative

common_confusions: BC-MIS-03013 (each order treated as a new construction)
BC-SKL-03032 (writing the order correctly rather than computing it)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-03008 (a third or higher order derivative, often of a supplied derivative expression)
adaptive.mastered_if: Differentiation is repeated one order at a time to the order requested, each intermediate derivative written out, so a fourth derivative is reached through the third rather than guessed; BC-ERR-03021 is absent, and where a product structure is supplied the product rule is reapplied at each stage as the 2023 Q6 part A scoring requires.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The iteration is correct as far as it goes and stops one order short, BC-ERR-03021 with signal BC-SIG-03013; or, following the 2023 Q6 part A distinctions, the derivative values are right and the factorial coefficients are omitted when the result is assembled.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The second derivative cannot be produced, a gap at BC-SKL-03030 rather than at higher orders.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-03013 (order n is the derivative of order n minus one). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-03030 (one clean step from first to second derivative).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a function or one of its derivatives, repeat differentiation to produce the derivative of the order requested, provided each intermediate derivative exists.
skills.description_plain: Keep differentiating, one order at a time.
skills.name: Produce a third or higher order derivative by repeating differentiation
skills.notation: f superscript n of x

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10017 (a bound invoked with no condition established first)
BC-SKL-10040 (the first omitted term, the alternating analogue)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10009 (the form point depends on the order of the derivative in the bound)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response identifies the derivative one order past the degree of the polynomial, so a polynomial of degree n calls for a bound on the absolute value of the n plus first derivative, and uses the bound supplied by the prompt on the closed interval between the centre and the input. BC-ERR-10032 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A bound is used and it is on the derivative of the same order as the polynomial rather than one higher, which is BC-SIG-10017, or the supplied bound is used on an interval other than the one between the centre and the input.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The order of the derivative cannot be tracked through the notation, which is BC-PRQ-06005, so the wrong row of the supplied information is used.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-CON-10001 (the order of the derivative the remainder uses) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-06005 (derivative order notation) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a Taylor polynomial of degree n and an interval between the centre and the input, identify a bound for the absolute value of the n plus first derivative on that interval, using a supplied bound when one is given.
skills.description_plain: Find or use the supplied bound on the derivative one order past the polynomial.
skills.name: Identify the maximum of the next derivative on the interval

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10018 (the bound written as the exact error)
BC-SKL-10042 (the alternating series bound, which uses a term rather than a derivative)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10009 (the form of the bound is a point of its own)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response writes the bound as the maximum of the absolute value of the n plus first derivative times the absolute value of x minus a raised to the n plus first power, divided by n plus one factorial, with all three parts present and their orders agreeing. BC-ERR-10032 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The bound is assembled with two of the three parts correct, most often the power of x minus a carrying n instead of n plus one, or the factorial being n factorial, which is BC-ERR-10032 and takes the comparison point with it.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The factorial cannot be evaluated, which is BC-PRQ-10002, or the power of the displacement cannot be formed, which is BC-PRQ-06002.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-CON-10001 (the structure of the Lagrange remainder) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10002 (the factorial denominator) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the degree, the centre, the input, and a bound on the next derivative, write the error bound as that bound multiplied by the absolute value of the difference raised to the n plus first power divided by n plus one factorial.
skills.description_plain: Assemble the bound from the derivative bound, the power, and the factorial.
skills.name: Write the Lagrange error bound in the correct form

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10018 (bound treated as exact error)
BC-SKL-10042 (the alternating series comparison against a tolerance)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10009 (the second point is showing the error is at most the tolerance)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response evaluates the assembled Lagrange bound to a number and presents the inequality that the absolute error is at most that number and that the number is at most the stated tolerance, using inequality symbols throughout. BC-ERR-10026 and BC-ERR-10027 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The bound is assembled correctly and the relation to the error is written with an equals sign, which is BC-ERR-10026, or the number is produced and never compared with the tolerance, which is BC-ERR-10027; a later simplification slip costs this comparison alone.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The factorial or the power in the bound cannot be evaluated, which is BC-PRQ-10002, or the inequality cannot be resolved, which is BC-PRQ-10001.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10018 (at most against equals) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10002 (evaluating the bound) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the assembled bound and a tolerance, evaluate the bound and present the inequality stating that the error is at most the bound and that the bound is at most the tolerance.
skills.description_plain: Evaluate the bound and show it is at most the number required.
skills.name: Compare the Lagrange bound with a stated tolerance

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06001 (a Riemann sum treated as a sum of the listed values)
BC-MIS-06002 (the endpoint convention treated as cosmetic)
BC-MIS-06003 (Riemann sums treated as exact)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06001 (Riemann sum from a table with over or under estimate reasoning)
adaptive.mastered_if: Each term of the sum is a product, never a bare table value. The learner reads the subintervals the table indicates, takes f at the left endpoint of each, multiplies by that subinterval's own width computed as a difference of consecutive inputs, and adds the products, so a three-term sum shows six factors and a term carries the units of the accumulated quantity rather than the units of the rate. The word left in the stem is honoured, and BC-ERR-06001 (one common width on an unevenly spaced table), BC-ERR-06002 (the opposite endpoint convention), and BC-ERR-06003 (values added with no width factor) are all absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: BC-SIG-06001 records all six factors correct with a total that does not match the displayed products, which re-adding settles as arithmetic. BC-SIG-06003 records a fully correct sum built on the convention that was not asked for, which is BC-ERR-06002 and still earns the form point in 2025 by sg-25:13. BC-ERR-06001 shows as one width applied throughout, which the BC-FRQ-2024-Q1-B commentary calls out as equal widths assumed.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: BC-SIG-06002 is the marker, every tabulated value multiplied by the same number on an unevenly spaced table, and asking for the width list alone separates BC-PRQ-06012 (widths as differences of consecutive partition points) from a copying slip. Reading f at a stated input incorrectly points instead to BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06001 (one term of the sum, with its units, on an unevenly spaced table) for the conceptual failure. BC-SIG-06004 showing rate units on the total points there too, while correct products with a wrong total point instead to the addition itself, not the method.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given selected values of f at partition points, approximate the integral of f over the interval as the sum over subintervals of f at the left endpoint multiplied by the width of that subinterval, with widths taken as differences of consecutive partition points.
skills.description_plain: Use the value at the left end of each subinterval times its width and add.
skills.name: Compute a left Riemann sum from a table of values

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06016 (integrands inspected for structural markers, with techniques whose preconditions fail ruled out)
adaptive.mastered_if: An integrand such as e to the negative t squared is identified as having no closed-form antiderivative, and the accumulation is then left as a definite integral or sent to numerical evaluation rather than forced through an antidifferentiation rule. When a tabulated or given initial value is present, the reported quantity is that value plus the definite integral of the rate over the stated interval, with the interval taken from the prompt and not extended back to time zero.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The integral form is set up but the initial condition is dropped and the integral alone is reported, one of the distinguishing failures in BC-FRQ-2024-Q1-C. Elsewhere the integrand is not recognised as needing technology and antidifferentiation is attempted by hand, and in BC-FRQ-2026-Q1-C the integral starts at day zero although the prompt fixed the interval, or the unrounded decimal is reported against a rounding instruction.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: No prerequisite is listed for this skill in the record. When the failure is reading the initial value from the wrong row of the table, as BC-FRQ-2024-Q1-C describes, the breakdown is in table reading rather than in recognising the integrand.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-SKL-06046 (accumulation represented by an integral when no elementary antiderivative exists) for the conceptual failure; the procedural failure, where the integral is right but the initial value or the interval is mishandled, points to BC-FRQ-2024-Q1-C scoring behaviour on the initial condition point.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an integrand such as e to the negative t squared, recognise that it has no closed-form antiderivative and that the accumulation must be represented by a definite integral or approximated numerically.
skills.description_plain: Notice when no elementary antiderivative exists and keep the integral form.
skills.name: Recognise an integrand with no closed-form antiderivative

common_confusions: BC-MIS-09010 (the integral of a velocity component read as the coordinate)
BC-SKL-09021 (the forward case of the same accumulation)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-09005 (the known position is at the later time, so sign and limit order are the scored detail)
adaptive.mastered_if: When the known position is at the later time, the earlier coordinate is written as the known value minus the definite integral over the intervening interval, or equivalently with the limits running backwards, and the direction of time is stated in the work; the answer lies on the correct side of the known value, and BC-ERR-09021 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The initial value plus accumulation structure is present and the integral between the two times is added although the known time is the later one, which is BC-ERR-09021 and the observation in BC-SIG-09007.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Which of the two times the position is known at cannot be extracted from the stem, so the direction is guessed, which is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-09010 (what the accumulation adds to and from where) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-09021 (writing the accumulation with the limits in the right order) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: When the known position is at a later time than the requested one, write the earlier coordinate as the known value minus the definite integral over the intervening interval, or equivalently reverse the limits.
skills.description_plain: Going back in time reverses the order of the limits.
skills.name: Accumulate backwards in time from a known later position

common_confusions: BC-MIS-09012 (the direction of motion read from the sign of the position)
BC-SKL-09016 (the velocity components whose signs the argument uses)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-09008 (the coordinate and its rate have different sign patterns, so the two readings give different intervals)
adaptive.mastered_if: The times at which the particle moves toward the axis are found by requiring the relevant velocity component to have the sign opposite to that of the corresponding coordinate on the interval, and the answer states that sign relation as the reason; the interval reported is supported by the sign of the rate, and neither BC-ERR-09025 nor BC-ERR-09026 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The correct subinterval is reported with no statement about the sign of the rate, which is BC-ERR-09026 and the observation in BC-SIG-09009; or an interval is chosen from where the coordinate itself is negative rather than from the sign of its derivative, which is BC-ERR-09025.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The equation locating where the velocity component changes sign is not solved on the interval, so the subinterval boundaries are wrong, which is BC-PRQ-08001.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-09012 (that approach to an axis is governed by the sign of the rate against the sign of the coordinate) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08001 (locating the sign change of the component) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: isolated by BC-QA-09008
skills.description_formal: Given the sign of a coordinate on an interval, determine the times at which the particle moves toward the corresponding axis by finding where the derivative of that coordinate has the opposite sign.
skills.description_plain: Compare the sign of the coordinate with the sign of its rate.
skills.name: Determine when a particle moves toward or away from a coordinate axis

common_confusions: BC-MIS-04005 (speed and velocity conflated, so the sign is discarded)
BC-SKL-04012 (communicating the sign across the whole interval)
BC-SKL-04008 (the magnitude, which carries no direction)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-04004 (direction over a whole interval, where considering the sign of the velocity is a scored step)
adaptive.mastered_if: The direction of travel is argued from the sign of the velocity on the interval, with positive velocity named as motion in one direction along the line and negative as the other, and the position function is not used for the claim; BC-ERR-04008 is absent, so the quantity that must be negative for motion in the negative direction is correctly identified.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The direction is asserted from whether the position is positive or negative, BC-ERR-04008 with signal BC-SIG-04006; or, as the 2024 Q2 part D distinctions record, the correct derivative is analysed and the interval reported is the one where its sign is the opposite of what the direction requires.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Velocity is not obtained from the supplied position function, a gap at BC-SKL-04006; or the sign of an expression cannot be determined on an interval, BC-PRQ-04009.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-04005 (the sign of the velocity, not the position, records direction). Procedural failure: BC-PRQ-04009 (determining the sign of a function on an interval).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the velocity of a particle on a line over an interval, state the direction of motion from the sign of the velocity on that interval.
skills.description_plain: Positive velocity means one direction along the line and negative velocity the other.
skills.name: Determine the direction of motion from the sign of velocity
skills.notation: sign of v of t

common_confusions: BC-MIS-03014 (derivative notation treated as a label on an answer)
BC-MIS-03013 (higher orders seen as separate objects with their own symbols)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-03008 (orders of differentiation are named in the prompt and must be matched in the work)
adaptive.mastered_if: The same derivative is written in both notations without change of meaning, so f double prime of x and d squared y over d x squared are used interchangeably and the operator d/dx is distinguished from the quantity dy/dx within a single line; BC-ERR-03022 is absent, and the response can read the line aloud naming each symbol.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The computed derivative is correct and prime and Leibniz notations are mixed inside one equation in ways that do not agree, or dy is written where dy/dx is meant, BC-ERR-03022 with signal BC-SIG-03014; the 2025 Chief Reader report records this notation costing points in implicit differentiation responses.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The meaning of the first derivative symbol is itself unclear, a gap at BC-PRQ-03005 rather than a notation translation gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-03014 (d/dx is an operator and dy/dx is its result). Procedural failure: BC-PRQ-03005 (writing each order consistently in one notation).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a derivative in one notation, write the same derivative in the other, using d squared y over d x squared, f double prime of x, y double prime, or the nth order forms.
skills.description_plain: Move between prime notation and Leibniz notation without changing the meaning.
skills.name: Read and write higher-order derivative notation
skills.notation: d squared y over d x squared; f superscript n of x

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06012 (accumulation function with a variable, possibly composite, upper limit differentiated and then evaluated at a point)
adaptive.mastered_if: Before any differentiation happens, the response says that f must be continuous on an interval containing a and x, and only then writes that the derivative of the integral from a to x of f(t) dt equals f(x). The hypothesis survives the composite case in BC-QA-06012, where the upper limit is a function of x and the chain rule factor is attached to the upper limit while the continuity requirement is still stated about the integrand. No named errors are catalogued for this skill in the record, so the evidence rests on the hypothesis being volunteered rather than supplied by the question stem.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The conclusion is produced correctly and the hypothesis is omitted, or continuity is asserted about the accumulation function instead of about f. The BC-FRQ-2024-Q5-A scoring behaviour shows the neighbouring procedural slips that accompany this state, where the integrand is antidifferentiated instead of read off by the theorem, or a chain rule factor is introduced although the upper limit is plain x. In BC-FRQ-2025-Q4-A the theorem point can still be earned through an implied application, so a response that uses the theorem silently and never names continuity sits here.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The response cannot say what the derivative of an accumulation function is at all, which points back to BC-TOP-0115 rather than to the hypothesis itself. The tell is that the difficulty appears when asked to write the conclusion, not when asked what f must satisfy.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-TOP-0115 (the statement of the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus part one, including which function carries the continuity requirement); a procedural failure to evaluate the resulting derivative points instead to BC-QA-06012 (substituting the requested input into the integrand)

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: State that the conclusion that the derivative of the integral from a to x of f(t) dt equals f(x) requires f to be continuous on an interval containing a and x.
skills.description_plain: Name what must be true of f before the theorem may be used.
skills.name: State the continuity hypothesis of the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus part one

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08024 (every definite integral read as an area)
BC-MIS-08009 (an interpretation treated as complete once the quantity is named)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08014 (the integral is displayed and only its identification is scored, so interval and object separate cleanly)
adaptive.mastered_if: A displayed integral of the square root of one plus a squared derivative is named as the length of the graph of that function, and the interval is stated as running between the two limits of integration; both the object and the interval appear in the sentence, and neither BC-ERR-08043 nor BC-ERR-08044 is present.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The integral is named as the length of the curve with no interval given, which is BC-ERR-08043 and the observation in BC-SIG-08017; or the radical integral is described as the area under the graph, which is BC-ERR-08044.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The function whose derivative sits inside the radical cannot be identified from the notation, so the sentence has no subject, which is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08024 (a radical integrand against an area integrand) for the conceptual case; BC-ERR-08043 (naming the interval alongside the object) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a definite integral of the square root of one plus a squared derivative, state that it is the length of the graph of the function on the interval given by the limits.
skills.description_plain: Recognise the radical form and say which curve and interval it measures.
skills.name: Identify a given integral as an arc length and name the interval

common_confusions: BC-MIS-09007 (any interval containing the curve assumed to give its length or area)
BC-SKL-09037 (identifying one loop of a polar curve, the same question in polar form)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-09003 (the curve retraces on a longer interval, so the limits alone change the answer)
adaptive.mastered_if: The parameter interval is named as the values that carry the curve from one end of the described piece to the other, and it is checked that the interval traces that piece exactly once, by the zeros of the components or by the period of the trigonometric parts; BC-ERR-09016 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The integrand is correct and the limits span an interval that covers part of the curve twice, so the reported length exceeds the length of the piece, which is BC-ERR-09016.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Which parameter interval traces a curve exactly once cannot be decided for a standard curve, which is BC-PRQ-09004 rather than a length gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-09007 (what the limits have to do beyond containing the curve) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-09004 (testing that an interval traces the curve once) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an arc length integral or a described curve, name the parameter interval that bounds the piece of curve whose length is being computed, and check that the interval traces it once.
skills.description_plain: Say which parameter values bound the piece being measured.
skills.name: Identify the parameter interval over which a length is measured

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06016 (integrands of different structure are classified and the technique each one's markers select is named or applied)
adaptive.mastered_if: Each basic trigonometric integrand is matched to the differentiation rule it inverts, with the sign handled correctly so that the antiderivative of sine carries the minus and the antiderivative of cosine does not. Where the argument is a linear expression, the reciprocal of the inner coefficient appears in front, and where a product is recognisable as a trigonometric derivative it is read backwards directly rather than expanded. The constant of integration is present on every indefinite result.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Rules are inverted correctly in isolation but the inner constant is dropped from the sine antiderivative, which BC-FRQ-2024-Q5-D lists as the chain factor lost. A second state omits the constant of integration, treating an indefinite integral as definite, also recorded in that part. A third produces the right family with the sign reversed between sine and cosine.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The integrand needs a Pythagorean, double angle, or reciprocal identity before any antiderivative rule applies and the rewriting never happens, which is BC-PRQ-06004 failing and not this skill. A second earlier failure is BC-SKL-02035, where a limit that is a trigonometric derivative in disguise is not recognised as such, leaving no derivative rule to invert.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-PRQ-06004 (identities that rewrite an integrand into a form with a basic antiderivative) for the conceptual failure; procedural loss of the inner constant or the constant of integration points instead to BC-SKL-06042 itself.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an integrand that is a basic trigonometric function or a product recognisable as a trigonometric derivative, determine the antiderivative from the corresponding differentiation rule.
skills.description_plain: Read the trigonometric derivative rules backwards.
skills.name: Antidifferentiate basic trigonometric integrands

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10009 (the p-series criterion applied to series that are not p-series)
BC-SKL-10025 (limit comparison, which tolerates a mismatch in constant factors)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10004 (the comparison series is the object the test is run on)
BC-QA-10015 (the endpoint series is matched against a standard reference)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response names an explicit comparison series b sub n, a geometric series or a p-series, whose terms match the dominant behaviour of a sub n for large n, states it in sigma or general term form, and restricts the comparison to nonnegative terms. BC-ERR-10015 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A comparison series is named and its exponent or ratio does not match the dominant behaviour, so the inequality that follows cannot be established, or a comparison is attempted on a series whose terms change sign, which is BC-ERR-10015.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The dominant behaviour cannot be identified because the ratio of powers in n is not simplified, which is BC-PRQ-10004, or the exponent after a root conversion is wrong, which is BC-PRQ-06002.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-CON-10001 (dominant behaviour of terms for large n) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10004 (ratios of powers in n) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a series with nonnegative terms, select a geometric series or p-series whose terms agree with the dominant behaviour of a sub n for large n, and state the comparison series explicitly.
skills.description_plain: Pick a standard series whose terms match the dominant behaviour.
skills.name: Choose a comparison series for a given series

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10010 (comparison treated as association between similar series)
BC-SKL-10026 (limit comparison, where no inequality direction is needed)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10004 (the reason point depends on the inequality supporting the claim)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response writes the inequality between a sub n and b sub n in the direction the intended conclusion needs, valid for every n from the starting index onward, and supports it by a visible feature such as a larger denominator or a bounded numerator. BC-ERR-10016 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A serviceable comparison series is chosen and the inequality is written in the direction that does not support the verdict, bounding above by a divergent series or below by a convergent one, which is BC-SIG-10013 and BC-ERR-10016.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The relative size of the two general terms cannot be established for large n, which is BC-PRQ-10004 rather than a comparison gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10010 (which direction of inequality licenses which conclusion) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10004 (comparing sizes of terms) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a series and a chosen comparison series with nonnegative terms, state and support the inequality between a sub n and b sub n valid for all n from the starting index onward.
skills.description_plain: Show which series has the larger terms, for every index in range.
skills.name: Establish the term-by-term inequality for a direct comparison

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10010 (the direction of the inequality untied from the conclusion)
BC-SKL-10023 (establishing the inequality, the step before this one)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10004 (the verdict with a reason is the scored object)
BC-QA-10015 (the endpoint verdict rests on the comparison)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response combines the stated inequality with the known behaviour of b sub n into the verdict the direct comparison test supports, convergence when the larger series converges and divergence when the smaller one diverges, and names which series the verdict is about. BC-ERR-10016 and BC-ERR-10003 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The inequality and the reference behaviour are both correct and the conclusion drawn is the one the direction does not support, which is BC-ERR-10016, or the verdict is right and no series is identified where several appear, which is BC-ERR-10003.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The behaviour of the comparison series is not known, so nothing can be transferred: that is a p-series or geometric recall gap, BC-SKL-10019 or BC-SKL-10007, rather than a comparison gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10010 (what each direction of comparison implies) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-10019 (behaviour of the reference p-series) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a term-by-term inequality and the known behaviour of the comparison series, state the conclusion that the direct comparison test supports, and name the series concluded about.
skills.description_plain: Combine the inequality with the known behaviour of the comparison series.
skills.name: Conclude convergence or divergence by direct comparison

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10009 (the convergence boundary placed away from p equal to one)
BC-SKL-10006 (geometric form, where the index sits in the exponent instead of the base)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10004 (the named test follows directly from the family)
BC-QA-10001 (family recognition is the cue for test choice)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response names the family the series belongs to, harmonic, alternating harmonic, or p-series with the value of p stated, after rewriting any root or negative exponent as a single exponent on n; a series with a constant ratio or a factorial is correctly excluded from these families. BC-ERR-10014 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The family is named and the exponent is read off wrongly after a root is converted, so a p at most one is labelled convergent, which is BC-ERR-10014, or the alternating harmonic series is classified as harmonic with the sign factor ignored.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The root or reciprocal form cannot be converted to a power of n at all, which is BC-PRQ-06002, or the alternating factor is not read out of the sigma, which is BC-PRQ-10008.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10009 (what defines a p-series) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-06002 (converting roots to exponents) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a series, identify it as the harmonic series, the alternating harmonic series, a p-series with a stated p, or none of these.
skills.description_plain: Name which standard family a series belongs to.
skills.name: Classify a series as harmonic, alternating harmonic, or p-series

common_confusions: BC-MIS-02001 (a change in the quantity taken to be the rate)
BC-SKL-02002 (the two point form, which uses x minus a in place of h)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-02002 (the difference quotient must be written for a given rule before any limit is taken, which isolates the increment form)
adaptive.mastered_if: The quotient of f(a plus h) minus f(a) by h is written with the shifted input evaluated as a function value rather than distributed, and the quotient is then evaluated to a number for the given a and h, so both the difference and the division are visible in the work (BC-ERR-02001 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The shifted and base values are subtracted correctly but the division by h is omitted, which is BC-ERR-02001 and, in the 2025 guidelines, leaves the answer point unearned because a difference alone is not a rate.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: f(a plus h) cannot be identified as a single function value at a shifted input, which is a gap at BC-PRQ-02005, and inability to reduce the expanded numerator is BC-PRQ-02001 rather than a rate gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-02001 (the division that turns a change into a rate) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-02005 (reading a function value at a shifted input) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given f, a base point a, and an increment h, compute the quotient of f(a plus h) minus f(a) by h.
skills.description_plain: Use the quotient of the change in the function over an increment added to the base point.
skills.name: Compute an average rate of change from the increment difference quotient
skills.notation: the quotient of f(a plus h) minus f(a) by h

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01017 (an average over an interval read as the rate at a point in it)
BC-SKL-02005 (writing the instantaneous rate as a limit, which follows this distinction)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-02012 (a derivative presented in one notation must be said to denote a rate at an instant, which forces the contrast)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response states that an average rate is computed over an interval of nonzero length while an instantaneous rate is defined at a single input as a limit of such averages, and applies the distinction to a specific question by saying which of the two the number produced answers.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The two are described as different but the description of the instantaneous rate omits the limiting process, so it reads as an average over a very small interval rather than as a limit.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The rate at a point cannot be described as a limit of averages at all, which is a gap at BC-SKL-01003.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01017 (what changes when the interval closes to a point) for the conceptual failure; BC-SKL-01003 (the limit description of an instantaneous rate) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: State that an average rate of change is computed over an interval of nonzero length while an instantaneous rate of change is defined at a single input by a limit of such averages.
skills.description_plain: Say which of the two describes an interval and which describes a single moment.
skills.name: Distinguish an average rate of change from an instantaneous rate of change

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05004 (an existence theorem read as naming the input rather than asserting one exists)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05002 (a function and a closed interval given, with the interior input where the instantaneous rate equals the average rate required)
adaptive.mastered_if: Setting f prime of x equal to the average rate of change, solving, and then keeping only the solutions strictly inside (a,b) is done as one movement, with the equation itself written out so the reported number is supported rather than bare. Endpoint solutions are discarded and said to be discarded. A calculator solve is backed by the equation on the page. BC-ERR-05005 (a reported value that is an endpoint or lies outside the interval) does not occur.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: BC-SIG-05004 describes the usual halfway point, a correct derivative equation with a reported input at an endpoint or outside the interval. A second pattern is the bare numerical value with no supporting equation, which the BC-QA-05002 scoring treats as earning neither point, and the 2025 Q1 part B behaviour of an equation solved with the setup never written is the same omission.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: A wrong right-hand side in the derivative equation traces to BC-SKL-05003, since the average rate itself was formed wrongly, and an inability to isolate the roots of the resulting equation or to see where a denominator vanishes traces to BC-PRQ-05001.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05004 (the theorem guarantees a c without telling you where it is, so the interval condition is yours to impose); a procedural failure in the algebra points instead to BC-PRQ-05001 (solving equations and locating where an expression is zero or undefined)

skills.assessability_basis: isolated by BC-QA-05002
skills.description_formal: Solve f'(x) equal to the average rate of change over the interval and report the solutions that lie strictly inside it.
skills.description_plain: Set the derivative equal to the average rate and solve.
skills.name: Solve for a value of c that the theorem provides

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01012 (unbounded behaviour assumed the same on both sides)
BC-MIS-01018 (infinite limit notation exchanged with limit at infinity notation)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01009 (asymptote locations and one sided behaviour in correct notation carry separate credit)
adaptive.mastered_if: The statement records that f increases or decreases without bound as x approaches c, with the side carried on the arrow whenever the two sides behave differently, and the response does not write a single two sided infinite statement where the signs differ (BC-ERR-01019 absent) nor treat the statement as an existence claim for a real limit (BC-ERR-01020 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The unbounded behaviour is described correctly and the notation carries the wrong direction on one side, or the one sided markers are omitted although the two sides carry opposite signs, which is BC-ERR-01019.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The sign of the quotient on each side of the zero of the denominator cannot be determined, which is a gap at BC-PRQ-01009 and produces the same notation failure for a different reason.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01012 (the infinity symbol as a description of behaviour, and its sign per side) for the conceptual failure; BC-SKL-01055 (the sign analysis that fixes each side) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Write the statement that f increases or decreases without bound as x approaches c, including the one sided form when the two sides behave differently.
skills.description_plain: Use the infinity symbol to record unbounded growth, with the side when it matters.
skills.name: Write an infinite limit using correct notation

common_confusions: BC-MIS-04014 (indeterminate forms and infinity treated as numbers)
BC-SKL-04014 (the rate at a finite input rather than its end behaviour)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-04005 (the limit expression and its value are scored as two separate points)
adaptive.mastered_if: A limit expression is written for the rate as the independent variable increases without bound and is then evaluated, with the limit taken on the derivative rather than on the quantity and with limit notation carried through to the value; BC-ERR-04014 and BC-ERR-99007 are absent, so infinity is never substituted into the expression.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The end behaviour value is right and the supporting line substitutes infinity into the expression, signal BC-SIG-04010 and BC-ERR-04014, which the 2025 scoring notes treat as scratch work; or, as the 2025 Q1 part C rubric records, the limit is written on the function rather than on its derivative, which earns the notation point and not the value point.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The limit at infinity of the expression cannot be evaluated once written, an end behaviour gap at BC-SKL-01060 rather than a notation gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-04014 (infinity names a behaviour, not a value to compute with). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-01060 (evaluating an end behaviour limit once it is written).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a rate expression modelling a quantity, write a limit expression describing its end behaviour and evaluate that limit, using limit notation rather than arithmetic with infinity.
skills.description_plain: Write the limit of the rate as the independent variable grows without bound, then evaluate it.
skills.name: Interpret an end behaviour limit of a rate in context
skills.notation: limit of the rate as the variable increases without bound

common_confusions: BC-MIS-09016 (a local extremum argument taken to settle a farthest point)
BC-MIS-09013 (the polar radius treated as a Cartesian coordinate)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-09011 (a Cartesian coordinate is maximised along a polar curve on a closed angle interval, so an endpoint can carry the extreme)
adaptive.mastered_if: The relevant Cartesian coordinate is written in theta, differentiated, set equal to zero and solved on the angle interval, and the farthest point is settled by comparing the coordinate at the candidate with its values at both ends of the interval; the equation that was solved is on the page, so neither BC-ERR-09033 nor BC-ERR-09034 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The critical angle is found correctly and the justification is a first or second derivative test offered as settling the farthest point, which is BC-ERR-09033 and the state in BC-SIG-09011; or the angle is written down with nothing showing what was set equal to zero, which is BC-ERR-09034.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The trigonometric equation from setting the derivative to zero is not solved on the interval, which is BC-PRQ-08001; writing a justification that covers every candidate is BC-SKL-05028.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-09016 (why the endpoints of the angle interval enter the argument) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-05028 (writing the global justification) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: isolated by BC-QA-09011
skills.description_formal: Set the derivative with respect to theta of the relevant Cartesian coordinate equal to zero, solve on the interval, and justify the extreme value by comparing the coordinate at the candidate with its values at the endpoints.
skills.description_plain: Set the derivative of that coordinate equal to zero and compare candidates.
skills.name: Locate the point on a polar curve farthest from a coordinate axis

common_confusions: BC-MIS-09014 (the derivative of r read as the speed along the curve)
BC-SKL-09032 (the time rate of the distance, which does involve the angular rate)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-09009 (the interpretation of dr/dtheta is asked directly)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response states that dr/dtheta is the rate at which the distance from the origin changes with respect to the polar angle, and reads a positive value as moving away from the origin and a negative value as moving toward it; the sentence does not name a speed along the curve, so BC-ERR-09029 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The sign of dr/dtheta is read correctly for approach or recession and the quantity is described as the speed of the particle along the curve, which is BC-ERR-09029.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The symbol r is not tied to the distance from the origin in the polar description, so the sentence has no referent, which is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-09014 (distance from the origin against distance along the path) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-09030 (producing the derivative the sentence describes) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: State that dr/dtheta is the rate of change of the distance from the origin with respect to the polar angle, and read its sign as moving away from or toward the origin.
skills.description_plain: Say that it measures how the distance from the origin changes with the angle.
skills.name: Interpret dr/dtheta as the rate at which the distance from the origin changes

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06007 (the plotted curve is taken to be the function under discussion)
BC-MIS-06009 (restating a definition believed to count as a reason)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06003 (accumulation function analysed from a graph of the integrand made of segments and circular arcs)
adaptive.mastered_if: A single description of g holds all four pieces at once, the value at the starting input where the integral from a to a is zero, the intervals of rise and fall from the sign of f, the extrema at the sign changes of f, and the concavity from whether f is rising or falling. The description or sketch is consistent with itself, so a stated maximum sits at the end of a stated interval of increase, and each claim is attributed to a feature of the plotted f rather than to g, which is what BC-ERR-06010 omits. The curve being described is never the curve on the page, so BC-ERR-06008 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Some features are read from the right function and others from the plotted curve, which produces a description that contradicts itself, the mixed form of BC-ERR-06008. Another state gives an internally consistent description with every reason phrased about g changing concavity or g turning, which is BC-ERR-06010 and costs the reason points while the answer points stand. BC-FRQ-2025-Q4-A also records the accumulated area to the input reported in place of the derivative statement, so the function and its derivative are exchanged in the opening step and the rest of the description inherits it.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: A description that is right about monotonicity and silent or wrong about bending points at BC-SKL-06025, while wrong inflection inputs with correct increase intervals point at BC-SKL-06024, and a wholesale failure of the sign reading points at BC-SKL-06022. The tell is that the assembly is orderly and exactly one of the three component claims is unsupported.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06007 (holding the plotted integrand and the accumulation function apart across a whole multi part description) for the conceptual failure; when each feature is located correctly and only the written support is generic, the target is BC-ERR-06010 (tying every claim about g to the given graph of f)

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the graph of f, describe or sketch g(x) = the integral from a to x of f(t) dt, including its value at the starting input, its intervals of increase and decrease, its extrema, and its concavity.
skills.description_plain: Assemble monotonicity, extrema, and concavity into a description of g.
skills.name: Describe the graph of an accumulation function from the graph of the integrand

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06007 (the plotted curve is taken to be the function under discussion)
BC-MIS-06008 (a zero of the integrand is treated as a general turning feature of the accumulation function)
BC-MIS-06009 (restating the defining property of concavity is believed to count as a reason)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06003 (accumulation function analysed from a graph of the integrand made of segments and circular arcs)
adaptive.mastered_if: Inflection inputs for g come from the turning points of the plotted f, the places where f changes from increasing to decreasing or the reverse, and the written reason names that change in f rather than saying that g changes concavity. Junctions between two pieces of a piecewise graph are inspected as candidates, and the declared set is exact, since BC-FRQ-2025-Q4-B forfeits both the answer and the reason point for any extra declared input. Three errors are absent together, BC-ERR-06008 reading features of g off the plotted curve, BC-ERR-06009 placing inflection points at the zeros of f, and BC-ERR-06010 giving a reason in terms of g alone.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: BC-SIG-06009 records inflection inputs that coincide exactly with the axis crossings of the plotted curve, which is BC-ERR-06009 and produces the same list the extremum question would produce. BC-SIG-06010 records the opposite balance, correct inputs paired with a reason that names g changing concavity, which is BC-ERR-06010 and costs the reason point while the answer point stands. BC-FRQ-2018-Q3-D and BC-FRQ-2025-Q4-B also show two of three inputs given when a turning point at a junction between pieces is skipped.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: An absent BC-SKL-06018 shows as a response that never establishes g prime equal to f, so the second derivative relationship g double prime equal to f prime is unavailable and the student reads the figure for whatever feature looks salient. The tell is that the monotonicity of f is described accurately while the conclusion is attached to the wrong function.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-06008 (distinguishing the rule for extrema of g from the rule for inflection points of g) for the conceptual failure; when the inputs are right and only the justification fails, the target is BC-MIS-06009 (grounding a reason in the supplied graph instead of restating a definition)

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given the graph of f and g(x) = the integral from a to x of f(t) dt, locate the points of inflection of g at the inputs where f changes from increasing to decreasing or from decreasing to increasing, since g'' = f'.
skills.description_plain: Find where f changes from increasing to decreasing or the reverse.
skills.name: Locate points of inflection of an accumulation function from turning points of the integrand

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10003 (closed form used without checking the size of the ratio)
BC-MIS-10023 (the interior taken as the complete convergence answer)
BC-SKL-10072 (closed form recognition for a numerical power series)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10003 (the closed form is scored with the condition on the ratio attached)
BC-QA-10020 (the ratio argument decides convergence at a stated input)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response treats an expression in x as the common ratio, writes the closed form with that expression in the denominator, and records the inequality on the absolute value of the ratio that makes the closed form valid, converting it into a condition on x. BC-ERR-10005 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The closed form in x is written and the validity inequality is omitted, so the representation is claimed for every x, which is BC-ERR-10005, or the inequality is written in the ratio and never solved for x.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The absolute value inequality in the ratio cannot be turned into an interval in x, which is BC-PRQ-10001, or the constant quotient is not identified, which is BC-PRQ-10005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10003 (validity of a geometric closed form) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10001 (absolute value inequalities in x) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a power series that is geometric in x, identify the first term and the ratio as expressions in x, write the closed form, and state the inequality on the ratio that makes it valid.
skills.description_plain: Treat the expression in x as the ratio, sum it, and record where the sum is valid.
skills.name: Sum a geometric series whose ratio contains the variable

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10021 (the representation assumed valid at every input)
BC-MIS-10023 (endpoints never examined so the interval is incomplete)
BC-SKL-10059 (stating the interval with correct endpoint inclusion)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10020 (one point for the answer with the position of the input as the reason)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response names the interval of convergence in play, places the given input inside it, at an endpoint, or outside it, and states whether the series converges to the function at that input with that position as the reason; an interval carried in from an earlier part is used consistently. BC-ERR-10043 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The verdict is correct and no reason is attached, which is BC-SIG-10023 and BC-ERR-10043, or the position is described against the radius rather than against the interval so an endpoint case is left unresolved.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The interval cannot be read or compared with the input because interval notation is the blocker, which is BC-PRQ-10006.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10021 (where a series equals its function) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10006 (locating an input in an interval) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a series, its interval of convergence, and a specific input, state whether the series converges to the function at that input and give the position of the input relative to the interval as the reason.
skills.description_plain: Check whether the input lies inside the interval and say what follows.
skills.name: Decide whether a series converges to the function at a stated input

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05023 (the second derivative test treated as always decisive)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05013 (second derivative test applied at a critical point)
adaptive.mastered_if: Before any second derivative is evaluated, the learner records that f prime is zero at the input, then reports f double prime there and reads a negative value as a relative maximum and a positive value as a relative minimum. The direction of the correspondence holds under rewording and the classification is never applied at a non critical input, so BC-ERR-05036 (test used where the first derivative is not zero) and BC-ERR-05037 (sign convention reversed) both stay out.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Arithmetic on f double prime is correct and the extremum type comes out the opposite way, the BC-SIG-05028 observation and BC-ERR-05037. Another state evaluates the second derivative at an input never shown to be critical and classifies from it, which is BC-ERR-05036 and costs the justification point. A third pattern, visible in BC-FRQ-2026-Q2-C, classifies from the sign of the radial function rather than from the derivative.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: If the inputs fed into the test are not critical points at all, the earlier failure is BC-SKL-05010 (finding critical points where the first derivative equals zero), and the tell is a second derivative evaluated at a convenient input with no zero of f prime written anywhere. A learner who cannot say which way a curve bends for a negative second derivative is short of BC-SKL-05030.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05023 (no room held for the inconclusive case) for the conceptual failure. A reversed verdict with sound mechanics points instead to BC-SKL-05030 (reading concavity from the sign of the second derivative), since the sign to shape link is what has slipped.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: At an input where f' is zero, evaluate f'' and classify the point as a relative maximum when f'' is negative and a relative minimum when f'' is positive.
skills.description_plain: Use the sign of the second derivative at the point to classify it.
