common_confusions: BC-MIS-07006 (the field read as a plot rather than as directions)
BC-SKL-07013 (describing the pattern, which is the evidence this decision uses)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-07002 (two or three distinguishing points separate the candidates)
adaptive.mastered_if: Candidate equations are tested against computed slopes at points where they disagree and against the locus where the segments are horizontal, so the match rests on numbers and on the zero slope set rather than on the general look of the figure; BC-ERR-07016 and BC-ERR-07013 are absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A candidate is chosen with no computed slope and no zero slope locus mentioned, BC-ERR-07016 with signal BC-SIG-07015, which often fails when two candidates share a visible feature; or the dependence on one variable is misread from the field, BC-ERR-07013.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The slope a candidate assigns to a point cannot be computed, a gap at BC-SKL-07010; or the variable dependence cannot be read from the right side, BC-SKL-07013.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-07006 (the equation generates the segments point by point). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-07010 (evaluating each candidate where they differ).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Test candidate equations against the observed pattern of the field, using where the segments are horizontal and how the slope varies with each variable.
skills.description_plain: Say which equation could have drawn the field.
skills.name: Match a slope field to a differential equation

common_confusions: BC-MIS-02010 (transcendental functions differentiated by the power rule)
BC-SKL-02026 (the reciprocal as a negative power, which is the derivative and not the function here)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-02007 (an expression containing the natural logarithm, where giving the logarithm as its own derivative is visible)
adaptive.mastered_if: The derivative of the natural logarithm is written as the reciprocal of the input, restricted to the domain where the logarithm is defined, and the logarithm is not reproduced as its own derivative or treated as a power.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The reciprocal is produced but the domain restriction is not mentioned, so the derivative is asserted on inputs where the original function has no value.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Logarithm properties are not available, so a logarithmic expression is not simplified before differentiating or an absolute value is omitted, which is a gap at BC-PRQ-06003.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-02010 (the rule that belongs to the logarithm) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-06003 (logarithm rules and domain) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Write the derivative of the natural logarithm as the reciprocal of the input, on the domain where the logarithm is defined.
skills.description_plain: Recall that the natural logarithm gives one over the input.
skills.name: Differentiate the natural logarithm

common_confusions: BC-MIS-02014 (the plotted height used where a slope is wanted)
BC-SKL-02012 (the tangent slope interpretation this reading depends on)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-02009 (values of functions and of their derivatives are read from graphs and then used in a rule, so a height read as a slope propagates visibly)
adaptive.mastered_if: A tangent line is placed at the named point on the curve and its slope read from a rise and a run over a nearby interval, with the value reported as a slope and not as the height of the curve, and the sign of the slope matching the direction of the curve there.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The tangent direction is read correctly but the value is taken from a secant over a wide interval without acknowledging it as an approximation, or the rise and run are read from mismatched axis scales.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The height approached at a named input cannot be read from the graph at all, which is a graph reading gap at BC-SKL-01009.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-02014 (the derivative as a slope rather than a height) for the conceptual failure; BC-SKL-01009 (reading the graph at a named input) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a graph of a function, estimate the derivative at an input by reading the slope of the tangent line there, for instance from a rise and a run over a nearby interval.
skills.description_plain: Read the steepness of the curve at the point from the graph.
skills.name: Estimate a derivative at a point from a graph

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05011 (the plotted curve is treated as the function under discussion)
BC-MIS-05020 (concavity and monotonicity treated as the same property)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05009 (relating the graphs of a function and its first two derivatives, with three objects in play at once)
adaptive.mastered_if: Given a named feature, the response pairs it with the correct object every time: a relative extremum of f with a sign change of f prime, a point of inflection of f with a sign change of f double prime, an interval of decrease of f with f prime negative there. The pairing survives moving between an analytic description, a plotted curve, and a table of values, and BC-ERR-05043, matching a feature of the function with the wrong derivative, never appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The correspondences are internally consistent but every one is shifted by a single derivative in the same direction, which is BC-SIG-05034 and the pattern named in BC-ERR-05043, so a point of inflection gets paired with a zero of f prime and an extremum with a zero of f double prime. A weaker state mixes rising with being positive, the substance of BC-ERR-05043 when combined with confusing concavity and monotonicity. Scoring on BC-FRQ-2026-Q4-B shows the cost: listing zeros of the derivative when inflection was at issue, and writing an ordered pair instead of an input value, which earns the input point but forfeits eligibility for the reason.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The failure sits in BC-SKL-05031, determining concavity from whether the derivative graph rises or falls, when the response cannot say what f double prime does without first drawing something. The sign is that questions about intervals of decrease are answered correctly while any question naming bending is answered by slope, pointing back to BC-SKL-05015 for the monotonicity half.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05020 (rising and bending upward collapsed into one property) for the conceptual failure; a uniform one-derivative displacement with the concepts intact points instead to BC-SKL-05031 (concavity from whether the derivative graph rises or falls)

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a feature such as a relative maximum, a point of inflection, or an interval of decrease, name the corresponding feature on the graph of f' or f''.
skills.description_plain: Say which feature of one graph corresponds to a feature of the other.
skills.name: Match a named feature of a function with the corresponding feature of its derivative

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05012 (a gap in the domain not treated as interrupting an interval of behaviour)
BC-MIS-05020 (concavity and monotonicity treated as the same property)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05009 (relating the graphs of a function and its first two derivatives, with three objects in play at once)
adaptive.mastered_if: The number line is cut at the zeros and the undefined points of f prime and of f double prime, not anywhere else, and each resulting piece carries two recorded signs from which increasing or decreasing and concave up or concave down are read together. Gaps in the domain break the pieces rather than being swallowed inside a reported interval. BC-ERR-05048, partitioning at the zeros of the function itself, is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The first derivative row is correct throughout while the second derivative row is wrong on at least one piece, which is BC-SIG-05038. A different partial state builds the whole partition on the zeros of f as BC-ERR-05048 describes, so the cuts never align with the sign changes that matter. Scoring on BC-FRQ-2026-Q4-C shows the intersection step failing on its own: the union of the increasing intervals given instead of the intersection, the concave down intervals given with the increasing condition dropped, or a correct interval whose reason cites only one of the two required clauses about the plotted derivative.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: An unreliable single row points to BC-SKL-05016, building a sign chart on critical points and domain boundaries, visible when even the f prime row omits a domain boundary or a point where f prime is undefined. When the f prime row is sound and only the bending row fails, the earlier skill is BC-SKL-05030, determining intervals of concavity from the sign of the second derivative.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05012 (an interval reported across an input where the function does not exist) for the conceptual failure, and BC-SKL-05016 (building the sign chart on critical points and domain boundaries) when the partition itself is the step that breaks

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Partition the domain at the zeros and undefined points of f' and f'', then record both signs on each piece and read off the behaviour of f.
skills.description_plain: Record both derivative signs interval by interval.
skills.name: Build a combined sign table for the first and second derivatives

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06016 (substitution renames a variable without changing the problem, so limits and differentials carry over unchanged)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06008 (antiderivative or definite integral by substitution, where the integrand is a composite times a constant multiple of the inner derivative)
adaptive.mastered_if: The work commits to one bookkeeping route and stays there. Either the limits are rewritten as u values at the moment du is formed, or the antiderivative is carried back to x before the original endpoints are substituted, and the written line shows which route was taken. No line applies an x endpoint to an expression still carrying u, so BC-ERR-06018 (original limits kept after a substitution) is absent, and the endpoint evaluation on the definite integral from a to b reads consistently in a single variable.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The substitution itself is sound and the antiderivative in u is right, yet the final evaluation mixes variables, which is BC-ERR-06018 (original limits kept after a substitution) and blocks the answer point even when the arithmetic lands on the correct number (sg-23:17, sg-23:16). A second intermediate state shows the substituted endpoint expression written correctly but the numerical evaluation left undone, which under BC-FRQ-2026-Q5-A still earns the antiderivative point P1 and the value point P2 when the endpoint form is present (sg-26:18). An unsupported correct value with no antiderivative shown sits in the same band, earning P2 alone.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: When the u expression is never returned to x at all, the failure belongs to BC-SKL-06049 (back-substitute to express an indefinite integral in the original variable) rather than to limit handling. When the endpoints are rewritten but with the wrong u values, the gap is BC-SKL-06050 (change the limits of integration when substituting in a definite integral), and the tell is a numerically clean evaluation of an antiderivative in u against endpoints that were never recomputed from the inner expression.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure points to BC-MIS-06016 (substitution as a change of variable, not a relabelling), since the learner who believes u is shorthand has no reason to touch the limits at all. Procedural failure, where the change of variable is understood but the two routes are crossed mid-solution, points instead to BC-SKL-06050 (changing the limits of integration when substituting).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a definite integral evaluated by substitution, either convert the limits to u values or back-substitute to the original variable before applying the original limits, and do not mix the two.
skills.description_plain: Keep the original limits only if you convert back to x first.
skills.name: Evaluate a definite integral by substitution with back-substitution before the limits are used

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08013 (the differential treated as a label for slicing direction)
BC-SKL-08026 (choosing the variable for an area, the same decision in a plane region)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08011 (the stem names the axis of perpendicularity, so the variable is dictated rather than chosen)
adaptive.mastered_if: From the phrase naming the axis the cross sections are perpendicular to, the variable of integration is selected, the boundary functions are rewritten in that variable, and the limits are the extent of the base in it; integrand, limits, and differential agree on one variable, and BC-ERR-08023 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The correct variable is named from the phrase and the integrand is left in the other variable, so an expression in x sits under dy or the reverse, which is BC-ERR-08023 and the state in BC-SIG-08009.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The boundary equation cannot be solved for the other variable, so the rewrite is impossible rather than omitted, which is BC-PRQ-08002.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08013 (that the differential fixes the variable the integrand must be written in) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08002 (rewriting the boundaries in that variable) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a description of cross sections perpendicular to an axis, select the variable of integration and express the boundary functions in that variable.
skills.description_plain: Read whether the slices stand on the x axis or the y axis and integrate in that variable.
skills.name: Determine the axis the cross sections are perpendicular to

common_confusions: BC-MIS-02009 (constants and radicals not seen as powers)
BC-SKL-02025 (the integer exponent case)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-02006 (an expression built from powers, radicals, and reciprocals, where an untouched term is visible in the derivative)
adaptive.mastered_if: A radical or a reciprocal is rewritten as x to a fractional or negative power before differentiating, the power rule is applied with the original exponent as a factor (BC-ERR-02015 absent), no such term is copied through unchanged (BC-ERR-02017 absent), and the result is returned to radical or reciprocal form when that is requested.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The polynomial terms are differentiated correctly while a radical or reciprocal term is carried through untouched, which is BC-SIG-02011 and BC-ERR-02017, so the rewriting step is the only one missing.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: A square root cannot be written as a one half power or a reciprocal as a negative power, which is an exponent gap at BC-PRQ-06002, and omitting the coefficient once rewritten is a BC-SKL-02025 gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-02009 (radicals and reciprocals as powers) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-06002 (rewriting with negative and fractional exponents) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Rewrite a radical or a reciprocal as x to a negative or fractional power, apply the power rule, and return the result to the requested form.
skills.description_plain: Turn the root or the fraction into an exponent first, then apply the rule.
skills.name: Differentiate a power function after rewriting a radical or a reciprocal as a power

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10021 (substitution made at an input outside the interval)
BC-SKL-10057 (endpoint substitution, the same operation at the ends of the interval)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10002 (the numerical series is then summed or classified)
BC-QA-10008 (the numerical series is what the error bound is written about)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response substitutes the given input for the variable x in the Taylor series, not for the index, simplifies each term to a number, and presents the numerical series in sigma or expanded form, keeping any alternating factor the input produces. BC-ERR-10034 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The substitution is made and the sign factor produced by a negative input is dropped, which is BC-ERR-10034, or the input is placed where the index sits so the terms do not reduce to numbers.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The general term cannot be read from the sigma, which is BC-PRQ-10008, or the resulting powers cannot be evaluated, which is BC-PRQ-06002.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10021 (where a series represents its function) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10008 (substituting into the general term) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a Taylor series and an input in its interval of convergence, substitute the value and present the resulting numerical series in sigma or expanded form.
skills.description_plain: Substitute the input into the series and read the numbers that result.
skills.name: Evaluate a Taylor series at a point to obtain a numerical series

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10017 (an error bound applied as a formula with no hypotheses)
BC-MIS-10018 (the bound written as the exact error)
BC-SKL-10039 (confirming the alternating conditions)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10009 (the Lagrange route, where a derivative bound is supplied)
BC-QA-10008 (the alternating route, where the omitted term is the bound)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response checks whether the series at the input alternates with absolute values decreasing to zero and, when it does, uses the first omitted term as the bound; where those conditions are not met it writes the Lagrange bound instead, and it states which conditions drove the choice. BC-ERR-10033 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A bound is chosen and used cleanly while the reason for choosing it is not stated, or the Lagrange bound is reached for where the series alternates and no derivative bound is available, which is BC-ERR-10033.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The form of the series at the input cannot be read, so neither set of conditions can be checked, which is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10017 (the hypotheses each bound requires) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-10039 (checking the alternating conditions) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a Taylor approximation, decide whether the series alternates with terms decreasing to zero, in which case the alternating series bound applies, or whether the Lagrange bound is the available tool, and state the reason for the choice.
skills.description_plain: Pick the bound whose conditions the situation satisfies.
skills.name: Choose between the Lagrange and alternating series error bounds

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10021 (the series taken as valid at every input)
BC-MIS-10003 (the closed form used without a size check on the ratio)
BC-SKL-10072 (recognising a geometric power series in closed form)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10017 (substitution into this series produces most related expansions)
BC-QA-10003 (the geometric closed form and its condition)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response writes one over one minus x as the sum of x to the n starting at n equal to zero and states that the representation holds for the absolute value of x less than one, giving the condition alongside the series rather than after it is used. BC-ERR-10040 and BC-ERR-10005 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The series is written correctly and the restriction on x is omitted, so the closed form is claimed everywhere, which is BC-ERR-10005, or a sign pattern belonging to one over one plus x is attached.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The constant ratio x is not recognised as what makes this series geometric, which is BC-PRQ-10005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10021 (the interval attached to a representation) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10005 (the constant ratio) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Reproduce the Maclaurin series for one over one minus x as the sum of x to the n, and state that it converges for absolute value of x less than one.
skills.description_plain: Write the geometric series for one over one minus x and its interval.
skills.name: Recall the Maclaurin series for one over one minus x

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01006 (the indeterminate form treated as an answer)
BC-SKL-01024 (the factoring route, which does not resolve a trigonometric indeterminacy)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01004 (a quotient that gives zero over zero and must be rewritten into an equivalent form before evaluation)
adaptive.mastered_if: A trigonometric quotient that is indeterminate at c is rewritten with a Pythagorean, double angle, or reciprocal identity into an expression whose limit can be read off, the identity used is visible in the work, and the value follows from the rewritten form rather than from substitution into the original.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: An identity is applied correctly but the resulting expression is not simplified far enough to remove the indeterminacy, so the response stops at a second zero over zero form.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Exact values of sine and cosine at the target angle are unavailable, or the oscillating factor cannot be bounded, which is a gap at BC-PRQ-01005; not seeing that the form requires rewriting is a BC-SKL-01028 gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01006 (an indeterminate form as a signal to rewrite) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-01005 (exact trigonometric values and bounds) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a trigonometric quotient that is indeterminate at c, apply an identity or an alternate form to produce an equivalent expression whose limit can be read off.
skills.description_plain: Use an identity to turn the expression into one that can be evaluated.
skills.name: Evaluate an indeterminate limit by rewriting with trigonometric identities

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01007 (cancellation treated as a move on repeated symbols)
BC-MIS-01006 (the indeterminate form read as an answer)
BC-SKL-01025 (the conjugate route, used when a radical blocks factoring)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01004 (an indeterminate quotient that must be rewritten, with separate credit for establishing the form and for the value)
adaptive.mastered_if: Substitution is shown to give zero over zero with the limits of numerator and denominator presented separately, the numerator and denominator are factored, the common factor is divided out with the restriction to inputs other than c respected, and the simplified expression is evaluated at c; a summand is never cancelled in place of a factor (BC-ERR-01010 absent) and zero is not reported from the numerator alone (BC-ERR-01008 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The factorisation and cancellation are correct but the substitution into the simplified expression gives a wrong number, which BC-SIG-01003 records as an arithmetic rather than conceptual loss, or the form is written as a limit set equal to zero over zero instead of as two separate limits.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The quadratic or cubic cannot be factored, so the response substitutes, reaches zero over zero, and stops, which is a factoring gap at BC-PRQ-01001; not knowing that the form calls for a rewriting at all is a BC-SKL-01028 gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01007 (factors divide out, terms do not) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-01001 (factoring and dividing out a common factor) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a quotient whose numerator and denominator both tend to zero at c, factor both, divide out the common factor valid for inputs other than c, and evaluate the resulting expression at c.
skills.description_plain: Factor top and bottom, cancel the shared factor, then substitute.
skills.name: Evaluate an indeterminate limit by factoring and dividing out a common factor

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01006 (the symbol zero over zero treated as a value, whether zero, undefined, or nonexistent)
BC-SKL-01029 (classifying the form, which includes the nonzero over zero case this skill excludes)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01004 (credit for establishing the form requires the two limits presented separately, which is the behaviour at issue)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response presents the limit of the numerator and the limit of the denominator separately, both zero, states that substitution assigns no value, and announces that an equivalent expression is needed; the form is not written as a limit set equal to zero over zero (BC-ERR-01011 absent), not read as the answer zero (BC-ERR-01008 absent), and not read as nonexistence (BC-ERR-01009 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The limit is written equal to the indeterminate symbol and the response then rewrites correctly and reaches the right value, which BC-SIG-01005 records as a notation habit rather than a gap.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The response identifies the form and stops because no factorisation is attempted, which BC-SIG-01004 and BC-PRQ-01001 place in the algebra of factoring rather than in reading the form.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01006 (two expressions with the same form and different limits) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-01001 (producing the factorisation the form calls for) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: State that a quotient whose numerator and denominator both tend to zero has no value assigned by substitution and that an equivalent expression is required before the limit can be determined.
skills.description_plain: See that zero over zero carries no value and that the expression must be changed.
skills.name: Recognise an indeterminate form as a signal that rewriting is needed

common_confusions: BC-MIS-02006 (the two properties treated as equivalent)
BC-SKL-02021 (the converse direction, where continuity does not deliver a derivative)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-02004 (the implication between the two properties is the object of the argument)
adaptive.mastered_if: Given a discontinuity at a point, the response concludes that the function is not differentiable there and names the contrapositive of the implication from differentiability to continuity as the reason, with the discontinuity itself established from the three conditions.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The conclusion is correct but the reason is given as the graph being broken rather than as the contrapositive, so the logical step is not exhibited.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The discontinuity is not established in the first place because the three conditions were not tested, which is a gap at BC-SKL-01044, and not holding the implication at all is BC-SKL-02019.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-02006 (the implication and its contrapositive) for the conceptual failure; BC-SKL-01044 (establishing the discontinuity) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given that a function is discontinuous at a point, conclude that it is not differentiable there, as the contrapositive of the implication that differentiability gives continuity.
skills.description_plain: Read the implication backwards to rule out a derivative where the function breaks.
skills.name: Conclude non-differentiability from a discontinuity

common_confusions: BC-MIS-02007 (differentiability treated as a visual property)
BC-SKL-02023 (a vertical tangent, where the one sided quotients are unbounded rather than unequal)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-02005 (the reason must refer to the one sided behaviour of the difference quotient, which is exactly this evidence)
adaptive.mastered_if: The one sided limits of the difference quotient at the point are evaluated as two numbers, shown to exist and differ, and the nonexistence of the derivative is concluded from that comparison rather than from the sharpness of the drawing (BC-ERR-02013 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The verdict that the derivative does not exist is correct but is supported only by the appearance of the graph, which is BC-SIG-02009 and BC-ERR-02013, so the reason point is lost while the verdict stands.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: One sided limits cannot be read from a graph at all, which is a gap at BC-SKL-01010, and inability to reduce the difference quotient to a form that can be evaluated is BC-PRQ-02001.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-02007 (the one sided slopes as the evidence) for the conceptual failure; BC-SKL-01010 (reading one sided values) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Evaluate the one sided limits of the difference quotient at a point and conclude that the derivative does not exist there when they exist and differ.
skills.description_plain: Show that the slope approached from the left differs from the slope approached from the right.
skills.name: Identify a corner from unequal one sided limits of the difference quotient

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01002 (one side taken as sufficient)
BC-SKL-01044 (the continuity test, which adds the comparison with the defined value)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01006 (a piecewise rule at a named input, where the two branch evaluations are separately visible)
adaptive.mastered_if: At a branch boundary the left hand limit is evaluated from the branch that applies to the left and the right hand limit from the branch that applies to the right, the two are compared, and the two sided limit is reported only when they agree, with each substitution visibly taken into the branch whose condition covers that side (BC-ERR-01017 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: One of the two one sided limits is computed from the branch that does not apply on that side, which is BC-ERR-01017, so the comparison is carried out on a wrong value, or the two values agree and the response never states the two sided conclusion.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The branch conditions cannot be matched to inputs at all, so the boundary input is substituted into whichever expression is written first, which is a piecewise reading gap at BC-PRQ-01003.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01002 (why both branches must be evaluated) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-01003 (matching a branch condition to a side of the boundary) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: For a piecewise defined function, evaluate the left hand and right hand limits at a boundary from the relevant branch expressions and report the two sided limit when they agree.
skills.description_plain: Evaluate each branch at the boundary and compare.
skills.name: Determine a two sided limit by matching one sided limits of a piecewise rule

common_confusions: BC-MIS-03004 (y as an independent symbol)
BC-SKL-03010 (isolating dy/dx is the algebra that follows this step)
BC-MIS-03014 (derivative notation treated as decoration, so the operator is dropped)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-03004 (the eligible attempt point turns on whether an equation survives the differentiation)
adaptive.mastered_if: Every term of both sides is differentiated with respect to x and the result is still an equation, with the derivative of a constant right hand side written as zero rather than dropped; y terms carry dy/dx and mixed terms carry the product rule, so BC-ERR-03009 and BC-ERR-03007 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The left hand side is differentiated correctly and the equals zero is dropped, leaving an expression, which is BC-ERR-03009; the 2025 Chief Reader report records that responses in this state were generally unable to recover the first two points.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Individual terms are differentiated wrongly, so the gap is at BC-SKL-03007 for the y terms or BC-SKL-03008 for the mixed terms rather than in the term by term sweep itself.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-03014 (d/dx is an operator applied to both sides, not a label). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-03007 (term by term differentiation with the dy/dx factor).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an equation in x and y, differentiate each term of both sides with respect to x, retaining the right hand side including a zero when the right hand side is constant.
skills.description_plain: Differentiate every term on both sides, and keep the equation an equation.
skills.name: Differentiate both sides of an implicit equation term by term
skills.notation: d/dx applied to both sides

common_confusions: BC-MIS-03005 (a short mixed term treated as a single symbol)
BC-MIS-03004 (y treated as independent, so no factor appears)
BC-SKL-03007 (a y term alone needs the factor but no product rule)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-03004 (the mixed term is where the product rule point is won or lost)
adaptive.mastered_if: A term containing both variables is differentiated as a product, so six x y becomes six y plus six x dy/dx, with the product rule visible and the dy/dx factor carried on the y factor; BC-ERR-03008 is absent, and the two pieces are separable in the way the 2025 Q5 part A rubric separates the product rule point from the chain rule point.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: One of the two product terms is present and the other is dropped, which under the 2025 scoring guidelines earns the chain rule point and not the product rule point; or the product rule is applied and the dy/dx factor is missing from the y factor, BC-ERR-03007 with signal BC-SIG-03004.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The product rule is not applied to a term in x alone either, an elementary rule gap upstream at BC-PRQ-03005 and BC-SKL-02036 rather than an implicit differentiation gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-03005 (a mixed term is two factors, each varying). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-03007 (the dy/dx factor on the y factor of the product).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a term that is a product of an expression in x and an expression in y, differentiate with respect to x using the product rule, applying the chain rule to the factor in y.
skills.description_plain: A term like x times y needs the product rule, and the y factor still carries dy/dx.
skills.name: Apply the product rule to a term containing both x and y
skills.notation: d/dx of six x y equals six y plus six x dy/dx

common_confusions: BC-MIS-03006 (dy/dx expected to come out in x alone)
BC-SKL-03014 (verifying a supplied form rather than producing one)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-03004 (the isolated expression has to match a stated form, so premature division shows)
adaptive.mastered_if: All dy/dx terms are moved to one side, dy/dx is factored out, and the equation is divided once to give dy/dx as a single quotient in x and y; the y remaining in the answer is accepted as the finished form rather than manipulated away, and BC-ERR-03010 is absent because no division happens while dy/dx still stands on both sides.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The differentiated equation is correct and the response divides before collecting, so the isolated expression is not dy/dx, which is BC-ERR-03010; or the work halts at a correct differentiated equation with no collection at all, signal BC-SIG-03005.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Given a differentiated equation already written, the response still cannot factor and isolate a common linear factor, an algebra gap at BC-PRQ-03002 rather than a calculus gap, which is exactly the separation signal BC-SIG-03005 prescribes.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-03006 (the slope of an implicit curve depends on both coordinates). Procedural failure: BC-PRQ-03002 (collecting like terms and factoring a common factor).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an equation containing dy/dx linearly, collect the dy/dx terms on one side, factor dy/dx, and divide to produce an expression for dy/dx in x and y.
skills.description_plain: Gather the dy/dx terms, factor dy/dx out, and divide.
skills.name: Solve the differentiated equation for dy/dx
skills.notation: dy/dx equals a quotient in x and y

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06014 (converting between a limit of Riemann sums in sigma notation and a definite integral)
adaptive.mastered_if: Starting from a definite integral of a continuous function over [a,b], the learner produces the limit as n approaches infinity of a sigma expression whose width is (b minus a) over n and whose sample point is stated explicitly, for instance a plus i times that width, and the integrand is evaluated at that sample point rather than at the bare index. The direction of this construction is understood as the reverse of reading an integral out of a sum, and the interval endpoints appear in the sum only through the width and the sample point, never as limits of summation.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A sum of the right shape appears but the width is written as 1 over n with a and b forgotten, so the construction only works on an interval of length one. Another state is a sigma expression assembled correctly with the limit as n approaches infinity omitted, which leaves an approximation where an equality was required.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: BC-SKL-06013 is the earlier skill that fails first, and the sign is that the learner can say what the answer should look like but cannot build the sigma expression for a stated function, interval, and partition. BC-PRQ-06006 is implicated when the index and its limits are themselves unstable.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-PRQ-06006 (summation notation and the general term) when the conceptual link between an integral and an indexed sum is missing; a procedural failure to produce the width and sample point points instead to BC-SKL-06013 (writing a Riemann sum in sigma notation for a given function, interval, and partition).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a definite integral of a continuous function over [a,b], write an equivalent limit of Riemann sums with an explicit subinterval width and sample point.
skills.description_plain: Go the other way and write the integral as a limit of sums.
skills.name: Express a definite integral as the limit of a Riemann sum

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06014 (converting between a limit of Riemann sums in sigma notation and a definite integral)
adaptive.mastered_if: Reading a limit of Riemann sums, the response pulls the width factor out of the general term to recover delta x, deduces the interval length b minus a from it, reads the sample point expression to fix the lower limit a, and then writes the definite integral from a to b of the recovered integrand. The letter used for the index disappears and the variable of integration is introduced fresh, and the answer is an integral rather than a numerical value, since no antidifferentiation is asked for here.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The integrand is recovered but the limits of integration are guessed, typically 0 to 1 regardless of the sample point, which shows the second and third steps of BC-QA-06014 being skipped. A further intermediate state is an integral written with the index still present in the integrand, so the limit of the sum was rewritten symbol for symbol rather than interpreted.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: BC-SKL-06012 is the earlier failure hiding here when the learner cannot expand the sigma expression into explicit products, so the value and width parts of the general term are never separated. BC-SKL-01006 shows up when the limit statement as n approaches infinity is treated as decoration and the response works with a fixed n, and BC-PRQ-06006 shows up when the index limits themselves cannot be read.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-SKL-01006 (interpreting a limit statement given in analytic notation) when the conceptual role of the limiting process is absent; a procedural failure to split the general term into a value and a width points instead to BC-SKL-06012 (expanding summation notation into an explicit Riemann sum).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a limit of Riemann sums as n approaches infinity or as the maximum subinterval width approaches 0, identify the integrand, the lower limit, and the upper limit, and write the equivalent definite integral.
skills.description_plain: Read the integrand and the limits of integration out of a limit of sums.
skills.name: Convert the limit of a Riemann sum into a definite integral

diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06016 (a mixed set of integrands where each structure has to select its own technique)
adaptive.mastered_if: One over one plus x squared is read as arctangent and one over the square root of one minus x squared as arcsine, and the two are told apart by the structural marker rather than by guessing. A constant in place of the one is factored out so the form matches before the rule is applied, and a linear inner argument brings its reciprocal constant with it. The candidate can be differentiated back to the integrand as a check.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The inverse trigonometric family is identified but the wrong member is chosen, so a square root denominator is answered with arctangent or the reverse. In other work the form is matched only when the constants are already one, and any rescaling of the denominator sends the response toward an unrelated technique, which BC-QA-06016 exposes when the preconditions of the ruled-out techniques are never checked.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The derivatives of inverse sine, cosine, and tangent cannot be stated on demand, so there is nothing to invert. That is BC-SKL-03021 rather than this skill, and the tell is a correct structural reading of the integrand followed by a fabricated antiderivative.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-SKL-03021 (stating the inverse trigonometric derivatives) for the conceptual failure; when the rule is known but the constants are not factored to match the form, the target is BC-PRQ-06004 (rewriting an integrand into a recognisable form).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an integrand matching the derivative of an inverse trigonometric function, determine the antiderivative as that inverse trigonometric function.
skills.description_plain: Recognise the one over one plus x squared and one over the root of one minus x squared forms.
skills.name: Antidifferentiate integrands whose antiderivatives are inverse trigonometric

common_confusions: BC-MIS-07006 (segments read as points of a curve)
BC-SKL-07016 (choosing among candidate equations using this pattern)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-07002 (the pattern along rows and columns is one of the distinguishing features)
adaptive.mastered_if: The form of the right side is used to say whether the slope depends on the independent variable, the dependent variable, or both, and the corresponding pattern is named, so a field constant along rows is matched to a right side free of one variable; BC-ERR-07013 is absent, and the claim is checked against segments that are actually identical.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The right side is read correctly and the field is described as varying along a line on which the printed segments are identical, or the reverse, BC-ERR-07013 with signal BC-SIG-07012, which then supports a match on a false feature.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Individual slopes cannot be computed to test the claim, a gap at BC-SKL-07010.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-07006 (which variables appear in the right side governs the pattern). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-07010 (computing two slopes on the same line to test the claim).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Decide from the form of the right side whether the slope depends on the independent variable, the dependent variable, or both, and describe the resulting pattern in the field.
skills.description_plain: Notice when the field repeats along rows or along columns.
skills.name: Describe how a field depends on only one of the variables

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08013 (the differential treated as changeable without changing the integrand)
BC-SKL-08026 (choosing the variable of integration, a separate decision)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08009 (the left and right boundaries are curves, so the rewrite in y is unavoidable)
adaptive.mastered_if: The equation relating x and y is solved for x in terms of y, the branch chosen is the one that bounds the region, and the sign taken on a square root or the range chosen on an inverse is justified by a point on that boundary; the rewritten expression contains y and no x, so BC-ERR-08023 cannot arise downstream.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The equation is rearranged and the expression retained still contains x, or both branches of a square root are carried forward with no choice made, so an integrand in x is paired with dy, which is BC-ERR-08023 and the observation in BC-SIG-08009.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The algebra of isolating one variable, including taking a root or an inverse of both sides, does not go through, which is BC-PRQ-08002 rather than a slicing gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08013 (that the integrand must be written in the variable of the differential) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08002 (solving the equation for x) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a curve described by an equation in x and y, solve for x as a function of y on the branch that bounds the region.
skills.description_plain: Solve the equation so that x is written in terms of y.
skills.name: Rewrite a curve as a function of y

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08013 (the differential treated as changeable without changing the integrand)
BC-SKL-08018 (the same comparison for upper and lower in x)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08009 (horizontal slices, where right and left replace upper and lower)
adaptive.mastered_if: Both curves are expressed in y, a y value interior to the interval is substituted into each, and the curve returning the larger x is named as the right boundary; that decision then places the right expression first in the difference, and BC-ERR-08020 does not appear in the integrand that follows.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The comparison at the interior y is carried out correctly and the integrand is still written left minus right, giving a negative value that is reported or silently made positive, which is BC-ERR-08020 with the pattern recorded in BC-SIG-08007.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Substituting a y value into an expression written in y is itself mishandled, which is BC-PRQ-06005 rather than an ordering gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08013 (which variable the comparison is made in) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-08025 (placing the chosen order into the dy integral) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given two curves written in y and an interval of y values, determine which one gives the larger x value there.
skills.description_plain: Decide which graph is farther right before writing the difference.
skills.name: Identify which curve is to the right on an interval of y

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08013 (the differential treated as changeable without changing the integrand)
BC-MIS-08012 (limits treated as a viewing window rather than a boundary)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08009 (the region is bounded left and right, so both the limits and the integrand live in y)
adaptive.mastered_if: A definite integral in y is written with integrand the right curve minus the left curve, both expressions in y, dy as the differential, and limits that are the y values bounding the region, and it is then evaluated to a nonnegative number; neither BC-ERR-08024 nor BC-ERR-08018 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The integrand is correct in y while the limits are the x values of the region, which is BC-ERR-08024; or the whole expression is right except the missing dy, which is BC-ERR-08018; an integrand still containing x under dy is the not mastered state in BC-SIG-08009.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The boundary curves were never solved for x in terms of y, so nothing can be integrated with respect to y, which is BC-PRQ-08002 rather than a setup gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08013 (matching integrand, limits, and differential to one variable) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08002 (rewriting each boundary as a function of y) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Write a definite integral in y with integrand the difference of the two curves in the order right minus left, with limits the y values bounding the region, and evaluate it.
skills.description_plain: Write the integral of right minus left, dy, and evaluate it.
skills.name: Set up and evaluate an area integral with respect to y

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01002 (one side treated as settling the limit)
BC-SKL-01009 (the two sided estimate, which requires comparing the two readings)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01001 (requests one sided values at a break as separate answers, so each side is scored on its own)
adaptive.mastered_if: The height approached from the left and the height approached from the right are reported as two separate answers with the side attached to each, including at an input where the two differ and at an input where the graph has a closed point at neither height, and neither one is promoted to a two sided claim (BC-ERR-01002 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Both one sided heights are read correctly but the response labels them with the wrong sides, or answers the one sided question with a single two sided statement, which is BC-ERR-01002.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The reading is taken at the wrong input or the vertical and horizontal axes are interchanged, which is a graph reading gap at BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01002 (each side is a claim in its own right) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-06005 (reading a graph at a named input) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a graph of f, report the left hand and right hand limits at a target input as separate values.
skills.description_plain: Read separately the height approached from the left and from the right.
skills.name: Estimate one sided limits from a graph

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01001 (the limit treated as another name for evaluation)
BC-MIS-01003 (a limit expected to be attained)
BC-SKL-01043 (continuity, which is where the two quantities are compared rather than distinguished)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01001 (asks for the limit and the function value at the same input as separate answers, which is exactly the separation BC-SIG-01002 tests)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response states that the limit at c is determined by values of f at inputs near c and not equal to c, and exhibits the separation concretely, for example a graph with an open circle at one height and a closed point at another where the limit and the value are reported as two different numbers, with the limit still reported where f(c) is undefined (BC-ERR-01001 and BC-ERR-01003 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The two quantities are named as different in principle but the plotted value is handed in when the limit is requested, which is BC-ERR-01001, or nonexistence is claimed at an input where f is undefined although both sides approach the same height, which is BC-ERR-01003.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The height read from the graph belongs to the wrong input altogether, or f and f prime are interchanged, which is a reading gap at BC-PRQ-06005 rather than a confusion between limit and value.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01001 (the limit as a statement about nearby inputs) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-06005 (reading an open and a closed point at one input) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: State that the limit of f at c is determined by values of f at inputs near c and not equal to c, so it may exist where f(c) is undefined and may differ from f(c).
skills.description_plain: Say that the limit describes nearby outputs and not the output at the point itself.
skills.name: Distinguish the limit at a point from the function value at that point

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01002 (a limit claimed from whichever side was examined)
BC-SKL-01012 (nonexistence from unbounded values, a different mechanism)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01001 (a graph with a jump, where the two one sided readings and the nonexistence verdict are scored separately)
adaptive.mastered_if: Both one sided limits at c are named as values, the response states that they differ, and the conclusion is that the two sided limit does not exist, with the two values kept in the answer rather than replaced by one of them (BC-ERR-01002 absent); the conclusion holds whether the rule is piecewise or the evidence is a graph with a jump.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The two one sided limits are reported correctly and then one of them is named as the two sided limit, which is BC-SIG-01001 and BC-ERR-01002, so the comparison step is the only thing missing.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The one sided values themselves are wrong because the boundary input was substituted into the branch that does not apply on that side, which is a piecewise reading gap at BC-PRQ-01003, or because an absolute value was not split into branches, which is BC-PRQ-01006, rather than a failure of the comparison.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01002 (why agreement of the two sides is what existence means) for the conceptual failure; BC-SKL-01010 (reading each one sided limit) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a graph or rule whose left hand and right hand limits at c exist and differ, conclude that the two sided limit at c does not exist and name the two values.
skills.description_plain: Say the limit does not exist when the two sides head to different heights.
skills.name: Determine that a limit fails to exist because the one sided limits differ

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05026 (a table of values believed to settle behaviour between the listed inputs)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05009 (relating the graphs of a function and its first two derivatives, with three objects in play at once)
adaptive.mastered_if: Sign changes of f prime or f double prime between tabulated inputs are reported as what the table permits, and any claim of monotonicity or concavity across a whole interval is either withheld or explicitly conditioned on an assumption stated in the response. The notation is handled cleanly, so a value of f prime at an input is distinguished from f prime as a function. BC-ERR-05049, reading a finite table as settling behaviour between the listed inputs, does not appear.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The signs in the table are read correctly and the conclusion overreaches, asserting monotonicity or concavity across an interval from three tabulated values, which is BC-SIG-05039 and BC-ERR-05049. The claim then exceeds what the data support and the justification point is unavailable even though the underlying sign reading was right.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: When the two rows of the table cannot be combined into a statement about f at all, the earlier skill is BC-SKL-05047, building a combined sign table for the first and second derivatives. A different tell, answering about f when the table listed f prime, is BC-PRQ-06005, reading function notation and distinguishing a function from its value at a point.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05026 (a finite table taken as a full description of the function) for the conceptual failure; misreading which object the table lists points instead to BC-PRQ-06005 (function notation, composition, and evaluation)

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: From selected values of f' or f'' in a table, determine sign changes, monotonicity, and concavity of f, noting what a finite table cannot settle.
skills.description_plain: Use a table of derivative values to say what the function does.
skills.name: Answer a question about a function from tabulated derivative values

common_confusions: BC-MIS-07025 (the capacity assumed to need the solved equation)
BC-MIS-07024 (the limiting factor treated as incidental)
BC-SKL-07012 (the zero slope locus of a general slope field)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-07009 (the value and the reason are scored from the equation rather than from a formula)
adaptive.mastered_if: The nonzero value of the quantity at which the right side vanishes is reported as the carrying capacity, read off the factored form rather than obtained by solving the equation; BC-ERR-07040 is absent, so neither zero nor the constant of proportionality is offered in its place.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The logistic equation is written correctly and the constant of proportionality, or zero, is reported as the capacity, BC-ERR-07040 with signal BC-SIG-07039; or partial fractions are used to solve for a value the factored right side already shows.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The limiting factor is missing from the equation, a gap at BC-SKL-07039; or the zeros of a product cannot be found, BC-PRQ-05001.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-07025 (the capacity is a zero of the right side). Procedural failure: BC-PRQ-05001 (setting each factor of the product to zero).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Find the nonzero value of the quantity at which the right side vanishes and report it as the carrying capacity.
skills.description_plain: Read the ceiling straight off the equation.
skills.name: Identify the carrying capacity from the form of the equation

common_confusions: BC-MIS-07026 (the limit thought to need the solution formula)
BC-MIS-07025 (the capacity thought to need solving)
BC-MIS-07009 (an equilibrium level treated as crossable)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-07009 (the value and the reason drawn from the equation are the two points)
adaptive.mastered_if: The sign of the right side between the equilibrium levels is combined with the initial value to state the limit of the quantity as the independent variable grows without bound, and the reason names which values make the rate positive; BC-ERR-07041, BC-ERR-07044, and BC-ERR-99035 are absent, so no partial fractions solution is produced for a value the equation gives directly.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The limiting value is correct and nothing says why solutions move toward it from the given start, BC-ERR-07041 with signal BC-SIG-07040; or the equation is separated and solved to reach the same number, BC-ERR-07044, which spends the part on work the question did not ask for.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The carrying capacity was misread from the equation, a gap at BC-SKL-07040; or long run behaviour cannot be argued from a field or a sign, BC-SKL-07017.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-07026 (the sign of the rate on each side of the capacity settles the limit). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-07040 (reading the equilibrium levels off the right side).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Use the sign of the right side between the equilibrium levels together with the initial condition to state the limit of the quantity as the independent variable grows without bound.
skills.description_plain: Say where the quantity is heading, using the equation and the starting value.
skills.name: Determine the limiting value without solving the equation

common_confusions: BC-MIS-07023 (a number treated as a complete interpretation)
BC-MIS-07026 (the solution formula thought necessary before anything can be said)
BC-SKL-07037 (interpreting the rate constant of an exponential model)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-07009 (each value is paired with a reason drawn from the equation and stated in context)
adaptive.mastered_if: The carrying capacity, the sign of the rate on each side of it, and the fastest change value are each read back into the situation, naming the modelled population or quantity and its units, so the numbers are stated as facts about that population; BC-ERR-07043, BC-ERR-99027, BC-ERR-99005, and BC-ERR-07044 are absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The capacity and the fastest change value are correct and neither is read back into the situation, signal BC-SIG-07042 and BC-ERR-07043, so the sentence lacks the quantity or the units; or the equation is solved to support an interpretation the equation already gives, BC-ERR-07044.

adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-07023 (an interpretation states what the number measures for the population). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-07003 (naming the quantity and its units before interpreting).

common_confusions: BC-MIS-09004 (the second derivative assumed to follow the pattern of the first)
BC-SKL-09008 (the division by dx/dt that completes the second derivative)

adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The first derivative dy/dx is correct and the next step replaces each component derivative by its second derivative, which is BC-ERR-09009 and exactly the observation in BC-SIG-09002.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The quotient rule applied to the expression for dy/dx goes wrong in its own terms, which is a differentiation gap rather than a parametric one; misreading which expression is to be differentiated is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-09004 (what is being differentiated at the second step) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-09007 as a quotient rule application for the procedural case.

common_confusions: BC-MIS-09004 (the second derivative assumed to follow the pattern of the first)

adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The derivative of dy/dx with respect to the parameter is computed correctly and handed in as the second derivative, the second division by dx/dt omitted, which is BC-ERR-09010; or the whole step is replaced by a quotient of second derivatives, which is BC-ERR-09009 and BC-SIG-09002.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The derivative of dy/dx with respect to t was not obtained, so there is nothing to divide, which is BC-SKL-09007; reading dy/dx as a function of t at all is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-09004 (why the chain rule supplies a second division by dx/dt) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-09007 (differentiating the slope with respect to the parameter) for the procedural case.

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10001 (terms and total not separated)

BC-ERR-10001 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A correct closed form for S sub n is produced and the limit step is omitted, so the answer stops at a partial sum, which is BC-ERR-10002 and matches BC-SIG-10024, or the limit of a sub n is taken in place of the limit of S sub n, which is BC-ERR-10001.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The limit of the closed form cannot be evaluated because the ratio of expressions in n is not handled, which is BC-PRQ-10004 rather than a partial-sum gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10002 (the series value defined as the limit of its partial sums) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10004 (limits in the index) for the procedural case

common_confusions: BC-MIS-09007 (any interval containing the curve assumed to give its area)

adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The zeros of r are located correctly and limits spanning two consecutive loops, or a full period, are used, so the loop is covered more than once, which is BC-ERR-09016.

adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-09007 (what a single loop requires of the limits) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-09002 (solving r equal to zero) for the procedural case.

common_confusions: BC-MIS-02007 (a vertical tangent read as a slope)
BC-SKL-02022 (a corner, where the one sided slopes are finite and unequal)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-02005 (the existence of the derivative at a continuous point must be decided with a reason, which separates a corner from a vertical tangent)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response states that the difference quotient is unbounded where the tangent line is vertical, so no derivative value exists although the function is continuous there, and does not report the derivative as zero at such a point (BC-ERR-02014 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The point is identified as one where the derivative fails to exist but the reason given is the appearance of the curve rather than the unbounded difference quotient, so the verdict is right and the mechanism is not named.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Nonexistence of a limit from unbounded values cannot be recognised, which is a gap at BC-SKL-01012 rather than a confusion about tangent orientation.

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01019 (continuity read from the family of the formula rather than from its domain)
BC-SKL-01048 (determining continuity on intervals, which uses this list)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01006 (a piecewise rule tested at a named input, where the candidate inputs must first be located)
adaptive.mastered_if: Every candidate input is listed, meaning each boundary of the partition and each input excluded from the branch expression that covers it, and the list is produced from the rule rather than from a graph, with branch conditions matched to sides correctly (BC-ERR-01017 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The partition boundaries are all listed but inputs where a branch expression is itself undefined, such as a zero of a denominator inside a branch, are omitted, so the search is limited to the seams of the rule.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Branch conditions cannot be read, so an input is assigned to the wrong branch, which is BC-PRQ-01003, or the excluded inputs of a rational or radical branch cannot be found, which is BC-PRQ-01008.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01019 (a break can sit inside a branch, not only at a seam) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-01008 (domains of branch expressions) for the procedural failure

common_confusions: BC-MIS-02003 (the limit symbol as an ornament on the answer)
BC-SKL-02008 (the derivative function, which replaces a by the variable)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-02002 (the difference quotient inside a limit is scored separately from the simplification and the value)
adaptive.mastered_if: f prime of a is written as the limit as h tends to zero of the quotient of f(a plus h) minus f(a) by h, with the limit symbol on every line that still contains h (BC-ERR-02006 absent), and the object produced is a number at the fixed input a rather than a function (BC-ERR-02030 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The quotient is correct and the limit symbol appears only on the final line, which is BC-ERR-02006 and costs a notation point where the definition itself is assessed.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: f(a plus h) is not read as one function value at a shifted input, which is a gap at BC-PRQ-02005, and inability to form the quotient at all is BC-SKL-02001.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-02003 (what each intermediate line asserts before the limit is taken) for the conceptual failure; BC-SKL-02001 (forming the increment quotient) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts

common_confusions: BC-MIS-02003 (the limit symbol attached to the answer only)

adaptive.mastered_if: f prime of a is written as the limit as x tends to a of the quotient of f(x) minus f(a) by x minus a, and the response states that this form and the increment form describe the same number, naming what plays the role of h in each.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The two point form is written correctly but the equivalence with the increment form is asserted without saying that x minus a is the increment, so the two are held as separate formulas.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The two point difference quotient cannot be formed at all, which is a BC-SKL-02002 gap, and misreading which value is subtracted is BC-PRQ-02005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-02003 (the limit as governing the whole quotient) for the conceptual failure; BC-SKL-02002 (forming the two point quotient) for the procedural failure

common_confusions: BC-MIS-06023 (the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus part one applied as a fixed template with no chain rule)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-06012 (differentiating an accumulation function with a variable upper limit and evaluating the derivative at a point)
adaptive.mastered_if: Two factors appear in the answer. For h(x) equal to the integral from a to u(x) of f(t) dt the response writes h prime of x as f of u(x) times u prime of x, states where the chain rule enters, and evaluates the integrand at the composite upper limit rather than at x or at t. BC-ERR-06027 (the extra factor omitted) is absent, and the structure holds when u is something like x squared or 2x rather than only in a memorised case.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: BC-SIG-06022 describes the usual halfway state, where the reported derivative is the integrand at the composite upper limit with no extra factor, and BC-ERR-06027 records the consequence that the answer is not credited although the theorem may be. Asking for u prime on its own tells an omission from an absent rule, since a correct value there means the chain rule is available but was not brought into the accumulation setting.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: BC-SKL-03002 is the earlier failure that masquerades as this one, visible when u prime cannot be produced for a two layer composite even outside any integral. BC-SKL-06018 is implicated when the simple case g prime equals f is itself unavailable, and BC-PRQ-06005 when f(u(x)) cannot be read as the composition it is.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-SKL-06018 (the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus part one in the simple case) when the conceptual link between the theorem and the upper limit is missing; a procedural failure to produce u prime points instead to BC-SKL-03002 (differentiating a two layer composite function with the chain rule).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08002 (the definite integral itself read as the average)
BC-MIS-06011 (integral read as area regardless of sign)

adaptive.partially_mastered_if: All the geometric pieces are computed correctly and the integral value is reported as the average, the division by the interval length never appearing, which is BC-ERR-08001; or a portion of the graph below the axis is counted as a positive contribution, which is BC-ERR-08003 and leaves the quotient structure intact while the number is too large.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The area of a trapezoid, triangle, or semicircle on the figure is itself wrong, which is BC-PRQ-06007 rather than an averaging gap; reading area from a graph at all, including the sign convention, sits at BC-SKL-06028.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08002 (the division that turns accumulated signed area into a mean value) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-06028 (signed area from a piecewise linear and circular graph) for the procedural case.

common_confusions: BC-MIS-07021 (proportional growth read as linear growth)
BC-MIS-07001 (proportional to read as equal to)

adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A model is written with the right variables and a constant, and it is linear in form, so the quantity grows by equal amounts rather than at a rate proportional to itself, BC-ERR-07034 with signal BC-SIG-07033; or the constant of proportionality is dropped, BC-ERR-07001.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The proportionality cannot be turned into a constant multiple at all, a gap at BC-SKL-07001 and BC-PRQ-07003.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-07021 (a constant rate constant is not a constant rate). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-07001 (writing the derivative equal to a constant times the quantity).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts

common_confusions: BC-MIS-07021 (linear growth expected from proportional growth)
BC-MIS-07016 (the constant omitted, so the initial value has no place to go)

adaptive.mastered_if: The proportional model is solved with the stated initial value to give the initial value multiplied by the exponential of the constant times the independent variable, so the initial amount is the leading coefficient and the rate constant sits in the exponent; BC-ERR-07035 is absent, and the formula returns the initial value at the initial input.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The exponential family is chosen correctly and the initial value appears inside the exponent, or the rate constant multiplies outside it, BC-ERR-07035 with signal BC-SIG-07034, so the formula fails either the initial condition or the equation.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The separation and constant work that produces the exponential form is incomplete, a gap at BC-SKL-07027 and BC-SKL-07029; or the proportional model was never written, BC-SKL-07034.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-07021 (the exponential is what proportional growth produces). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-07029 (fixing the leading coefficient from the initial value).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Solve the proportional growth equation with the stated initial value, obtaining the initial value multiplied by the exponential of the constant times the independent variable.

common_confusions: BC-MIS-07022 (the constant assumed readable from one data pair)
BC-MIS-07021 (a linear reading of the growth)

adaptive.mastered_if: A second input and output pair is substituted into the exponential solution and the rate constant is extracted with a logarithm, the initial value having already fixed the leading coefficient; BC-ERR-07036 is absent, so two pieces of data are used rather than one.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The exponential form is correct and the constant is computed from the initial condition alone, so it remains undetermined and the reported number is arbitrary, BC-ERR-07036 with signal BC-SIG-07035.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The exponential solution is misassembled, a gap at BC-SKL-07035; or the logarithm needed to isolate the exponent is unavailable, BC-PRQ-07001 and BC-PRQ-06003.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-07022 (the initial value and a second pair play different roles). Procedural failure: BC-PRQ-07001 (taking a logarithm to isolate the exponent).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Substitute a second input and output into the exponential solution and solve for the constant using a logarithm.
