common_confusions: BC-MIS-05011 (the plotted curve is treated as the function under discussion)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05009 (relating the graphs of a function and its first two derivatives, with three objects in play at once)
adaptive.mastered_if: The drawn curve rises exactly on the stretches where the plotted f prime sits above the axis, falls where it sits below, and changes bending at the inputs where f prime turns, with every relative extremum of the sketch placed at a crossing of the axis by f prime rather than at a turning point of it. BC-ERR-05042, putting turning points of the sketch at the zeros of the wrong object, is absent, and so is BC-ERR-05016, reporting concavity when monotonicity was asked for or reading increase of f off a rising f prime.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Slopes and directions come out right on part of the domain while the bending information is read off the wrong feature, matching BC-SIG-05033, where the drawn function turns where the given derivative turns instead of where it crosses the axis. Another partial state keeps the shape roughly correct but swaps the two vocabularies, which is BC-ERR-05016, increase of the derivative confused with positivity of the derivative, so extrema and inflection points end up interchanged across the sketch in the way BC-ERR-05042 describes.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Reading the sign of f prime off the plot is itself unreliable, which is BC-SKL-05015, reading intervals of increase and decrease from the graph of the derivative. The tell is that the sketch rises and falls on stretches that do not line up with where the plotted curve is above or below the axis, so no amount of attention to bending repairs it. A second earlier failure is BC-SKL-05031, deciding concavity from whether the derivative graph rises or falls, shown by a sketch whose bends are unrelated to the slopes of f prime.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05011 (the plotted curve read as the function itself) for the conceptual failure, while a sketch built on the right referent but drawn with features in the wrong places points instead to BC-SKL-05015 (reading intervals of increase and decrease off the derivative graph)

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05012 (a gap in the domain treated as not interrupting an interval of behaviour)
BC-MIS-05010 (increase and decrease decided from whether the function values are positive or negative)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05008 (intervals of increase or decrease supported by the sign of the named derivative)
adaptive.mastered_if: The number line is cut at the critical points of f and at every point of discontinuity, a vertical asymptote or a domain gap included, and a sign for f prime is recorded on each open piece with nothing claimed across a break. Reported intervals therefore stop at the gap instead of spanning it, the chart reads the same whether f arrives as a formula in BC-REP-01 or as a described situation in BC-REP-04, and BC-ERR-05017, partitioning at the zeros of the derivative alone while ignoring a domain gap, is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Signs are correct on every piece of a chart that was partitioned at the zeros of f prime only, so an interval spans an input where f does not exist, which is BC-ERR-05017. A weaker intermediate state splits the line at the zeros of f rather than of f prime, matching BC-SIG-05013, and another reports one continuous interval of increase straight through a vertical asymptote.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: A chart with the right partition points and a wrong sign on a piece is BC-SKL-05014 unfinished rather than a charting failure, while an inability to say where f is undefined for a piecewise, rational or radical form is BC-PRQ-05003, visible as a chart with no gap marked at all.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05012 (behaviour cannot be claimed across an input where the function does not exist) for the conceptual failure. Where the domain is understood and the signs themselves are wrong, the target is BC-SKL-05014.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Partition the domain at the critical points and the points of discontinuity, then record the sign of f' on each open piece.
skills.description_plain: Lay the critical points and gaps on a line and mark the sign in each gap.

common_confusions: BC-MIS-04001 (amount and rate read as the same information)
BC-MIS-04002 (the sign of a rate treated as decoration)
BC-SKL-04005 (interpreting a rate once it is correctly identified)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-04001 (both a function value and a derivative value are available in the stem)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response says whether the question asks for a value of the modelled function or a value of its derivative, and says which of the two the stem supplies, using the units in the stem as the test; BC-ERR-04003 is absent, so an amount is not returned where a rate was requested or the reverse.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The computation is carried out correctly on the quantity the stem happens to emphasise and answers the other question, BC-ERR-04003 with signal BC-SIG-04002, a state that resolves when the units of the requested answer are asked for first.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The stem cannot be parsed into a quantity and its rate at all, a contextual reading gap at BC-PRQ-04008 rather than a derivative gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-04001 (amount and rate are different quantities with different units). Procedural failure: BC-PRQ-04008 (reading the question for which of the two it names).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a contextual question, decide whether the quantity requested is a value of the modelled function or a value of its derivative, and say which of the two the given information supplies.
skills.description_plain: Say whether the question is asking how much there is or how fast it is changing.
skills.name: Distinguish the value of a function from the value of its derivative in context
skills.notation: amount against rate

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08006 (the integral of a rate read as the amount of the quantity)
BC-SKL-08009 (the same structure one level up, position from velocity)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08003 (acceleration is given and a velocity at a later time is requested)
adaptive.mastered_if: Velocity at time b is expressed as the given velocity at time a plus the definite integral of acceleration from a to b, with the initial velocity present as a term and the limits running from the time of the known value to the time requested; the reported velocity keeps its sign, and BC-ERR-08011 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The integral of acceleration is computed correctly and reported as the velocity, the known velocity at the earlier time left out of the expression, which is BC-ERR-08011 applied one derivative level down from position.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The initial value plus accumulation structure is itself missing, which is BC-SKL-06037; confusing a(t) with v(t) in the prompt, so the wrong function is integrated, is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08006 (accumulated acceleration as change in velocity) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-06037 (adding the initial value to an accumulation) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an initial velocity at time a and an acceleration function, evaluate the velocity at time b as the initial velocity plus the definite integral of acceleration from a to b.
skills.description_plain: Add the accumulated change in velocity to the starting velocity.
skills.name: Determine a velocity value from an initial velocity and acceleration

common_confusions: BC-MIS-09001 (the parameter treated as the horizontal coordinate)
BC-SKL-09002 (the quotient of the two derivatives, which is a later step)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-09001 (the two component derivatives are needed before any slope, so each can be checked alone)
adaptive.mastered_if: Both x and y are differentiated with respect to the parameter and the two results are reported separately and labelled, chain and product rules applied where the components require them; the derivatives are taken with respect to t rather than with respect to each other, and BC-ERR-09001 does not appear in either component.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: One component derivative is correct and the other carries a differentiation slip, so every later quantity built on it is off, which is BC-ERR-09001; the structure of the parametric work stands while one of the two rates does not.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The notation x(t) and y(t) is read as though t were the horizontal coordinate, so the derivative taken is not with respect to the parameter, which is BC-PRQ-06005 together with the belief in BC-MIS-09001.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-09001 (what the parameter is and what it is not) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-09001 as a differentiation step, with the chain rule on the component that needs it, for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given x and y as functions of the parameter, compute the derivative of each with respect to the parameter.
skills.description_plain: Find dx/dt and dy/dt separately.
skills.name: Differentiate each component of a parametric curve with respect to the parameter

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10015 (the two labels treated as one)
BC-MIS-10016 (the two classifications ordered on a single scale)
BC-SKL-10035 (the absolute case)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10007 (the classification requires both verdicts and a named series)
BC-QA-10015 (a conditionally convergent endpoint series is the usual setting)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response reports two findings, that the signed series converges and that the series of absolute values diverges, and gives the label conditionally convergent with both findings as the reason. BC-ERR-10023 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Both tests are run and the label attached reverses them, which is BC-ERR-10023, or only one of the two findings is produced and the label is written as though both had been established.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: One of the two tests cannot be carried out on its series, so only one verdict exists: that points at BC-SKL-10034 or BC-SKL-10030 rather than at the classification.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10016 (conditional and absolute as exclusive, not graded) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-10034 (testing the absolute value series) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given that a series converges and that the series of absolute values diverges, state that the series converges conditionally and give both findings as the reason.
skills.description_plain: Say the series converges but its absolute value series does not.
skills.name: Classify a series as conditionally convergent

common_confusions: BC-MIS-03001 (differentiation treated as acting on the outermost shell only)
BC-MIS-03002 (both chain rule factors read at the same input)
BC-SKL-03026 (classifying by outermost operation across all rules, not only composition)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-03001 (a symbolic composite with a product or a second layer inside forces the decomposition to be explicit)
BC-QA-03009 (rule choice is scored before any derivative is written)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response names the outer function and the inner function of a composite formula before any differentiation happens, so that a nested power, radical, or exponential is labelled by the operation applied last rather than by its appearance, and the labelling holds when the inside is itself a product or a quotient; BC-ERR-03001 is absent because the inner function is identified as a separate object.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The outer shell is named correctly and the inner function is described only as what is left over, so a second layer inside the inner function goes unnamed; or the decomposition is right and the response still proceeds to differentiate the outer shell alone, which is BC-ERR-03001, the inner derivative left out of the product.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The response cannot say which operation is applied last when the formula is evaluated at a number, a function notation and composition gap at BC-PRQ-03001 rather than a chain rule gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-PRQ-03001 (composition as one function fed into another, evaluated from the inside out). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-03026 (reading the last operation performed off the written form).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a formula built by composition, identify the outer function and the inner function so that the chain rule can be applied.
skills.description_plain: Name which operation is applied last and which is applied first in a formula.
skills.name: Decompose a composite function into outer and inner functions
skills.notation: f of g of x

common_confusions: BC-MIS-02010 (every function differentiated by the power rule)
BC-SKL-02044 (tangent and cotangent, where these two derivatives are inputs to a quotient rule)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-02007 (an expression containing sine or cosine differentiated term by term, where a sign error is isolated)
adaptive.mastered_if: The derivative of sine is written as cosine and the derivative of cosine as the negative of sine, with the negative sign present (BC-ERR-02018 absent), and neither function is differentiated by lowering an exponent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The pairing of sine with cosine is right and the sign on the derivative of cosine is dropped, which is BC-SIG-02012 and BC-ERR-02018, so only the sign is at fault.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Exact values and the bounds of sine and cosine are not available, so the behaviour that fixes the sign cannot be checked, which is a gap at BC-PRQ-01005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-02010 (which rule belongs to a transcendental function) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-01005 (the behaviour of sine and cosine near the origin) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Write the derivative of the sine function as the cosine function and the derivative of the cosine function as the negative of the sine function.
skills.description_plain: Recall that sine gives cosine and cosine gives negative sine.
skills.name: Differentiate sine and cosine

common_confusions: BC-MIS-04017 (sampled values taken to establish behaviour on an interval)
BC-MIS-04005 (a zero of speed confused with a zero of velocity)
BC-SKL-04012 (reporting the sign analysis rather than finding the zeros)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-04004 (the zeros of the velocity partition the interval the analysis must cover)
adaptive.mastered_if: The equation velocity equal to zero is solved on the stated interval rather than probed at integer times, so a non integer zero is found, and the sign of the velocity on either side of each zero is checked to decide where the particle changes direction; BC-ERR-04010 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Integer times are substituted into the velocity in place of solving, so some zeros are located and a non integer one is missed, BC-ERR-04010, which the 2025 Chief Reader report ties to the loss of the analysis points; or the zeros are all found and no sign change is tested, so being at rest and changing direction are not distinguished.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The equation cannot be solved on the interval even with technology available, an equation solving gap at BC-PRQ-04009 rather than a motion gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-04017 (a zero can sit between any two sampled inputs). Procedural failure: BC-PRQ-04009 (solving the velocity equation on the stated interval).

skills.assessability_basis: isolated by BC-QA-04010
skills.description_formal: Given a velocity function, solve the equation velocity equal to zero on the stated interval and determine at which of those times the sign of the velocity changes.
skills.description_plain: Solve for the times when the velocity is zero, then check whether the sign changes there.
skills.name: Find when a particle is at rest or changes direction
skills.notation: v of t equals zero

common_confusions: BC-MIS-03010 (radical and rational forms exchanged)
BC-MIS-03001 (only the outer shell differentiated)
BC-SKL-03025 (an inverse trigonometric factor inside a product needs the enclosing rule)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-03007 (an inner expression that is not a single variable separates substitution from recall)
adaptive.mastered_if: The inner expression replaces the variable everywhere in the standard formula, so an inverse tangent of u yields u prime over one plus u squared with the inner derivative multiplied on, and the same substitution reaches inside a radical for the inverse sine form; BC-ERR-03018 is absent because neither the substitution nor the inner factor is partial.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The correct standard formula is written with the variable left in the denominator instead of the inner expression, or with the inner expression substituted and the inner derivative factor missing, BC-ERR-03018 with signal BC-SIG-03010.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The wrong member of the inverse trigonometric family is recalled before any substitution happens, BC-ERR-03017 and a gap at BC-SKL-03021; or the chain rule factor is missing on ordinary composites too, a gap at BC-SKL-03002.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-03001 (the inner expression is a varying input, so its rate multiplies). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-03021 (the standard formula itself).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given an inverse trigonometric function composed with a differentiable inner function, substitute the inner function into the standard formula and multiply by the derivative of the inner function.
skills.description_plain: Use the formula with the inner expression in place of x, then multiply by the derivative of the inner expression.
skills.name: Differentiate an inverse trigonometric function of an inner expression
skills.notation: derivative of arctan u equals u prime over one plus u squared

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10007 (the name of the test taken as the argument)
BC-MIS-10014 (a ratio limit of one read as a result)
BC-SKL-10022 (choosing the comparison series once comparison is chosen)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10001 (the choice is free, so the verdict rests on the conditions of whatever test is chosen)
BC-QA-10015 (the two endpoint series often need different tests)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response names a test whose hypotheses this series meets and ties the choice to a visible feature of a sub n, a constant quotient for the geometric test, a factorial or a power of n for the ratio test, a rational expression for comparison or limit comparison against a p-series, a sign changing factor for the alternating series test, or a positive decreasing continuous f for the integral test, and the conditions are verified rather than asserted. BC-ERR-10009 and BC-ERR-10015 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A test that does fit is named and its conditions are never established, which is BC-ERR-10009, or a comparison is aimed at an alternating series or the alternating series test at a series of positive terms, which is BC-ERR-10015.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The general term cannot be read out of the sigma, so no form cue is available, which is BC-PRQ-10008, or a constant quotient is not recognised, which is BC-PRQ-10005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10007 (matching hypotheses to the series) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10008 (reading the general term) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a series, name a test whose hypotheses the series meets, using cues such as a constant ratio for the geometric test, a factorial or a power of n for the ratio test, a rational expression for comparison or limit comparison to a p-series, an alternating factor for the alternating series test, and a positive decreasing continuous function for the integral test.
skills.description_plain: Choose the test that matches the shape of the terms before computing anything.
skills.name: Select an appropriate convergence test from the form of the general term

common_confusions: BC-MIS-02006 (the implication read as running both ways)
BC-MIS-02007 (differentiability judged from the appearance of the curve)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-02005 (a function continuous at a point where the existence of the derivative must be decided with a reason)
adaptive.mastered_if: A specific function is produced that is continuous at a point where it has no derivative, such as an absolute value at its corner or a cube root at its vertical tangent, the continuity at that point is checked, and the response states that continuity does not imply differentiability (BC-ERR-02012 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A correct example is named but the failure of the derivative is supported only by how the graph looks, which is BC-ERR-02013, so the example is right and the reason is not tied to the one sided slopes.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: A jump discontinuity cannot be classified, so the example offered is discontinuous and settles nothing about the converse, which is a gap at BC-SKL-01040.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-02006 (the direction of the implication) for the conceptual failure; BC-SKL-02022 (producing the one sided slopes that make the example work) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Produce a function continuous at a point at which it has no derivative, such as an absolute value at its corner or a cube root at its vertical tangent, and state that continuity does not imply differentiability.
skills.description_plain: Produce an example showing that the converse of the implication fails.
skills.name: Give a continuous function that fails to be differentiable at a point

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01009 (continuity taken to be a single condition)
BC-MIS-01001 (the limit reported as the value, which makes the comparison vacuous)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01006 (a piecewise function at a named input, with the value and limit scored separately from the justification)
adaptive.mastered_if: f(c) is evaluated from the branch that defines the value at c, the left and right limits are evaluated from the branches applying on those sides, the limit is compared with f(c), and the verdict follows from that comparison, with no conclusion drawn from the defined value alone (BC-ERR-01014 absent), from matching one sided limits alone (BC-ERR-01015 absent), or from a value substituted into the wrong branch (BC-ERR-01017 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Both one sided limits at the boundary are correct and the conclusion ignores the defined value, which is BC-SIG-01007 and BC-ERR-01015, or the definition is stated in full and then only one of the conditions is actually tested, which is BC-SIG-01006.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The boundary input is substituted into the branch that does not apply on that side, which is BC-PRQ-01003 and BC-ERR-01017, or the three conditions cannot be listed at all, which is a BC-SKL-01043 gap rather than a failure to execute the test.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01009 (why all three conditions are checked) for the conceptual failure; BC-SKL-01023 (evaluating the one sided limits from the correct branches) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: For a given function and input, evaluate f(c), determine the limit at c, compare them, and conclude whether f is continuous at c.
skills.description_plain: Work through the three conditions in order and report the outcome.
skills.name: Test continuity at a point by checking the three conditions

common_confusions: BC-MIS-07024 (the logistic model read as exponential with a harmless extra factor)
BC-MIS-07021 (proportional growth read as linear)
BC-SKL-07034 (the plain exponential model)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-07009 (the capacity and the limit are read off the factored right side)
adaptive.mastered_if: A joint proportionality to the amount and to the room remaining is written as a constant multiplied by the quantity multiplied by the difference between the carrying capacity and the quantity, so the rate vanishes both at zero and at the capacity; BC-ERR-07039 is absent, so the limiting factor that supplies the ceiling is present.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The constant and the quantity are written correctly and the factor encoding the capacity is missing, so the model is exponential with no ceiling, BC-ERR-07039 with signal BC-SIG-07038.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: A single proportionality cannot be written as a constant multiple, a gap at BC-SKL-07001 and BC-PRQ-07003.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-07024 (the second factor makes the rate vanish at the capacity). Procedural failure: BC-SKL-07001 (translating each proportionality factor into the product).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Write the derivative as a constant multiplied by the quantity multiplied by the difference between the carrying capacity and the quantity.
skills.description_plain: Turn jointly proportional to the amount and the room left into an equation.
skills.name: Write the logistic equation from a joint proportionality statement

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10021 (validity assumed at every input)
BC-SKL-10061 (the exponential series, which does not alternate)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10017 (substitution into these series is the standard route to a related series)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response writes sine as the alternating sum of odd powers over odd factorials and cosine as the alternating sum of even powers over even factorials, with the sign factor, the parity of the exponents, and the factorials all correct and consistent between the displayed terms and the general term. BC-ERR-10040 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: One of the two series is correct and the other carries the wrong parity, so cosine appears with odd powers, or the alternating factor is dropped from an otherwise correct expansion.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The alternating factor cannot be expressed in the index, which is BC-PRQ-10008, or the factorials cannot be handled, which is BC-PRQ-10002.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-CON-10001 (the parity structure of the trigonometric series) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10008 (writing the alternating factor) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Reproduce the Maclaurin series for sin x and cos x, including the alternating factor, the odd or even powers, and the factorials.
skills.description_plain: Write the sine and cosine series from memory, with the correct parities.
skills.name: Recall the Maclaurin series for sine and cosine

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01018 (vertical and horizontal asymptote statements exchanged)
BC-SKL-01041 (vertical asymptotes, which come from infinite limits at a finite input)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01010 (end behaviour written as a limit and evaluated, which is what the asymptote claim rests on)
adaptive.mastered_if: Once the limit of f at an infinite end is a real number L, the response states that the line y equals L is a horizontal asymptote, and keeps that statement distinct from a vertical asymptote claim about unbounded outputs at a finite input (BC-ERR-01033 absent), with the leading coefficient ratio used only where the degrees agree (BC-ERR-01023 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The end behaviour value is correct but the asymptote is written as x equals L, or the statement is attached to one end without checking the other, so the conversion from limit to line is incomplete.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The limit at infinity itself is wrong because the degrees were not compared, which is a BC-SKL-01058 and BC-PRQ-01004 gap rather than a failure to name the asymptote.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01018 (where the infinity symbol sits in each statement) for the conceptual failure; BC-SKL-01058 (evaluating the limit at infinity) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given that the limit of f as the variable increases or decreases without bound is a real number L, state that the line y equals L is a horizontal asymptote of the graph of f.
skills.description_plain: Turn a finite end behaviour value into a horizontal asymptote.
skills.name: Identify horizontal asymptotes from limits at infinity

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01013 (infinity read as one substitutable value for both ends)
BC-SKL-01059 (naming the asymptote once a value is known)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01010 (behaviour for inputs of large magnitude, which admits both ends and exposes an assumed symmetry)
adaptive.mastered_if: The limits as the variable increases without bound and as it decreases without bound are evaluated as two separate calculations, and two horizontal asymptotes are reported when the values differ, with the sign of the variable handled where a radical or an absolute value makes the ends behave differently (BC-ERR-01024 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The positive end is evaluated correctly and the negative end is asserted by symmetry, so the second value is copied rather than computed, which is BC-ERR-01024 where a radical is present.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Neither end can be evaluated because the degree comparison is unavailable, which is a gap at BC-PRQ-01004 rather than a failure to separate the two ends.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01013 (the two ends as distinct limits) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-01004 (evaluating end behaviour at each end) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Evaluate the limits of f as the variable increases without bound and as it decreases without bound separately, and report both horizontal asymptotes when the two values differ.
skills.description_plain: Check both ends separately because they can differ.
skills.name: Distinguish the limit at positive infinity from the limit at negative infinity

common_confusions: BC-MIS-07001 (proportional to read as equal to)
BC-MIS-07021 (proportional growth read as linear growth)
BC-SKL-07039 (a joint proportionality that also needs the limiting factor)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-07006 (the equation is built from words alone, so the constant is either written or lost)
adaptive.mastered_if: The sentence that a rate of change is proportional to the amount is written as the derivative of the quantity equal to a constant multiplied by that quantity, with the constant of proportionality present and named; BC-ERR-07001 is absent, so the derivative is not set equal to the quantity itself, and the response can say what changes in the model when the quantity grows twice as fast.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The derivative is on the left and the quantity on the right with no constant between them, BC-ERR-07001 with signal BC-SIG-07001; or the equation is written for the amount rather than for its rate, the failure BC-ERR-07005 describes.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The phrase proportional to cannot be turned into a constant multiple in any setting, an algebra of models gap at BC-PRQ-07003 rather than a differential equation gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-07001 (proportionality introduces an unknown constant). Procedural failure: BC-PRQ-07003 (writing a proportionality as a constant multiple).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Write the statement that the rate of change of a quantity is proportional to the size of the quantity as the derivative of the quantity equal to a constant multiplied by the quantity.
skills.description_plain: Turn the rate of change is proportional to the amount into an equation.
skills.name: Translate a proportionality statement into a differential equation

common_confusions: BC-MIS-07002 (a differential equation read as an equation for the amount)
BC-MIS-07023 (a number treated as a complete interpretation)
BC-SKL-07037 (interpreting the rate constant once the variables are named)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-07006 (the setup stage where variables and units are established before any calculus)
adaptive.mastered_if: The dependent and independent variables are named with their units and the units of the derivative are given as the quotient of the two, so every letter in the model stands for a stated quantity; BC-ERR-07003, BC-ERR-99005, and BC-ERR-99033 are absent because no symbol is introduced undefined.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The model is written correctly in letters that are never given meanings or units, signal BC-SIG-07002 and BC-ERR-07003, which removes the later interpretation points; or the units reported are those of the quantity rather than of its rate, BC-ERR-99005.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The verbal description cannot be read into a quantity and an independent variable at all, a context gap at BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: Conceptual failure: BC-MIS-07002 (the left side measures a rate, which fixes its units). Procedural failure: BC-ERR-99033 (defining each symbol where it is introduced).

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Name the dependent and independent variables of the model, state their units, and give the units of the derivative as a quotient of the two.
skills.description_plain: Say which quantity is which and in what units.
skills.name: Assign the variables and their units from a verbal description

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10009 (the threshold placed elsewhere than at one)
BC-MIS-10005 (terms tending to zero taken as sufficient)
BC-SKL-10007 (the geometric condition on the ratio)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10004 (the verdict and its reason are scored together)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response compares the exponent p with one, states that the p-series converges when p is greater than one and diverges when p is at most one, and applies that to the exponent actually present, including the case p equal to one. BC-ERR-10014 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The criterion is stated with the boundary at one and the strict case is mishandled, so p equal to one is called convergent, or the criterion is applied to a series that is not a p-series.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The exponent is misread because a radical or a reciprocal was not converted, which is BC-PRQ-06002 rather than a gap in the criterion itself.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-10009 (the p-series threshold) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-06002 (reading the exponent) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a p-series, state that it converges when p is greater than one and diverges when p is at most one, and apply that to the exponent present.
skills.description_plain: Compare the exponent with one and state convergence or divergence.
skills.name: Apply the p-series criterion

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05009 (the derivative assumed to exist wherever the function does, so corners, cusps and vertical tangents never appear)
BC-MIS-05008 (a zero derivative read as the definition of a turning point, so no sign change is checked)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05006 (absolute extremum by the candidates test with a justification covering the whole interval)
adaptive.mastered_if: Corners, cusps and vertical tangents inside the domain of f are hunted for and added to the critical point list alongside the zeros of f prime, with the reason given in terms of f prime failing to exist there rather than being zero. The same sweep happens from a formula as in BC-REP-01 and from a plotted curve as in BC-REP-02, where a break in the derivative graph is marked, and BC-ERR-05011, omitting the inputs at which the derivative fails to exist, does not occur even when the candidates list is long.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Every zero of f prime is present and the corner or cusp is missing, which is BC-SIG-05008 and leaves the candidates list one short so the comparison can select the wrong extremum. A related intermediate state notices the corner but files it as an extremum without checking the sign of f prime on each side.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: A response that cannot say where a radical or rational expression stops being defined is short on BC-PRQ-05003 rather than on this skill, and the sign is a candidate list restricted to a domain the student never wrote down. Failure to locate where the derivative expression is undefined at all points back to BC-PRQ-05001.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05009 (differentiability is a stronger condition than existence of the function) for the conceptual failure. When the family of non-differentiable points is known but never located, the procedural target is BC-PRQ-05003, the domain analysis that says where such points can sit.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Locate inputs in the domain of f where f' is undefined, such as a corner, a cusp, or a vertical tangent, and include them among the critical points.
skills.description_plain: Find the domain inputs where the derivative does not exist.
skills.name: Determine critical points where the first derivative fails to exist

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01009 (one of the three conditions held as the whole definition)
BC-MIS-01001 (the limit read as the value, which collapses the third condition)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01006 (the failing condition must be named, which requires the three to be held apart)
adaptive.mastered_if: All three conditions are stated, that f(c) exists, that the limit of f at c exists, and that the limit equals f(c), as separate requirements, and the response does not offer the existence of f(c) alone or agreement of the one sided limits alone as the definition (BC-ERR-01014 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Two of the three conditions are stated and the third, usually the equality of the limit with the value, is folded into one of the others, so the definition is close but not separable into what can be checked.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The symbols f(c) and the limit of f at c cannot be told apart in writing, which is a function notation gap at BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01009 (the three conditions as independent requirements) for the conceptual failure; BC-PRQ-06005 (writing f(c) and the limit distinctly) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: State that f is continuous at c provided f(c) exists, the limit of f at c exists, and the limit equals f(c).
skills.description_plain: Name the value, the limit, and their agreement.
skills.name: State the three conditions of continuity at a point

common_confusions: BC-MIS-01010 (restating the definition treated as justification)
BC-MIS-01009 (one condition held as the whole definition, so the wrong one is named)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-01006 (carries a justification point that requires naming the failed condition rather than restating the definition)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response names which of the three conditions fails and displays the values that show the failure, for instance the two unequal one sided limits or the limit alongside a different f(c), rather than citing the definition of continuity as the reason (BC-ERR-01016 absent).
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The verdict is correct and a condition is named, but no values are supplied to show the failure, so the reason remains a label rather than an argument.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The values themselves are wrong because the test was executed incorrectly, which is a BC-SKL-01044 gap, and reading f and its limit off the wrong input is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-01010 (what makes a claim justified rather than asserted) for the conceptual failure; BC-SKL-01044 (producing the values the reason cites) for the procedural failure

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Support a claim that f is not continuous at c by naming which of the three conditions fails and giving the values that show the failure.
skills.description_plain: Point to the exact condition that breaks rather than restating the definition.
skills.name: Justify a continuity conclusion by naming the failed condition

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08015 (every volume integral treated as carrying a factor of pi)
BC-MIS-08017 (the difference of squares equated to the square of the difference)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08011 (the named shape is a square, so any pi in the integrand is diagnostic)
adaptive.mastered_if: The volume is written as the definite integral of the square of the difference of the boundary functions over the spanning interval, with no factor of pi, and the squared difference is kept as a single squared quantity rather than distributed term by term; neither BC-ERR-08029 nor BC-ERR-08030 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The squared difference integrand is correct and a factor of pi is carried in front of it, which is BC-ERR-08029 and the state in BC-SIG-08011; or the square of the difference is expanded as the difference of the squares, which is BC-ERR-08030 and drops the cross term.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The side of the square was never written as the distance between the curves, so the wrong quantity is squared, which is BC-PRQ-08004 rather than a volume setup gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08015 (which shape the area formula inside the integral describes) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-08031 (writing the side as the difference of the curves) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Write the volume of a solid with square cross sections as the definite integral of the square of the difference of the boundary functions over the spanning interval.
skills.description_plain: Square the side and integrate it over the interval.
skills.name: Set up the volume integral for square cross sections

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08016 (the cross sectional dimension read as a function value)
BC-MIS-08015 (a factor of pi attached to every volume)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08011 (the base is bounded by two curves, so the side is a difference rather than a single value)
adaptive.mastered_if: The side of the cross section at an input is written as the distance between the two boundary curves there, upper minus lower for vertical slices or right minus left for horizontal ones, so both endpoints of the slice appear in the expression; the axis contributes nothing unless it is itself a boundary, and BC-ERR-08028 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The slicing direction is right and the side is taken as the upper function alone, the lower boundary dropped, which is BC-ERR-08028; the volume that follows is then too large by the strip between the lower curve and the axis.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Distance along an axis between two values is not formed as a subtraction, so the side is never a difference, which is BC-PRQ-08004 rather than a cross section gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08016 (that the slice reaches from one boundary curve to the other) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08004 (writing the distance as a difference) for the procedural case.

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a region and an axis of slicing, write the side of the cross section at an input as the difference of the two boundary functions there.
skills.description_plain: Write the side as the top curve minus the bottom curve at that input.
skills.name: Express the side of a cross section as the distance between the curves

common_confusions: BC-MIS-05020 (concavity and monotonicity treated as the same property)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-05009 (relating the graphs of a function and its first two derivatives, with three objects in play at once)
adaptive.mastered_if: Every relative extremum on the finished sketch sits at an input where f prime changes sign, and every point of inflection sits where f double prime changes sign, so no bending change coincides with a horizontal tangent unless the derivative information actually put one there. The sketch can be checked against the derivative data point by point without contradiction, and BC-ERR-05044, drawing a point of inflection at a turning point of the curve with no justification, does not occur.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Turning points land correctly while inflection points are attached to the same inputs, the situation BC-ERR-05044 describes, so the finished drawing contradicts the derivative data it was built from. BC-SIG-05033 covers the harsher case, where the drawn function turns where the given derivative turns rather than where it crosses the axis, leaving both families of features misplaced together.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The earlier break is BC-SKL-05041, sketching a possible graph of a function from the graph of its derivative, recognisable when the overall rise and fall pattern is already wrong before any feature is placed. When rise and fall are right but the second derivative sign change is never checked, the gap is BC-SKL-05033, confirming a point of inflection by a sign change of the second derivative.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-05020 (slope and bending used interchangeably) for the conceptual failure, and BC-SKL-05033 (confirming a point of inflection by a sign change of the second derivative) when the idea is sound but the check is skipped

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Position every relative extremum at a sign change of f' and every point of inflection at a sign change of f'' when drawing the curve.
skills.description_plain: Put the turning points and bending changes where the derivative information puts them.
skills.name: Place extrema and points of inflection consistently on a sketch

common_confusions: BC-MIS-10005 (the nth term test read as working in both directions)
BC-SKL-10001 (the same limit computed as a statement about a sequence)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-10004 (the test computation is scored separately from the verdict)
BC-QA-10001 (the form of a sub n drives the choice of test)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response extracts a sub n from the sigma, including any alternating factor, and evaluates the limit of a sub n as n increases without bound, with the limit symbol present and the ratio of like degrees in n resolved to the quotient of leading coefficients rather than to zero. BC-ERR-10007 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The general term is extracted correctly and the limit value is wrong, typically a ratio of equal degrees reported as zero, which is BC-ERR-10007, so any verdict resting on it carries no reasoning credit.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The general term cannot be read out of the sigma at all, which is BC-PRQ-10008, or the limit of the ratio in n is the blocker, which is BC-PRQ-10004.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-CON-10001 (the general term as the object of the limit) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-10004 (limits of ratios in n) for the procedural case

skills.assessability_basis: no archetype requiring at most two skills names this skill; assessable only inside multi-skill parts
skills.description_formal: Given a series in sigma form, extract the general term and evaluate its limit as n increases without bound.
skills.description_plain: Take the limit of a sub n as the index grows.
skills.name: Evaluate the limit of the general term of a series
